name: 3/4 Sit-Up
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent to roughly 90 degrees and your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Anchor your feet by hooking them under a sturdy object, a partner's hands, or a foot pad so your lower body stays planted throughout.
Place your fingertips lightly behind or to the sides of your head; do not lace your fingers and pull on your neck.
Tuck your chin slightly toward your chest and gently brace your core to flatten your lower back into the floor. This is your starting position.
Exhale as you flex your hips and spine, curling your torso up off the floor toward your knees in a smooth, controlled motion.
Continue until your torso is roughly perpendicular to the floor (fully upright) and you feel a strong contraction in your abs.
Inhale and lower yourself back down under control, but only travel three-quarters of the way down, stopping before your shoulder blades fully touch the floor.
Keep continuous tension on the abdominals by not resting at the bottom, then immediately begin the next rep.
Avoid jerking with your arms or yanking on your neck; let the abdominals do the work and keep the movement deliberate.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: 90/90 Hamstring
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with one leg extended straight along the floor.
Bend the opposite hip and knee both to 90 degrees, so your thigh points straight up at the ceiling and your shin is parallel to the floor.
Place your hands behind that thigh (just below the knee) to support and stabilize the leg in the 90/90 position.
Keep your head, shoulders, and lower back relaxed and flat on the floor, and keep the extended leg straight with the foot relaxed. This is your starting position.
Slowly straighten the bent leg by extending the knee, raising the foot toward the ceiling until you feel a comfortable stretch along the back of the thigh.
Keep the thigh locked at 90 degrees (pointing up) the entire time; only the lower leg should move.
Pause briefly at the top where you feel the hamstring stretch, without bouncing or forcing the range.
Slowly bend the knee back to the 90/90 starting position under control, exhaling as you relax.
Keep the motion smooth and gentle; never jerk the leg or push into sharp pain.
Perform 10 to 20 controlled repetitions, then switch and repeat with the other leg.

name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your torso tall and your weight balanced evenly on both sit bones.
Position your front leg so the hip and knee are both bent to about 90 degrees, with the shin angled out in front of you and the outer side of that leg resting on the floor.
Position your back leg out to the side, also bent to roughly 90 degrees, with the inner side of that thigh and shin on the floor.
Sit up straight, lengthen your spine, and place your hands on the floor in front of the front shin for support. This is your starting position.
Keeping your back flat and chest lifted, slowly hinge forward at the hips, leaning your torso out over the front shin.
Lower only as far as you can while maintaining a long, neutral spine; you should feel the stretch deep in the outer hip and glute of the front leg.
Breathe slowly and relax into the position, holding for 20 to 40 seconds without bouncing.
Slowly rise back up to a tall seated posture, then reposition your legs to switch the front and back leg and repeat on the other side.

name: Ab Crunch Machine
instructions: Select a light to moderate resistance on the weight stack so you can move with control.
Sit down on the ab crunch machine and adjust the seat so the chest or shoulder pads sit comfortably against your upper body.
Hook your feet under the foot pads provided and rest your triceps or grip the top handles so your arms are bent at roughly 90 degrees.
Sit tall with your back against the pad, your core lightly braced, and your spine neutral. This is your starting position.
Exhale and crunch your upper torso forward by flexing your abs, curling your rib cage toward your pelvis; if the machine allows, simultaneously bring the legs up.
Focus on initiating the movement with your abdominals rather than pushing with your arms or hands.
Continue curling until your abs are fully contracted, keeping the motion slow and controlled.
Pause for one second at the bottom of the crunch and squeeze your abs hard.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position, resisting the weight on the way back and keeping tension on the abs.
Do not let the weight stack slam down or use momentum to swing; control every inch of the range.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Ab Roller
instructions: Kneel on a padded mat and hold the ab roller (ab wheel) with both hands using a firm overhand grip, one hand on each handle.
Place the wheel on the floor directly beneath your shoulders so you are on all fours in a kneeling position, arms straight.
Brace your core tightly and tuck your pelvis slightly so your lower back is flat, not arched. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly roll the wheel straight forward, allowing your hips and torso to extend toward the floor as your arms reach out in front of you.
Keep your core braced and your back flat throughout; do not let your lower back sag or your hips pike up.
Extend out as far as you can control without letting your body or chest touch the floor, feeling the stretch and tension through your abs.
Pause briefly at the fully stretched position, maintaining tension in your midsection.
Exhale and pull the wheel back toward your knees by contracting your abs and hip flexors, returning to the starting position.
Move slowly and keep your abs tight at all times; never let the wheel run away from you or collapse your spine.
If you are a beginner, shorten the range of motion and roll out only partway until you build the strength to extend fully.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Adductor
instructions: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie face down with your forearms on the ground supporting your upper body.
Bend one leg out to the side and bring that knee up toward your hip, rotating the leg so the inner thigh rests on top of the foam roller.
Position the roller against the inner thigh between your hip and your knee, and shift as much body weight onto it as you can comfortably tolerate.
Keep your core engaged and your supporting forearms steady to control the pressure. This is your starting position.
Consciously relax the muscles of the inner thigh, then slowly roll your body so the foam moves along the adductor from near the knee up toward the hip.
Roll back and forth at a slow, controlled pace, covering the length of the inner thigh.
When you find a tender or tight spot (a trigger point), pause and hold steady pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds until the tension eases.
Breathe slowly and avoid rolling directly over the knee joint or up into the groin.
Switch to the other leg and repeat the process on the opposite inner thigh.

name: Adductor/Groin
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs raised and extended straight up toward the ceiling.
Spread your legs apart into a comfortable V, then have a partner kneel at your feet and hold the outsides of your feet or ankles.
Abduct (open) your legs as far apart as you comfortably can while your partner supports them. This is your starting position.

Contract the inner-thigh muscles and attempt to squeeze your legs back together against your partner's resistance, holding the effort for 10 or more seconds (an isometric contraction with no actual movement).
After the hold, fully relax the muscles of your inner thighs and let your legs go loose.
As you relax, have your partner gently push your feet farther apart, easing your legs into a deeper stretch.
Hold the deepened stretch only to the point of mild tension, breathing slowly and steadily.
Clearly communicate with your partner and tell them to stop as soon as the stretch feels adequate, to avoid overstretching or straining the groin.
Relax, bring the legs back to neutral, and repeat the contract-relax sequence as desired.

name: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Stand with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and clean a kettlebell up to the rack position on one side.
Press the kettlebell directly overhead and lock out the elbow, so the weight is stacked above your shoulder with the wrist straight and firm.
Turn both feet to point about 45 degrees away from the side holding the kettlebell, and tuck the non-working arm behind your lower back.
Keep your eyes on the overhead kettlebell at all times and keep that arm fully locked out throughout the entire movement. This is your starting position.
Inhale and begin the descent by pushing your hips out laterally in the direction of the locked-out kettlebell, hinging at the hip.
Allow your torso to bend sideways and forward, sliding your non-working hand down the inside of your front leg toward the floor.
Keep the loaded arm vertical and the weight directly over your shoulder as you lower, maintaining a long spine rather than rounding.
Descend as far as your mobility allows, ideally until your free hand touches the floor or your lower leg, feeling the stretch through the hamstrings and obliques.
Pause for a second at the bottom while keeping the kettlebell locked overhead.
Exhale and reverse the motion by driving your hips back under you and contracting your obliques and glutes to return to a tall standing position.
Move slowly and deliberately, never letting the overhead arm bend or drift; control is critical with the weight overhead.
Complete all reps on one side, then carefully bring the kettlebell down and repeat on the other side.

name: Air Bike
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your lower back gently pressed into the floor.
Place your fingertips lightly behind your head with your elbows wide; do not lace your fingers or pull on your neck.

Lift your shoulder blades off the floor into a crunch and raise your legs so your knees are bent to about 90 degrees, thighs perpendicular to the floor and shins parallel to it. This is your starting position.
Exhale and begin a slow bicycle-pedal motion: extend your right leg out straight while drawing your left knee in toward your chest.
At the same time, rotate your torso to bring your right elbow toward your left knee, crunching across your body.
Keep your lower back in contact with the floor and your core braced so the movement comes from your abs, not momentum.
Inhale as you switch: extend the left leg out, draw the right knee in, and rotate to bring your left elbow toward your right knee.
Keep the pace slow and controlled, focusing on twisting through the obliques rather than rushing or flaring the elbows in.
Do not pull your head forward with your hands; keep your neck relaxed and chin slightly tucked.
Continue alternating sides smoothly until you have completed all prescribed repetitions for each side.

name: Airplane Balance
instructions: Stand tall on one leg with a slight, soft bend in the knee of the supporting leg.
Extend your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, like airplane wings, to help you balance.
Engage your core and the glute of the standing leg to stabilize your hips. This is your starting position.
Slowly hinge forward at the hip of the standing leg, lowering your torso toward the floor while extending the free leg straight back behind you.
Continue until your torso and rear leg form roughly a straight horizontal line parallel to the floor, balancing on the single leg.
Keep your back flat, your spine long, and your hips level and square to the ground; do not let the lifted hip rotate open.
Hold the balanced position, breathing steadily and keeping your gaze fixed on a point on the floor for stability.
Slowly return to standing by driving through the glute and hamstring of the supporting leg to bring your torso back upright.
Move with control rather than wobbling; if you lose balance, reset and continue.
Hold for the prescribed time, then switch and repeat on the other leg.

name: All Fours Quad Stretch
instructions: Begin on your hands and knees on a padded mat, with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Shift your weight to support yourself on one hand and the opposite knee, keeping your core braced and back flat.
Lift the foot of the free leg up toward your glutes and reach back with the same-side hand to grasp the top of that foot or the ankle.
Gently pull the heel in toward your buttock, keeping the knee fully flexed, so you feel a stretch along the front of the thigh and hip flexor. This is your starting position.
Keep your hips square and your lower back from over-arching by engaging your core.
Focus on extending your hip and gently thrusting it toward the floor to deepen the stretch in the quadriceps and hip flexor.
Breathe slowly and hold the stretch steadily without bouncing, keeping your supporting arm strong for balance.
Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then release the foot, return to all fours, and repeat on the other leg.

name: Alternate Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your torso straight and a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at full length by your sides.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and turn your wrists so your palms face inward toward your body (neutral grip). This is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your shoulders back, and hold your upper arms stationary against your sides.
Exhale and curl the right dumbbell upward by contracting the biceps and brachialis, keeping the palm facing inward throughout (do not rotate the wrist).
Continue raising the dumbbell until your bicep is fully contracted and the weight is at shoulder level, moving only your forearm.
Hold the top contracted position for a second and squeeze the muscle.
Inhale and slowly lower the right dumbbell back to the starting position under control, fully extending the arm.
Repeat the same curling motion with the left arm; one curl on each side equals one repetition.
Keep your torso still and avoid swinging the weights or using momentum from your back or hips.
Continue alternating arms in this manner for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Alternate Heel Touchers
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, placed about 18 to 24 inches apart.
Extend your arms straight down along your sides, palms facing in, with your shoulders just lifted slightly off the floor.
Tuck your chin slightly and brace your abs to keep your lower back stable. This is your starting position.
Exhale and crunch your torso forward and up about 3 to 4 inches, bending to the right and sliding your right hand down to touch your right heel.
Hold the contraction for a second, squeezing the right side of your obliques.
Inhale and slowly return your torso to the starting position, keeping your shoulders slightly off the floor.
Exhale and crunch forward and up to the left side, sliding your left hand down to touch your left heel, and hold for a second.
Inhale and return to the starting position; touching both heels once counts as one repetition.
Keep the movement controlled and lateral, letting the obliques do the work rather than jerking with your arms or neck.
Continue alternating sides until all prescribed repetitions are completed.

name: Alternate Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to roughly a 45 to 60 degree incline and sit back against it with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down at your sides so the dumbbells are at full extension, with your palms facing inward toward your body and elbows close to your torso.
Press your back into the bench, keep your shoulders relaxed and pinned, and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl the right dumbbell upward by contracting the biceps, and as you lift, rotate your wrist so the palm turns to face up (supinate).
Continue raising the dumbbell until your bicep is fully contracted and the weight is at shoulder level, keeping the upper arm stationary so only the forearm moves.
Hold the top position for a second and squeeze the bicep hard.
Inhale and slowly lower the right dumbbell back to the starting position under control, rotating the palm back to neutral as you reach full extension.
Repeat the curling motion with the left arm; one curl on each side equals one repetition.
Keep your back against the bench and avoid swinging your elbows forward or using momentum; the incline keeps the biceps under a deep stretch, so stay strict.
Continue alternating arms for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
instructions: Find an open, flat surface with good traction and warm up thoroughly, as this is an explosive plyometric drill.
Assume a comfortable athletic stance with your knees slightly bent, one foot positioned slightly in front of the other.
It can help to use a line on the ground as a reference to gauge how far you travel side to side. This is your starting position.
Push off explosively with your front leg, driving the opposite knee forward and as high as possible while leaping diagonally across the line.
Swing your arms naturally to generate power and momentum, just as you would when sprinting.
Aim to cover as much horizontal distance to the side as possible with each bound, landing on the opposite foot.
Land softly on the ball of your foot with a slightly bent knee to absorb the impact, then immediately push off again in the opposite diagonal direction.
Keep your torso upright and your core braced, and stay light and reactive on contact rather than crashing down.
Continue alternating legs, bounding diagonally from side to side, for the prescribed number of reps or distance.
Rest fully between sets to maintain explosive quality on every bound.

name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
instructions: Set the pulleys on a dual cable tower to the bottom position and select an appropriate, matching weight on each side.
Stand between or just in front of the towers and grasp one handle in each hand.
Bring the handles up to shoulder height with your palms facing forward and your elbows bent and pointing down and out.
Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, core braced, head and chest up, and a slight natural arch in your lower back. This is your starting position.
Exhale and extend through one elbow to press that handle directly overhead until the arm is fully but not harshly locked out.
Keep the opposite handle stationary at shoulder height and keep your torso upright; do not lean or twist to push the weight.
Inhale and lower that handle back to shoulder height under control, resisting the cable's pull on the way down.
Press the opposite side overhead in the same controlled manner, then lower it back.
Keep your core tight throughout so the cables do not pull you off balance or arch your lower back excessively.
Continue alternating sides for the prescribed number of repetitions on each arm.

name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, knees softly unlocked, and core braced so your torso stays still throughout the set.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip, palms facing your thighs, and let your shoulders sit down and back, away from your ears.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in both elbows for the entire exercise; this protects the elbow joint and keeps tension on the deltoids rather than the joints.

For the first rep, exhale and raise both dumbbells straight in front of you with controlled effort until they reach shoulder height, keeping your wrists neutral and thumbs roughly level with your shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top, then inhale and lower the dumbbells back to your sides under control without letting them drop or swing.
For the next rep, exhale and raise both dumbbells laterally out to your sides until your arms are parallel to the floor at shoulder height, leading slightly with your elbows.
Pause at the top of the lateral raise, then inhale and lower the weights back to your sides with control.
Continue alternating between front raises and lateral raises, keeping each rep slow and deliberate.
Do not use momentum, lean back, or swing the weights up; if you have to heave, the dumbbells are too heavy and the front and side delts stop doing the work.
Keep your neck relaxed and gaze forward, maintaining an upright chest the whole time.

name: Alternating Floor Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with two kettlebells positioned just outside each hip, then lie back so you are flat on the floor with your knees bent and feet planted.
Roll each kettlebell up to your shoulders one at a time and grip the handles with your palms facing forward, letting the bells rest against the outside of your forearms.
Set your upper arms at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso so your elbows are not flared straight out; this keeps the shoulders safe.
Brace your core, press your lower back gently into the floor, and squeeze both kettlebells tight in your fists to engage your forearms and lats.
Press both kettlebells straight up over your chest until your arms are fully extended and the bells stack directly over your shoulders; this is your starting position.
Inhale and lower one kettlebell under control until your triceps and elbow lightly touch the floor, keeping the other arm locked out and stable overhead.
Pause for a moment when your elbow contacts the floor; do not bounce or let the weight crash down.
Exhale and press that kettlebell back up to full lockout, turning the wrist as needed to track straight over the shoulder.
Repeat on the opposite arm, keeping the supporting arm rigid and the core tight so your torso does not twist or rock.
Continue alternating arms for the prescribed reps, keeping both shoulder blades pulled down and back into the floor throughout.

name: Alternating Hang Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, slightly in front of the line of your toes.
Hinge at your hips by pushing your butt back and bending your knees slightly, keeping your chest up, spine neutral, and eyes forward.
Grip both kettlebell handles with a firm overhand grip and pull them up to a standing position so they hang at arm's length in front of your thighs; this hanging position is your start.
Brace your core and keep your back flat; the power comes from your hips and hamstrings, not your arms or lower back.
Initiate the first clean by hinging slightly and then explosively extending your hips, knees, and ankles to drive one kettlebell upward.

As that kettlebell rises, pull your elbow back and rotate your wrist so your palm turns inward, guiding the bell smoothly to the rack position at your shoulder rather than letting it bang against your forearm.
Keep the other kettlebell hanging at arm's length in your opposite hand while the working bell is racked.
Lower the racked kettlebell back down to the hanging position under control, again rotating the wrist so it returns smoothly.
Immediately repeat the explosive hip extension to clean the opposite kettlebell to its shoulder, alternating sides each rep.
Exhale on the explosive clean and inhale as you lower; keep the movement driven by the hamstrings and glutes, and never round your lower back at the bottom.

name: Alternating Kettlebell Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and clean two kettlebells up to the rack position at your shoulders, so the bells rest on the outside of your forearms with palms facing inward.
In the rack position, keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs, wrists straight and stacked over your elbows, and the kettlebells settled against your forearms.
Brace your core hard, squeeze your glutes, and keep a tall, neutral spine; do not lean back to help press the weight up.
Exhale and press one kettlebell straight overhead by extending your elbow, rotating your wrist as you go so the palm finishes facing forward at lockout.
Finish each press with the arm fully extended, the kettlebell stacked directly over your shoulder, and your bicep near your ear.
Keep the other kettlebell held still in the rack position at your shoulder while you press, maintaining a stable, braced torso.
Inhale and lower the pressed kettlebell under control back to the rack position, reversing the wrist rotation.
Immediately press the opposite kettlebell overhead, alternating arms with each rep.
Keep your core tight and avoid arching your lower back or pushing your hips forward; if you cannot press without leaning back, reduce the weight.

name: Alternating Kettlebell Row
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the floor just in front of your feet, set about shoulder-width apart.
Stand with your feet roughly shoulder-width, bend your knees slightly, and hinge forward at the hips by pushing your butt back until your torso is close to parallel with the floor.
Keep your spine neutral and chest up; do not round your upper back, and let your arms hang straight down as you grip both kettlebell handles with an overhand grip.
Brace your core and set your shoulder blades; this is your starting position with both bells held at arm's length.
Exhale and pull one kettlebell up toward your stomach or lower ribcage, first retracting that shoulder blade and then driving your elbow back and up close to your side.
Squeeze the working-side lat and mid-back at the top, keeping your elbow tucked rather than flared out wide.
Inhale and lower that kettlebell back down to the hanging start position under control, getting a full stretch in the lat.
Keep the non-working kettlebell hanging steady and your hips square; do not twist or rotate your torso to heave the weight up.
Repeat the row with the opposite arm, alternating sides each rep.
Maintain the hip hinge and flat back the entire set, and keep the movement controlled rather than jerking the weight with momentum.

name: Alternating Renegade Row
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the floor about shoulder-width apart, handles aligned so you can grip them comfortably in a push-up position.
Grip the kettlebell handles and assume a high plank, hands stacked under your shoulders on the bells, arms straight, and body in one straight line from head to heels.
Set your feet wider than hip-width for a stable base; a wider stance makes it much easier to resist rotation during the row.
Brace your core hard, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips level and square to the floor; avoid letting your butt pike up or sag down.
Shift your weight slightly toward the supporting arm and press that kettlebell firmly into the floor to anchor yourself.
Exhale and row the other kettlebell up by driving your elbow back toward your hip, retracting that shoulder blade and pulling the bell to your side.
Keep your hips and shoulders as level as possible during the row; the main challenge is resisting the urge to twist your torso open.
Inhale and lower the kettlebell back to the floor under control until it rests on the ground.
Repeat the row with the opposite arm, alternating sides each rep while keeping the plank rigid.
Move slowly and deliberately; if your hips rotate or your form breaks down, widen your feet further or reduce the weight.

name: Ankle Circles
instructions: Stand next to a sturdy object such as a squat rack, wall, or chair and place one hand on it for balance.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right foot a couple of inches off the floor.
Point your right toes and begin tracing a large, slow circle in the air with your big toe, as if drawing a wide circle on a wall in front of you.
Move only through the ankle joint, keeping the rest of your leg relatively still, and take each circle through the fullest comfortable range of motion.
Breathe normally and complete the prescribed number of circles in one direction, counting each full circle as one repetition.
Reverse and perform the same number of circles in the opposite direction with the same foot.
Lower the right foot, switch your weight to the right leg, and repeat the full sequence with the left foot.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled rather than fast; the goal is to mobilize the ankle through its complete range.

name: Ankle Mobility Rock
instructions: Drop into a half-kneeling position with your right foot flat on the floor in front and your left knee resting on the ground behind you.
Position your front foot so your shin is roughly vertical, and keep that front heel firmly planted on the floor the entire time.
Place your hands on your front knee or thigh for light support and keep your torso upright with a neutral spine.
Slowly rock your body forward, driving your front knee out over and past your toes while keeping the heel glued down.
Push only as far as you feel a comfortable stretch through the front of your ankle and calf, without letting the heel lift.
Rock back to the start position under control, then repeat the forward-and-back rocking for the prescribed reps or time.
Switch your front foot and repeat the same rocking motion on the other ankle.
Keep the movement slow and rhythmic, gradually pushing a little deeper as the ankle loosens.

name: Ankle On The Knee
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat with your knees bent and both feet planted flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left thigh just above the knee, letting your right knee open out to the side so you feel a slight opening in the right hip.
Flex your right foot to keep the ankle stable and protect the joint as you cross it over.
Reach both hands through and around to grasp the back of your left thigh or the front of your left knee.
Gently pull both legs in toward your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch deep in the right glute and hip.
Relax your neck, shoulders, and head against the floor, and breathe slowly and evenly while you hold.
Hold the stretch for 10 to 20 seconds without bouncing, easing slightly deeper on each exhale.
Release, lower both feet, and repeat on the other side by crossing the left ankle over the right thigh.

name: Anterior Tibialis-SMR
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs bent and feet flat, or shift into a kneeling position so you can reach the front of your shins.
Identify the anterior tibialis muscle, the strip of muscle running down the outer front of your shin just to the side of the shinbone.
Take a muscle roller, rolling pin, or similar firm tool and place it against that muscle on one leg, just below the knee.
Apply steady, moderate pressure and slowly roll the tool down the muscle from just below the knee toward just above the ankle.
Keep the pressure on the muscle belly itself, not directly on the bony shinbone, to stay comfortable and effective.
When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold pressure there for 10 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly until the tension eases.
Continue rolling the full length of the muscle a few times, working through any knots you find.
Switch to the other leg and repeat the same process from below the knee to above the ankle.

name: Anti-Gravity Press
instructions: Set an incline bench to a moderate angle and place a loaded barbell on the floor behind the head end of the bench.
Lie face down (chest-supported) on the incline bench so your head is at the top and your chest is supported against the pad.
Reach down and grip the barbell with a pronated (overhand) grip at roughly shoulder width.
Curl the bar up off the floor by flexing your elbows, performing a reverse curl until the bar is near your upper chest or chin; this is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your shoulder blades retracted so your upper back does the stabilizing work.
Exhale and press the barbell straight out in front of your head by extending your elbows until your arms are nearly straight.
Keep your upper arms parallel to the floor throughout, so the bar travels horizontally away from your head rather than rising or dropping.
Pause briefly at full extension, feeling the rear deltoids and upper back working.
Inhale and pull the bar back toward your head under control by re-flexing the elbows, returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, keeping the movement smooth and your arms level with the floor the entire time.

name: Archer Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a push-up position with your hands placed wider than normal, roughly one and a half to two times shoulder width apart.
Spread your fingers, turn your hands slightly outward, and set your feet about shoulder-width apart for a stable base.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms one straight line from head to heels with no sagging hips.
Inhale and bend one arm to lower your chest toward that hand, keeping the opposite arm straight and extended out to the side like an archer drawing a bow.
Let the straight arm stay nearly locked with the palm planted, while the bending elbow tracks back at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Lower until your chest is just above the hand of the bending arm, keeping your body rigid and hips square the whole way down.
Exhale and press firmly through the bent arm to push yourself back up to the starting position.
On the next rep, shift your weight and lower toward the opposite hand, alternating sides each repetition.
Keep your hips from twisting or dipping; if the full version is too hard, bend the straight arm slightly to share the load.

name: Arm Circles
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your core lightly braced.
Extend both arms straight out to the sides so they are parallel to the floor and at a 90-degree angle to your torso, forming a T shape.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed, away from your ears, and your palms facing down.
Begin making small, controlled circles about one foot in diameter with both outstretched arms at the same time.
Breathe normally and keep your arms straight and level with the floor as you circle.
Continue circling forward for about ten seconds, keeping the motion smooth and steady.
Reverse direction and circle your arms backward for about ten seconds.
Gradually increase the size of the circles as your shoulders warm up, but stop if you feel any pinching in the joint.

name: Arnold Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an upright position with back support and sit down with your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and bring them up in front of your upper chest with your palms facing your body, elbows bent and tucked in close, as if at the top of a dumbbell curl.
Press your back into the bench, brace your core, and keep your chin slightly tucked with a neutral spine.
Exhale and begin pressing the dumbbells upward while simultaneously rotating your wrists so your palms turn from facing you to facing forward.
Continue the smooth press-and-rotate until your arms are fully extended overhead with palms facing forward and the dumbbells nearly touching above you.
Pause for a second at the top with the weights stacked over your shoulders, keeping your shoulders down rather than shrugged.
Inhale and reverse the motion, lowering the dumbbells while rotating your palms back toward your body so you return to the starting position in front of your chest.
Keep the rotation gradual and controlled throughout so the shoulders stay safe and the movement stays smooth.
Avoid arching your lower back or using momentum; if you cannot control the rotation, reduce the weight.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Around The Worlds
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a flat bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor and your head, shoulders, and hips supported.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand resting near your thighs with your palms facing up toward the ceiling and your arms roughly parallel to the floor.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout the entire movement to protect the joints and shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the bench for a stable base.
Inhale and sweep both dumbbells outward and upward in a wide semicircular arc, moving them from beside your thighs around toward a point above your head.
Keep your arms parallel to the floor and the elbows softly bent for the whole arc, so the dumbbells trace a large half-circle around your body.
Continue until the dumbbells meet near each other above your head at the top of the arc.
Exhale and reverse the same wide semicircular path under control to bring the dumbbells back down to the starting position beside your thighs.
Use a light, manageable weight and keep the motion slow and controlled, since the long lever puts significant stress on the shoulder joints.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, never letting the weights drop or swing quickly.

name: Atlas Stone Trainer
instructions: Load the desired weight onto the Atlas stone trainer (typically made from bar ends or heavy pipe) and set it on the floor in front of you.
Stand over the implement so it sits between or just in front of your feet, with your feet about shoulder-width apart for a stable base.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower down, wrapping both arms underneath and around the implement to hug it close.
Set your back flat with a neutral spine, chest up, and arms locked tightly around the weight; do not round your lower back.
Brace your core hard, then begin standing by extending through your hips and knees to pull the weight up past your knees.
As the weight clears your knees, lap it by resting it on your thighs and sitting back slightly, hugging it tightly into your chest.
From the lap, drive your hips forward and extend your knees explosively to stand the weight up as high as possible.
Keep the implement pulled in tight against your body the entire time to keep the load close and protect your back.
Lower the weight back to your lap or down to the floor under control, re-hinging at the hips for each successive repetition.
Exhale as you extend and stand the weight up, and keep your spine neutral throughout rather than yanking with a rounded back.

name: Atlas Stones
instructions: Position the atlas stone directly between your feet, with your feet set slightly wider than shoulder width and toes pointed slightly out so the stone sits centered against your shins.

Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower your torso over the stone, wrapping both arms vertically down the sides and underneath it. Dig your fingers under the bottom edge (use the flat spot if the stone has one) and pull the stone firmly into your chest and stomach so there is no air gap.
Set your back flat with chest up and lats engaged, brace your core hard, and take a big breath before initiating the pull.
Drive through the back half of your feet (heels and midfoot) and extend the hips and knees together to break the stone off the floor, keeping it glued to your body the entire way up.
As the stone clears your knees, sit your hips back and slightly drop your bodyweight to 'lap' the stone, resting it on top of your thighs while you re-grip.
Squat down and shift your hands up and over the top of the stone, hugging it high onto your upper chest and locking your forearms underneath it.
Stand explosively by driving through your hips and extending your knees, keeping the stone pressed tight to your torso so it does not roll away from your center of gravity.
Step in close to the loading platform, then lean your torso back and snap your hips forward to extend the stone upward and place it on the platform.
Exhale as you complete the load. Keep your spine braced and never let your back round under the stone, as rounding is the most common cause of injury in this lift.

name: Axle Deadlift
instructions: Center the thick axle bar over your midfoot and step in so your shins are roughly an inch from the bar, with feet about hip width apart and toes pointed slightly out.

Hinge at the hips and bend forward to grip the bar just outside your legs at shoulder width. Because the axle is thick and has no knurling spin, use an over/under (mixed) grip to keep it from rolling out of your hands.
Set your grip, then drop your hips and bend your knees until your shins lightly touch the bar. Pull your shoulder blades down and back and let them protract slightly over the bar.
Lift your chest, set your back into a flat, neutral arch, look forward, and take a big breath into your belly to brace your core tightly.
Take the slack out of the bar by pulling up gently until you feel the weight engage, then drive through your heels to push the floor away and raise the bar.

Keep the bar dragging close against your shins and thighs the entire ascent. Once it passes your knees, aggressively pull it back into your body, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and drive your hips forward into the bar.
Lock out tall with hips fully extended, glutes squeezed, and shoulders stacked over the bar. Do not lean back excessively or hyperextend the lower back.
Lower the bar by first pushing your hips back, then bending the knees once the bar passes them, guiding it down the same path to the floor under control.
Reset your breath and brace before each repetition rather than bouncing the bar off the ground.

name: Back Flyes - With Bands
instructions: Loop a resistance band around a stable vertical post such as the upright of a squat rack, at roughly chest height.
Grab one handle or end of the band in each hand and step back until the band develops noticeable tension with your arms extended.
Stand with feet planted firmly at shoulder width, knees softly bent, core braced, and a tall upright torso.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height so they are parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso. This is your starting position.
Keeping a slight, fixed bend in the elbows, exhale and sweep both arms outward and back in a wide arc, leading with the backs of the hands.
Focus on squeezing your rear delts and shoulder blades together rather than yanking with your arms, and continue until your arms are extended out to your sides in line with your torso.
Pause and feel the contraction in the rear shoulders, keeping your shoulders down and avoiding any shrug toward your ears.
Inhale and return your arms slowly and under control to the starting position in front of you, resisting the band the whole way.
Keep your torso still throughout; do not rock backward or use momentum to fling the arms open.

name: Backward Drag
instructions: Load a sled or prowler with your desired weight and attach a rope, strap handles, or harness that you can hold with both hands.
Grab the rope or handles and step back to take up the slack until the line is taut, facing the sled.
Stand with feet about hip to shoulder width apart, lean your torso back away from the sled to counterbalance the load, and bend your knees into a quarter-squat athletic stance.
Brace your core, keep your chest up, and hold your arms firm with the rope pulled into your body so your trunk does the bracing, not just your grip.
Begin walking backward using short, quick, choppy steps, driving hard through your quads and the balls of your feet on each step.
Stay low and keep leaning back so the line of pull stays roughly horizontal, which maximizes quad tension.
Maintain a steady, aggressive pace for the prescribed distance, keeping each step controlled so you do not stumble.
Keep your back flat and avoid rounding forward against the load; the lean should come from a braced, neutral spine.

name: Backward Medicine Ball Throw
instructions: This drill is best done with a partner standing behind you; if alone, throw against a sturdy wall or into a wide-open space and retrieve the ball.
Stand tall with feet shoulder width apart, both you and your partner facing the same direction, with your partner a few meters behind you.
Hold the medicine ball with both hands and let it hang down between your legs with your arms extended.
Set your back flat, chest up, and core braced. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to lower into a squat, letting the ball travel down between your thighs.
Forcefully reverse direction: drive explosively through your heels, extend your hips and knees, and rise onto the balls of your feet.
As you reach full extension, swing your straight arms up and overhead and release the ball backward over your head toward your partner, using the momentum of the hip drive.
Throw for maximum height and distance, treating it as one continuous explosive movement rather than two separate phases.
Have your partner roll the ball back, reset your stance, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Balance Board
instructions: Place a balance board on a flat, non-slip surface directly in front of you, and ideally stand near a wall or rail you can touch for support.
Step one foot onto the center of the board, then bring the second foot up so both feet are roughly hip to shoulder width apart and centered over the board's pivot.
Keep your knees softly bent, your core braced, and your gaze fixed on a point straight ahead to help stabilize.
Make small, constant adjustments through your ankles, calves, and feet to keep the board level and prevent the edges from touching the floor.
Hold your balanced position for the desired duration, keeping your upper body relaxed and your weight evenly distributed.
To progress, try balancing with arms crossed, eyes closed, or on one foot once you are comfortable and stable.

name: Ball Leg Curl
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your arms at your sides, palms down for stability.
Place your lower legs and heels on top of an exercise ball, then adjust so that with your legs fully extended your ankles and Achilles rest on top of the ball. This is your starting position.
Press your arms and shoulder blades into the floor, then lift your hips off the ground so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to feet, keeping your weight on your upper back and the ball.
Maintaining the raised hips, exhale and flex your knees to roll the ball toward your glutes by digging your heels in and contracting your hamstrings.
Pull the ball in as close to you as you can while keeping your hips high and squeezing the hamstrings hard at the top.
Pause briefly at the peak contraction without letting your hips sag toward the floor.
Inhale and slowly straighten your legs to roll the ball back out to the starting position under full control.
Keep your hips elevated for the entire set rather than dropping them between reps, and avoid using momentum to swing the ball.

name: Band Assisted Pull-Up
instructions: Choke a resistance band around the center of the pull-up bar by threading one end through the other so it cinches tight; choose a thicker band for more assistance and a thinner one for less.
Pull the hanging loop of the band down and step or kneel one foot/knee into it, then push down to seat the band securely so it cannot slip free.
Reach up and take a medium to wide overhand grip on the bar, hands slightly wider than shoulder width.
Hang from the bar with arms fully extended, let the band support some of your weight, engage your shoulder blades by pulling them down and back, and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Initiate the pull by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades, then drive your elbows down toward your sides as you contract your lats.
Pull yourself upward smoothly until your chin clears the bar, keeping your chest up and leading with the upper chest toward the bar.
Avoid swinging, kipping, or jerking; let the band assist a controlled, strict pull rather than bouncing you up.
Pause briefly at the top with chin over the bar, then lower yourself slowly and under control until your arms are fully extended again.
Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower, keeping tension on the lats throughout.

name: Band Good Morning
instructions: Stand on one end of a 41-inch loop band with your feet placed about hip width apart, trapping the band firmly under both feet.
Hinge forward and loop the top end of the band behind your neck and across your upper traps (not on the bones of your neck), letting the band run down your back.
Stand back up tall so the band is under tension, with your chest up, shoulders back, and core braced. This is your starting position.
Keeping your legs nearly straight with only a soft bend in the knees, push your hips back and hinge your torso forward at the hips, lowering your chest toward the floor against the band's resistance.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your spine flat and neutral the entire way down.
Reverse the motion by driving your hips forward and extending through the hips and hamstrings to return to the upright starting position.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without leaning back or overextending the lower back.
Critically, never round your back during the descent; the movement must come from hinging at the hips, not from flexing the spine.

name: Band Good Morning (Pull Through)
instructions: Loop a resistance band around a low, sturdy anchor point such as the base of a post or rack, near floor level.

Step a short distance away from the anchor, facing away from it, and loop the free end of the band around the back of your neck and upper traps, using your hands to hold the band in place against your body.
Set your feet about shoulder width apart, take a step or two forward until the band has tension, brace your core, and set your back flat. This is your starting position.
Begin by pushing your hips back as far as possible, sending your glutes rearward while keeping your knees only slightly bent.
Hinge your torso forward to roughly 90 degrees, keeping your back flat and feeling a deep stretch through the hamstrings as the band pulls you backward.
Drive through your hips and squeeze your glutes to extend back up to a tall standing position, finishing with hips fully locked out.
Keep the movement a pure hip hinge; do not turn it into a squat by bending the knees excessively or let the back round at any point.
Control the descent rather than letting the band snap you forward, and maintain band contact at the neck throughout.

name: Band Hip Adductions
instructions: Anchor a resistance band securely around a solid, low post or other immovable object near ankle height.
Stand with your left side facing the post and loop the band around your right ankle, the leg farther from the anchor.
Step away from the post until the band is taut, stand up straight, and hold the post or a nearby rail with your hand for balance. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your torso upright and still, with your standing (left) leg firm.
Keeping your right knee straight, pull your right leg across the front of your body toward the midline and slightly past it, against the band's resistance, driving from the inner thigh.
Squeeze the adductors at the end of the range, then slowly return the leg out to the starting position under control rather than letting the band yank it back.
Avoid swinging the leg or twisting the torso; the motion should come purely from the hip adductors.
Complete all reps on the right leg, then turn around and switch sides to work the left leg.

name: Band Pull Apart
instructions: Stand tall with feet about shoulder width apart, knees soft, and core braced.
Hold a resistance band with both hands using an overhand grip, hands roughly shoulder width or slightly wider apart.
Raise your arms straight out in front of you at chest/shoulder height so they are parallel to the floor, with a slight tension already in the band. This is your starting position.
Initiate a reverse-fly motion by pulling your hands apart and outward to your sides, keeping your elbows extended and arms straight throughout.
Drive the movement from your shoulder blades, squeezing them together as you stretch the band across and toward your chest.
Keep your shoulders pulled back and down (no shrugging toward the ears) and your wrists neutral as the band reaches your chest.
Pause and hold the fully separated position for a moment, feeling the contraction in the rear delts and mid-back.
Return your hands together to the starting position slowly and under control, resisting the band's pull the entire way.
Exhale as you pull apart and inhale as you return, and keep your torso upright without leaning back.

name: Band Skull Crusher
instructions: Secure a resistance band low to the base of a rack or the leg of a bench so the anchor sits behind where your head will be.
Lie face up on the bench with the crown of your head near the anchored end so the band lines up directly behind and above your head.

Reach back and grab the band with both hands, then raise your upper arms so they point toward the ceiling, perpendicular to the floor, with elbows bent and the band running over your head behind you. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms fixed in place and your elbows pointed forward, tucked in rather than flaring out, with your core braced and feet flat on the floor.
Extend through the elbows to straighten your arms, driving your hands up and slightly forward until your arms are fully locked out over your chest, against the band's resistance.
Squeeze your triceps hard at full extension, keeping the upper arms stationary the entire time.
Pause at the top, then slowly bend the elbows to lower your hands back behind your head to the starting position under control.
Move only at the elbow joint; do not let the upper arms drift or turn this into a pullover, and keep your wrists straight throughout.
Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.

name: Barbell Ab Rollout
instructions: Load an Olympic barbell with a light plate (5-10 lbs) on each side so it rolls smoothly, and place it on the floor in front of you.

Get into a standing push-up/plank-style position with your hands gripping the bar at about shoulder width, arms extended and perpendicular to the floor, and your feet set back so your body forms a strong line. This is your starting position.
Brace your core hard, set a slight natural arch in your lower back, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips stable.
Exhale and lift your hips slightly as you roll the barbell toward your feet, contracting your abs to draw your body up and in.
Crunch your abs and bring your glutes up at the top, keeping your arms perpendicular to the floor so the work stays in the abs rather than the shoulders and back.
Hold the top contraction for a second, keeping the abs tight and the spine neutral.
Inhale and slowly roll the barbell forward, extending your body back out to the starting plank position under full control.
Keep the abs braced throughout and never let your lower back sag or hyperextend as you extend out; control is more important than range.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Ab Rollout - On Knees
instructions: Load an Olympic barbell with a light plate (5-10 lbs) per side, kneel on the floor (use a pad under your knees for comfort), and place the bar on the floor in front of you.

Grip the bar at about shoulder width with an overhand grip, arms extended, so you are on your hands and knees in a kneeling push-up position with the bar under your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, set a slight natural arch in your lower back, and keep your hips, torso, and head in a straight line.
Inhale and slowly roll the barbell straight forward, allowing your body to extend and reach out as far as you can while keeping the abs engaged.
Lower until your body is nearly straight and stretched out, going as far as you can without letting your torso or hips touch the floor and without your lower back collapsing into a sag.
Pause for a second at the fully stretched position, maintaining tension through your abs.
Exhale and pull yourself back by contracting your abs to roll the barbell back toward your knees to the starting position.
Move slowly and keep your abs tight at all times; do not yank with your arms or let the hips pike up to cheat the return.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Bench Press - Medium Grip
instructions: Lie back flat on a bench with your eyes positioned directly under the barbell, feet planted firmly on the floor, and a slight natural arch in your lower back.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back and squeeze them together against the bench to create a stable base, keeping your chest up and glutes on the bench.
Grip the bar with a medium-width overhand grip, set so that at the bottom of the press your forearms are vertical and there is a 90-degree angle between forearms and upper arms.
Unrack the bar by extending your arms and move it out over your chest until it is directly above your shoulders with arms locked. This is your starting position.

Take a breath, brace your core, and lower the bar slowly and under control until it lightly touches your mid-chest at roughly nipple level, keeping your elbows tucked at about a 45-75 degree angle rather than flared straight out.
Pause briefly at the chest without bouncing, keeping your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows.
Exhale and drive the bar back up by pushing through your chest, pressing it in a slight arc back to the starting position over your shoulders.
Lock your arms out and squeeze your chest at the top, hold for a moment, then begin the next descent.
Aim for a controlled tempo where lowering takes roughly twice as long as pressing up, and keep your feet, glutes, and upper back in contact with the bench/floor throughout.
When finished, carefully guide the bar back into the rack with locked arms.

name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Load a straight or EZ barbell on the floor or a rack and stand tall with your feet roughly hip-width apart, knees soft, and weight balanced over your midfoot.
Grip the bar with both hands at shoulder width using a supinated (underhand) grip, palms facing forward and wrists stacked neutrally so they do not bend back under load.
Lift the bar and let your arms hang straight down with the bar resting against your thighs; pin your upper arms and elbows tight against your sides where they will stay for the entire set.
Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades down and back, lift your chest, and keep a slight knee bend with a neutral spine; this is your starting position.
Exhale and curl the bar upward in a smooth arc by flexing only at the elbows, keeping the upper arms locked in place so the forearms do all the work.
Continue until the bar reaches roughly shoulder height and your biceps are fully contracted, then squeeze hard at the top for a one-second hold.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly under control over about two to three seconds until the arms are fully extended and the biceps are stretched.
Keep the movement strict throughout: do not swing the torso, rock the hips, or let the elbows drift forward to cheat the weight up.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, maintaining the same controlled tempo on every rep.

name: Barbell Curls Lying Against An Incline
instructions: Set an incline bench to roughly 45 to 60 degrees and load a light to moderate barbell, as this position removes all momentum and is harder than a standing curl.
Sit on the seat and lie back with your chest and stomach against the bench pad, facing it, so your arms hang straight down off the front edge.
Reach down and grip the bar at shoulder width with a supinated (underhand) grip, palms facing forward, and let the arms hang fully extended and vertical.
Keep your chest pressed into the pad, shoulders down, and core braced so the upper arms stay perpendicular to the floor and motionless; this is your starting position.
Exhale and curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending only at the elbows, keeping the upper arms locked against the bench so the forearms do all the moving.
Curl as high as possible while squeezing the biceps, then hold the peak contraction for a one-second count.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and fully back to the hanging start position, allowing a complete stretch at the bottom without bouncing.
Do not swing the arms or lift your chest off the pad to gain leverage; the strictness is the point of this variation.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions with a controlled tempo.

name: Barbell Deadlift
instructions: Load a barbell on the floor and stand with your mid-foot directly under the bar, feet about hip-width apart and toes pointed slightly out, shins roughly an inch from the bar.

Bend at the hips and knees to lower down and grip the bar just outside your shins with a shoulder-width double-overhand grip; switch to a mixed grip (one palm up, one down) or use straps if grip fails on heavy loads.
Drop your hips until your shins touch the bar, then lift your chest, set a neutral flat back, and pull your shoulder blades over the bar so your shoulders sit just in front of it.
Take a big breath into your belly and brace your core hard, then take the slack out of the bar by pulling up gently until you feel the bar and plates engage.
Drive the floor away with your legs, keeping the bar dragging close against your shins and the hips and shoulders rising at the same rate.
As the bar passes the knees, drive your hips forward to lock out, standing tall with chest up, glutes squeezed, and shoulders back, without leaning back or hyperextending the lower spine.
Reverse the movement by first pushing your hips back, then bending the knees once the bar clears them, keeping the back flat and the bar close to the legs the whole way down.
Lower under control until the plates touch the floor, reset your breath and brace, and begin the next rep from a dead stop.
Throughout the lift never round or arch the lower back, never let the bar drift out in front of you, and keep the bar path vertical.

name: Barbell Full Squat
instructions: Set the bar in a squat rack at about mid-chest to shoulder height, load it, and position safety pins or spotter arms at the bottom of your squat depth.
Step under the bar and place it across your upper traps (high-bar) or rear delts (low-bar), gripping it just outside shoulder width and pulling your elbows down to create a tight shelf of muscle.
Take a deep breath, brace your core, and stand the bar out of the rack by driving up through both legs, then take one or two steps back to clear the rack.
Set your feet at shoulder-to-slightly-wider-than-shoulder width with toes turned out about 15 to 30 degrees, weight balanced over the midfoot, and chest up with a neutral spine.
Take a big breath into your belly, brace hard, then initiate by pushing your hips back and bending the knees simultaneously, tracking your knees out over your toes.
Descend under control until your hip crease drops below the top of your knees (hamstrings near calves) for a full squat, keeping your heels flat and torso angle stable.
Drive back up by pushing the floor away through your heels and midfoot, exhaling as you pass the hardest point and extending the hips and knees together.
Stand fully tall and re-brace at the top, keeping the knees from caving inward and the lower back from rounding at the bottom (avoid the buttwink).
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then carefully walk the bar back into the rack and re-rack it on both hooks.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and roll a loaded barbell over your legs until it sits directly across the crease of your hips; use a barbell pad or folded towel to protect the hip bones.
Lie flat on your back on the floor, then bend your knees and plant your feet flat, roughly hip-width apart and close enough that your fingertips can almost touch your heels.
Grip the bar with both hands just outside your hips to hold it secure against your pelvis; this is your starting position with your back flat on the ground.
Tuck your chin slightly, brace your core, and posteriorly tilt your pelvis so your lower back is not arched.
Drive through your heels and exhale as you extend your hips straight up, pushing the bar toward the ceiling until your thighs and torso form a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top and hold for a one-second count, keeping your weight supported on your upper back and heels.
Avoid hyperextending your lower back at the top; the lockout should come from glute contraction, not from arching the spine.
Inhale and lower your hips slowly and under control back down toward the floor.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, keeping the bar stable over the hips throughout.

name: Barbell Guillotine Bench Press
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench with your eyes roughly under the bar, feet planted firmly on the floor, and a slight natural arch in your lower back; note this is a chest-isolation variation that places stress on the shoulders, so use light to moderate weight.
Grip the bar with a medium-to-wide overhand grip, wide enough that your forearms will be vertical at the bottom of the rep.
Unrack the bar and hold it locked out straight over your neck and upper chest, rather than over the mid-chest as in a standard press; this is your starting position.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted and pinned to the bench and your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly toward the base of your neck or very upper chest, flaring the elbows out to the sides, stopping about one inch above the skin.
Do not let the bar drop or bounce; control is critical here because of the increased shoulder strain in this position.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position by driving through the chest, taking at least twice as long to lower as to press.
Lock the arms out and squeeze the chest at the top for a one-second hold before the next rep.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then carefully guide the bar back onto the rack hooks.

name: Barbell Hack Squat
instructions: Stand a loaded barbell on the floor directly behind your heels and set your feet about shoulder-width apart with toes pointed slightly out.
Squat down and reach behind you to grip the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip, palms facing back; use wrist wraps if grip is a limiter.
Lift the bar by extending your legs and hips until you are standing tall with the bar hanging at arm's length behind your thighs and glutes; this is your starting position.
Set your spine neutral, chest up, eyes forward, and brace your core with weight balanced over your heels.
Inhale and squat down slowly by bending the knees and pushing the hips back slightly, keeping the bar close to your body, until your thighs reach about parallel to the floor.
Keep your torso as upright as possible and your heels flat; you may need a small heel elevation to keep balance since the bar is behind you.
Exhale and drive back up by pressing through your heels and squeezing the thighs, extending the knees and hips to return to standing.
Avoid letting the bar bang into the backs of your legs or letting your torso pitch forward as you stand.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Set a flat bench against a wall or a sturdy fixed object so it cannot slide, then sit on the floor with your upper back against the long edge of the bench.
Roll a loaded barbell over your legs until it rests directly in the crease of your hips, and place a barbell pad or folded towel under it to cushion the hip bones.
Position your upper back and shoulder blades against the bench pad so the bench supports you just below the shoulder blades.
Plant your feet flat, roughly shoulder-width apart, with shins set so they will be vertical at the top of the movement; grip the bar on both sides to keep it secured over the hips.
Tuck your chin, brace your core, and posteriorly tilt your pelvis; this is your starting position with hips lowered toward the floor.
Drive through your heels and exhale as you extend your hips upward, pushing the bar toward the ceiling until your thighs are parallel to the floor and your torso and thighs form a flat tabletop.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, keeping your chin tucked and ribs down so you do not overextend the lower back.
Inhale and lower the hips under control back toward the starting position without letting the bar crash down.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, keeping the shins vertical and the movement driven by the glutes.

name: Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip
instructions: Set an incline bench to roughly 30 to 45 degrees and position it under the bar in a rack so the bar clears your face on the unrack.
Lie back with your head, upper back, and glutes on the pad, feet planted flat on the floor, and a slight natural arch in your lower back.
Grip the bar with a medium width grip, wide enough that your forearms will be vertical at the bottom of the rep, with palms facing forward.
Retract and depress your shoulder blades, pinning them to the bench, then unrack the bar and hold it locked out straight over your upper chest; this is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control toward your upper chest just below the collarbone, keeping the elbows tucked at roughly a 45 to 60 degree angle from the torso.
Lightly touch the upper chest without bouncing, keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows and shoulder blades pinned back.
Exhale and press the bar back up and slightly back over the upper chest until the arms lock out, taking at least twice as long to lower as to press.
Squeeze the chest at the top for a one-second hold, keeping the shoulders down and away from the ears.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then carefully rack the bar on both hooks.

name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to roughly 30 to 45 degrees and load a light barbell, since this is a small-range scapular movement targeting the serratus and shoulder girdle.
Lie back on the incline with your head and back supported and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar with a grip slightly wider than shoulder width, palms facing forward, and press it up so your arms are straight and locked over your upper chest; this is your starting position.
Keep your arms completely straight with elbows locked for the entire movement; this is not a press.
Exhale and lift the bar straight up toward the ceiling by protracting your shoulder blades, pushing the shoulders up and forward off the bench a few inches.
Focus on the movement coming purely from the shoulder blades sliding around the ribcage, not from bending the elbows.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly back down by retracting the shoulder blades until they rest against the bench again.
Keep the range short and controlled and avoid any elbow flexion throughout.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Lunge
instructions: Set the bar in a squat rack just below shoulder height, load it, then step under the bar and rest it across your upper traps and rear delts, gripping just outside shoulder width.
Brace your core, stand the bar out of the rack by driving through both legs, and take a couple steps back into open space.
Set your feet about hip-width apart, stand tall with chest up, eyes forward, and a neutral braced spine; this is your starting position.
Take a controlled step forward with your right leg, planting the foot flat with enough distance that your front shin can stay roughly vertical at the bottom.
Inhale and lower straight down by bending both knees, dropping your back knee toward the floor while keeping your torso upright and balanced.
Descend until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor and your back knee hovers just above the ground, keeping the front knee tracking over the toes and not collapsing inward.
Exhale and push back up by driving through the heel of the front foot, returning to the tall standing start position.
Keep your torso upright and core braced the whole time; do not let the front knee shoot far past the toes.
Complete all reps on the right leg, then repeat on the left (or alternate legs), then walk the bar back and re-rack it.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
instructions: Load a barbell and stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, gripping the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Bend your knees slightly, then hinge forward at the hips, pushing your hips back and keeping the natural arch in your back until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders with the bar beneath your chest; brace your core and keep your neck neutral; this is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the bar up toward your upper chest and collarbone area, driving your elbows out wide and away from your body so your upper arms move out to the sides.
Think of it as a reverse bench press: the upper arms should travel perpendicular to your torso, forming a T shape at the top.
Squeeze your rear deltoids and upper back hard at the top, keeping the wrists straight and using the hands only as hooks rather than pulling with the biceps.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control back to the fully hanging start position.
Keep your torso fixed and parallel throughout; do not jerk upright or use momentum to swing the weight.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Rollout from Bench
instructions: Place a loaded barbell with round plates on the floor near the end of a flat bench, and kneel on top of the bench with both knees so the bar is within arm's reach in front of you.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip at roughly shoulder width or slightly narrower, arms extended down to the bar.
Set your core tight and your spine neutral with a slight posterior pelvic tilt so your lower back does not sag; this is your starting position.
Slowly roll the bar forward and away from you by extending at the hips and shoulders, letting your body lower toward horizontal as the bar travels out.
Keep your arms straight throughout and your core braced hard so the lower back never arches or sags as you extend.
Roll out as far as you can while maintaining a flat, braced torso, stopping before your hips drop or your back loses its neutral position.
Exhale and pull yourself back to the starting position by contracting your abs and flexing the hips and shoulders to draw the bar back in toward the bench.
Move slowly and under control in both directions; the abs, not momentum, should drive the return.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, reducing the range if your lower back starts to arch.

name: Barbell Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Place a sturdy block or low step about 12 inches in front of a flat bench.
Sit on the end of the bench and place the balls of both feet on the edge of the block, with your heels hanging off and free to drop below the level of the block.
Have a training partner lay a loaded barbell across your upper thighs, about 3 inches above your knees, and use a pad or towel under it to protect your thighs; hold the bar in place with both hands.
Sit tall with a neutral spine; this is your starting position with your heels lowered and calves stretched.
Exhale and raise your heels as high as possible by pushing through the balls of your feet and contracting the calves.
Squeeze the calves hard at the top and hold the peak contraction for a one-second count.
Inhale and lower your heels slowly and under control well below the block to get a deep stretch at the bottom of each rep.
Use the full range of motion from a deep stretch to a high contraction; do not bounce or use short partial reps.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then have your partner remove the bar.

name: Barbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Set a bench with an upright back support inside a squat rack and position the bar on the rack hooks at about head height; load it appropriately.
Sit with your back firmly against the support, feet planted flat on the floor, and grip the bar with a pronated (overhand) grip just outside shoulder width.
Unrack the bar and press it up to lock out overhead with arms straight, holding it at about shoulder level and slightly in front of your forehead; this is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your ribs down so you do not overarch your lower back, and stack your wrists over your elbows.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control down to about chin or upper-chest level, moving your head back slightly to let the bar pass your face.
Keep your elbows roughly under the bar and pointed slightly forward rather than flared straight out to the sides.
Exhale and press the bar back up overhead in a straight vertical line, returning your head to neutral as the bar clears your face, until the arms lock out.
Avoid using leg drive or excessive back arch; keep the movement strict and the core tight.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then carefully rack the bar back onto the hooks.

name: Barbell Shrug
instructions: Load a barbell and stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.
Grip the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, palms facing your thighs, hands slightly wider than shoulder width; use wrist wraps or straps for a more secure grip on heavy loads.
Lift the bar and hold it at arm's length against the front of your thighs, arms straight, chest up, shoulders relaxed down; this is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your arms completely straight throughout; the elbows should never bend.
Exhale and raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can, shrugging the traps without rolling the shoulders.
Hold the contracted position at the top for a one-second count and squeeze the traps hard.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control back to the starting position, letting the shoulders drop fully.
Do not bend the elbows to help lift the bar with your biceps, and avoid rolling the shoulders forward or backward, as straight up-and-down is safest and most effective.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Barbell Shrug Behind The Back
instructions: Set a loaded barbell on the safety pins of a squat rack at roughly mid-thigh height, then stand directly in front of the bar with your back to it, feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointing forward.

Reach behind your hips and grip the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, palms facing back and hands set slightly wider than shoulder width; wrist straps are recommended here because the behind-the-back position makes the bar awkward to hold.
Stand tall to lift the bar off the pins, locking out your knees and hips so the bar rests against the back of your thighs and glutes with your arms hanging fully straight.
Set your posture: chest up, shoulders pulled slightly back, spine neutral, core braced, and gaze straight ahead; let the bar hang naturally without bending your elbows.
Keeping your arms completely straight, exhale and elevate your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible, contracting the upper traps.
Hold the top contraction for a full second and resist the urge to roll your shoulders or bend your arms; the only movement is shoulder elevation.
Inhale and lower the shoulders slowly under control back to the fully stretched bottom position, feeling the traps lengthen.
Avoid using your biceps to curl the bar or jerking with your legs; the arms stay long and straight and the legs stay locked throughout.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then step back to the rack and re-rack the bar onto the pins.

name: Barbell Side Bend
