instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height, step under it and position it across your upper traps just below the base of your neck, the same as you would for a back squat.
Grip the bar evenly on both sides a few inches outside your shoulders, unrack it, and step back, planting your feet shoulder-width apart with toes pointing forward.
Stand fully upright with your chest up, head facing forward, spine neutral, and core braced; this is your starting position.
Keeping your hips and legs completely stationary and your back straight, inhale and bend laterally at the waist directly to the right as far as comfortably possible.
Move in a straight side-to-side plane only; do not lean forward or backward, twist, or let your hips shift to the opposite side.
Hold the stretched position on the right for a brief moment, feeling the left obliques lengthen.
Exhale and contract your obliques to pull your torso back up to the fully upright starting position.
Inhale and repeat the movement bending to the left this time, holding briefly at the bottom, then return upright as you exhale.
Keep the tempo slow and controlled and avoid heavy loads that force you to use momentum; this is a small-range oblique movement.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions per side, then step forward and re-rack the bar.

name: Barbell Side Split Squat
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height, duck under it and rest it across your upper traps just below the neck, then grip it slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unrack the bar by standing up and stepping back into open space, since this movement requires a very wide stance.
Take a very wide stance, well outside shoulder width, with the foot of your lead (working) leg angled out to the side roughly 45 degrees and the trailing foot pointing more forward.
Set your posture: chest up, spine neutral, core braced, and gaze forward; this is your starting position.
Inhale and shift your weight toward the lead leg, bending its knee and sitting the hip back and down while keeping the trailing leg relatively straight with only a slight bend.
Lower until your lead thigh approaches parallel, keeping the lead knee tracking in line with its angled-out foot and your torso upright; do not let the lead knee cave inward.
Keep your weight on the heel and mid-foot of the lead leg and keep both feet flat on the floor throughout.
Exhale and drive through the lead heel, extending the hip and knee to push yourself back up to the starting wide-stance position.
Complete all prescribed reps on the lead leg, then switch the angled foot and working side and repeat for the opposite leg.
When finished, step forward and re-rack the bar.

name: Barbell Squat
instructions: Set the bar in a squat rack at about mid-chest to just below shoulder height so you can unrack it with only a slight knee bend; set the safety pins or spotter arms just below your bottom depth.

Step under the bar and place it across your upper back; for a high-bar squat rest it on the upper traps just below the neck, gripping the bar evenly with hands a comfortable distance outside your shoulders.

Pull your elbows down and squeeze your shoulder blades together to create a solid muscular shelf for the bar, brace your core, then stand up to lift the bar off the hooks by driving through both legs.
Take one or two steps back and set a shoulder-width stance with your toes pointed slightly outward; keep your head up and your back straight. This is your starting position.
Take a big breath into your belly and brace your core hard, then begin the descent by bending at the hips and knees simultaneously, sitting your hips back and down.
Continue lowering under control until the crease of your hip drops to about parallel with your knees (upper leg near horizontal), keeping your chest up and back flat throughout.
Track your knees outward in line with your toes; do not let the knees cave inward and keep your heels planted flat on the floor the entire time.

Drive back up by pushing the floor away through your heels and mid-foot, extending the knees and hips together while keeping your torso angle consistent, and exhale through the hardest part of the rep.
Avoid rounding your lower back or letting your chest collapse forward; the bar should travel in a vertical line over your mid-foot.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then step forward and re-rack the bar onto the hooks.

name: Barbell Squat To A Bench
instructions: Set up inside a squat rack and place a flat bench or box behind you at a height that lets you reach your target squat depth when you sit back to it; the bench teaches you to sit your hips back and hit consistent depth.
Set the bar in the rack at about chest height, step under it and rest it across your upper traps just below the neck, gripping the bar evenly a comfortable distance outside your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, brace your core, and stand up to unrack the bar by driving through your legs.
Step back so the bench is directly behind you and set a shoulder-width stance with toes pointed slightly out; keep your head up and back straight. This is your starting position.
Take a big breath, brace your core, and begin the descent by sitting your hips back toward the bench while bending the knees, keeping your chest up and spine neutral.
Lower under control until your glutes lightly touch the bench; touch it gently and stay tight rather than relaxing or plopping your full weight onto it.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your heels flat throughout, and make sure your knees do not slide forward past your toes.
Reverse the movement by driving through your heels, extending the hips and knees together to stand back up to the starting position, exhaling through the effort.
Avoid rounding your lower back or fully resting on the bench between reps; maintain core tension the whole set.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then step forward and re-rack the bar.

name: Barbell Step Ups
instructions: Position a sturdy elevated platform, box, or flat bench in front of you at roughly knee height; a higher box increases glute and hamstring involvement.
Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height, step under it and rest it across your upper traps just below the neck, gripping it evenly a bit wider than shoulder width.
Brace your core and stand up to unrack the bar, then step back and stand tall facing the platform with feet about hip-width apart. This is your starting position.
Place your entire right foot flat on top of the platform, making sure the whole foot is planted and your knee is stacked over your ankle.
Exhale and drive through the right heel to extend the right hip and knee, lifting your body up onto the platform, then bring your left foot up to stand fully upright on top.
Drive primarily with the working leg on the box rather than pushing off the floor with the bottom foot, and keep your torso upright with chest up throughout.
Inhale and step back down under control, lowering with the left leg first by flexing the right hip and knee, until the left foot returns to the floor.
Bring the right foot back down next to the left to return to the starting standing position; keep movements controlled and avoid bouncing or using momentum.
Complete the prescribed repetitions leading with the right leg, then repeat leading with the left leg, then step forward and re-rack the bar.

name: Barbell Walking Lunge
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height, step under it and rest it across your upper back on the traps just below the neck, gripping it evenly a comfortable distance outside your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, brace your core, and stand up to unrack the bar, then walk into open floor space with enough room to lunge forward several steps.
Stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, chest up, and gaze forward. This is your starting position.
Take a controlled step forward with one leg, planting the foot flat, then bend both knees to lower your hips straight down.
Descend until your rear knee nearly touches the floor and your front thigh is roughly parallel, keeping your torso upright and your front knee stacked over your front ankle.
Keep your front knee tracking over your toes and do not let it cave inward; the descent should be vertical rather than lunging your weight forward over the front foot.
Drive through the heel of the front foot, extending both knees and hips to bring yourself up and forward, stepping the rear foot up to meet the front in a tall standing position.
Without pausing, step forward with the opposite leg and repeat the lunge, continuing to walk forward alternating legs.
Inhale on the way down and exhale as you drive up out of each lunge, and keep your core braced to protect your lower back the entire time.
Continue for the prescribed number of steps or distance, then return to the rack and re-rack the bar.

name: Battling Ropes
instructions: Anchor a heavy battle rope at its center around a fixed post or anchor point, then back away until the rope is laid out and you stand about 15 to 20 feet from the anchor with modest slack.
Grip one end of the rope in each hand with a firm overhand or neutral grip, holding the ends near the very tips for maximum range.
Set an athletic stance: feet slightly wider than shoulder width, toes forward, knees softly bent into a quarter-squat, hips back, chest up, and core braced.
Hold your arms relatively extended and hanging at your sides with a slight bend in the elbows; this is your starting position.
Initiate the wave by rapidly driving one arm up to about shoulder height, snapping the rope upward to send a wave toward the anchor.
As that arm whips back down toward the starting position, simultaneously drive the opposite arm up, creating a continuous alternating up-and-down wave.
Keep your knees bent, hips loaded, and core tight throughout; generate power from your whole body, not just the shoulders and arms.
Continue alternating left and right as fast and forcefully as you can, breathing in a steady rhythm, for the prescribed time or rounds.
Maintain the athletic posture and avoid standing fully upright or rounding your back as you fatigue.

name: Bear Crawl Hold
instructions: Start on all fours on the floor with your hands stacked directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips.
Tuck your toes under and set your knees about hip-width apart, then push the floor away so your upper back is flat and your shoulder blades are spread.
Lift both knees about one inch off the floor so they hover, keeping your shins parallel to the ground; this is the bear-plank hold position.
Set a flat back from your hips to your shoulders, keep your hips low and level (no piking up or sagging down), and brace your core hard.
Keep your neck neutral by gazing at the floor just ahead of your hands, and press firmly through your palms and toes.
Breathe steadily and shallowly while maintaining full-body tension; do not hold your breath.
Hold this hovering position for the prescribed time, keeping the knees just off the floor the entire time without letting them touch down or drift wide.
To finish, lower your knees gently to the floor and release.

name: Bear Crawl Sled Drags
instructions: Load a sled with an appropriate weight and attach a strap or chain to it; fasten the other end to a harness or a loose weight belt around your hips so the sled trails behind you.
Face away from the sled with the line taut, then bend down and place both hands flat on the floor in front of you, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Set a bear-crawl position: knees bent and hovering just off the ground, toes tucked, back flat, hips low, and core braced. This is your starting position.
Begin crawling forward by driving through your legs, moving the opposite hand and foot together (left hand with right foot, then right hand with left foot).
Use your hands mainly for balance and a little pull while your legs do the primary work of dragging the sled forward.
Keep your back flat and your hips low throughout; do not let your hips pike up high or your knees touch the ground.
Maintain steady deliberate steps and keep tension on the strap so the sled drags smoothly behind you, breathing rhythmically.
Continue crawling for the prescribed distance, then stop and reset for the next bout.

name: Bear Plank Hold
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands stacked directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, with your toes tucked under.
Spread your fingers and press the floor away to flatten and broaden your upper back, and set your spine in a neutral position.
Lift both knees about one inch off the floor so they hover, keeping your shins level and your knees bent at roughly 90 degrees.
Brace your core hard, keep your hips low and level with your shoulders (avoid piking up or sagging), and keep your back flat like a tabletop.
Keep your neck neutral with your gaze on the floor just in front of your hands, and drive firmly through your palms and the balls of your feet.
Breathe steadily and evenly while holding maximal core tension; do not hold your breath.
Maintain the knees-hovering position for the prescribed time without letting them touch down or drift, then lower your knees to finish.

name: Behind Head Chest Stretch
instructions: Sit upright on the floor with your legs comfortably positioned and your partner kneeling or standing directly behind you.
Place both hands behind your head with your fingers interlaced or resting on the back of your skull, and draw your elbows out wide and back as far as you comfortably can.
Have your partner gently grip the front of your elbows or upper arms; sit tall with your chest lifted and spine upright. This is the starting position.

Gently attempt to pull your elbows forward against your partner's resistance while keeping your hands behind your head, holding this isometric contraction for 10 or more seconds while breathing steadily.
Relax your chest and shoulder muscles completely, then signal your partner to slowly and gently draw your elbows back, opening the chest further.
Allow the deeper stretch across your chest and front shoulders, keeping your torso upright and avoiding arching your lower back.

Communicate clearly with your partner and tell them to stop as soon as the stretch feels adequate to avoid overstretching or injury, then hold the comfortable end range for the prescribed time before slowly releasing.

name: Bench Dip
instructions: Sit on the edge of a sturdy flat bench and place your hands on the edge beside your hips, fingers wrapped over the front edge and hands about shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs out in front of you with your feet together and heels on the floor; keeping them straighter and farther out makes the exercise harder, bending the knees makes it easier.
Slide your hips and glutes off the front of the bench so your body weight is supported on your hands, with your torso upright and arms straight. This is the starting position.
Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears, chest up, and core braced throughout.
Inhale and lower your body straight down by bending at the elbows until they reach about a 90-degree angle, keeping your back close to the bench.
Keep your elbows pointing straight back and tracking close to your body rather than flaring out to the sides, and keep your hips close to the bench as you descend.
Exhale and press down through your palms, extending your elbows to drive your body back up to the starting position with arms straight.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders up or dropping so low that you feel strain in the front of the shoulder; control the tempo both directions.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Bench Dips
instructions: Place a flat bench behind your back so it is perpendicular to your body, and stand facing away from it.
Reach back and grip the front edge of the bench with both hands fully extended, hands about shoulder-width apart and fingers curled over the edge.

Walk your feet out in front of you so your legs are extended forward and your body is bent at the hips, torso roughly perpendicular to your thighs and weight supported on your hands. This is the starting position.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears, chest lifted, and core braced; the closer to straight and the farther out your legs, the harder the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower your body by bending at the elbows until the angle between your upper arm and forearm is slightly less than 90 degrees.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your body and pointing straight back, with your forearms pointing straight down throughout the descent.
Using your triceps, exhale and press through your palms to extend the elbows and lift your torso back up to the starting position.
Avoid flaring the elbows out or letting the shoulders roll forward and shrug up, which stresses the shoulder joint.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Bench Jump
instructions: Place a sturdy box or bench about one to two feet in front of you and stand facing it with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes forward. This is your starting position.
Ensure you have a clear, flat landing area on the far side of the bench and that the bench is stable enough not to tip.
Initiate the jump by dropping quickly into a short quarter-squat, bending your hips and knees while swinging both arms back behind you to load.
Explosively reverse out of the squat, extending powerfully through your hips, knees, and ankles to jump up and over the bench while swinging your arms forward and up for momentum.
Clear the bench and land softly on the other side on the balls of your feet, immediately bending your knees and hips to absorb the impact through your legs.
Land with your knees tracking over your toes and your chest up; avoid landing stiff-legged or letting your knees cave inward.
Stabilize, then turn around to face the bench from the opposite side.
Repeat the loading squat and jump back over the bench, again landing soft and controlled.
Continue alternating sides for the prescribed repetitions, resetting your balance between jumps.

name: Bench Press - Powerlifting
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench and position yourself so your eyes are roughly under or slightly behind the bar; aim to get your head as far up the bench as possible.

Plant your feet firmly and pull them back underneath you so your shins are nearly vertical, then drive through your feet to arch your upper back and squeeze your shoulder blades down and together against the bench.

Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulders off the bench, retract your scapulae hard, and pin your upper traps into the bench to create a tight, stable platform; maintain this arched, locked-in position throughout the entire lift.
Grip the bar so your hands cover the rings on the bar (a wider grip shortens the range of motion); squeeze the bar tightly and try to bend or pull it apart to engage your lats and forearms.

Unrack the bar by pulling it out of the hooks without losing your scapular retraction (do not let your shoulders protract forward), and move it to a stable position over your shoulders with arms locked.

Take a big breath, brace your core, and lower the bar under control to your lower chest or upper stomach, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly 45 to 75 degrees so the bar, wrist, and elbow stay stacked in a vertical line.
Pause briefly when the bar touches your torso while maintaining full-body tightness and your arch, keeping your feet driving and shoulder blades pinched.
Drive the bar back up with maximum force in a slight diagonal path back toward your shoulders, keeping the elbows tucked until you reach lockout, and exhale through the press.
Keep your glutes and upper back in contact with the bench and your feet planted at all times; do not let your hips rise off the bench or your elbows flare wide.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then re-rack the bar securely with control.

name: Bench Press - With Bands
instructions: Set up a flat bench and loop a resistance band securely around the leg or base of the bench nearest your head, so the band anchors below and behind you.

Grab one handle of the band in each hand, then lie back on the bench with your eyes roughly under where the band crosses behind you, feet planted flat on the floor about shoulder-width apart for a stable base.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down and press them into the bench, keeping a slight natural arch in your lower back and your glutes in contact with the pad throughout.
Press both arms up and extend them so the handles are held in front of you at shoulder width, directly over your chest, with elbows nearly locked.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face away from you (toward your feet); the band should already be taut to create tension. This is your starting position.

Inhale and lower the handles slowly and under control toward the sides of your chest, allowing your elbows to bend to roughly 90 degrees and tucking them at about a 45-degree angle to your torso rather than flaring them straight out.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows and the band tension constant; do not let the handles drift up toward your shoulders or down toward your stomach.
Exhale and press the handles back up and slightly together by driving through your chest, finishing with arms extended in the locked-out position.
Squeeze your pecs hard at the top and hold for a one-count, feeling the resistance increase as the band stretches further at lockout.
Lower under control on the next rep, taking roughly twice as long to lower as to press, and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Bench Press with Chains
instructions: Drape a length of heavy chain over each sleeve of the barbell, adjusting the leader (anchor) chain so that several links remain on the floor at the bottom of the press and the chain lifts off the floor near lockout, adding resistance as you press up.
Lie on the flat bench positioned so your eyes are roughly under the bar, and if possible let your head sit just beyond the bar toward the uprights.

Plant your feet firmly and tuck them slightly back underneath you, then arch your upper back and press your traps and shoulder blades hard into the bench, retracting and depressing the blades to create a tight, stable shelf.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip so your hands cover the rings on the bar (roughly 1.5x shoulder width), squeeze the bar hard, and keep your wrists stacked straight over your elbows.
Using a spotter or your own drive, lift the bar out of the rack without letting your shoulders roll forward (no protraction), and hold it locked out over your upper chest as the starting position.
Inhale, brace your core, and lower the bar under control to your lower chest or upper stomach, keeping your elbows tucked so the bar, wrist, and elbow stay stacked in a vertical line.
Pause briefly when the bar lightly touches your torso without bouncing, keeping full-body tension and your back arched.
Exhale and drive the bar up explosively with maximum force, accelerating against the increasing chain weight, and keep your elbows tucked until you reach full lockout.
Maintain the tight body position and continuous tension throughout, then repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Bench Sprint
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy bench or low box, close enough that you can comfortably place one foot on top with your heel near the front edge.
Place one foot flat on top of the bench with your heel close to the edge and your knee bent, keeping your other foot flat on the floor behind you.
Set your torso slightly forward, chest up, core braced, and arms ready to drive in a running motion to assist momentum.
Push down hard through the foot on top of the bench, explosively extending that hip and knee to drive your body upward.
Switch your legs in the air, swinging the trailing leg up and forward so its foot lands on top of the box while the previously elevated foot returns to the floor.
Land softly with a bent knee on top of the box and immediately absorb the impact, keeping your chest up and avoiding any collapse at the knee or ankle.
Drive your arms to help power each switch and keep a fast, rhythmic cadence as if sprinting in place.
Continue alternating feet rapidly from one foot to the other, keeping your foot placement near the front edge each time, until you complete the set.

name: Bent Over Barbell Row
instructions: Load a barbell and stand with your feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart, the bar over your mid-foot, and grip it with a pronated (overhand, palms-down) grip just outside shoulder width.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, pushing your hips back and lowering your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor while keeping your back flat and a neutral spine.

Keep your head in line with your spine (eyes a few feet ahead on the floor), brace your core, and let the bar hang straight down from your shoulders with arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso stationary and stable, exhale and pull the bar up toward your lower ribs and upper abdomen by driving your elbows up and back.
Keep your elbows close to your body and lead with the elbows, using your forearms only to hold the bar so the back muscles do the work.
At the top, squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold the contracted position for a brief pause without jerking the weight up with your lower back.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back along the same path to the starting position with arms fully extended, keeping control and tension in the back.
Do not round your spine or use your hips to heave the weight; keep the torso angle fixed throughout, and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench
instructions: Set an incline bench to a moderate angle and stand at the high end of it, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping your back straight and its natural arch, and lean in until your forehead rests gently against the top of the incline pad to support and stabilize your torso.

With your torso supported and roughly parallel to the floor, let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders with palms facing each other and a slight bend in the elbows. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso forward and motionless and your arms only slightly bent and fixed, exhale and lift the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc.
Raise the weights until both arms are roughly parallel to the floor, leading with your elbows and pinkies, focusing the effort in your rear delts.
Avoid swinging your torso or pulling the arms back behind you like a row; keep the movement strictly out to the sides.
Hold the top contracted position for about one second, squeezing the rear delts and shoulder blades.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control, then repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Bent Over Low-Pulley Side Lateral
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low-pulley cable and select a light weight, since this is an isolation movement for the rear and side delt.
Stand beside or slightly across from the pulley and grasp the handle with your right hand so the cable runs across the front of your body.
Hinge forward at the waist until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat, knees slightly bent, and place your left hand on your lower left thigh for support.
Let your right arm hang down and across in front of you from the shoulder with a slight bend in the elbow, feeling tension in the cable. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso fixed and the slight elbow bend constant, exhale and raise your right arm out to the side in a wide arc until it is parallel to the floor and roughly in line with your right ear.
Lead with your elbow and keep the movement controlled, avoiding any swinging of the torso or jerking with the lower back.
Pause briefly at the top and feel the rear and side delt contract.
Inhale and slowly lower the handle back across your body to the starting position under control.
Complete all reps on the right side, then switch the handle to your left hand and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
instructions: Load weight onto one end of an Olympic barbell and wedge the opposite (empty) end securely into the corner of two walls or under a heavy object so it cannot slide backward (a landmine attachment also works).
Straddle or stand alongside the loaded end with your feet about shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is as close to parallel with the floor as you can manage, keeping your back flat and a neutral spine.
Grab the bar with one hand just behind the plates, and brace your other hand on your knee or thigh for support. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso stationary, exhale and pull the bar straight up with your elbow tucked in close to your body to maximize back engagement.
Continue pulling until the plates touch or nearly touch your lower chest, then squeeze your back muscles and hold for a second at the top.
Do not allow any swinging or twisting of the torso; only your arm should move through the rep.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, getting a full stretch in your lat without letting the plates rest on the floor (small 25-lb plates give a better range of motion).
Complete all reps on one side, then switch arms and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Bent Over Two-Arm Long Bar Row
instructions: Load weight onto one end of an Olympic barbell and secure the opposite (empty) end in the corner of two walls or under a heavy object so it cannot slide backward (a landmine attachment also works).
Stand straddling the bar facing the loaded end, feet about shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is as close to parallel with the floor as possible, keeping your back flat and spine neutral.
Grasp the bar with both hands just behind the plates, ideally hooking a stirrup or double-handle cable attachment under the bar for a neutral grip. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your torso fixed, exhale, and pull the bar straight up with your elbows tucked in close to maximize back engagement.
Row until the plates touch or nearly touch your lower chest, then squeeze your back muscles and hold the contraction for a second.
Keep the torso angle constant and avoid using your lower back or hips to heave the weight up.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly back to the starting position, getting a full stretch in the lats without letting the plates touch the floor (small 25-lb plates allow a fuller range).
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart, palms facing your torso (neutral grip).
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the waist, pushing your hips back and lowering your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor while keeping your back flat.
Keep your head up and in line with your spine, brace your core, and let the dumbbells hang straight down from your shoulders with arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso stationary, exhale and lift the dumbbells up toward the sides of your torso by driving your elbows up and back, keeping them close to your body.
Use only enough forearm tension to grip the dumbbells and let your back muscles do the pulling, rather than curling the weight.
At the top contracted position, squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control, feeling a stretch in the lats.
Keep the torso angle fixed and avoid jerking with your lower back, and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row With Palms In
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart, palms facing each other (neutral grip) throughout the movement.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the waist, keeping your back straight, until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Keep your head up and spine neutral, brace your core, and let the dumbbells hang straight down in front of you with arms perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso stationary, exhale and pull the dumbbells up toward your sides while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keep your elbows tracking close to your body and lead with the elbows so the back muscles, not the arms, drive the movement.
At the top contracted position, squeeze your back muscles hard and hold for a second.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control, allowing a full stretch in the lats.
Keep the torso angle fixed and avoid swinging, and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Bent Press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and place a kettlebell on the floor just outside one foot.
Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through your legs and hips to drive it up, rotating your wrist so the bell rests on the back of your forearm in the rack position at your shoulder.
Set your stance with the kettlebell-side foot slightly turned out, brace your core, and keep your eyes locked on the kettlebell throughout the lift. This is your starting position.
Begin leaning and bending laterally toward the side opposite the kettlebell, hinging at the hips and waist while screwing your loaded arm into a fixed position.
As you continue lowering your torso, allow your elbow to straighten so the kettlebell presses vertically upward; you are essentially lowering your body under the bell rather than pressing it up.

Keep your loaded arm perpendicular to the ground and the kettlebell stacked over your shoulder and hip, continuing until you can touch the ground with your free hand and your arm is fully locked out overhead.
Once the arm is locked, brace hard and stand back up to a fully upright position with the kettlebell held directly overhead and the elbow locked.
Carefully reverse the kettlebell back down to the shoulder rack position under control, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: Bent-Arm Barbell Pullover
instructions: Load a barbell with a manageable weight and lie flat on your back along a flat bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor for stability.
Grip the bar with a pronated (overhand) grip about shoulder-width apart and press it up so it is held straight over your chest.
Bend your elbows to keep your arms in a fixed bent-arm position, and brace your core with a slight natural arch in your lower back. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms locked in that bent-arm position, inhale and slowly lower the bar in an arc back behind and beyond your head.
Continue lowering until you feel a deep stretch across your chest and lats, keeping the descent controlled and avoiding any sudden drop.
Exhale and pull the bar back over your chest along the same arc by engaging your lats and chest, keeping the elbow angle constant.
Hold the bar over your chest at the top for a second, keeping tension in the target muscles.
Repeat the controlled arc for the prescribed number of repetitions, keeping your hips and lower back stable throughout.

name: Bent-Arm Dumbbell Pullover
instructions: Stand a single dumbbell vertically on the end of a flat bench, ensuring its plates are secure and locked so it cannot come apart during the set.
Lie perpendicular across the bench so only your upper back and shoulders rest on the pad, forming a cross with the bench, with your head off the end and your hips dropped below bench height.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor with knees bent for a stable base, and keep your core braced and hips slightly lowered.
Cup both palms flat against the underside of the top plate of the dumbbell and press it straight up over your chest with a bend in your arms. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms locked in the bent-arm position, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc back behind your head until you feel a strong stretch across your chest.
Keep the descent slow and controlled, and avoid letting the dumbbell drift toward your face.
Exhale and pull the dumbbell back over your chest along the same arc by contracting your chest and lats, keeping the elbow bend constant.
Hold the top position for a second with tension in the chest, and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, keeping your hips slightly lower than the bench to maximize the stretch.

name: Bent-Knee Hip Raise
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat with your arms resting alongside your body, palms down for support.
Bend your knees to roughly a 75-degree angle and lift your feet a couple of inches off the floor, keeping your lower back in contact with the ground.
Brace your core and keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor. This is your starting position.
Using your lower abs, exhale and draw your knees up and in toward your chest while maintaining that 75-degree bend in your legs.
Continue the motion by rolling your pelvis backward to lift your hips off the floor, finishing with your knees over your chest.
Use your abdominal muscles to curl the pelvis, not momentum from swinging your legs, keeping the movement slow and deliberate.
Squeeze your abs at the top for a second, then inhale and slowly lower your hips and legs back to the starting position under full control.
Avoid letting your feet touch the floor between reps to keep tension on the abs, and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Bicycle Crunch
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your lower back pressed gently into the floor and your knees bent.
Place your hands lightly behind your head with elbows wide, without pulling on your neck, and lift both feet off the floor with knees raised toward a tabletop position.
Curl your head, neck, and shoulder blades slightly off the floor and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Rotate your torso to bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while simultaneously extending the other leg out straight at a low angle.
Focus on twisting from your torso and obliques rather than yanking with your arms, and keep your lower back flat against the floor.
Smoothly switch sides, bringing the opposite elbow toward the now-bent opposite knee while extending the other leg.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled pedaling motion, exhaling on each crunch and keeping the movement deliberate rather than rushed.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions or time, keeping constant tension on the abs throughout.

name: Bicycling
instructions: Seat yourself on the bike and adjust the saddle height so that, with the pedal at its lowest point, your knee has only a slight bend (about 25 to 30 degrees) and your hips do not rock side to side.
Adjust the handlebars to a comfortable reach so your back stays neutral and you are not overly hunched, then set your initial resistance to a light, warm-up level.
Place the balls of your feet over the pedal spindles and secure any foot straps or clips, keeping your ankles relaxed.
Grip the handlebars lightly, keep your core engaged, shoulders relaxed, and maintain an upright or slightly forward neutral posture.
Begin pedaling at a steady, comfortable cadence to warm up, driving smoothly through the full circle by pushing down and pulling through rather than mashing.
Once warm, increase the resistance and/or cadence to reach your target effort, breathing rhythmically and keeping your pedal stroke fluid.
Maintain a consistent cadence and posture for the duration of your interval or session, avoiding bouncing in the saddle or locking out your knees.
Gradually reduce resistance and cadence to cool down at the end before dismounting.

name: Bicycling, Stationary
instructions: Sit on the saddle and adjust the seat height so that, with the ball of your foot on the pedal at the bottom of its stroke, your knee has only a slight 25-35 degree bend; your hips should not rock side to side as you pedal.
Adjust the fore-aft seat position and, on an upright bike, the handlebar height so your torso is comfortably upright or slightly forward without rounding your lower back.
Place the balls of your feet on the pedals and secure the toe straps if present, keeping your heels relatively level rather than dropping or pointing them.
Sit tall with a braced core, shoulders relaxed and down, and a neutral spine, gripping the handlebars lightly without leaning heavily on your arms.
Start pedaling to wake the console, then select a manual setting or a preset program, entering your age and weight if you want a calorie estimate.
Set an initial resistance that lets you hold a smooth cadence of roughly 60-90 RPM, keeping the pedal stroke controlled rather than jerky.
Drive through the full pedal circle, pushing down and pulling through the bottom and over the top, rather than only mashing downward.
Breathe in a steady rhythm matched to your effort, keeping it the same on each side without holding your breath.
Raise resistance for strength or interval work and lower it for recovery or steady cardio, avoiding any hip bouncing, which signals the seat is too high.
Grip the heart-rate handle contacts periodically to keep your intensity in the desired zone, and finish with light pedaling to cool down before stopping.

name: Bird Dog
instructions: Start on all fours on a mat with your hands stacked directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, about hip-width apart.
Spread your fingers and press the floor away to keep your shoulder blades flat, then set a neutral spine with a long neck so your head, upper back, and tailbone form a straight line.
Brace your core as if preparing for a light punch, and gently tuck your chin so you are gazing at the floor a few inches ahead of your hands.
Without shifting your weight, slowly extend your right arm straight forward to shoulder height, thumb up, while simultaneously extending your left leg straight back to hip height.
Reach actively through your fingertips and your back heel so both limbs are long and level with your torso, not lifted above it.
Keep your hips square to the floor and your shoulders level; imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back so it does not tip or rotate.
Hold the fully extended position for one to two seconds while continuing to breathe and keeping the core braced.
Return your hand and knee under your body with control, lightly tapping the floor, then repeat with the opposite arm and leg.
Avoid arching or sagging your lower back and avoid rushing; the goal is a stable anti-rotation hold, not a swinging tempo.

name: Board Press
instructions: Set a flat bench in a power rack with the barbell at a height you can unrack with a slight arm bend, load the bar, and have a partner ready to hold the board, or secure a one-to-five-board stack of 2x6 lumber on your chest.
Lie back so your eyes are roughly under or just behind the bar, and position the board over your lower chest and sternum where the bar will touch.
Plant your feet flat and firm, tuck them slightly under you, and drive your heels down to build leg tension.

Pull your shoulder blades down and back and squeeze them together, lifting your chest into a stable arch, then press your upper back and traps hard into the bench and hold this tight position throughout.
Grip the bar with either a standard bench-width grip or a closer shoulder-width grip to bias the triceps, keeping your wrists stacked straight over your elbows.
Squeeze the bar hard as if trying to pull it apart, unrack it without letting your shoulders roll forward, and hold it locked out over your chest.
Take a big breath, brace, and lower the bar under control to the board, keeping your elbows tucked toward your sides rather than flared.
Let the bar settle on the board for a brief, controlled pause without bouncing or letting your shoulders sink.
Drive the bar up explosively through your triceps, keeping your elbows tucked until the final lockout, and exhale as you pass the hardest point.
Reset your breath and full-body tightness before each rep, and re-rack only after fully locking out the final rep.

name: Body Tricep Press
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack or Smith machine at roughly chest height and confirm it is secure and will not slide.
Stand facing the bar and take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Walk your feet back two to three feet with your feet together so your body forms a straight, rigid line leaning forward into the bar with arms extended; this is your starting position.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag or pike, keeping your head neutral in line with your spine.
Flex at the elbows to lower your forehead and chest toward the bar, keeping your upper arms angled so the elbows travel forward rather than flaring wide.
Lower with control until your head is just below the bar, maintaining the straight plank-like body line throughout.
Pause briefly at the bottom without letting your hips drop or your shoulders shrug up.
Extend the elbows powerfully to press your body back to the starting lean, focusing the effort in your triceps.
To make it harder, step your feet farther back to lower the bar angle, or drape chains over your shoulders for added resistance.

name: Body-Up
instructions: Assume a forearm plank on a mat, supporting your weight on your toes and forearms with your elbows under your shoulders and forearms parallel, shoulder-width apart.
Set a straight line from your head through your hips to your heels by bracing your core and squeezing your glutes, not letting your hips sag or pike.
Keep your neck neutral, gaze just ahead of your hands, and press your forearms firmly into the floor; this is your starting position.
Place your palms flat and, pressing firmly into the ground, extend through one elbow and then the other to push your torso up onto your hands.
Keep your torso rigid and your hips level as you rise, avoiding any twisting or arching of the lower back.
Pause briefly at the top in the straight-arm plank with your shoulders stacked over your wrists.
Slowly lower back down by flexing the elbows one at a time, returning to the forearm plank under control rather than dropping.
Maintain steady breathing and a tight core throughout, and alternate which arm leads on successive reps so both triceps work evenly.

name: Bodyweight Flyes
instructions: Place two equally and lightly loaded EZ-curl bars on a smooth floor, parallel and about shoulder-width apart, and confirm the plates allow the bars to roll freely.
Kneel between the bars and grip one bar in each hand with a neutral grip, hands directly under your shoulders.
Step your feet back into a push-up position, supporting your weight on your toes and the bars, arms extended and body forming a straight rigid line; this is your starting position.
Brace your core hard and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag, and set a slight bend in the elbows that you will maintain for the whole set.
Inhale and slowly roll the bars outward, away from your midline, letting your chest lower toward the floor as your arms spread apart.
Control the descent carefully and only go as far as you can while keeping the elbows softly bent and the torso rigid, never letting your back arch or stomach drop.
Feel the stretch across your chest at the widest point, pausing momentarily without resting your weight on the floor.
Exhale and pull the bars back together by squeezing your chest, rolling them inward until you return to the starting push-up position.
Keep the movement slow and deliberate, since the long lever is very demanding, and reduce the load or range if your hips begin to sag.

name: Bodyweight Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against the long edge of a sturdy, braced bench, knees bent and feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart.
Position the bench edge just below your shoulder blades so it acts as a pivot, and walk your feet in or out until your shins will be vertical at the top of the movement.
Tuck your chin slightly so your head stays neutral, and set your gaze forward and slightly down toward your knees.
Brace your core and tilt your pelvis slightly under so your lower back stays neutral rather than overarched; this is your starting position.
Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor and your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
At the top, push your hips up an extra inch by maximally contracting your glutes, keeping your shins vertical and your ribs down.
Hold the top contraction for a one-to-two-second squeeze without arching your lower back or pushing through the spine.
Lower your hips with control back toward the floor, stopping just short of resting, then immediately begin the next rep.
Keep the chin tucked and the work in your glutes; if you feel it mainly in your lower back or hamstrings, move your knees more over your toes and focus on the glute squeeze.

name: Bodyweight Mid Row
instructions: Set up at a low horizontal pull-up apparatus or a fixed bar at roughly hip-to-waist height that you can reach while hanging beneath it.
Take a medium-to-wide overhand grip with palms facing away from you and hang from the bar with arms straight.

Tuck your knees toward your chest and lean back, swinging your legs up and over to your side of the apparatus so your shins rest near or over the bar and your body is angled back; this is your starting position.
Set your shoulders down and back, brace your core, and keep your hips lifted so your body stays in a relatively straight line rather than sagging.
Begin with your arms straight, then pull by driving your elbows down and back and retracting your shoulder blades to raise your chest toward the bar.
Continue until your torso comes up and your legs make contact with the apparatus, squeezing your mid-back at the top.
Keep the movement smooth and avoid yanking with the arms only; think of leading with the elbows and pinching the shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top contraction, then lower yourself under control back to the fully extended starting position.
Breathe out as you pull up and in as you lower, keeping your core braced so your hips do not drop throughout the set.

name: Bodyweight Squat
instructions: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes turned slightly outward, weight balanced across the whole foot.
Place your hands behind your head, crossed on your chest, or extended in front of you for balance, then lift your chest and set your shoulders back.
Brace your core, keep a neutral spine, and fix your gaze forward; this is your starting position.
Begin by breaking at the hips and knees together, sitting your hips back and down as if reaching for a chair behind you.
Push your knees outward in line with your toes as you descend, keeping your heels planted and your chest up.
Descend to full depth if your mobility allows, ideally with your hip crease at or below the top of your knees, without rounding your lower back or letting your heels rise.
Keep your weight centered over your mid-foot and your torso angle consistent throughout the descent.
Drive up through your heels and mid-foot, extending your knees and hips together to return smoothly to standing.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without overarching, inhaling on the way down and exhaling as you stand back up.

name: Bodyweight Walking Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, hands on your hips, chest up and core braced, and choose a clear path several steps long.
Set your gaze forward and keep your torso upright with a neutral spine throughout the exercise.
Take a controlled step forward with one leg, landing on the mid-foot with your knee tracking over your toes.
Lower straight down by bending both knees until your rear knee nearly touches the floor and your front thigh approaches parallel to the ground.
Keep your front knee stacked above or just behind your front foot, with most of your weight in the front heel.
Maintain an upright posture, not leaning your chest forward over the front leg, and keep your hips square.
Drive through the heel of your front foot and extend both knees to bring yourself back up to a tall position.
Instead of stepping back, bring your rear foot forward to meet the front and immediately step out with that foot into the next lunge.
Continue alternating legs as you walk forward, inhaling as you lower and exhaling as you push up, keeping each rep smooth and balanced.

name: Bosu Ball Cable Crunch With Side Bends
instructions: Attach a single-grip handle to each low pulley of a cable machine and set both pulleys to their lowest position.
Place a Bosu Ball dome-up on the floor centered in front of the machine, a little farther than arm's reach from the pulleys.
Sit on the Bosu and lie back so the small of your back arches over the dome, with your hips low and glutes hovering just above the floor.
Set your feet in a wide stance with knees bent for a stable base, then reach back overhead with both hands and grab the two handles.
Bring your arms straight and in front of you between your knees, keeping them aligned with the upward angle of the cables so your hands sit around knee level; this is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight and rigid, exhale and crunch your torso up by contracting your abs, letting the cable resistance be moved by your trunk rather than your arms.
Pause and squeeze your abs at the top of the crunch without bending or dropping your arms.
Inhale and slowly lower back over the Bosu with control, letting your abdominals stretch and your back re-arch around the ball.
Repeat the cable crunches with steady tempo until you reach abdominal failure, keeping your arms locked the entire time.
At failure, keep your abs tight and raise your torso so your back lifts off the Bosu into a stable plank-like position.
Lower your straight arms to your sides and begin alternating side bends, reaching each hand down toward the same-side heel to target the obliques, controlling each bend before switching sides.

name: Bottoms Up
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs straight and your arms at your sides, palms down for stability.
Press your lower back gently toward the floor and brace your core so your spine does not overarch; this is your starting position.
Begin by tucking your knees toward your chest, flexing at the hips and knees.
Continue by extending your legs straight up so they point toward the ceiling, perpendicular to the floor.
Curl your pelvis up and toward your face, lifting your glutes and lower back off the floor so your feet press straight up, keeping the movement controlled rather than swinging your legs.
Use your lower abs to drive the lift, avoiding pushing off with your hands or generating momentum.
Pause briefly at the top with your hips elevated and feet pointed upward.
Reverse the motion slowly, lowering your pelvis and then bringing the legs back down to the starting position with control.
Exhale as you lift the hips and inhale as you lower, keeping your neck relaxed and core engaged throughout.

name: Bottoms-Up Clean From The Hang Position
instructions: Stand upright with your feet about shoulder-width apart and a kettlebell held in one hand at arm's length in front of your thighs.
Hinge slightly at the hips with a flat back and grip the kettlebell handle firmly, knuckles forward, keeping your wrist straight and the bell hanging below.
Brace your core, set your shoulder down and back, and keep your gaze forward; this is your starting position.
Hinge at the hips and let the kettlebell swing back between your legs, keeping your arm close to your body and your spine neutral.
Forcefully reverse the swing by snapping your hips forward to generate upward momentum on the bell.
As the kettlebell rises, crush the handle as hard as possible and guide it up to your shoulder, rotating your hand so the bell finishes balanced bottoms-up above your fist.
Catch with your forearm vertical and the bell pointing straight up, wrist locked straight and elbow tucked to your ribs, keeping a fierce grip to stabilize it.
Keep your core and grip tight to balance the inverted bell for a moment in the rack-like position.
Lower the kettlebell back down under control along the same path to the hang, then repeat for reps before switching hands.

name: Box Jump
instructions: Place a sturdy box on a non-slip surface and stand facing it about six to twelve inches away, feet hip-to-shoulder-width apart.
Choose a box height you can land on cleanly with your feet flat, starting conservative and building up over time.
Set your core braced, chest up, and weight balanced over your mid-foot; this is your starting position.
Dip into a quarter squat by hinging at the hips and bending the knees while swinging your arms back behind you to load.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles while swinging your arms forward and up to jump onto the box.
Drive your knees up so your feet clear the box, and land softly near the center with both feet flat and knees bent to absorb the impact.
Land in an athletic quarter-squat with knees tracking over your toes, chest up, and avoid letting your knees cave inward.
Stand fully upright on top of the box to complete the rep, extending your hips at the top.
Step down one foot at a time rather than jumping down to protect your joints, then reset and repeat each rep from a stable start.

name: Box Jump (Multiple Response)
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy box or platform about an arm's length away, with your feet hip-to-shoulder-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
Pick a moderate box height that lets you land cleanly and repeatedly, since this is a continuous reactive drill rather than a single max jump.
Set your knees slightly bent, core braced, and chest up; this is your starting position.
Dip quickly into a quarter squat, swinging your arms back to load for the jump.
Using your arms to aid the initial burst, jump upward and forward, extending your hips and knees explosively.
Land with both feet simultaneously and softly on top of the box, knees bent to absorb the landing.
Immediately and without pausing, drop or jump back down to your original starting position, landing softly with bent knees.
As soon as your feet touch the floor, minimize ground contact time and rebound straight into the next jump onto the box.
Keep the reps rhythmic and reactive, focusing on quick, soft, controlled landings rather than maximum height, and stop the set before your form or landing softness breaks down.

name: Box Skip
instructions: Line up several low boxes in a row, spaced roughly eight feet apart, on a flat non-slip surface.
Stand facing the first box about a stride away in a staggered stance with one leg slightly behind the other and arms relaxed.
Brace your core, stay tall, and prepare to use a powerful skipping action driven by the hips; this is your starting position.
Drive off your back leg and punch your lead knee up, aiming to gain as much height through the hips as possible while swinging the opposite arm upward for drive.
Land on top of the first box on your lead foot with a soft, bent-knee, balanced landing.
Immediately upon landing, drive the trailing leg forward and upward to leap off the box, gaining height and distance.
Land on the floor in the gap between the first and second boxes on the same leg that landed on the box, absorbing the landing with a bent knee.
Take a step to the next box and repeat the skipping sequence, continuing down the line of boxes.
Use a coordinated, rhythmic arm and knee drive on each skip, keeping landings soft and controlled, and reset at the end before repeating the run.

name: Box Squat
instructions: Set a box, bench, or stack of plates behind you inside a power rack at a height that puts your hip crease roughly level with or just below your knee when seated (parallel); go higher to train above parallel or lower for more depth as needed.
Set the barbell in the rack just below shoulder height, load it, and step under so the bar rests across the meat of your upper traps and rear delts, not on your neck.

Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, squeeze your shoulder blades together to build a muscular shelf, and pull your elbows down and slightly forward to lock the bar tight against your back.
Take a big breath into your belly, brace your core hard as if bracing for a punch, set a tight arch in your lower back, then stand the bar out of the rack.

Step back and set your feet just outside shoulder width, toes turned out 15 to 30 degrees; a wider stance shifts emphasis to glutes, adductors, and hamstrings, a closer stance to the quads. Keep your gaze forward.
Initiate the descent by sitting your hips back toward the box first, spreading your knees out over your toes, and keep your weight on your heels and mid-foot with shins close to vertical.

Descend under control until you are fully seated on the box; settle your weight onto it and momentarily relax your hip flexors, but keep your upper back, core, and arch tight. Never bounce or rock off the box.
From the seated position, drive your feet hard into the floor, push your knees out, and explode your hips forward and up, leading with your chest and head.
Stand fully erect, exhale near the top, re-brace, and reset for the next rep, maintaining whole-body tightness from head to toe throughout.
A common mistake is letting the lower back round when you sit onto the box; keep the chest tall and arch locked so you load the hips and quads, not the spine.

name: Box Squat with Bands
instructions: Place a box behind you inside a power rack at a height that brings you to parallel (hip crease level with the knee), adjusting higher or lower to suit your training goal.

Loop resistance bands over each end of the barbell sleeves and anchor the bottoms to band pegs, the base of the rack, or heavy dumbbells; if using dumbbells, pin them with extra plates so they cannot lift or slide.

Set the band tension so the bands are taut at the bottom of the squat and stretch tighter toward the top; widen the band base on the floor or choke the bands to add tension, and make sure the anchor weight is heavy enough not to move.
Step under the bar and rest it across your upper traps and rear delts, gripping slightly wider than shoulder width.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, rotate your elbows down and forward to lock the bar tight, take a deep belly breath, brace your core, and set a firm lower-back arch.

Stand the bar out, step back, and plant your feet just outside shoulder width with toes flared 15 to 30 degrees; widen the stance for more posterior-chain work or narrow it for quads. Keep your head facing forward.
Begin by sitting your hips back toward the box, pushing your knees out, keeping shins near vertical and weight through your heels and mid-foot.
Lower under control until fully seated on the box, settle and briefly relax the hip flexors while keeping your back and core tight; never bounce off the box.
Drive your feet into the floor and explode up, pushing the knees out and accelerating against the increasing band tension all the way to lockout, leading with your chest.
Stand tall, exhale, re-brace, and repeat; the bands demand you accelerate harder near the top, so never decelerate before lockout. Carefully rack the bar when finished.
Because the bands add load at the top, control the descent extra carefully and stay tight so the band pull does not yank you out of position.

name: Box Squat with Chains
instructions: Position a box behind you in a power rack at a height that brings you to a parallel squat, going higher or lower as your training calls for.
Set up the chains by looping a thin leader chain over each barbell sleeve, then attach the heavy chain to the leader with a snap hook.

Adjust the leader-chain length so that at the top of the squat a few links of the heavy chain still rest on the floor, and at the bottom most or all of the chain is piled on the floor, deloading the bar.
Step under the bar, set it across your upper traps and rear delts, and grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Pull your shoulder blades together, rotate your elbows down and forward to lock the bar in place, take a deep breath into your belly, brace hard, and set a tight lower-back arch.

Stand the bar out and step back, planting your feet just outside shoulder width with toes turned out 15 to 30 degrees; wider emphasizes glutes, adductors, and hamstrings, narrower the quads. Keep your gaze forward.
Sit your hips back toward the box, spread your knees out over your toes, keep shins near vertical, and keep weight on your heels and mid-foot as you descend.
Lower under control until fully seated on the box, settle and briefly relax the hip flexors while staying tight through the back and core; never bounce off the box.
Drive your feet into the floor and explode upward, leading with your chest and head, accelerating as the chain weight progressively reloads the bar toward lockout.
Stand fully erect, exhale, re-brace, and repeat each rep with full-body tightness; the rising chain load trains you to keep driving hard through the top range.
A common error is slowing down as the chains get heavier near lockout; keep accelerating so you finish the rep strong.

name: Brachialis-SMR
instructions: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie on your side next to it.
Position the roller under your upper arm so the outer portion of your arm just below the biceps, over the brachialis, rests against it, with the arm extended roughly in line with your body.
Stack your body so your weight can press the arm into the roller, supporting yourself on your feet and that arm.
Lift your hips slightly off the floor so more body weight loads onto the roller, increasing the pressure on the muscle.
Slowly roll a short range back and forth along the brachialis and outer biceps, pausing on any tender or tight spots for several seconds until the tension eases.
Keep your neck relaxed and breathe steadily; never roll directly over the elbow joint or onto bony areas.
Continue for 10 to 30 seconds, then switch to the other arm and repeat.

name: Bradford/Rocky Presses
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about shoulder height and, if available, sit on an upright military press bench with back support, or stand tall with a stable shoulder-width stance.

Grip the bar with a pronated grip (palms facing forward) set wider than shoulder width, wide enough that your forearms are vertical and your upper arms form a 90-degree angle at the elbow when the bar is at shoulder level.
Unrack or clean the bar to the front of your shoulders at chin height, brace your core, keep your chest up, and tuck your chin slightly. This is your starting position.
Press the bar up just high enough to clear the top of your head, raising it only a few inches over the crown rather than locking fully out, exhaling as you push.
Lower the bar smoothly behind your head to the base of your skull or upper neck level, inhaling as it descends and keeping the bar path close to your head.
Press the bar back up over the top of your head, then lower it down to the front shoulder starting position; this front-to-back-to-front cycle is one repetition.
Keep the movement smooth and continuous with no pausing or locking out, maintaining a braced core and stable torso so you do not arch your lower back.
Only lower the bar behind the head as far as your shoulder mobility comfortably allows; if you feel pinching or strain, reduce the range or skip the behind-the-head portion.
Alternate front and back presses in this controlled manner until you complete the recommended repetitions.

name: Broad Jump
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart, toes pointed forward, on a flat non-slip surface with clear space ahead.
Set your weight over your mid-foot, keep your chest up, and look forward to a target landing spot.
Initiate by hinging at the hips and bending the knees into a quarter to half squat while swinging both arms back behind you to load up.
In one explosive motion, swing your arms forward and up, extend your hips, knees, and ankles fully, and jump forward as far as you can.
Drive horizontally rather than straight up, reaching your feet out in front of you as you near the landing.
Land softly on both feet at the same time, absorbing the impact by bending your hips and knees and keeping your chest up so you do not fall forward or back.
Stick the landing under control, then stand up, walk back to the start, and fully reset before the next jump.
Focus on a powerful arm swing and full hip extension; avoid collapsing the knees inward on landing, and prioritize a balanced, quiet landing over distance.

name: Burpee
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, arms at your sides, on a flat surface with room to move.
Drop down by bending your knees and hips into a squat and place both hands flat on the floor just outside your feet, shoulder width apart.
Shift your weight onto your hands and kick both feet straight back at once, landing in a high plank with your body in a straight line from head to heels and core braced.
Perform a push-up by lowering your chest toward the floor with elbows tracking back at about 45 degrees, then press back up; keep your hips level and do not let them sag or pike.
Jump both feet forward to land just outside your hands, returning to the bottom of the squat with your chest up.
Explode straight up into a vertical jump, reaching your arms overhead and fully extending your hips, knees, and ankles.
Land softly with bent knees to absorb the impact, immediately drop your hands back to the floor, and repeat for the prescribed reps or time.
Keep a tight core throughout so your lower back stays protected during the plank and landing; to scale, step the feet back and in or omit the push-up rather than letting form break down.

name: Butt Lift (Bridge)
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat with your arms resting at your sides, palms down for stability.
Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor about shoulder width apart, heels positioned a few inches from your glutes.
Tuck your chin slightly, relax your shoulders into the floor, and gently brace your core. This is your starting position.
Pushing primarily through your heels, lift your hips off the floor while keeping your torso rigid, raising until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Exhale as you lift and squeeze your glutes hard at the top, holding the contraction for one second without overarching your lower back.
Slowly lower your hips back toward the floor under control as you inhale, stopping just before they fully touch to keep tension on the glutes.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, driving the movement with your glutes and hamstrings rather than arching the lower back or pushing through your toes.

name: Butt-Ups
instructions: Get onto the floor in a forearm plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your forearms flat on the ground, arms bent to about 90 degrees.
Extend your legs back with your weight on your toes, feet about hip width apart, and allow a slight natural arch through your back rather than a perfectly flat plank.
Brace your core to start. This is your starting position.
Raise your glutes up toward the ceiling by piking at the hips, squeezing your abs to draw your ribcage and hips closer together until you reach a high inverted-V bridge position.
Exhale as you lift and pause briefly at the top, keeping your shoulders stacked over your elbows and your heels reaching toward the floor.
Lower your hips back down slowly under control as you inhale, returning to the starting plank without letting your lower back sag toward the floor.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, driving the movement with your abs rather than your shoulders, and keeping the motion smooth and controlled throughout.

name: Butterfly
instructions: Adjust the pec deck machine seat height so that when seated the handles or arm pads sit at roughly chest height and your upper arms will be parallel to the floor.
Select an appropriate weight on the stack and sit with your back flat against the pad, head upright, and feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grasp the handles or place your forearms against the pads with your upper arms parallel to the floor and elbows bent at about 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Keeping your back against the pad and a slight, fixed bend in the elbows, push the handles together in a smooth arc by squeezing your chest, bringing them toward the midline in front of you.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and hold the peak contraction for one second, focusing on squeezing the pecs rather than pushing with the arms.
Return slowly and under control as you inhale, allowing the handles to spread apart until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest, without letting the weight stack slam down.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, keeping your shoulders down and back and avoiding overstretching at the back of the movement to protect the shoulder joints.

name: Butterfly Stretch
instructions: Sit upright on the floor or a mat with good posture and your core gently engaged.
Bend both knees and bring the soles of your feet together, letting your knees fall out to the sides.
Draw your heels in toward your groin to a comfortable distance; closer to the body increases the stretch.
Clasp your hands around your feet or ankles and sit tall, lengthening your spine and lifting through the crown of your head.
Gently press your knees down toward the floor using your hip muscles, or rest your elbows lightly on your thighs to add mild pressure, until you feel a stretch through your inner thighs and groin.
Hold the position for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and keeping your back straight rather than rounding forward.
To deepen the stretch, hinge gently forward from the hips while keeping your spine long, then ease back and release.

name: Cable Chest Press
instructions: Set the two pulleys to about chest height on a dual cable station and select an appropriate weight on each stack, attaching single handles.
Grasp a handle in each hand and either sit on a bench placed between the towers facing away from the machine, or stand in a split stance with one foot forward for stability.
Bring your hands up to chest level with your upper arms out to the sides at about 45 degrees to your torso and your elbows bent to roughly 90 degrees.
Set your posture with head and chest up, shoulder blades pulled back and down, and your core braced. This is your starting position.
Press the handles forward and slightly together by extending through the elbows, driving them straight out in front of your chest until your arms are nearly straight.
Exhale as you press and keep your shoulder blades retracted throughout so the chest does the work rather than the front of the shoulders.

Pause briefly at full extension and squeeze your chest, then return the handles slowly to the starting position, keeping constant tension on the cables and not letting the elbows drift behind your torso.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions; you can vary the movement by performing it standing, at an incline or decline angle, or alternating one arm at a time.

name: Cable Crossover
instructions: Set both cable pulleys to a high position above head height and select an appropriate matching weight on each stack, attaching single handles.
Grasp a handle in each hand with a neutral grip, then step forward to the center between the two towers so the cables maintain tension.
Take a staggered stance with one foot in front of the other for balance, and lean your torso slightly forward from the waist.
Bring your hands together out in front of you with your arms spread wide and a slight, fixed bend in the elbows. This is your starting position.
Keeping that slight elbow bend to protect the biceps tendon, open your arms out wide to the sides in a controlled arc until you feel a good stretch across your chest, inhaling as you do.
Throughout the movement keep your torso and arms otherwise stationary, allowing motion only at the shoulder joints, not bending the elbows further.
Bring your hands back down and together in front of you along the same wide arc, squeezing your chest hard as the handles meet, exhaling as you contract.
Hold the squeeze for one second at the bottom, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions, keeping the movement smooth and avoiding any pressing or jerking with the arms.

name: Cable Crunch
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and select an appropriate weight that lets you feel the abs work without the lower back taking over.
Grasp the rope ends and kneel on the floor a foot or two in front of and below the pulley, knees about hip width apart.
Pull the rope down so your hands are held alongside your face or at the sides of your head, and keep them fixed in that position throughout.
Flex your hips slightly and let the cable weight gently pull your torso up so your lower back is in a slight extension. This is your starting position.
Keeping your hips stationary, crunch downward by flexing at the waist and contracting your abs, curling your elbows down toward the middle of your thighs as you round your upper back.
Exhale as you crunch and squeeze your abs hard at the bottom, holding the contraction for one second; the movement comes from spinal flexion, not from bending at the hips.
Return slowly to the starting position as you inhale, controlling the weight back up and keeping constant tension on the abs without letting the stack rest.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, and avoid going so heavy that you start pulling with your arms or lower back instead of crunching with the abs.

name: Cable Deadlifts
instructions: Set the cables to the lowest position on both towers of a dual cable station and select an appropriate weight on each stack, attaching handles.
Stand directly between the two uprights with your feet about hip to shoulder width apart and toes pointed slightly out.
Squat down by hinging at the hips and bending the knees until you can reach down and grasp a handle in each hand at your sides.
Set your starting position with your chest and head up, back flat with a natural arch, shoulders back, and arms hanging straight down at your sides holding the handles.
Brace your core, then begin the ascent by driving through your heels and extending your hips and knees together to stand tall.
Keep your arms straight and the handles hanging at your sides throughout, letting your legs and hips do the work rather than pulling with the arms.
Stand fully erect at the top with hips extended and shoulders back, then exhale.
Lower under control by hinging your hips back and bending your knees, returning the handles to the starting position while keeping your back flat, and repeat for the recommended repetitions.
Keep the cables close to your body and your spine neutral throughout; avoid rounding your lower back as you descend.

name: Cable Hammer Curls - Rope Attachment
