instructions: Attach a rope to a low pulley and select an appropriate weight, then stand facing the machine about 12 inches away with your feet shoulder width apart.
Grasp the rope with a neutral grip, palms facing each other, and stand up straight keeping the natural arch of your back and your chest up.
Pin your elbows in close to your sides and keep them fixed there for the entire movement; only your forearms should move, not your upper arms. This is your starting position.
Curl the rope up by contracting your biceps, raising your forearms until your biceps are fully contracted near your shoulders, exhaling as you lift.
Keep your elbows tucked and your upper arms stationary throughout, and keep the wrists neutral so the brachialis and forearms work along with the biceps.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top for a one-second contraction.
Slowly lower the rope back to the starting position under control as you inhale, resisting the weight on the way down and keeping tension on the muscles.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, avoiding any swinging of the torso or driving with the elbows to lift the weight.

name: Cable Hip Adduction
instructions: Set the pulley to the lowest position on the cable tower and attach a padded ankle cuff to the carabiner. Select a light to moderate weight to start.
Fasten the ankle cuff securely around the ankle of the leg closest to the machine, snug enough that it will not slide but not so tight it cuts off circulation.

Stand sideways to the stack with the cuffed leg nearest the pulley, then step away from the machine to create cable tension, taking a wide enough stance that the working leg is pulled out to the side away from your midline.

Grip the machine frame or a stable upright with the near hand for balance and stand tall on the outer (non-cuffed) leg, keeping your supporting knee soft and your torso upright with your chest up and core braced.
Allow the cuffed leg to be drawn outward by the cable until you feel a light stretch in the inner thigh; the working leg should be straight or only slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Exhale and drive the cuffed leg across your body toward and past the midline of the supporting leg, leading with the inner thigh and keeping the knee straight throughout.
Squeeze the adductors hard at the fully crossed position and hold for a one-count without letting your hips twist or your supporting knee cave inward.
Inhale and let the leg travel slowly back out to the side under control, resisting the cable the entire way rather than letting it snap your leg back.
Keep your pelvis level and avoid leaning your torso to compensate; the movement should come from the hip, not from swinging the body.
Complete all reps on one leg, then unclip, switch the cuff to the other ankle, turn around, and repeat for the opposite side.

name: Cable Incline Pushdown
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a moderate incline (about 30 to 45 degrees) and position it a couple of feet in front of a high-pulley cable station fitted with a straight bar attachment.
Sit on the bench facing away from the machine so the cable comes over the top of your head, then lie back against the incline pad with your head, upper back, and glutes supported.

Reach overhead and grasp the straight bar with a pronated (overhand, palms-down) grip at roughly shoulder width, then bring your arms down and forward so the bar finishes near your upper thighs with your arms straight.
Set your shoulders down and back into the pad, brace your core, and keep your upper arms angled slightly in front of your torso. This is your starting position with the lats already under tension.

Keeping your elbows only slightly bent and locked in place, inhale and raise the bar in a wide semicircular arc back over your head until your arms are extended overhead and you feel a full stretch across the lats.
Pause briefly at the top in the stretched position without letting the weight stack jerk your shoulders.
Exhale and drive the bar back down and forward in the same arc by pulling with your lats, leading from the armpits rather than bending the elbows.
Squeeze the lats hard as the bar returns to your thighs and hold the contraction for a one-count.
Move slowly and deliberately so the lats do the work; avoid heaving with your chest or excessively bending the elbows, which turns it into a triceps movement.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Cable Incline Triceps Extension
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a moderate incline (about 30 to 45 degrees) a couple of feet in front of a high-pulley cable station fitted with a straight bar.
Sit facing away from the machine and lie back against the pad with your head, upper back, and hips supported and your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Reach overhead and take the straight bar with a pronated (overhand, palms-down) grip slightly narrower than shoulder width.

Draw your elbows down and tuck them in close to the sides of your head so your upper arms sit at roughly a 25-degree angle above horizontal and point up toward the pulley. Keep them fixed there for the whole set. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and pin your shoulder blades into the pad so only your forearms will move.
Exhale and extend your elbows, driving the bar forward and down along the arc until your arms are fully straight and the triceps are fully contracted.
Squeeze the triceps and hold the locked-out position for a one-count.
Inhale and let the bar travel slowly back along the same path, bending only at the elbows until you feel a stretch in the triceps.
Keep your upper arms locked in beside your head throughout; if your elbows drift or flare you lose triceps tension and recruit the lats.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Cable Internal Rotation
instructions: Set the pulley to about elbow height and attach a single-handle grip; select a light weight, as the rotator cuff is a small muscle group.
Stand or sit sideways to the machine with the working arm (the one nearest the cable) closest to the stack.
Grasp the handle with the near hand using a neutral grip, then pin that elbow tight against your side, bent to 90 degrees, so the forearm points straight out toward the pulley.
Roll a small towel between your elbow and your ribs if you want to guarantee the upper arm stays fixed, then stand tall with your shoulders square and core braced. This is your starting position.
Keeping the elbow glued to your side, exhale and rotate your forearm inward across your body, pulling the handle toward your stomach while keeping the forearm parallel to the floor.
Continue until your forearm is across your abdomen and you feel the front of the shoulder contract; do not let the elbow drift away from your side.
Pause briefly in the contracted position, keeping the wrist neutral and the forearm perpendicular to your torso.
Inhale and let the handle rotate slowly back outward under control until the forearm again points toward the pulley and you feel a light stretch.
Keep the movement isolated to rotation at the shoulder; do not lean or twist your torso to move the weight.
Complete all reps, then turn around and repeat with the opposite arm.

name: Cable Iron Cross
instructions: Set both pulleys of a dual cable station to the high position and select a moderate weight on each side, then attach a single handle to each pulley.
Take a handle in each hand and step into the center of the machine so you are standing midway between the two stacks.
Adopt a staggered stance with one foot slightly ahead of the other for stability, knees soft, core braced, and chest lifted.
Raise both arms out to your sides until they form a straight horizontal line, so your body makes a "T" with a slight bend at the elbows that you will hold constant. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows fixed in that slight bend, exhale and pull both handles down and in across the front of your body in a wide hugging arc, as if wrapping your arms around a large barrel.
Bring your hands together in front of your lower chest or stomach and squeeze the chest hard at the peak contraction, holding for a one-count.
Inhale and let your arms travel slowly back out along the same arc until they return to the outstretched "T" and you feel a stretch across the chest.
Keep your torso upright and stationary; resist the urge to lean forward or to bend and straighten the elbows, which turns the movement into a press.
Continue for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Cable Judo Flip
instructions: Attach a rope to the cable and set the pulley to the lowest position; select a moderate weight that lets you move explosively but with control.
Stand side-on to the machine with a wide, athletic stance, knees bent, and grab the rope with both hands stacked, arms extended down toward the low pulley.
Step away from the stack if needed to load tension into the cable, then sink into a slight squat with your weight on the leg nearest the machine and your core braced.
Set your starting position with the rope down by the hip closest to the pulley and your torso rotated slightly toward the machine.
Exhale and explosively rotate your torso away from the pulley, pulling the rope diagonally up and across your body and over the opposite shoulder, as if throwing an opponent over your back.
Shift your bodyweight from the near foot to the far foot as you twist, pivoting the rear foot and crunching the obliques to drive the rotation.
Finish with the rope over the far shoulder, hips and shoulders fully rotated away from the machine, abs and obliques tightly contracted.
Inhale and reverse the path under control, rotating back and lowering the rope to the starting hip while re-loading your weight onto the near leg.
Keep the movement powered by your trunk rotation rather than just your arms, and avoid rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Repeat for the prescribed reps or to failure, then switch sides and repeat with the opposite orientation.

name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and place a flat bench in line with the cable, a couple of feet out from the stack so the cable runs along the floor toward the bench.
Sit on the end of the bench nearest the pulley, grasp the bar with a narrow overhand (pronated) grip, then lie back, drawing the bar with you; having a partner hand it to you makes this easier.
Lie flat with your head near the pulley end of the bench, feet planted firmly on the floor, and press the bar up so your arms are extended and the bar is positioned above your torso.

Adjust your shoulder position so your upper arms point back slightly toward the pulley and your arms form roughly a 90-degree angle with your torso, with the cable line of pull running along your arms. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and pin your shoulders to the bench so the upper arms stay fixed throughout.
Inhale and bend only at the elbows, lowering the bar in a controlled arc until it comes down to just above your forehead and you feel a stretch in the triceps.
Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing toward the ceiling; do not let them flare outward.
Exhale and extend your elbows, flexing the triceps to drive the bar back up to the starting position over your torso.
Squeeze the triceps and hold the contracted, extended position for a one-count.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then carefully sit up and return the bar to the stack.

name: Cable One Arm Tricep Extension
instructions: Set the pulley to the high position and attach a single handle; select a light to moderate weight.
Stand facing the machine, directly in front of the weight stack, and grasp the handle with one hand using a supinated (underhand, palms-up) grip.
Pull the handle down until your upper arm and elbow are locked against the side of your body, with your forearm and upper arm forming an acute angle (less than 90 degrees).
Stagger your feet slightly, one forward and one back, for balance, keep your free hand on your hip or waist, and brace your core with your torso upright. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arm pinned to your side and motionless, exhale and extend the elbow, driving the handle straight down until your arm is fully straight along your side.
Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom and hold the contracted position for a one-count.
Inhale and let the handle rise slowly back up under control, bending only at the elbow until you return to the acute-angle starting position.
Ensure only your forearm moves; if your upper arm drifts forward or your elbow lifts away from your side, lighten the load.
Complete all reps with one arm, then switch the handle to the other hand and repeat for the opposite side.

name: Cable Preacher Curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and place a preacher bench about two feet in front of the machine so the angled pad faces the stack.
Sit on the preacher bench and settle your chest against the top of the pad, draping the backs of your upper arms and elbows firmly over the angled pad so they are fully supported.
Have a partner hand you the bar, or reach down and grasp it, using a supinated (underhand, palms-up) grip at about shoulder width.
Fully extend your arms down the pad so your elbows are nearly straight and you feel a stretch in the biceps, keeping your wrists neutral and your shoulders down. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms flat against the pad throughout; they should never lift off during the set.
Exhale and curl the bar up toward your shoulders by flexing the biceps, moving smoothly through the full range.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top and hold the peak contraction for a one-count without letting your elbows slide up the pad.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control back to the fully extended starting position, resisting the cable the whole way.
Avoid bouncing out of the bottom or letting the arms fully snap straight under load; stop just short of locking out to protect the elbows.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Set both pulleys of a dual cable station to a high position, above head height, and select a light weight on each side, then attach a single handle to each pulley.
Stand in the center between the two stacks with a shoulder-width stance, knees soft, core braced, and chest up.

Reach up and across to grab the handles so the cables cross in front of you: take the left pulley's handle in your right hand and the right pulley's handle in your left hand, arms extended out in front and slightly up.
Set a slight, fixed bend in your elbows and pull your shoulder blades down. This is your starting position with the cables crossed.

Exhale and pull your arms back and outward in a wide arc, leading with the elbows and squeezing the rear delts and upper back, until your arms are extended out to your sides and the cables are no longer crossed.
Keep your arms straight (in that fixed slight bend) throughout; do not bend and straighten the elbows like a row.
Pause and squeeze the rear delts at the fully spread position for a one-count.
Inhale and let your arms travel slowly back forward and inward under control until the cables cross again in front of you.
Keep your torso upright and stationary, avoiding any swing or lean to move the weight; the motion comes purely from the shoulders.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Cable Reverse Crunch
instructions: Attach an ankle-strap (or cuff) to a low pulley and lay an exercise mat on the floor in front of the machine.
Sit on the mat with your feet pointing toward the pulley and fasten the strap securely around both ankles or feet.
Lie back on the mat, lift your legs, and bend your knees to about 90 degrees so the cable runs in a straight line from the pulley to your ankles; adjust the pulley height if the cable angle is off.

Place your hands behind your head or flat on the floor beside you for stability, and press your lower back gently toward the mat to engage the abs. This is your starting position with tension already on the cable.
Exhale and contract your lower abs to pull your knees in toward your chest, curling your pelvis upward and lifting your hips off the floor.
Drive the movement with your abdominals, not by swinging your legs; keep the knee angle roughly constant so the hip flexors do not take over.
Pause and squeeze the abs at the top with your hips raised and knees over your chest.
Inhale and lower your hips back to the floor slowly and under control, returning your knees to the 90-degree starting angle while maintaining tension on the abs.
Avoid letting the weight stack pull your legs back fast or yanking your head with your hands.
Repeat the controlled movement for the prescribed reps or to failure.

name: Cable Rope Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a rope to the lowest pulley position of the cable machine and select a moderate weight.
Grasp both ends of the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), then turn to face away from the machine and step forward to load tension.
Press the rope up so your hands are directly overhead with your arms fully extended and knuckles aimed at the ceiling; your elbows should be in close to your head and your upper arms vertical.
Adopt a staggered stance, one foot ahead of the other, and brace your core with a tall torso and a slight forward lean. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and your elbows pointing forward and tucked near your head, inhale and bend only at the elbows to lower the rope behind your head.
Continue lowering until your forearms drop past parallel and you feel a deep stretch in the triceps; pause briefly at the bottom.
Exhale and extend your elbows, flexing the triceps to drive your hands back up overhead, and spread the rope ends apart slightly at the top for a stronger contraction.
Squeeze the triceps and hold the fully extended overhead position for a one-count.
Keep your elbows from flaring wide; they should stay narrow and pointed forward so the tension stays on the triceps.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
instructions: Attach a rope to a low pulley at a seated cable row station and sit on the seat or platform with your feet braced against the foot plate.
Grasp the rope with an overhand grip, one hand on each end, and sit up tall with your lower back upright and a slight bend in your knees.

Extend your arms straight out toward the pulley so they are roughly parallel to the floor, letting your shoulders stretch forward, with your elbows flared out to the sides. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your chest up and torso vertical; do not lean back to row the weight.
Exhale and pull the rope toward your upper chest, just below the neck, driving your elbows up and out to the sides rather than down toward your hips.
Keep your upper arms horizontal and perpendicular to your torso throughout, and continue pulling until your elbows travel slightly behind your back and you squeeze the rear delts and mid-back.
Pull the rope ends apart slightly as you reach the contracted position to maximize rear-delt engagement, and hold for a one-count.
Inhale and let your arms extend slowly back out under control until they are straight and your shoulders stretch forward again.
Avoid jerking with the lower back or letting the elbows drop; keep them high to target the rear delts rather than the lats.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Cable Russian Twists
instructions: Attach a single handle to a cable set at roughly mid-pulley height and select a light to moderate weight.

Position a stability ball perpendicular to the cable and sit on it, then walk your feet out and lean back so your upper back and shoulders rest on the ball with your hips elevated and your body flat from head to knees, like a tabletop.
Plant your feet firmly hip to shoulder width apart for a stable base, and position yourself about arm's length from the pulley so there is tension on the cable.

Grasp the handle with both hands and extend your arms straight up above your chest, with your hands directly in line with the pulley; adjust the pulley height until the cable line is level. This is your starting position.
Keep your hips lifted and your core braced so your trunk stays rigid throughout.
Exhale and rotate your torso away from the pulley a full quarter-turn, keeping your arms straight and moving them as one unit with your shoulders and chest.
Drive the rotation from your obliques and trunk, not from your arms, and keep your hips level so they do not sag as you turn.
Pause briefly at the end of the rotation with the obliques contracted, then inhale and rotate slowly and under control back to the starting position directly in line with the pulley.
Maintain side tension on the cable in the resting position so the abs stay engaged the whole set.
Repeat to failure, then reposition on the opposite side and repeat the movement rotating the other direction.

name: Cable Seated Crunch
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and place a flat bench a short distance in front of the machine so its end is just below the pulley.
Sit on the bench with your back toward the high pulley, feet planted firmly on the floor about shoulder width apart.

Reach up and grasp the rope with both hands using a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and pull it down so your hands are held securely against the tops of your shoulders, one rope end at each shoulder.
Allow the weight to gently pull you into a slight hyperextension at the lower back so your abs start in a lengthened, stretched position. This is your starting position.
Keep your hips stationary and seated firmly on the bench so the movement comes only from flexing the spine, not from the hip flexors.
Exhale and crunch down by flexing at the waist, curling your chest and elbows down toward your hips one vertebra at a time.
Continue until your abs are fully contracted and your torso is curled forward, and squeeze the abs hard at the bottom for a one-count.
Inhale and uncurl slowly back up under control to the starting stretched position, resisting the pull of the weight the whole way.
Keep the rope fixed against your shoulders and avoid pulling with your arms; the abs alone should drive the crunch.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Cable Seated Lateral Raise
instructions: Set the pulleys of two opposing low cable stations to their lowest position and select a light weight on each; attach a single handle to each pulley.
Place a flat bench directly in the center between the two stacks, oriented so its narrow end points toward you, and stand in the middle.
Sit on the end of the bench facing out, with your feet planted on the floor in front of your knees and your knees bent.
Bend forward from the hips while keeping your back flat, resting your torso down against your thighs.

Reach down and across to grab the handles, taking the left pulley's handle in your right hand and the right pulley's handle in your left so the cables run under your knees; your arms hang extended with palms facing each other and a slight fixed bend at the elbows. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your back flat and chest near your thighs throughout the set.
Exhale and raise your upper arms out to the sides in a wide arc until they reach shoulder height and are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping the slight elbow bend fixed (about 10 to 30 degrees).
Lead with your elbows, not your hands, and keep your upper arms perpendicular to your torso so the tension stays on the rear and side delts.
Hold the top contraction for a one-count, squeezing the delts, without shrugging the traps up toward your ears.
Inhale and lower your arms slowly and under control back to the hanging starting position, then repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Cable Shoulder Press
instructions: Set both pulleys of a dual cable tower to the lowest position, attach single D-handles to each side, and select a moderate weight you can press for the target reps.
Stand directly centered between the two uprights with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward, and brace your core to keep your spine neutral.

Grab one handle in each hand and bring them up to shoulder height so your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, elbows pointing down and slightly forward, palms facing forward. This is your starting position.
Keep your chest up, head neutral, and squeeze your glutes to prevent your lower back from arching as the cables pull you backward.
Exhale and press both handles straight up overhead by extending through the elbows, bringing the handles toward each other near the top without clanging them together.
Stop just short of fully locking the elbows to keep tension on the shoulders, and pause briefly at the top with arms extended.
Inhale as you lower the handles under control back down to shoulder height, resisting the cable on the way down.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms throughout, and do not let the cables yank your hands back behind your shoulders.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, keeping your torso upright and avoiding any backward lean to cheat the weight up.

name: Cable Shrugs
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley on a cable tower and select a challenging but controllable weight.
Grasp the bar with a shoulder-width or slightly wider overhand grip, palms facing your body, and stand close to the pulley.
Stand tall with feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, knees slightly soft, chest up, and core braced; let your arms hang straight down in front of you holding the bar. This is your starting position.
Keep your arms completely straight throughout. They act only as hooks, so do not bend the elbows or try to curl the weight.
Exhale and lift the bar by elevating your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible.
Squeeze and hold the contraction at the top for a full second, focusing on the trapezius doing the work.
Inhale as you lower the bar back down under control to the starting position, allowing your shoulders to drop fully and stretch.
Do not roll your shoulders in circles; move them straight up and down to protect the joint and keep tension on the traps.
Keep your head and neck neutral, avoiding shrugging your chin forward, and repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Cable Wrist Curl
instructions: Place a flat bench in front of a low pulley cable fitted with a straight bar attachment, positioning the bench close enough that the cable stays under tension.
Select a light to moderate weight, since the forearms fatigue quickly and excessive load compromises the range of motion.
Sit on the end of the bench facing the pulley and grab the bar with a narrow to shoulder-width supinated grip, palms facing up.
Rest your forearms on top of your thighs so your wrists and hands hang just past your knees, with the cable pulling down on the bar. This is your starting position.
Keep your forearms pressed firmly against your thighs so they remain completely stationary throughout the movement.
Let the bar roll down toward your fingertips, opening your hands slightly to get a full stretch in the forearm flexors.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward as high as possible, closing your hands and lifting the bar by flexing only at the wrist joint.
Squeeze and hold the top contraction for a second, feeling the forearms work.
Inhale as you slowly lower your wrists back down to the stretched starting position under control.
Move only at the wrists; if your forearms lift off your thighs, reduce the weight, and repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Calf Press
instructions: Adjust the seat of the seated calf press or leg press machine so that with your feet on the platform your knees are only slightly bent in the start position.
Place the balls of both feet firmly on the lower edge of the platform, about hip- to shoulder-width apart, with your heels hanging off the edge and toes pointing forward.
Select an appropriate weight and grasp the handles or sit back firmly against the seat to anchor your body.
Straighten your legs by extending the knees just enough to lift the weight off the stack, but keep a soft, unlocked knee. This is your starting position.
Let your heels drop and your toes point up so your ankles fully flex, getting a deep stretch in the calves at the bottom.
Exhale and press the platform away by extending your ankles, driving through the balls of your feet and pushing your toes as far as possible.
Squeeze your calves hard and pause briefly at the top with the ankles fully extended.
Keep your knees stationary the entire time; do not bend or pump them to move the weight, since this is purely an ankle movement.
Inhale as you reverse the motion under control, lowering back into the deep stretch, and repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Calf Press On The Leg Press Machine
instructions: Sit down in the leg press machine with your back and hips flat against the padded supports and place both feet on the platform at a medium, shoulder-width stance.
Release the safety bars and press the platform up until your legs are fully extended without locking your knees, so your torso and legs form roughly a 90-degree angle.
If your machine allows, leave the safety catches engaged for added security on the loaded platform.
Carefully slide your feet down so only your toes and the balls of your feet rest on the lower portion of the platform, with your heels extending off the edge.
Point your toes forward (or inward/outward to bias different calf heads) and keep your legs straight but knees unlocked. This is your starting position.
Let your heels drift down toward your body, bending at the ankles until you feel a full stretch in your calves.
Exhale and press the platform by raising your heels, extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing the calves hard.
Keep your knees completely stationary throughout; there should be no bending or pumping of the knees at any point.
Hold the contracted position for a second at the top.
Inhale as you slowly lower your heels back to the stretched position, controlling the platform the entire way, and repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Calf Raise On A Dumbbell
instructions: Choose a sturdy upright or rack to hold for balance and stand next to it within easy reach.
Place one dumbbell on the floor, preferably one with round plates so it rolls slightly and forces your calf and foot to work harder to stabilize.
Step the ball of one foot onto the dumbbell handle, keeping your heel and the rest of the foot off the handle, and tuck your other foot behind your working ankle or let it hang.
Roll your foot slightly forward so your heel drops below the handle and you feel a deep stretch in the calf. This is your starting position.
Hold the support with one hand to stay balanced, keep your working leg straight but knee unlocked, and brace your core.
Exhale and lift your calf by rolling your foot up and over the top of the handle, rising onto your toes for a full extension.
As you come up, let the dumbbell roll slightly backward and squeeze the calf hard at the top, holding for one second.
Inhale as you lower under control, rolling the dumbbell slightly forward to sink back into a deep stretch at the bottom.
Move slowly and deliberately; the rolling handle makes balance harder, so avoid rushing, and repeat for the recommended repetitions before switching legs.

name: Calf Raises - With Bands
instructions: Grab a resistance band with handles and stand on the middle of it with the balls of both feet, hip- to shoulder-width apart.
Make sure the length of band between each foot and hand is equal on both sides so the tension is balanced.
Hold a handle in each hand and raise your arms up beside your head as if setting up for a shoulder press, palms facing forward with elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
This arm position pre-loads tension into the band; keep your torso upright and core braced. This is your starting position.
Keep your hands fixed by your shoulders throughout; do not press the band overhead, as your hands serve only to anchor the resistance.
Exhale and rise up onto your toes, extending your ankles fully and contracting your calves hard at the top.
Hold the peak contraction for one second, balancing on the balls of your feet.
Inhale as you slowly lower your heels back toward the floor under control, feeling the calves stretch at the bottom.
Keep your legs straight with knees unlocked and avoid bouncing; repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Calf Stretch Elbows Against Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall a couple of feet away with your feet together and pointing straight at the wall.
Lean forward and place both forearms against the wall, resting your weight on your elbows and forearms.
Keep your legs straight, your body in a straight line from heels to head, and press your hips slightly forward.
Actively work to keep both heels flat on the ground, which drives the stretch into your calves.
Hold the position for 10 to 20 seconds, breathing steadily and relaxing into the stretch.
To increase the stretch, step your feet further from the wall; to ease it, move closer.
Avoid bouncing; hold a steady, gentle stretch and repeat as needed.

name: Calf Stretch Hands Against Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall several feet away and stagger your stance, stepping one foot forward and keeping the other foot back.
Keep your back leg straight with the knee unlocked, the back foot flat and pointing straight at the wall.
Lean forward and rest both hands on the wall at about shoulder height, arms extended.
Keep your back heel, hip, and head aligned in a straight line, pressing your hips gently toward the wall.
Drive the stretch into the calf of your back leg by keeping that heel pressed firmly into the floor.
Bend your front knee as needed to lean further forward and deepen the stretch.
Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, breathing steadily, then switch legs and repeat on the other side.

name: Calf Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place the ball of one foot up against the base of the wall, keeping that heel on the floor.
Keep your stretching leg straight with the knee unlocked and your foot pointing straight forward.
Place your hands on the wall for balance if needed and keep your torso upright.
Lean your hips and chest toward the wall, driving your heel down and forward until you feel a stretch through your calf and Achilles.
Hold the stretch steadily for 10 to 20 seconds without bouncing, breathing slowly.
Release and switch sides, repeating with the other foot.

name: Calf-Machine Shoulder Shrug
instructions: Step into a standing calf raise machine and position the shoulder pads so they rest squarely on top of your shoulders.
Stand with your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, flat on the platform, with your knees and hips locked out so your legs stay straight and rigid throughout.
Stand tall with your torso upright, chest up, core braced, and arms hanging relaxed by your sides. This is your starting position.
Let the pads push your shoulders down so the traps are stretched at the bottom.
Exhale and raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears, lifting the pads as high as possible by contracting the traps.
Hold the top contraction for a full second, squeezing the trapezius.
Inhale as you slowly lower your shoulders back down to the stretched starting position under control.
Move your shoulders straight up and down without rolling them, and keep your legs locked so the movement comes only from the traps; repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Calves-SMR
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and place a foam roller underneath your lower leg, positioned under the calf.
Either cross your other leg over the working leg to add pressure, or place that foot flat on the floor to support some of your weight and reduce intensity.
Place your hands flat on the floor at your sides or just behind your hips for support.
Press down through your hands to lift your hips off the floor, shifting much of your bodyweight onto the calf resting on the roller. This is your starting position.
Slowly roll your body so the roller travels along the muscle from just below the knee down to just above the ankle.
When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold the pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds until the tension eases.
Keep your breathing relaxed and avoid rolling directly over the back of the knee joint or the ankle bone.
Continue rolling for the desired time, then switch and repeat on the other leg.

name: Car Deadlift
instructions: Approach the loaded car deadlift apparatus, which usually has neutral-grip handles set at frame level (some use a straight bar that can be gripped like a conventional deadlift).
Set your feet about hip-width apart, toes pointing forward, with your shins close to the apparatus.
Position yourself relative to the handles based on your strength: center yourself between them if you are a strong squatter, or stand back an inch or two if you are a strong deadlifter.
Hinge at the hips and bend down to grip the handles firmly with a neutral grip, locking your hands in.
With your grip set, take a big breath into your belly and brace hard, then lower your hips and flex your knees into the starting position.
Look forward, keep your chest up, your back flat and arched, and your shoulders pulled down and back.
Drive through your heels and the mid-foot to push the apparatus upward, keeping the load close to your body.
As the weight rises, pull your shoulder blades together and drive your hips forward to lock out tall and upright at the top.
Keep your arms straight throughout; they are hooks, not levers, so do not bend the elbows.
Lower the weight under control by hinging at the hips and bending the knees, guiding the apparatus back to the floor, and repeat or reset as required.

name: Car Drivers
instructions: Select a single weight plate light enough that you can hold it at arm's length and rotate it with control.
Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly soft, chest up, and core braced.
Grip the plate with both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions, palms facing each other.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you at about shoulder height, holding the plate vertically. This is your starting position.
Keep your arms straight and your torso still throughout; the motion should come from your shoulders, not from twisting your body.
Initiate the movement by rotating the plate as far as possible to one side, exactly like turning a steering wheel.
Reverse smoothly and rotate the plate all the way to the opposite side.
Keep the plate at arm's length and at shoulder height the entire time, moving slowly and under control.
Continue rotating side to side for the recommended number of repetitions, breathing steadily.

name: Carioca Quick Step
instructions: Begin in an athletic stance with your feet a few inches apart, knees soft, and weight on the balls of your feet, ready to move laterally.
Bring your arms up into a relaxed running position, with the left arm up if you are starting by moving to your right.
Choose a direction to travel and stay light on your feet, looking straight ahead the entire time.
Quick-step your trailing foot behind your lead leg, crossing it behind, then immediately pull that knee up.
Drive your arms in sync with your legs, firing them up powerfully as you pull the knee up.
Make sure your lifted knee travels straight up and down rather than swinging out to the side.
Avoid turning or twisting your feet and hips as you move; keep your shoulders and head facing forward.
Continue the cross-behind, knee-up rhythm quickly down your travel distance, then repeat in the opposite direction to work both sides.

name: Cat Stretch
instructions: Position yourself on the floor on your hands and knees in a quadruped position.
Place your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, with your back flat and neutral to start.
Exhale and pull your belly button in toward your spine, drawing your core tight.
Round your entire spine up toward the ceiling, segment by segment, through your lower back, mid-back, shoulders, and neck.
Let your head drop naturally so your gaze falls toward your thighs, deepening the stretch through the back.
Press the floor away through your hands to spread the shoulder blades and maximize the rounding of the upper back.
Hold the rounded position for about 15 seconds, breathing slowly and feeling the stretch along your spine.
Release gently back to a flat, neutral spine, and repeat as desired.

name: Cat-Cow
instructions: Get onto all fours on a mat in a tabletop position: place your hands directly under your shoulders with fingers spread and palms flat, and your knees directly under your hips, hip-width apart, with the tops of your feet relaxed on the floor.

Set a neutral starting spine with your back flat like a table, your neck long, and your gaze down at the floor between your hands. Engage your core lightly so the movement comes from your spine, not from rocking your hips forward and back.
Begin the Cat phase by exhaling slowly and pulling your belly button up toward your spine, rounding your back up toward the ceiling one vertebra at a time.
As you round, tuck your chin toward your chest and tuck your tailbone under, pressing the floor away with your hands to spread the upper back. Feel the stretch travel along your entire spine.
Transition into the Cow phase by inhaling slowly and reversing the motion: drop your belly toward the floor, arch your back, and let your chest move forward and down.

As you arch, gently lift your chest and tilt your gaze slightly upward, and lift your tailbone toward the ceiling, creating a gentle dip through the lower back. Do not crank the neck back hard or sag completely in the lower back.
Keep the tempo slow and continuous, syncing each movement with your breath: exhale to round (Cat), inhale to arch (Cow). Keep your arms straight and shoulders away from your ears throughout.
Continue flowing smoothly between the two positions for the prescribed time or reps, moving only as far as is comfortable and pain-free.

name: Catch and Overhead Throw
instructions: Choose a medicine ball you can control overhead, and stand facing a sturdy wall or a partner roughly 6 to 10 feet away. If using a wall, stand close enough to comfortably field the rebound.
Set an athletic stance with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward, knees softly bent, and weight balanced through the middle of your feet.
Hold the ball with both hands on the sides of it, arms extended, and brace your core so your torso stays stable.

Load the throw by raising the ball overhead and reaching it back behind your head, allowing a slight arch and stretch through your lats, chest, and shoulders. Keep your hips and knees stable rather than leaning back excessively.
Initiate the throw by forcefully contracting your lats and abs to pull the ball forward over the top, snapping it down and out toward the wall or partner. Exhale sharply as you release.
Follow through with your arms toward the target and let your torso flex slightly forward, finishing with the hands pointing where the ball is going.

Immediately reset your hands and stay ready to catch the rebound: receive the ball with both hands, absorb it by letting your arms give slightly, and guide it back overhead into the next loaded position.
If throwing against a wall, aim slightly higher than you would to a partner so the rebound returns to a catchable height. Keep your core braced on every rep to protect your lower back.
Repeat for the prescribed number of throws, maintaining an explosive throw and a controlled catch each time.

name: Chain Handle Extension
instructions: Gather two cable handle attachments and a length of chain, and clip the middle of the chain to each handle so the chain hangs as the resistance. Position a flat bench in clear space.
Lie back flat on the bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor on either side for stability, and keep your head, upper back, and glutes in contact with the bench.

Grip one handle in each hand with a neutral or pronated grip, and press your arms up so your upper arms are vertical, pointing your elbows straight up toward the ceiling. The chains will drape down toward your head.
Set your starting position with elbows fully bent and the handles lowered near your forehead, upper arms locked in place and perpendicular to the floor. This is your start.
Brace your core and keep your upper arms completely still throughout; only your forearms should move, like a hinge at the elbow.
Exhale and extend through the elbows, driving the handles up until your arms are straight and locked out overhead, keeping your wrists pronated and firm.
Pause briefly at full lockout and squeeze the triceps, feeling the chain weight resist the movement.
Inhale and reverse the motion under control, bending only at the elbows to lower the handles back to the starting position near your forehead without flaring your upper arms.
Avoid letting your elbows drift apart or your shoulders take over; keep the tension on the triceps. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Chain Press
instructions: Attach a length of chain to two cable handle attachments so the chains provide the load, and set them within reach of a flat bench. Chains add resistance progressively as they lift off the floor.
Lie back on the flat bench in a standard pressing setup: feet flat on the floor, glutes and upper back on the bench, and a slight natural arch in the lower back.

Take one handle in each hand and press them up so your arms are extended and perpendicular to the floor, wrists pronated (palms facing toward your feet). The chains will hang down, partially resting on the floor at the bottom and lifting as you press.
Set your starting position with arms straight and stacked over your shoulders, core braced, and shoulder blades pulled down and back into the bench.
Inhale and lower the handles by bending your elbows, bringing them down and slightly out to about chest level, allowing some of the chain to unload onto the floor as you descend.
Continue lowering under control until your elbows form roughly a 90-degree angle and the handles are near your chest. Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows and do not let your shoulders shrug up.
Exhale and reverse by pressing through your palms, extending the elbows to drive the handles back up to lockout, picking the chain back up off the floor as you rise.
Keep your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso rather than flared straight out, and keep your wrists firm and neutral. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Chair Leg Extended Stretch
instructions: Sit upright toward the front of a stable chair with your back straight, chest lifted, and both feet flat on the floor.
Grip the sides of the seat with both hands to anchor your torso and keep your upper body stable and tall throughout.
Raise one leg and straighten the knee, extending the leg out in front of you until it is roughly parallel to the floor.
Flex your ankle by pulling your toes back toward your shin to deepen the stretch along the hamstring and back of the leg.
Keeping the leg straight and the ankle flexed, slowly move that leg outward to the side as far as you comfortably can to add a stretch through the inner thigh and adductors.
Move smoothly and avoid bouncing; only go as far as feels like a gentle stretch, not pain, and keep your torso upright rather than leaning toward the leg.
Slowly bring the leg back to center and then lower it to the floor under control.
Repeat with the other leg, performing the prescribed number of holds or repetitions per side.

name: Chair Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Sit upright on a stable chair with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and your spine tall.
Anchor yourself by gripping the side or seat of the chair with one hand on the side you are bending toward.
Raise your opposite arm up and over your head, reaching toward the side you are gripping.
Bend gently sideways at the waist toward the anchored hand, sliding your reaching arm over your head to lengthen the side of your torso and lats.
Keep facing forward and avoid twisting or rounding; bend purely to the side so you feel a stretch along your ribs, lats, and into the lower back.
Hold the stretch for about 10 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly and steadily, deepening slightly on each exhale without forcing it.
Return upright under control, then switch your hand positions and repeat the bend to the opposite side for an equal hold.

name: Chair Squat
instructions: Set the bar on the rack to a height that matches roughly your mid-chest to shoulder level so you can unrack it without a high climb. Load it with appropriate weight and secure collars.
Step under the bar and position it across the back of your shoulders, resting it on the meaty part of your upper traps (high bar) rather than on your neck.
Grip the bar with both hands facing forward, slightly wider than shoulder-width, pull your elbows down and your shoulder blades together to create a stable shelf, and lift your chest.
Unlock the bar and lift it off the rack by extending your legs, then step back and move your feet forward about 18 inches in front of where the bar started.
Set your stance shoulder-width with your toes pointed slightly out, brace your core, look forward, and maintain a neutral or slightly arched spine. This is your starting position.
Inhale, brace, and slowly lower by bending your knees and sitting your hips down and back, keeping your chest up and head facing forward. Track your knees in line with your toes.
Continue descending under control until the angle between your upper and lower leg breaks past 90 degrees (thighs at or just below parallel), keeping your heels planted.
Exhale and drive back up by pushing the floor away through the heels and mid-foot, extending the knees and hips together to return to the standing starting position.

Keep the spine neutral throughout and avoid letting your knees cave inward or your chest dropping forward. Repeat for the prescribed reps, then re-rack the bar by stepping forward and lowering it into the hooks.

name: Chair Upper Body Stretch
instructions: Sit on the front edge of a stable chair with your feet flat on the floor and hip-width apart, or stand facing the chair back, depending on your setup.
Reach and grip the back of the chair (or the seat behind you) with both hands, roughly shoulder-width apart.
Straighten your arms and keep your back flat and long, hinging at the hips as needed so your spine stays neutral rather than rounded.
Drop your chest and head down between your arms, pulling your upper body forward and down so you feel a stretch open across your shoulders, chest, biceps, and upper back.
Keep your arms straight and let your shoulder blades pull away from your ears as you sink gently into the stretch.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and relaxing deeper into the stretch on each exhale without bouncing.
Release by slowly raising your torso back to upright under control.

name: Chest And Front Of Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your legs together or hip-width apart, holding a body bar or broomstick across the front of your body.
Take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing down, and hold the pole in front of your thighs with your arms straight.
Set your posture: stand upright, brace your core lightly, and keep your shoulders down and back so the stretch targets the chest and front of the shoulders, not the lower back.
Keeping your arms as straight as comfortable, slowly raise the pole up in front of you and continue lifting it overhead.
Carefully continue the path back and down behind your head, allowing your chest to open and the front of your shoulders to stretch as the pole travels behind you.
Move slowly and only go as far as your flexibility allows without pain; widen your grip if the shoulders feel too tight. Avoid arching the lower back to compensate.
Hold the deepest comfortable position briefly, feeling the stretch across the chest and front delts, then slowly reverse the path to bring the pole back to the front.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, breathing steadily throughout.

name: Chest Push (multiple response)
instructions: Select a medicine ball you can throw explosively, and kneel on a mat facing a sturdy wall (or a partner) a few feet away.
Set up in a tall kneeling position with your knees about hip-width apart, hips extended, torso upright, and core braced.
Hold the ball with both hands, fingers spread on the sides, and pull it in tight against your chest with your elbows tucked down. This is your starting position.
Initiate the throw by exploding forward and outward: drive your hips forward and press the ball off your chest as hard as possible, extending your arms fully toward the target.
Exhale forcefully on release and snap the ball straight ahead at chest height, pushing through both hands evenly.
Allow your follow-through to carry you forward, catching yourself on the floor with your hands as your body falls toward the wall.
Immediately push back up and return to the upright tall-kneeling starting position, resetting the ball against your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of explosive pushes, keeping each rep powerful and controlling the landing each time.

name: Chest Push (single response)
instructions: Choose a medicine ball appropriate for explosive throwing and kneel on a mat in an open area or facing a wall.
Set a tall kneeling position with knees hip-width apart, hips extended, spine tall, and core braced for stability.
Hold the medicine ball with both hands gripping the sides and pull it in tightly against your chest with elbows tucked. This is your starting position.
Execute the throw by exploding forward and outward, driving your hips forward while pressing the ball off your chest as hard as possible to send it as far as you can.
Extend both arms fully toward the target and exhale sharply at release, pushing evenly through both hands.
Follow through by letting your body fall forward, catching yourself on the floor with your hands to safely absorb the momentum.
Reset to the upright kneeling position before performing the next single explosive throw. Repeat for the prescribed number of attempts.

name: Chest Push from 3 point stance
instructions: Choose a medicine ball for explosive throwing and set up in an open lane where you can step and throw forward.

Get into a three-point stance: squat down with your hips back and your back flat, place one hand on the ground in front of you for support, and stagger your feet with weight loaded ready to drive forward. Set the medicine ball on the ground directly in front of you.
Brace your core and keep your eyes up toward your throwing target so you stay in an athletic, ready posture.
Take your first explosive step forward, and as you do, scoop the ball up and pull it in to your chest, getting both hands positioned on the sides of the ball ready to throw.
As you plant your second step, drive your hips forward and explosively push the ball off your chest, releasing it forward as hard as possible toward the target.
Extend both arms fully through the throw and exhale forcefully at release, finishing with your hands pointing at the target.
Follow your momentum forward and reset before the next rep. Repeat for the prescribed number of throws, leading with the opposite stance as desired.

name: Chest Push with Run Release
instructions: Choose a medicine ball you can throw and sprint with, and set up in an open lane with at least 10 yards of clear running room ahead.
Get into an athletic stance with your knees bent, hips pushed back, back flat, and the ball held low near your legs in both hands. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your chest up and eyes forward, ready to drive into the throw.
Take your first explosive step forward and, as you do, draw the medicine ball up and in to your chest, setting both hands on the sides ready to push.
As you take your second step, drive your hips forward and explosively push the ball straight ahead off your chest, releasing it forward as powerfully as possible.
Immediately after the release, accelerate into a sprint and run for about 10 yards in the direction of the throw, exploding off the line.
If you are fast enough, chase down and catch your own pass; otherwise simply finish the 10-yard sprint under control.
Reset to the starting stance and repeat for the prescribed number of throw-and-sprint reps.

name: Chest Stretch on Stability Ball
instructions: Place an exercise (stability) ball on the floor and kneel on your hands and knees beside it, positioning the ball just outside one shoulder.
Set your base with knees under your hips and your supporting hand under your shoulder so your back stays flat and your core is engaged.
Place the elbow and forearm of the arm nearest the ball on top of the ball, keeping that arm extended out to your side at roughly shoulder height. This is your starting position.
Slowly lower your chest and torso toward the floor, keeping your elbow resting on top of the ball so the arm stays fixed and the shoulder and chest open up.
Sink only to the point of a comfortable stretch across the chest and front of the shoulder; keep your spine long and avoid forcing or bouncing.
Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and relaxing into it on each exhale.
Gently press back up to the starting position, then switch sides and repeat the stretch with the other arm on the ball.

name: Child's Pose
instructions: Get onto your hands and knees on a mat in a tabletop position, with hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips. (Avoid this position if you have significant knee problems.)
Bring your big toes together behind you and let your knees stay together or spread them slightly wider than your hips, whichever lets your torso settle comfortably.
Walk your hands forward in front of you along the floor, keeping your arms extended.
Slowly sit your hips back and down toward your heels, letting your arms drag along the floor as your torso lengthens and your spine stretches out.
Settle your buttocks onto your heels as far as is comfortable, keeping your arms reaching long in front of you to deepen the stretch through the lats and middle back.
Rest your forehead gently on the floor and let your shoulders and neck relax completely.
Breathe slowly and deeply, directing each breath into your back so you feel your ribs and lower back expand and the stretch deepen.
Hold for the prescribed time, then walk your hands back and rise up under control to release.

name: Chin To Chest Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor (or a chair) in an upright, comfortable position with your spine tall and shoulders relaxed down away from your ears.
Place both hands at the back of your head with your fingers interlocked, your thumbs pointing down toward your neck, and your elbows pointing forward.
Keep your back straight and your shoulders still so the stretch isolates the back of the neck and traps rather than rounding your whole spine.
Slowly and gently use the weight of your hands to draw your head down, bringing your chin toward your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch along the back of your neck and upper traps.
Apply only light pressure; do not yank on your head. Let the stretch build gradually.
Hold the position for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and relaxing your neck and shoulders deeper on each exhale.
Release by slowly lifting your head back to neutral and lowering your hands. Repeat for the prescribed number of holds.

name: Chin-Up
instructions: Stand under a fixed pull-up bar and reach up with both hands using a supinated (underhand) grip, palms facing you, hands set slightly closer than shoulder width.
Wrap your thumbs around the bar and grip firmly, then let your body hang with arms fully extended, feet off the floor; cross your ankles or bend your knees behind you if the bar is low.
Set your shoulders by pulling them down and back away from your ears, brace your core, and keep a slight arch in your lower back with your chest lifted toward the bar. This is your starting position.
Breathe out and pull yourself up by driving your elbows down and into your sides, leading with your chest, until your chin clears the bar.
Squeeze your biceps and lats hard at the top and hold for a one-count without swinging or kipping.
Breathe in and lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended and your shoulder blades are stretched at the bottom.
Keep your body from swinging by staying braced through the core and avoiding any leg kick. Do not shorten the range of motion at the bottom; full extension each rep builds the most strength.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Circus Bell
instructions: Set the oversized circus dumbbell on a thick rubber mat with the handle running between your feet, which should be roughly hip-width apart.
Squat down with a flat back, chest up, and grip the thick handle firmly with both hands stacked or side by side.
Brace your core, drive through your heels, and explosively extend your hips and knees to clean the bell up toward one shoulder, releasing the assisting hand as it rises.
Rotate your elbow under and catch the bell at the shoulder, making sure one of the bell heads sits behind and over your shoulder so the weight does not pull you off balance.
Stabilize the bell racked at the shoulder, keeping your wrist stacked and your torso upright and braced.
Dip slightly by bending your knees, then drive upward explosively, pressing the bell overhead while leaning your torso slightly away from the implement to get under it.
Lock the arm out overhead with the bell stable, then steady your stance with the weight fully supported.
Lower the bell back to the shoulder under control, then guide it carefully down to the mat using both hands, keeping it controlled throughout to protect your back and the floor.
Exhale forcefully on the clean and the press, and keep your lower back braced the entire time to avoid hyperextension.

name: Clap Push-Up
instructions: Set up in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width, fingers spread, and your weight on your hands and toes.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight rigid line from head to heels with no sag in the hips.
Pull your shoulder blades back, then lower your chest toward the floor under control by bending your elbows to roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
When your chest is just above the floor, drive explosively through your palms to push your hands off the ground.
While airborne, quickly clap your hands together in front of your chest.
Bring your hands back apart and land on them with the elbows slightly bent to absorb the impact.
Immediately sink into the next rep, keeping the core tight so the hips never pike or drop.
Exhale hard on the explosive press and reset your rigid plank position before each repetition; stop the set the moment your landings stop being soft and controlled.

name: Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the barbell over the middle of your feet, almost touching your shins.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the bar just outside your legs with a pronated or hook grip, arms straight and elbows rotated out.
Set your back flat, chest up, head facing forward, hips lower than your shoulders, and shoulders positioned slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through your heels and extending your knees, keeping your back angle constant and arms straight as the bar travels in a straight line to just above the knees.

Initiate the second pull as the bar reaches mid-thigh: aggressively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in a jumping motion to accelerate the bar upward, keeping it close to your body and your arms relaxed and straight.

At full extension, shrug your traps powerfully and pull your elbows high and to the sides, then transition into the third pull by aggressively pulling your body down and rotating your elbows around and under the bar.
Receive the bar racked on the front of your shoulders in a front squat position, with elbows high, torso upright, and the bar lightly touching your throat with relaxed hands.
Ride the catch down into a full front squat to absorb the bar, keeping your chest up and weight on your heels.
Recover by driving through your heels out of the squat, keeping your torso upright and elbows high, until you are standing fully erect.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout and avoid pulling early with the arms; the power must come from the legs and hips, not a reverse curl. Breathe in before the pull and brace hard.

name: Clean and Jerk
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and the barbell over the middle of your feet, close to your shins.

Grip the bar just outside your legs with a pronated or hook grip, set your back flat, chest up, head forward, hips below shoulders, and shoulders slightly ahead of the bar. This is your starting position.
Perform the first pull by driving through your heels and extending the knees, keeping the back angle constant and arms straight as the bar rises to just above the knee.
Perform the second pull at mid-thigh by explosively extending hips, knees, and ankles in a jumping motion to drive the bar upward while keeping it close to the body.

At full extension, shrug and pull yourself under the bar, rotating your elbows around it to receive it on your front shoulders in a front squat, then ride it down into a full squat with elbows high and torso upright.
Recover from the squat by driving through your heels until standing tall with the bar racked on your shoulders.
Set up for the jerk with feet directly under your hips; brace your core and dip straight down a few inches by bending only the knees, keeping the torso vertical and not letting the hips travel back.
Reverse the dip explosively, driving through your heels to launch the bar off your shoulders, and snap your head back slightly to clear the bar's path.
As the bar leaves the shoulders, split your feet by stepping one foot forward and one back, dropping under the bar and punching your arms to lock it out fully overhead.
Stabilize the overhead lockout in the split stance, then recover by stepping the front foot back halfway and the rear foot forward to finish standing tall with the bar locked overhead.
Keep the bar path vertical and the arms straight until the final pull-under; never let the elbows bend early during the clean or the dip during the jerk.

name: Clean and Press
instructions: Stand with a shoulder-width stance, knees inside your arms, and the barbell over the middle of your feet close to your shins.
Bend at the knees and hips with a flat back to grip the bar with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width, arms fully extended and elbows pointed out.
Position your shoulders over or slightly ahead of the bar, chest up, and establish a flat back. This is your starting position.
Begin the pull by extending the knees, raising your hips and shoulders at the same rate so the back angle stays constant, keeping the bar close as it travels straight up.
As the bar passes your knees, explosively extend your ankles, knees, and hips in a jumping motion, shrugging your shoulders and using the momentum to pull the bar as high as possible with elbows out.
At peak elevation, pull yourself under the bar, dropping into a partial squat as you rotate your elbows around and under it.
Rack the bar across the front of your shoulders, keeping your torso erect and flexing the hips and knees to absorb the weight.
Stand to full height with the bar racked in the clean position and your feet set flat.
Without moving your feet, brace your core, exhale, and press the bar straight overhead until your arms lock out, keeping the bar over your mid-foot.
Lower the bar under control back to the racked position on your shoulders, then reset for the next repetition.
Keep the bar close to your body during the pull and avoid leaning back excessively during the press; brace your abs to protect the lower back.

name: Clean Deadlift
instructions: Stand with the barbell over the middle of your feet, close to your shins, with feet directly under your hips and toes turned out slightly.
Bend down and grip the bar with a double-overhand or hook grip at about shoulder width, just outside or at the edge of your legs.
Drop your hips so your spine is in full extension, chest up, shoulders positioned slightly in front of the bar, and your back as upright as possible. This is your starting position.
Take a breath, brace your core, and begin by driving through the front of your heels, pushing the floor away.
Keep the back angle constant as the bar rises off the floor, flaring your knees out to the sides to keep them clear of the bar's path.
Maintain a straight bar path tight against your shins and thighs, with the arms straight and shoulders staying ahead of the bar until it clears the knees.
After the bar passes the knees, drive your hips forward into the bar until your hips and knees are fully extended and you are standing tall with shoulders back.
Lower the bar under control by hinging at the hips and bending the knees, keeping it close to your body, and reset before the next rep.
Keep your spine neutral throughout and do not let the hips shoot up first or the chest cave; the bar and shoulders should rise together.

name: Clean from Blocks
instructions: Set the loaded barbell on blocks or stands at the desired height, then stand with feet hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Grip the bar just outside your legs with a pronated or hook grip, arms straight and elbows rotated out.
Lower your hips into position with a flat back, chest up, head facing forward, weight on your heels, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
Initiate the pull by driving through your heels and extending the knees, keeping the back angle constant and arms straight as the bar leaves the blocks.
As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in a jumping motion to accelerate the bar upward close to your body.
At full extension, shrug powerfully and pull yourself under the bar, rotating your elbows around and under it.
Receive the bar in a front squat position, racked on your protracted shoulders lightly against your throat with relaxed hands and high elbows.
Ride the catch down into a full front squat, keeping your torso upright and chest tall.
Recover by driving through your heels until standing fully erect, then return the bar to the blocks under control for the next rep.
Because there is no momentum from the floor, focus on an explosive hip extension off the blocks and keep the bar tight to your body throughout.

name: Clean Pull
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and the barbell over the middle of your feet, close to your shins.
Grip the bar just outside your legs with a pronated or hook grip, arms straight and elbows rotated out to the sides.
Set your hips with a flat back, chest up, head forward, weight on your heels, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through your heels and extending the knees, keeping the back angle constant and arms straight as the bar moves under control to just above the knees.
Initiate the second pull at mid-thigh by violently extending your hips, knees, and ankles in a jumping motion, accelerating the bar upward as fast as possible while keeping it close to the body.

Finish in full extension on the balls of your feet, traps shrugged hard, torso leaning slightly back, and arms still straight; let the bar rise from leg and hip drive rather than pulling with the arms.
Make the extension violent and abrupt, then immediately stop and lower the bar under control back toward the floor.
Reset your position and breathing before each rep; do not prolong the extension or bend the arms early, as the goal is to train explosive triple extension.

name: Clean Shrug
instructions: Stand tall holding a barbell at mid-thigh with a shoulder-width, double-overhand or hook grip, arms hanging straight.
Set your feet hip-width apart, brace your core, keep your back straight and inclined slightly forward, and let your shoulders hang relaxed. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms completely straight, shrug your shoulders up and slightly back toward your ears, contracting the traps powerfully.
Hold the top contraction briefly and squeeze the traps hard without bending the elbows.
Lower your shoulders back down under control to the starting hang position.
Although you can use heavier weight than a full clean, do not overload to the point that the movement slows down or the elbows bend; the shrug must stay crisp and explosive.
Exhale as you shrug up and inhale as you lower, keeping your spine neutral throughout.

name: Clock Push-Up
instructions: Set up in a prone push-up position supporting your weight on your hands and toes, with hands about shoulder width and arms fully extended.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. This is your starting position.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows under control until your chest is just above the ground.
Reverse explosively by pushing through your palms as fast as possible until your hands leave the floor and you become airborne.
While airborne, shift your body about 30 degrees around an imaginary clock face by moving your outside foot away from your direction of travel, jumping roughly 12 to 18 inches to the side.
Land softly with bent elbows, immediately absorbing into the next push-up in the new position.
Continue pressing and rotating step by step all the way around the clock until you arrive back at your starting position.
Keep your body rigid and core braced on every rep so the hips do not sag, and land with soft elbows to protect the joints.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your eyes under the bar, feet planted firmly on the floor, and a slight natural arch in your lower back.
Grip the bar with both hands set about shoulder width apart, palms facing forward, wrists stacked over your forearms.
Retract your shoulder blades, plant them into the bench, and unrack the bar, holding it locked out straight over your chest. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your torso rather than flared out to maximize triceps involvement.
Lightly touch your middle-to-lower chest and pause for a moment without bouncing the bar.
Exhale and press the bar back up by extending your elbows, driving through the triceps, until your arms are locked out over your chest.
Hold the locked-out position briefly, then begin the next descent, taking about twice as long to lower as to press.
Keep your wrists straight and elbows tucked throughout; do not let the elbows flare or the grip narrow so much that your wrists strain.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then carefully rack the bar back onto the supports.

name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set a single dumbbell standing on its end at the top of a flat bench, making sure it is stable.
Lie back on the bench with your shoulders supported, feet planted firmly on the floor for a stable base.
Grasp the dumbbell with both hands, palms pressing flat against the underside of the top plate, fingers wrapped around the handle and heads.
Press the dumbbell up to arm's length straight over your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in close to your body. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell straight down to the center of your chest under control, keeping your elbows tucked tight to your sides.
Lightly touch your chest with the dumbbell and pause briefly.
Exhale and press the dumbbell back up by extending your elbows, driving through the triceps until your arms are locked out.
Keep your wrists firm and the elbows close throughout to keep tension on the triceps; do not let the elbows flare wide.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then carefully set the dumbbell down.

name: Close-Grip EZ Bar Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ curl bar at the inner narrow handles with a supinated grip, palms facing forward and slightly tilted inward to match the bar's angle.
Pin your elbows close to your sides, brace your core, keep your chest up and shoulders back, and let the bar hang at arm's length. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary against your torso, exhale and curl the bar up by flexing only at the elbows.
Continue curling until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar reaches shoulder level.
Hold the top contraction for a second and squeeze the biceps hard.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly back to the starting position under control until your arms are fully extended.
Avoid swinging the torso or letting the elbows drift forward; only the forearms should move so the biceps do the work.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl with Band
instructions: Loop a resistance band over each end of the EZ curl bar, then step one foot onto the middle of the band to anchor it to the floor.
Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, gripping the EZ bar at the inner narrow handles with a supinated grip, palms facing forward.
Pin your elbows close to your torso, brace your core, lift your chest, and hold the bar at arm's length with the band slightly tensioned. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms fixed against your sides, exhale and curl the bar up by flexing only at the elbows; expect the resistance to increase as the band stretches.
Continue until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Hold the top contraction for a second and squeeze the biceps hard against the band's peak tension.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control back to the starting position, resisting the band's pull as your arms extend fully.
Keep your torso still and elbows pinned so only the forearms move; control the eccentric so the band does not snap your arms down.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with an EZ bar loaded appropriately, feet planted firmly on the floor and a slight natural arch in your lower back.
Grip the bar at the inner narrow angled handles with a pronated grip, hands close together.
Unrack or lift the bar and hold it straight over your torso with your arms perpendicular to the floor and elbows tucked in. This is your starting position.
Breathe in and lower the bar under control toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides throughout.
Lightly touch your lower chest and pause briefly without bouncing.
Exhale and press the bar back up by extending your elbows, driving through the triceps until your arms are locked out over your torso.
Keep your wrists straight and the elbows tight to your body to maximize triceps tension; the angled handles should keep your wrists comfortable.
