Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then carefully rack or set the bar down.

name: Close-Grip Front Lat Pulldown
instructions: Attach a straight bar or a close-grip V-handle to the top pulley of the lat pulldown machine, then adjust the thigh pad so it sits snugly against the tops of your thighs to anchor you against the resistance.
Stand and grip the bar with both palms facing forward (overhand) and your hands spaced closer than shoulder width, roughly 8 to 12 inches apart, or grip the V-handle with palms facing each other.
Sit down with the bar in hand, slide your thighs under the pad, and plant both feet flat on the floor about hip width apart for a stable base.
Set your posture: chest up and proud, shoulders pulled back, a slight natural arch in your lower back, and brace your core. Lean your torso back about 20 to 30 degrees from vertical.
Begin with arms fully extended overhead so you feel a stretch through your lats; this is your starting position.
Initiate the pull by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades first, then drive your elbows down and slightly back, leading with the elbows rather than yanking with the hands.
Exhale as you pull the bar down to the top of your chest, keeping your torso stationary so only the arms move.
Squeeze your lats hard at the bottom for a one-second count, feeling the contraction across your back, not your biceps.
Inhale and slowly raise the bar back up under control, resisting the weight until your arms are fully extended and your lats are fully stretched.
Avoid leaning back excessively or using momentum to swing the weight down; keep the movement smooth and lat-driven, and do not let the forearms do the pulling.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up off of a Dumbbell
instructions: Stand a single dumbbell upright on the floor on one of its weighted ends so it forms a stable vertical post.
Kneel down and grip the top head of the dumbbell with both hands stacked or wrapped around it, hands directly under your chest and close together to emphasize the triceps.
Walk your feet back and support your weight on your hands and toes, forming a straight line from your heels through your hips to the crown of your head.
Tuck your elbows in tight against your sides rather than flaring them out, and brace your core and glutes so your torso stays rigid like a plank. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them tracking close to your ribs, until your chest is just above the top of the dumbbell.
Keep your hips level throughout; do not let them sag toward the floor or pike up toward the ceiling.
Exhale and press forcefully back up by extending your elbows until your arms are straight, focusing on driving through the heels of your hands.
Squeeze your triceps hard at the top, pause briefly, and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.
If balancing on a single dumbbell feels unstable, reduce the depth or use a heavier, wider-based dumbbell for a more secure post.

name: Close-Grip Standing Barbell Curl
instructions: Load a straight barbell and stand holding it with an underhand (supinated) grip, palms facing up, hands only a few inches apart and well inside shoulder width.
Stand tall with feet about shoulder width apart, knees slightly soft, torso upright, head up, and shoulders back.
Pin your upper arms and elbows against the sides of your torso; they stay fixed in this position for the entire movement. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and let the bar hang at arm's length against your thighs with a slight bend kept in the elbows to keep tension on the biceps.
Exhale and curl the bar upward in a smooth arc by flexing only at the elbows, keeping your upper arms motionless.
Continue until your forearms nearly touch your biceps and the bar reaches the top, then squeeze the biceps hard for a one-second count.
Because the close grip emphasizes the outer head of the biceps, focus on keeping your wrists neutral and elbows tucked rather than letting them drift outward.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control along the same path back to the starting position with arms fully extended.
Do not swing your torso, lean back, or use your hips to heave the weight; only the forearms should move.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Cobra Stretch
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your legs extended straight behind you and the tops of your feet flat against the floor.
Place your hands flat on the floor directly underneath your shoulders, fingers pointing forward and elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Press the tops of your feet, thighs, and pelvis firmly into the floor; your hips stay anchored down throughout the stretch.
Inhale and gently press through your hands to lift your chest and head off the floor, straightening your arms as far as is comfortable.
Draw your shoulders down and back away from your ears, opening the chest, and keep a long neck with your gaze slightly upward.
Stop raising when you feel a mild, comfortable stretch across your abdominals and front of the hips; do not force the back into a painful arch.
Hold the position with relaxed shoulders and steady breathing for the prescribed time, then lower back down slowly.

name: Cocoons
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs fully extended and together and your arms stretched straight out on the floor behind your head.
Press your lower back gently toward the floor and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Simultaneously tuck your knees in toward your chest while curling your arms up and over from behind your head.
As your knees come in, rotate your pelvis to lift your glutes and lower back off the floor, crunching your upper and lower body together at the same time.
Exhale during the contraction and aim to bring your hands and knees together near the center of your body, fully shortening the abs.
Squeeze your abdominals hard and pause briefly in the tucked position.
Inhale and slowly reverse the motion under control, extending your legs and arms back out to the fully stretched starting position without letting your heels or hands slam the floor.
Keep the movement controlled rather than using momentum, and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Commando Pull-Up
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and position yourself so the bar runs front-to-back relative to your body rather than side-to-side.
Grip the bar with both hands together using a neutral parallel grip, one hand in front of the other, palms facing each other and knuckles roughly touching.
Hang at full arm extension with your core braced, legs together or knees slightly bent and crossed for stability.
Engage your lats and pull yourself up, leading your head to one side of the bar so that side's shoulder rises toward the bar.
Exhale as you pull and aim to bring the bar level with the side of your jaw or shoulder, squeezing your lat and biceps at the top.
Inhale and lower yourself slowly and under control back to the dead hang.
On the next repetition, pull up to the opposite side of the bar, alternating sides each rep.
Keep your body from swinging excessively by tightening the core and glutes; control the descent rather than dropping.
Continue alternating until you complete the prescribed number of repetitions per side.

name: Conan's Wheel
instructions: Set up the Conan's wheel implement loaded to the prescribed weight, with the long bar pivoting around a central post.
Step up to the end of the bar and take a Zercher hold by placing the bar in the crooks of both elbows, then clasp your hands or grip one wrist to lock the bar in place.
Keep the weight resting in the crooks of your elbows and off your forearms, hugging the load tight against your torso.
Brace hard: chest up, shoulders back, core tensed, and lower back in a strong neutral position before you lift.
Stand the weight up from the ground by driving through your legs and hips, maintaining the tall, upright posture.
Do not hold your breath; breathe in short controlled bursts to keep intra-abdominal pressure while moving.
Begin walking the implement in a circle around the central post, taking short, fast steps and looking up and away in the direction of travel.
Fight to keep your torso upright and the chest high; do not let the weight pull you into a forward slump.
Continue circling for one or more complete turns or until you can no longer maintain posture, then carefully lower the weight to the ground.

name: Concentration Curls
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and your knees bent, thighs spread comfortably apart, holding one dumbbell between your legs.
Pick up the dumbbell with your working arm and rest the back of that upper arm against the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
Rotate your palm so it faces forward and away from your thigh, letting the arm hang extended with the dumbbell above the floor. This is your starting position.
Lean your torso slightly forward and keep your upper arm braced motionless against your thigh throughout the movement.
Exhale and curl the dumbbell up by flexing only at the elbow, contracting the biceps and keeping the upper arm pinned in place.
Continue until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level; at the top, turn the wrist so the little finger is slightly higher than the thumb to maximize the squeeze.
Hold the peak contraction for a one-second count, squeezing the biceps hard.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell under control back to the fully extended starting position; avoid any swinging or using your shoulder to assist.
Complete all reps with one arm, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat for the same number of repetitions.

name: Cossack Squat
instructions: Stand with a wide stance, feet noticeably wider than shoulder width and toes turned out slightly.
Keep your chest up, core braced, and arms held out in front or clasped at your chest for balance. This is your starting position.
Shift your weight onto one leg and bend that knee, sinking your hips down and back toward that side while the opposite leg stays straight.
Allow the foot of the straight leg to rotate so the toes point up and the heel stays down, keeping that leg fully extended.
Descend on the bent leg until your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor or as low as your mobility allows, keeping the heel of the working leg flat and the knee tracking over the toes.
Keep your torso as upright as possible and avoid letting the bent knee cave inward.
Drive through the heel of the bent leg to push back up to the wide standing center position.
Repeat the descent to the opposite side, continuing to alternate, and perform the prescribed number of repetitions per side.

name: Couch Stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor near a wall or the base of a couch with a mat or pad under your knees for comfort.
Place one shin vertically against the wall or couch so the top of that foot points up and the knee sits in the corner where the wall meets the floor.
Step the opposite foot forward and plant it flat on the floor so that knee is bent roughly 90 degrees in a half-kneeling lunge position.
Brace your core and tuck your pelvis under (posterior tilt) to flatten the lower back rather than arching it.
Squeeze the glute of the rear leg and gently drive your hips forward and down to increase the stretch through the front of the hip and quadriceps of the rear leg.
Keep your torso tall and upright; for a deeper stretch, raise the chest fully vertical against the wall.
Hold the position with steady breathing for the prescribed time, easing off if you feel any pinching in the knee or sharp pain.
Carefully come out of the stretch and switch to the other side.

name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides and palms facing inward toward your body in a neutral (hammer) grip.
Set your feet about shoulder width apart, brace your core, keep your chest up, and pin your elbows close to your sides.
Keeping your palm facing inward and without rotating your wrist, curl the right dumbbell up and across the front of your body toward your left shoulder.
Exhale as you curl and keep your upper arm and elbow as stationary as possible so only the forearm travels.
Bring the top of the dumbbell up to or near your opposite shoulder and squeeze the biceps and forearm for a one-second hold.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back down along the same diagonal path to the starting position.
Repeat the same cross-body motion with the left arm, curling toward the right shoulder.
Avoid swinging your torso or using momentum; keep the movement strict and controlled.
Continue alternating arms until the recommended number of repetitions is completed for each side.

name: Cross Over - With Bands
instructions: Anchor an exercise band securely around a stationary post or rack at roughly chest or shoulder height.
Face away from the post and grasp a handle in each hand, then step forward until there is tension on the band and your arms are pulled slightly back.
Stagger your feet for balance, one foot slightly ahead of the other, and brace your core with a slight forward lean of the torso.

Raise both arms out to your sides so they are roughly parallel to the floor and in line with your shoulders, forming a T, with palms facing forward and a slight bend held in the elbows. This is your starting position.
Keeping that slight elbow bend fixed, bring both hands forward and together in a wide semicircular arc across the front of your chest.
Exhale as you sweep your arms in and squeeze your chest hard when your hands meet or cross in front of you.
Hold the peak contraction for a one-second count, focusing on the pecs doing the work rather than the shoulders.
Inhale and slowly return your arms along the same arc back to the starting T position, controlling the band's tension.
Keep your elbows from collapsing or straightening fully, and perform the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Cross-Body Crunch
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent about 60 degrees and your feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands loosely behind your head with fingertips lightly supporting it, elbows out to the sides; do not pull on your neck. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and exhale as you simultaneously curl your right shoulder and elbow up and across your body while drawing your left knee in toward your left shoulder.
Aim to bring your right elbow toward your left knee, leading with the shoulder and twisting through the trunk rather than just flicking the elbow.
Focus on contracting the obliques and abs to create the rotation; lift the shoulder blade off the floor rather than just nodding the head.
Pause and squeeze at the top of the crunch.
Inhale and slowly lower back down to the starting position under control.
Repeat to the opposite side, bringing the left elbow toward the right knee.
Continue alternating sides smoothly until all prescribed repetitions are completed.

name: Crossover Reverse Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width apart, chest up, core braced, and arms relaxed or hands at your hips. This is your starting position.
Step one foot back and across behind your front leg in a curtsy-style path, landing on the ball of that rear foot.
As you step back, bend both knees and flex at the hips to lower into the lunge, keeping most of your weight on the front leg.
Simultaneously rotate your torso across the front leg, twisting toward the front-leg side to engage the trunk and lower back.
Descend until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor while keeping your front knee tracking over your foot and your spine long.
Keep your front heel planted and your torso from collapsing forward beyond the controlled rotation.
Pause briefly, then push through the front heel and untwist your torso to return to the upright starting position.
Repeat by stepping back and across with the opposite leg, continuing in an alternating fashion for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Crow Pose
instructions: Begin in a deep squat with your feet close together and your heels lifted, balancing on the balls of your feet.
Place both hands flat on the floor in front of you, shoulder-width apart, fingers spread wide and gripping the floor for stability.
Bend your elbows slightly to create a shelf, and lean your torso forward to bring your knees up onto the backs of your upper arms, near the armpits.
Set your knees high on the triceps and squeeze them inward against your arms to lock your body together.
Shift your weight forward onto your hands and engage your core hard, rounding your upper back slightly and gazing at the floor a short distance ahead.
Gradually lift one foot and then the other off the floor, drawing your heels up toward your glutes as your weight settles fully onto your hands.
Balance by pressing firmly through the fingertips and palms, keeping the core and shoulders active to stay stable.
Hold the balance for the prescribed time, then lower your feet back to the floor under control.
If you are new to the pose, place a cushion in front of you to ease the fear of tipping forward.

name: Crucifix
instructions: Select your implements, ideally the contest tools such as hammers or axes since their long levers feel very different from dumbbells, and set them on the floor at your sides.
Stand upright between the implements with your feet about shoulder width apart and brace your core and upper back.
Grip one implement in each hand and stand them up, keeping your shoulders packed down and back.
Raise both arms straight out to your sides until they are parallel to the floor, palms generally facing down, forming a crucifix or T position with your body.
Lock your arms in place with only a slight bend at the elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades and delts to support the static hold.
Keep your torso tall and rigid and resist the weights pulling your arms below parallel, as dropping below parallel ends the hold in competition.
Breathe steadily throughout rather than holding your breath, keeping tension through the shoulders and core.
Maintain the parallel hold for as long as possible; the weight should be heavy enough to bring you to failure in roughly 30 to 60 seconds.
When you can no longer hold parallel, lower the implements under control to the floor.

name: Crunch - Hands Overhead
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, set so there is roughly a 60-degree angle between your hamstrings and calves; keep your feet about hip width apart.
Press your lower back gently into the floor to engage your core and remove any excess arch in your lumbar spine.
Extend both arms straight overhead in line with your ears, palms crossed over one another so the arms form a single line with your head, neck, and shoulders. This is your starting position.
Brace your abs and curl your upper body forward by flexing the spine, lifting your shoulder blades just clear of the floor while keeping your arms locked in line with your head the entire time.
Exhale steadily as you curl up and hold the top contraction for one second, squeezing the abs hard; the overhead arm position increases the resistance, so do not let the arms swing forward to cheat.
Keep the movement small and controlled, lifting the shoulder blades only a few inches; do not yank with the neck or use momentum to throw yourself up.
Inhale as you slowly lower your shoulder blades back to the floor under control, returning to the starting position with arms still overhead.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, keeping the lower back pressed down throughout.

name: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor and rest your lower legs on top of an exercise ball so your hips and knees are each bent to about 90 degrees, with your calves and heels resting on the ball.
Position your feet three to four inches apart and point your toes inward so they lightly touch, which helps keep the legs stable on the ball.
Place your hands lightly on either side of your head with your elbows pointing out to the sides; do not lace your fingers behind your head or pull on your neck.
Press the small of your back down into the floor to flatten the lumbar spine and isolate the abdominals. This is your starting position.
Brace your abs and slowly roll your shoulders up off the floor while continuing to push your lower back down hard into the mat.
Lift the shoulders only about four inches; your lower back must stay in contact with the floor throughout, with the movement coming from spinal flexion, not hip flexion.
Exhale as you crunch up, squeeze the abdominals hard at the top, and hold the contraction for one second; keep the ball as still as possible so you are not using the legs.
Inhale and lower your shoulders back down slowly and under control to the starting position; avoid using momentum or bouncing.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Crunches
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your feet flat on the floor and knees bent to about 90 degrees; alternatively rest your lower legs on a bench, feet three to four inches apart with toes pointed inward and touching.
Place your hands lightly on either side of your head with your elbows in line with your ears or angled slightly out; do not interlock your fingers behind your head or pull on your neck.
Press the small of your back firmly into the floor to flatten your lumbar spine and better isolate the abdominals. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and begin to roll your shoulders up off the floor by flexing your spine, keeping your chin a fist-width off your chest and your gaze toward the ceiling.
Continue pushing your lower back down into the floor as you contract the abs; lift the shoulders only about four inches while the lower back stays on the floor.
Exhale as you curl up and squeeze the abdominals hard at the top, holding the contraction for one second; move slowly and avoid using momentum to swing yourself up.
Inhale and lower your shoulders back down slowly and under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Cuban Press
instructions: Stand tall with your feet shoulder width apart, knees soft, and core braced; hold a light dumbbell in each hand with a pronated (palms-down) grip.

Raise your upper arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor with your elbows bent to 90 degrees, letting your forearms and the dumbbells hang straight down in front of you in the 'scarecrow' position. This is your starting position.

Keeping your upper arms fixed at shoulder height and elbows bent, externally rotate at the shoulders to sweep the dumbbells upward through about 180 degrees until your forearms are vertical and your wrists are directly above your elbows.
Keep the upper arms parallel to the floor throughout this rotation; do not let the elbows drop or the wrists drift forward, as the goal is to work the external rotators of the shoulder.
From the top of the rotation, press the dumbbells overhead by extending your elbows until your arms are straight, keeping a stable, braced torso without leaning back.
Exhale as you press up; pause briefly with the weights overhead and your shoulders packed down.
Reverse the sequence exactly: lower the dumbbells back to the wrists-above-elbows position, then rotate them back down to the scarecrow start, inhaling as you do.
Use light weight and a slow, controlled tempo since the rotator cuff is doing the work, and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Curtsy Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart, chest up, shoulders back, and core braced; place your hands on your hips or clasp them in front of your chest for balance.
Shift your weight onto your front (standing) leg and step your other foot diagonally back and across behind it, like a curtsy, planting the ball of that rear foot on the floor.
Keep your hips and shoulders square to the front; the rear foot crosses behind, but your torso should not twist toward the side.
Bend both knees to lower straight down until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and your rear knee hovers just above the ground.
Keep your front knee tracking over your toes and your weight in the heel and midfoot of the front leg; do not let the front knee cave inward.
Keep your chest lifted and torso upright throughout; inhale as you descend under control.
Drive through the heel of your front leg to push back up to standing, bringing the rear foot back beside the other, and exhale as you rise.
Squeeze the glute of the front leg at the top, then alternate sides and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions per leg.

name: Dancer's Stretch
instructions: Sit upright on the floor with your left leg extended straight out in front of you, foot relaxed, and sit tall through your spine.
Bend your right knee and cross your right leg over the left, placing your right foot flat on the floor on the outside of your left thigh.
Place your left elbow or forearm against the outside of your bent right knee, and rest your right hand on the floor behind you for support.
Sit up tall, lengthen your spine, and gently rotate your upper body to the right, using your left arm to press lightly against the right knee to deepen the twist.
Turn your head to look over your right shoulder and feel a mild stretch through your lower back, glutes, and the outside of your hip; keep the stretch comfortable and never forced.
Breathe slowly and hold the position for 10 to 20 seconds, keeping both sit bones grounded on the floor.
Release the twist gently, switch leg positions, and repeat on the opposite side.

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with both arms extended straight up toward the ceiling, directly over your shoulders.
Lift your feet, knees, and hips so that your hips and knees are each bent to 90 degrees, with your shins parallel to the floor (tabletop position).
Exhale hard to draw your ribcage down toward your pelvis, flatten your lower back into the floor, tilt your pelvis slightly up, and squeeze your glutes; maintain this braced position the entire set.
This is your starting position; there should be no gap between your lower back and the floor.
Slowly extend one leg out, straightening the knee and hip until that foot hovers just above the ground, while keeping the opposite leg in tabletop and both arms reaching up.
For added difficulty, lower the opposite arm overhead toward the floor at the same time as the opposite leg extends, moving slowly and with control.
The key challenge is keeping your lower back pressed flat and your pelvis still; if your back arches or your ribs flare, reduce the range of motion.
Exhale as you extend and inhale as you return; bring the working limb back to the starting position under full control.
Repeat on the opposite side, alternating slowly until the set is complete.

name: Dead Hang
instructions: Set up under a sturdy pull-up bar; use a box or step if needed so you can reach the bar without jumping.
Grip the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, hands roughly shoulder width apart, and wrap your thumbs around the bar for a secure hold.
Step off the box and let your body hang with your arms fully straight and your feet clear of the floor.
Keep a firm, controlled grip and engage your shoulders slightly by drawing your shoulder blades down and back so you are not hanging completely loose at the joints.
Let your legs hang relaxed and keep your body still, avoiding any swinging or kicking.
Breathe steadily and hold the position for the prescribed time, focusing on grip and forearm endurance.
When your grip begins to fail or time is up, lower your feet back to the box rather than dropping abruptly to protect your shoulders and wrists.

name: Deadlift with Bands
instructions: Set up the resistance: for short bands, loop them over each end of the bar and step your feet through them so they are anchored under your feet; for long bands, anchor the bottoms to a secure base such as heavy dumbbells or the base of a rack, then loop them over the bar sleeves.
Center the bar over your midfoot with your feet about hip width apart and toes turned slightly out; the bar should be roughly over your shoelaces, almost touching your shins.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the bar just outside your legs at about shoulder width, using a double-overhand or mixed grip.
Set your back: take a big breath into your belly, brace your core, lower your hips, push your chest up, and pull the slack out of the bar so your lats are tight and your back is flat (not rounded).
Look forward or slightly down to keep a neutral neck, and ensure your shoulders are stacked just in front of the bar with shins touching it.
Begin the lift by driving through your heels and pushing the floor away, keeping the bar dragging close to your shins as it rises; the band tension increases as you stand, so accelerate through it.
Once the bar passes your knees, aggressively pull it back, drive your hips forward into the bar, and squeeze your glutes to finish standing fully upright with shoulder blades pulled together.
Do not hyperextend or lean back at the top, and keep the bar close to your body the whole way up.
Lower the bar under control by first pushing your hips back, then bending the knees once the bar passes them, guiding it down the same path to the floor.
Reset your breath and brace before each rep, and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Deadlift with Chains
instructions: Attach the chains either to the sleeves of the bar or drape the middle of each chain over the bar so that more chain links lift off the floor and add weight as you stand taller.
Approach the bar and center it over your midfoot with your feet about hip width apart and toes slightly out; the bar should sit roughly over your shoelaces near your shins.

Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grip the bar at about shoulder width just outside your legs, allowing your shoulder blades to protract; use a double-overhand grip, switching to an over/under (mixed) grip on heavier sets.
Take a big breath into your belly and brace your core hard, then lower your hips and bend your knees until your shins lightly contact the bar.
Look forward, lift your chest, and set a flat (slightly arched) back with your lats tight and the slack pulled out of the bar.

Drive through your heels to push the floor away and move the weight upward, keeping the bar gliding close along your shins; expect the load to feel heavier near the top as more chain lifts off the floor.
After the bar passes your knees, aggressively pull it back and drive your hips forward into the bar, squeezing your glutes and pulling your shoulder blades together to lock out tall.
Avoid rounding your lower back at any point and do not lean back excessively at the top.
Lower the bar by hinging at the hips first and then bending the knees once it clears them, guiding it back to the floor along the same path.
Re-brace before each repetition and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the decline bench and hook your feet or ankles securely under the leg roller pads, then lie back so your head is toward the lower end and the bar is positioned above your lower chest.
Grip the bar with a medium-width pronated grip, set so that at the midpoint of the press your forearms are vertical and form a 90-degree angle with your upper arms.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back into the bench, keep your chest up, and brace your core; ideally have a spotter help you unrack the bar to protect your shoulders.
Lift the bar off the rack and hold it straight over your lower chest with your arms fully locked and perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control until it lightly touches your lower chest, keeping your elbows at a moderate angle to your torso rather than flared straight out.
Pause for a brief moment at the chest without bouncing the bar.
Exhale and press the bar back up using your chest muscles until your arms are locked out over your lower chest, squeezing the chest at the top.
Use a controlled tempo, taking at least twice as long to lower the bar as to press it; keep the bar path slightly toward your lower chest, not your face.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, then carefully rack the bar with the help of your spotter.

name: Decline Close-Grip Bench To Skull Crusher
instructions: Set the decline bench and secure your legs under the leg roller pads, then lie back with your head toward the low end of the bench.
Grip the bar with a close grip, hands slightly less than shoulder width apart, with a pronated (palms-toward-feet) grip.

Unrack the bar (ideally with a spotter's help) and hold it straight over you with your arms locked and your elbows tucked in close to your torso; arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
For the close-grip press portion, inhale and lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked in close to your sides throughout to emphasize the triceps.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position by extending your elbows and driving through the triceps.

For the skull crusher portion, keep your upper arms stationary and pointing straight up; inhale and bend only at the elbows, lowering the bar in a semicircular arc back toward your forehead until it nearly touches.
Keep your elbows from flaring out as you lower toward the forehead, and control the descent so the bar does not actually hit your head.
Exhale and contract the triceps to lift the bar back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
That completes one full cycle (one close-grip press plus one skull crusher); repeat the sequence for the prescribed number of repetitions, then rack the bar with help.

name: Decline Crunch
instructions: Set a decline bench and hook your feet and lower legs securely under the leg roller pads, then lie back so your head is at the lower end.
Place your hands lightly on either side of your head with your elbows pointing in; do not lace your fingers behind your head or pull on your neck.
Press the small of your back down into the bench to flatten your lumbar spine and isolate the abdominals. This is your starting position.
Brace your abs and begin to roll your shoulders up off the bench by flexing your spine, keeping the movement coming from the abs rather than the hip flexors.
Continue pressing your lower back into the bench as you contract; lift your shoulders only about four inches while your lower back stays on the bench.
Exhale as you crunch up and squeeze the abdominals hard at the top, holding the contraction for one second; move slowly and avoid swinging up with momentum.
Inhale and lower your shoulders back down slowly and under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions; because the decline increases the load on the abs, keep every rep controlled.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the decline bench and secure your legs under the leg roller pads; sit at the high end holding a dumbbell on top of each thigh with your palms facing each other, then carefully lie back.
As you lower onto the bench, use your thighs to help guide the dumbbells up so they end at shoulder level on each side.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face away from you (toward your feet) and the dumbbells are held over your lower chest with arms extended and forearms vertical. This is your starting position.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back into the bench, keep your chest up, and brace your core.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly out to the sides of your lower chest under full control, keeping your forearms perpendicular to the floor and feeling a stretch across the chest.
Do not let the dumbbells drift or your elbows flare straight out; keep them at a moderate angle to your torso.
Exhale and press the dumbbells up using your pectoral muscles until your arms are locked out over your lower chest, and squeeze the chest at the top.
Hold the contracted position for a second, then begin lowering again; take at least twice as long to lower as to press.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, then sit up carefully or set the dumbbells down on your thighs to finish safely.

name: Decline Dumbbell Flyes
instructions: Set the decline bench and secure your legs under the leg roller pads; sit at the high end with a dumbbell on each thigh, palms facing each other, then carefully lie back.
As you lie back, bring the dumbbells up so they are held above your lower chest with your arms extended, palms facing each other, and arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, keep your chest up, and maintain a slight, fixed bend in your elbows to protect the biceps tendon; this elbow bend stays constant throughout.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms out to both sides in a wide arc, opening at the shoulders until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest.
Keep the movement only at the shoulder joint; the arms stay stationary in their bent shape, like hugging a large barrel, and do not turn this into a press.
Lower only to the point of a strong but pain-free stretch; do not overstretch the shoulders at the bottom.
Exhale and bring your arms back up along the same wide arc, squeezing your chest muscles together as the dumbbells rise.
Hold and squeeze the contracted position at the top for one second, then repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Decline Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Set the decline bench and secure your legs under the leg roller pads; sit at the high end with a dumbbell on each thigh, palms facing each other, then carefully lie back.
Bring the dumbbells up so they are held above your shoulders with your arms extended, palms facing each other, and arms perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms stationary and your elbows tucked in and pointing toward the ceiling throughout; only your forearms should move.
Inhale and slowly bend at the elbows, lowering the dumbbells in a semicircular arc toward your head until your thumbs are next to your ears.
Keep your elbows from flaring out to the sides as you lower; the upper arms must stay fixed to isolate the triceps.
Control the descent so the dumbbells do not strike your head, and feel the stretch in your triceps at the bottom.
Exhale and contract your triceps to lift the dumbbells back up to the starting position by straightening your forearms.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, keeping the tempo slow and controlled throughout.

name: Decline EZ Bar Triceps Extension
instructions: Set a decline bench to roughly a 15-30 degree decline and load an EZ-curl bar on the rack at the head end (or have a spotter hand it to you). Hook your feet or ankles securely under the leg pads so your body stays anchored on the bench.

Lie back on the bench with your head at the low end. Take a close pronated grip on the inner angled portions of the EZ bar, hands slightly less than shoulder width apart, so your wrists sit in a comfortable, neutral-ish angle.

Press the bar up (or take it from your spotter) and hold it locked out with arms perpendicular to the floor, directly over your shoulders. Tuck your elbows in toward each other rather than letting them flare. Brace your core and keep your lower back flat against the bench. This is your starting position.
Inhale, and keeping your upper arms fixed and pointing straight up, hinge only at the elbows to lower the bar in a smooth arc toward your forehead or just behind the top of your head.
Lower under control until you feel a stretch in the triceps and the bar is near your forehead. Keep your wrists straight and do not let your elbows drift wide or forward.
Exhale and extend your elbows to drive the bar back up along the same arc to the locked-out start, squeezing the triceps hard at the top without bouncing.
Use a controlled tempo of about two seconds down and one to two seconds up; never let the bar crash toward your head.
Keep your elbows pointed at the ceiling throughout. Letting the upper arms swing back and forth turns this into a pressing motion and removes tension from the triceps.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then re-rack the bar or hand it to your spotter before sitting up.

name: Decline Oblique Crunch
instructions: Set a decline bench and secure both feet and ankles under the padded rollers at the high end so your lower body is firmly anchored.
Lie back on the bench with your knees bent over the rollers and your torso resting down the decline.
Curl your upper body up off the bench until your torso sits at roughly a 35-45 degree angle from the floor, holding this slight crunch with your abs engaged.
Place the hand of the working side lightly beside your head (do not pull on your neck) and rest the other hand on the opposite thigh. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly crunch up while rotating your torso, bringing one elbow across toward the opposite knee. Drive the movement by twisting through the obliques, not by yanking the head.
Continue rotating until your elbow approaches or touches the opposite knee, then pause and squeeze the obliques hard for one second at the top.
Inhale and lower your torso back down slowly and under control to the starting angle, keeping continuous tension in the abdominals rather than relaxing fully.
Keep the movement slow and deliberate; momentum and swinging defeat the purpose and strain the neck and lower back.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch your hand position and repeat for the other side, focusing on a full twist and a strong contraction each rep.

name: Decline Push-Up
instructions: Place a sturdy box, bench, or step behind you. Get on the floor face down and position your hands flat on the ground slightly wider than shoulder width, fingers pointing forward.
Set your feet up on top of the box or bench so your body is angled head-down. The higher the surface, the greater the emphasis on the upper chest and shoulders.

Straighten your arms to hold yourself at the top with a straight line from heels through hips to head. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag or pike. This is your starting position.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor under control, allowing your elbows to travel back at roughly a 45 degree angle from your torso rather than flaring straight out.
Lower until your chest is just above or lightly touching the floor, keeping your body rigid and straight throughout.
Exhale and press through your palms to push your body back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest at the top.
Use a controlled tempo, about two seconds down and one second up, and avoid letting your hips drop or your head crane forward.
Pause briefly at the top with arms extended (not fully locked and relaxed), then repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Decline Reverse Crunch
instructions: Set a decline bench at a moderate angle and lie back on it with your head at the high end and your hips toward the low end.
Reach overhead and grip the top edge or the foot rollers of the bench firmly with both hands to anchor your upper body and stop yourself sliding down.
Extend your legs out so they are roughly parallel to the floor with a slight bend in the knees, keeping your knees and feet together. Hold them up using your abs. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl your legs toward your torso by rolling your pelvis backward and lifting your hips off the bench, driving your knees up toward your chest.
Focus on the movement coming from your abs rolling the pelvis, not from swinging the legs with momentum or pulling with the hip flexors.
At the top your knees should be near your chest and your hips clearly lifted off the bench; hold and squeeze the lower abs for one second.
Inhale and lower your legs back down slowly and under control to the parallel starting position, resisting gravity rather than dropping.
Keep the motion slow and controlled throughout, and avoid arching your lower back as you extend the legs back out.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Decline Smith Press
instructions: Position a decline bench centered under the Smith machine bar, with the bench set to roughly a 15-30 degree decline and your head at the low end. Secure your feet under the leg pads.
Set the bar height so that when you lie down and reach up, the bar sits just above your chest with your arms nearly extended.
Lie back and take a pronated (overhand) grip slightly wider than shoulder width, so that at the bottom your forearms will be roughly vertical.

Rotate and unlock the bar from its hooks, then hold it straight over your lower chest with arms extended. Brace your core and keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down. This is your starting position.

Inhale and lower the bar under control by bending the elbows, tracking it down to lightly touch your lower chest. The fixed Smith path keeps the bar moving vertically, so let your elbows flex at roughly 45 degrees from the torso.
Pause briefly with the bar at your chest without bouncing it off the body.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position by extending the elbows, driving with the chest and squeezing at the top.
Keep a controlled tempo of about two seconds down and one to two seconds up, and keep your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout.
Repeat for the prescribed reps. When finished, rotate the bar to lock it back onto the hooks before sitting up.

name: Deep Squat Hold
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart or slightly wider, toes turned out slightly to around 10-30 degrees.
Keep your chest up and brace your core, then push your hips back and bend your knees to lower down into a deep squat below parallel.
Aim to keep your heels flat on the floor throughout; if your heels lift, widen your stance, turn your toes out more, or elevate the heels slightly on a small plate.
Settle into the bottom position so your hips sink toward your ankles while your spine stays long and your chest stays tall.
Bring your elbows to the inside of your knees and gently press the knees outward, opening up the hips and stretching the adductors and groin.
Relax into the position, breathing slowly and deeply, and let gravity gradually deepen the stretch over time.
Hold for the prescribed duration, keeping your weight balanced over your mid-foot and your lower back from rounding excessively.
To finish, drive through your heels and stand back up under control.

name: Deficit Deadlift
instructions: Stand on a stable platform or stack of weight plates 1-3 inches high so the bar starts lower relative to you than a standard deadlift, increasing the range of motion.
Position your feet about hip width apart with the loaded bar centered over your mid-foot, close to your shins.
Hinge at the hips and bend down to grip the bar just outside your legs at about shoulder width, using a double-overhand grip (or a mixed over/under grip for heavier sets).
Take a big breath and lower your hips while bending your knees until your shins lightly contact the bar. Because of the deficit you will sit lower than usual, so keep your hips down and back flat.

Set your back in a flat, slightly arched position, lift your chest, pull the slack out of the bar, and engage your lats by squeezing the bar toward your body. Look forward or slightly down. This is your starting position.
Drive through your heels and push the floor away, keeping the bar dragging close to your shins as it rises. Keep your hips and shoulders moving up together.
Once the bar passes your knees, aggressively drive your hips forward into the bar and pull your shoulder blades together to lock out tall, with hips and knees fully extended.
Keep your core braced and back neutral the entire ascent; the lower start position makes maintaining a flat back especially important, so do not let the lower back round.
Reverse the movement by pushing your hips back first, then bending the knees once the bar passes them, guiding the bar under control back down to the platform.
Reset your breath and position between reps and repeat for the prescribed number.

name: Depth Jump Leap
instructions: Set up two boxes: a lower one 12-16 inches high to start on, and a higher one 22-26 inches high placed about two to three feet in front of it, facing you.
Stand on top of the lower box with your feet together and positioned slightly off the front edge, arms relaxed at your sides.
Step off the front edge of the box (do not jump up first) and drop down toward the floor, preparing to land on the balls of both feet simultaneously.
Land softly with both feet at once, knees bent to absorb the impact, and immediately transition into the takeoff with minimal time spent on the ground.
Explosively reverse the landing by driving upward and outward as forcefully as possible, swinging your arms up and fully extending your hips, knees, and ankles.
Project your body forward and up to land on top of the higher box, again landing softly on both feet and letting your legs absorb the impact by bending the knees.
Keep ground contact time on the first landing as short as possible, since the goal is a fast, reactive jump rather than a slow, deep squat between phases.
Step down carefully, reset on the lower box, and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, resting fully between reps to keep each jump maximal.

name: Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Get on the floor in a push-up position and place your hands close together directly under your chest, touching your thumbs and index fingers to form a diamond or triangle shape.
Extend your legs straight back with feet together (or slightly apart for more stability) and straighten your arms to support your body at the top.
Set a straight line from your heels through your hips to your head, bracing your core and squeezing your glutes so your hips neither sag nor pike up. This is your starting position.
Keep your elbows tucked in close to your sides rather than flaring them out, which keeps the emphasis on the triceps.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest down toward your hands under control, letting your elbows track back along your ribcage.
Lower until your chest is just above or lightly grazes your hands, keeping your body rigid the whole way.
Exhale and press forcefully through your palms to push back up to the starting position, fully extending the arms and squeezing the triceps at the top.
Use a controlled tempo and keep your hips level throughout; sagging the hips or flaring the elbows reduces triceps work and stresses the lower back and shoulders.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Dip Machine
instructions: Select your desired weight on the dip machine's stack and sit securely in the seat, adjusting any seat or pad so you are stable and upright.
Grasp the handles firmly, one in each hand, and position yourself so your torso stays tall and supported against the back pad.
Set your starting position with your elbows bent to about a 90 degree angle and tucked in close at your sides to emphasize the triceps. This is your starting position.
Exhale and contract your triceps to press the handles downward, extending your arms toward your sides.
Stop just short of fully locking out your elbows, keeping a slight bend so tension stays on the triceps rather than transferring to the joints.
Squeeze your triceps hard at the bottom of the press for a brief moment.
Inhale and let the handles rise back up slowly and under control to the 90 degree starting position, resisting the weight rather than letting it pull your arms up.
Keep your elbows tucked and your torso still throughout; avoid leaning forward or using body momentum to move the weight.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Dips - Chest Version
instructions: Step up to a set of parallel dip bars and grip one bar firmly in each hand. The wider the bars, the more chest involvement, so choose a slightly wide set if available.
Press yourself up to support your body at arm's length above the bars with your arms locked out. This is your starting position.
Lean your torso forward roughly 30 degrees and bend your knees, crossing your ankles behind you, to keep this forward lean throughout the set, which shifts emphasis to the chest.
Inhale and lower yourself slowly, letting your elbows flare out slightly to the sides as your body descends.
Continue lowering until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest, with your upper arms roughly parallel to the floor; avoid going so deep that you overstress the shoulders.
Exhale and press back up by driving through your chest and extending your arms, keeping the forward torso lean the entire way.
Squeeze your chest hard at the top for a second without fully shrugging or losing the forward lean.
Keep the movement controlled and avoid bouncing out of the bottom; use a tempo of about two seconds down and one to two seconds up.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Dips - Triceps Version
instructions: Step up to a set of parallel dip bars, ideally about shoulder width apart, and grip one bar firmly in each hand.
Press up and support your body at arm's length above the bars with your arms nearly locked out. Bend your knees and cross your ankles behind you for stability. This is your starting position.
Keep your torso as upright and vertical as possible and your elbows tucked in close to your body, since this maximizes triceps involvement.
Inhale and lower yourself slowly and under control, hinging at the elbows while keeping them pointing straight back rather than flaring out.
Lower until your upper arms and forearms form roughly a 90 degree angle, keeping your body upright the entire descent.
Exhale and press your body back up by extending your elbows and contracting your triceps to return to the locked-out start.
Squeeze the triceps at the top without losing your upright posture or shrugging the shoulders up around your ears.
Keep the tempo controlled and avoid swinging or bouncing at the bottom, which stresses the shoulders.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Donkey Calf Raises
instructions: Position yourself in a donkey calf raise machine so the padded lever rests across your lower back and hips, with the tailbone and hip area making contact with the pad.
Place the balls of both feet on the calf block with your heels hanging off the edge, and grasp the front handles for support.

Bend forward at the hips so your torso is roughly parallel to the floor and the load sits over your hips. Straighten your knees without locking them out. Point your toes forward (or slightly in or out to bias different parts of the calf). This is your starting position.
Let your heels drop below the level of the block to feel a full stretch in the calves at the bottom.
Exhale and raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles and forcefully contracting your calves, pushing up onto your toes.
Keep your knees stationary and straight throughout; there should be no bending or bouncing at the knee to assist the movement.
Hold the fully contracted top position for one second, squeezing the calves hard.
Inhale and lower your heels slowly and under control back to the deep-stretch starting position.
Use a deliberate tempo with a full range of motion on every rep, and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Doorway Pec Stretch
instructions: Stand in an open doorway and raise one arm so your forearm rests flat against the door frame, with your elbow bent to about 90 degrees and positioned at roughly shoulder height.
Set your feet in a small split stance, with the foot on the stretching side slightly forward, for a stable base.
Keeping your forearm pressed against the frame, slowly step or lean forward through the doorway until you feel a gentle stretch across the front of your chest and shoulder.
Keep your chest up, shoulder blade pulled back, and avoid shrugging the shoulder toward your ear; the stretch should be felt across the pec, not in the front of the joint.
Hold the stretch at a comfortable intensity, breathing slowly and never forcing into pain.
Ease out of the stretch, then switch your arm to the other side of the door frame and repeat for the opposite chest.
You can adjust elbow height higher or lower on the frame to target different fibers of the pectoral muscle.

name: Double Kettlebell Alternating Hang Clean
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, which should be about hip to shoulder width apart.
Hinge at the hips, push your butt back, keep your back flat, and grasp one kettlebell in each hand with a neutral grip. Look straight ahead.

Clean both kettlebells up to the racked position at your shoulders by driving through your hips and legs and pulling the bells up close to your body, rotating your wrists so the bells settle on the backs of your forearms.
From the rack, dip one kettlebell down into a hang at hip level by hinging slightly, keeping it close to your body, while the other stays racked at the shoulder. This is your starting position.
In one fluid, coordinated motion, snap your hips to drive the hanging kettlebell up to the rack while simultaneously lowering the racked kettlebell down into the hang.
Drive the movement from the hips and legs rather than curling or muscling the bells up with the arms; keep the bells close to your torso throughout.
Keep your core braced, spine neutral, and torso upright as the bells alternate, catching each one softly into the rack rather than letting it crash onto the forearm.
Continue alternating the kettlebells up and down in a smooth, rhythmic fashion for the prescribed number of repetitions, then lower both bells safely to the floor by hinging at the hips.

name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip to shoulder width apart and place a kettlebell on the floor on the outside of each foot, or hold one in each hand by the handle.

Clean both kettlebells to your shoulders by hinging at the hips, then explosively extending through the legs and hips to pull the bells up to the rack position. Rotate your wrists so the palms face inward/forward and the bells rest on the backs of the forearms. This is your starting position.
Set your elbows down onto your ribs and hips for a solid shelf, keep your torso upright, brace your core, and keep your feet flat.
Dip by bending your knees a few inches while keeping your torso vertical, allowing the kettlebells to ride down with your body. This is the first dip that loads the legs.
Immediately and explosively reverse direction, driving through your heels and extending the legs hard, almost jumping, to launch the kettlebells upward off your shoulders.
As the bells rise, drop your body under them by bending the knees again (the second dip) and press your arms to a full overhead lockout, catching the weights with arms straight and elbows locked.
Land in a slight split stance, with one foot stepped forward and one back, to absorb the catch and stabilize the overhead weights.
With the kettlebells locked out overhead, recover by bringing your feet back together and standing fully upright under control.
Lower the kettlebells back to the rack at your shoulders to begin the next rep, and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
instructions: Stand two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, set roughly shoulder-width apart with toes turned slightly out and your weight over your mid-foot.

Clean both kettlebells to the rack position simultaneously: hinge at the hips, grip the handles, then drive through your legs and pull the bells up close to your body, allowing your hands to spear through the handles so each bell rests on the back of the forearm against the front of the shoulder.

In the rack position, keep your elbows tucked down and slightly in front of the ribs, wrists straight and stacked over the elbows, knuckles facing forward, and the bells hugging the chest and shoulders.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, keep a tall neutral spine, and look straight ahead; this is your starting position.
Take a breath and dip by bending the knees a few inches straight down, keeping your torso vertical and your heels flat, like loading a spring.
Reverse explosively by driving the floor away with your legs, extending the hips and knees to launch the kettlebells upward off the dip.
As the leg drive sends the bells up, punch both arms overhead and press them to full lockout, biceps near your ears and the bells settling over the back of your wrists.
Lock out with elbows straight, shoulders pushed up toward the ceiling, and the bells balanced directly over your shoulders, hips, and ankles; exhale at the top.
Lower both kettlebells under control back to the rack position, absorbing them by softening the knees slightly, then reset and repeat.
Keep the dip shallow and strictly vertical; a forward lean turns the press into a sloppy thruster and dumps the bells away from you.

name: Double Kettlebell Snatch
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the floor about a foot behind your heels, with your feet set slightly wider than shoulder-width and toes turned out a touch.
Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to reach back and grip both handles, keeping a flat neutral back, chest up, arms long, and shoulders packed down away from your ears.
Hike both kettlebells back sharply between your legs, loading the hips by sending them back so your forearms contact your inner thighs at the top of the backswing.
Reverse direction by snapping your hips forward explosively, extending knees and hips together to drive the bells up and forward; this hip pop powers the whole movement.
As the bells rise, keep the arms relatively straight and let the momentum carry them, pulling the elbows high and keeping the bells close to your body in a vertical path.
When the bells reach chest height, punch your hands up and through the handles so the bells rotate smoothly over the backs of your wrists rather than slamming down on them.
Finish in a tall locked-out overhead position: arms straight, biceps by your ears, wrists neutral, core braced, glutes tight, and the bells stacked over your shoulders in one continuous motion.
Exhale forcefully at lockout and pause briefly to show control with both bells fixed overhead.
To descend, let the bells tip forward and guide them back down close to the body, hinging at the hips to receive them into the next backswing without letting them yank your shoulders.
Keep the bells from flipping over and banging your forearms by timing the hand punch precisely as they reach the top, not before.

name: Double Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Stand with one kettlebell on the floor just inside your front foot and a second kettlebell ready to be pressed overhead in the opposite hand.

Clean and press the overhead kettlebell to lockout: extend through the legs and hips to pull it to the shoulder, rotating the wrist so the palm faces forward, then press it straight overhead with the arm fully locked.
Turn both feet roughly forty-five degrees away from the side of the locked-out arm, keeping your feet about shoulder-width apart; the overhead bell stays fixed over the rear shoulder.
Keep your eyes locked on the overhead kettlebell for the entire movement and keep that arm vertical and locked at all times.
Begin by pushing your hips out toward the side of the overhead arm, shifting your weight onto that back leg while keeping it relatively straight.
Inhale and slowly hinge sideways and forward at the hips, lowering your torso toward the floor while sliding your free hand down the inside of your front leg toward the low kettlebell.

Continue descending under control, keeping your front leg straight and your back flat, until your lower hand reaches and grips the floor kettlebell; you should feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings and obliques.
Pause for a second at the bottom with the low bell in hand and the top bell still fixed directly overhead.
Reverse the motion by driving your hips back under you and standing tall, squeezing the obliques and glutes to return upright with both bells in hand.
Keep the overhead arm perfectly vertical throughout; letting it drift forward or bending the elbow is the most common fault and loads the shoulder dangerously.

name: Double Leg Butt Kick
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your arms relaxed at your sides ready to swing.
Keep your chest up, core braced, and gaze forward; this is an explosive plyometric jump, so warm up thoroughly first.
Drop quickly into a short quarter-squat by flexing the hips and knees, swinging your arms back to load for the jump.
Immediately reverse and explode straight up, driving through the balls of your feet and swinging your arms up for maximum vertical height.
At the peak of the jump, sharply flex both knees and tuck your heels up behind you, trying to touch your heels to your buttocks.
Quickly snap your legs back down and forward so your feet are underneath you, ready to land.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees only partially bent, absorbing the impact through your ankles, knees, and hips like a spring.
Reset your stance and immediately repeat for the prescribed reps, keeping ground-contact time short.
Avoid landing with stiff, locked legs; soft, controlled landings protect the knees and let you rebound into the next rep.

name: Downward Dog
instructions: Begin on all fours with your wrists stacked directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, fingers spread wide and pointing forward.
Tuck your toes under and press firmly into your palms, spreading your weight evenly across all ten fingers and the base of each hand.
Exhale and lift your hips up and back toward the ceiling, straightening your legs to form an inverted V shape with your body.
Press your hands into the floor and rotate your upper arms outward to broaden the shoulders, lengthening your spine from your hands to your hips.
Let your head hang between your arms with the neck relaxed and your ears in line with your upper arms; do not let your shoulders hunch up toward your ears.
Gently press your heels down toward the floor; they do not need to touch, but reaching toward the ground deepens the calf and hamstring stretch.
Soften a slight bend in the knees if your hamstrings are tight, prioritizing a long flat back over perfectly straight legs.
Hold the pose and breathe slowly and deeply through the nose, lengthening the spine a little more on each exhale.
Avoid rounding the upper back; the goal is to tilt the pelvis up and lengthen the spine, not to hunch forward.

name: Downward Facing Balance
instructions: Position an exercise ball on the floor and kneel behind it, then lie facedown over the top of the ball so it supports your stomach and hips.
Plant your hands on the floor in front of the ball and let your legs extend back behind you with your toes near the ground.
Slowly walk your hands forward along the floor, allowing the ball to roll back toward your thighs and shins as your body straightens out.
Continue walking out until the ball rests under your thighs or shins and your body forms a straight, rigid line from head to feet.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips from sagging toward the floor, maintaining a neutral spine.
From this stable position, simultaneously lift and extend your legs by straightening your knees and contracting your glutes and hamstrings.
At the same time keep your arms extended and elbows straight to hold your upper body steady and balanced on the ball.
Hold the balanced, fully extended position for the prescribed time, keeping the body in a straight line without arching the lower back excessively.
Lower under control and walk your hands back to bring the ball under your stomach before dismounting; the most common mistake is letting the hips drop, which strains the low back.

name: Drag Curl
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart and grasp a barbell with a supinated (underhand) grip, palms facing forward, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Let the bar hang at arm's length against the front of your thighs, keeping your knees softly bent and core braced.
Set your starting position by drawing your elbows back slightly behind your torso and tucking them in toward your sides; keep your chest up and shoulders down.
Exhale and begin curling the bar upward while simultaneously driving your elbows back behind you, so the bar drags straight up along the front of your torso.
Keep the bar in contact with your body the entire ascent, traveling close up the abdomen and chest rather than arcing out away from you.
Continue until the bar reaches your upper chest and your elbows are pulled well behind your body; squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
Hold the peak contraction briefly, keeping your shoulders down and avoiding any shrugging or swinging.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly back down along the torso, keeping it in light contact with your body until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, remembering that unlike a standard curl the elbows travel backward rather than staying pinned at your sides.

name: Dragon Flag
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a sturdy bench with your head near one end, and reach back overhead to firmly grip the edge of the bench or a post behind your head with both hands.
Pull your shoulder blades down and anchor your upper back and shoulders flat against the bench; your grip behind your head is your only point of leverage.
Brace your entire core hard and keep your whole body rigid from shoulders to toes, like a stiff plank.
Initiate by kicking your legs slightly and using your abs to raise your entire body upward as one unit, pivoting only on your upper shoulders.
Continue lifting until your body is nearly vertical, balanced on the back of your shoulders with hips, knees, and ankles all in a straight line.
Keep the body perfectly straight and rigid; the movement must come from the core holding the line, not from bending at the hips.
Slowly lower your straight, rigid body back down under full control, resisting gravity the entire way.
Critically, do not let your hips sag or your lower back arch off the line as you descend; keep the glutes and abs tight so the body stays board-straight.
Stop just before your heels touch the bench, maintaining tension, then reverse and repeat; regress by tucking the knees if you cannot hold a fully straight body.

name: Drop Push
instructions: Set up two low, stable boxes or platforms of equal height roughly two to three feet apart, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Position yourself in a pushup stance between the boxes with one hand planted firmly on top of each platform and your feet back, body in a straight line.
Maintain good posture with a braced core, flat back, glutes tight, and a straight line from head to heels; this is a plyometric drill, so warm up the chest and shoulders first.
Lower yourself slightly by bending the elbows, then press up explosively off both boxes to launch your hands up off the platforms.
While your hands are airborne, quickly bring them in toward each other to about shoulder width, ready to land on the floor in the gap between the boxes.
Land with both hands flat on the floor, immediately bending the elbows to cushion the impact and absorb the force through your arms and chest, sinking into the bottom of a pushup.
Catch yourself softly with control rather than crashing; the eccentric absorption of the landing is the main training stimulus.
From the bottom, press back up explosively, plant your hands back onto the boxes, and reset for the next rep.
Keep the body rigid and avoid letting the hips pike up or sag during the drop, and only attempt this once you have a strong, controlled standard pushup.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Bicep Curl
instructions: Stand upright with your torso tall, feet about shoulder-width apart, and a dumbbell in each hand hanging at arm's length by your sides.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and your palms facing in toward your thighs (neutral grip); brace your core and keep your shoulders back.
Keeping your upper arm completely stationary, curl the right dumbbell upward while rotating your wrist so the palm turns to face up as you lift.
Continue contracting the biceps and exhaling until the dumbbell is at shoulder level and the biceps is fully contracted, then squeeze hard at the top for a brief pause.
Move only at the elbow; the upper arm and shoulder should not swing, and your body should stay still without leaning back.
Inhale and lower the right dumbbell slowly back down, rotating the palm back to face your thigh as your arm straightens fully.
Once the right arm is back at the start, repeat the identical motion with the left arm; one curl on each side equals one repetition.
Continue alternating arms smoothly for the prescribed reps, keeping the non-working arm motionless at your side.
Avoid using momentum or swinging the torso; if you have to heave the weight up, it is too heavy and the biceps stops doing the work.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting on top of each thigh, palms facing each other.
Lie back onto the bench while using your thighs to kick the dumbbells up, ending with them held at shoulder level; plant your feet flat on the floor and retract your shoulder blades.
Set a slight natural arch in your lower back, keep your glutes on the bench, and pull your shoulder blades down and together for a stable base.
Rotate your wrists so the palms face forward (away from you) with the dumbbells just outside each side of your chest, upper arm and forearm forming roughly a 90-degree angle.
This is your starting position: elbows tucked at about a 45-degree angle from your torso rather than flared straight out to the sides.
Exhale and press the dumbbells up powerfully using your chest, driving them up and slightly inward until your arms are nearly locked out above your chest.
At the top, squeeze your chest and hold briefly; keep a slight bend to avoid clanging the dumbbells together and to keep tension on the muscle.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly and under control back to chest level, taking about twice as long to lower as to raise them, feeling a stretch across the chest.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows and your feet planted throughout; do not bounce the weights or let your elbows flare to 90 degrees, which stresses the shoulders.
To finish the set safely, bring the dumbbells back to your thighs and use your legs to help you sit up rather than dropping them to the sides.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press with Neutral Grip
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell on each thigh, then lie back kicking the weights up to shoulder level as you settle onto the bench.
Plant your feet flat on the floor, retract and depress your shoulder blades, and set a slight natural arch in your lower back for a stable base.
Press the dumbbells up so your arms are extended directly above you, perpendicular to the floor, holding a neutral grip with your palms facing each other; this is your starting position.
Keep the dumbbells parallel to each other throughout and your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows.
Inhale and begin lowering by flexing the elbows, keeping them tucked relatively close to your sides rather than flaring them wide.
Descend under control until the dumbbells reach the sides of your torso at about lower-chest level, feeling a stretch across the chest and front delts.
Pause briefly at the bottom without bouncing or resting the weights on your body.
Exhale and extend the elbows to press the dumbbells back up along the same path to the fully extended starting position, squeezing the chest at the top.
Keep your glutes and upper back in contact with the bench and feet planted the entire set; the neutral grip is easier on the shoulders, so keep the elbows tucked to take advantage of that.
When finished, lower the dumbbells to your thighs and use your legs to sit up rather than dropping them out to the sides.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet about shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand hanging at arm's length by your sides.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and rotate your palms so they face forward (supinated grip); this is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and shoulders back, and hold your upper arms fixed against your sides.
Exhale and curl both dumbbells upward by contracting the biceps, moving only at the elbow joint while keeping the upper arms stationary.
Continue raising the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level, then pause and squeeze the biceps hard.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly and under control back to the fully extended starting position, resisting the weight on the way down.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid letting the elbows drift forward or the shoulders shrug up during the lift.
Repeat for the recommended reps, and avoid swinging your torso or using momentum; if you must heave the weights, lighten the load so the biceps do the work.

name: Dumbbell Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides with a neutral grip (palms facing your body).
Lower the dumbbells toward the floor by hinging at the hips and bending the knees, pushing your hips back until the dumbbells are alongside your feet; keep a flat back, chest up, and arms straight.
Set your weight over your mid-foot, brace your core, and pack your shoulders down; this is your starting position.
Initiate explosively by jumping upward, violently extending your hips, knees, and ankles to accelerate the dumbbells upward (triple extension).
Keep the arms straight and the dumbbells close to your body as long as possible during the pull, letting your leg drive do the work rather than your arms.
At full extension, shrug and pull yourself under the weights by quickly re-bending your hips and knees to drop into a partial squat.
As you drop under, bend your elbows and whip the dumbbells up to catch them on the front of your shoulders in the racked position, with elbows pointing forward.
Receive the weight solidly in the squat position with the dumbbells on your shoulders, core braced and torso upright.
Stand up by extending the hips and knees to finish tall with the dumbbells racked on your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells back to the start under control to begin the next rep, and avoid pulling early with the arms; the power must come from the hip drive, not curling the weights up.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs, then roll back to lie flat with your knees bent and feet planted on the floor.
Press the dumbbells up to full extension directly above your chest, palms facing forward or slightly turned in, with your shoulder blades pulled down and together.
Set your starting position with arms locked out, wrists straight and stacked over the elbows, and your core braced.
