Decide your elbow path: tuck the elbows close to your sides to emphasize the triceps, or angle the arms slightly out to the sides to bring in more chest.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells under control until the backs of your upper arms (triceps) lightly touch the floor; the floor limits your range and protects the shoulders.
Pause briefly at the bottom with your upper arms resting on the floor, keeping tension and not bouncing off the ground.
Exhale and press the dumbbells back up by extending through the elbows, driving them up and slightly together until your arms are locked out at the top.
Squeeze the triceps at the top, then repeat for the prescribed reps, keeping the wrists firm and the dumbbells under control.
Avoid slamming your elbows into the floor; lower with control so the pause is gentle and the shoulders stay safe.

name: Dumbbell Flyes
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, palms facing each other.
Lie back onto the bench using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells, ending with them held above you at shoulder width, palms still facing each other.
Plant your feet flat on the floor, retract your shoulder blades, and press the dumbbells up as if pressing them, stopping just short of full lockout; this is your starting position.
Set a slight, fixed bend in your elbows to take stress off the biceps tendon; this elbow angle stays constant for the entire movement.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, opening at the shoulder joint only, until you feel a deep stretch across your chest.
Keep the arms stationary at the elbow; the movement should occur only at the shoulder, like hugging a large barrel, not like a press.
Lower until the dumbbells are roughly level with your chest and you feel a strong stretch, without letting the elbows drop far below the bench or overstretching the shoulders.
Exhale and squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back up along the exact same wide arc, returning to the starting position above your chest.
Hold the contracted position at the top for a second, squeezing the pecs together, then repeat for the prescribed reps.
Keep the elbow bend fixed throughout; straightening or bending the arms turns the fly into a press and removes tension from the chest.

name: Dumbbell Incline Row
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to roughly a 30 to 45 degree incline and grab a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip (palms facing each other).

Lie face-down (chest-supported) on the bench so your chest and stomach rest against the pad and your head clears the top edge; spread your feet on the floor or place them on the bench supports for stability.
Let both arms hang straight down toward the floor directly below your shoulders, dumbbells together, with a slight unlocked bend at the elbows. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your neck neutral (eyes down, not craning up), and avoid pushing through your feet or arching off the pad to cheat the weight up.
Begin the pull by retracting your shoulder blades, drawing them back and together before the arms move.

Driving with the elbows, row both dumbbells up toward your sides until your upper arms are roughly in line with your torso and the dumbbells reach the level of your lower ribs; exhale through this phase.
Keep the elbows tucked at about a 45 degree angle to the body rather than flared wide to bias the mid-back.
Squeeze the shoulder blades and pause for one second at the top of the contraction.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to the fully hanging start position, inhaling and feeling a stretch across the mid-back.
Keep the rep smooth and controlled; do not let the weights drop or your chest bounce off the pad. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Dumbbell Incline Shoulder Raise
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a moderate incline (around 45 to 60 degrees) and select two light dumbbells.
Sit back against the incline with a dumbbell resting on top of each thigh, then use a small knee-kick to help swing the weights up to your shoulders as you settle your back against the pad.

Press the dumbbells overhead and extend your arms so they are perpendicular to the floor, palms facing forward and knuckles pointing at the ceiling, arms locked straight. This is your starting position.
Plant your feet flat, brace your core, and keep your head and upper back in contact with the bench.
Keeping your arms completely straight and elbows locked, lift the dumbbells a few inches higher by protracting and elevating your shoulders up off the bench; exhale as you press up.
The movement is small and comes entirely from the shoulder girdle (shoulder blades sliding up and forward), not from bending the elbows.
Pause briefly at the top with shoulders fully shrugged toward the ceiling.
Lower the dumbbells back down by letting your shoulder blades retract and settle, returning to the start; inhale as you lower.
Move slowly and avoid bending the elbows or letting the weights drift backward over your face. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Dumbbell Lunges
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length by your sides, palms facing your thighs, using a neutral grip.
Set your feet about hip-width apart, brace your core, pull your shoulders back, and keep your torso upright and chest tall. This is your starting position.
Take a controlled step forward with your right leg, roughly two feet, planting the foot flat with the toes pointing straight ahead.
Lower your body straight down by bending both knees, descending until your back knee nearly touches the floor and your front thigh is about parallel to the ground; inhale as you descend.
Keep your front shin close to vertical and do not let your front knee travel past your toes, which protects the knee joint.
Keep your torso upright throughout, letting the dumbbells hang at your sides, and avoid leaning forward over the front leg.
Drive through the heel of your front foot to push back up and step the right foot back to the standing start position; exhale as you rise.
Keep your core tight and the dumbbells steady to maintain balance, taking the movement under control rather than dropping into it.
Complete the prescribed reps on the right leg, then repeat on the left (or alternate legs each rep).

name: Dumbbell Lying One-Arm Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a very slight incline, roughly 15 degrees off the floor, and grab one light dumbbell.
Lie chest-down (prone) on the bench so the pad supports your torso; hold the dumbbell in one hand and grip the bench leg or frame with the other hand for stability.
Let the working arm hang down with a neutral grip (palm facing your torso) and the elbow only slightly bent, arm essentially extended. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your neck neutral, and keep your chest pressed into the pad so you do not rotate your torso to swing the weight.
Leading with the elbow, raise the dumbbell out to the side in an arc until your elbow reaches shoulder height and the arm is roughly parallel to the floor; exhale as you lift.
Keep the working arm perpendicular to your torso and roughly straight throughout, so the rear deltoid does the work rather than the elbow bending.
Avoid jerking or using momentum; the rear delts are small, so use light weight and a deliberate pace.
Hold the contracted position at the top for one second, squeezing the rear shoulder.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the hanging start position, inhaling as you descend.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
instructions: Select a light dumbbell and lie face-down (prone) on a flat bench with one arm holding the dumbbell and the opposite hand folded under your head as a rest.
Position the working upper arm out to the side so it is parallel to the floor and forms roughly a 90 degree angle with your torso, with the elbow supported at the edge of the bench.
Bend that elbow to 90 degrees so the forearm hangs and the dumbbell points toward the floor, forearm perpendicular to the ground. This is your starting position.
Keep the upper arm fixed and parallel to the floor; only the forearm should rotate during the movement.
Keeping the 90 degree elbow bend, rotate the forearm upward and forward (external rotation) so the dumbbell rises in an arc; exhale as you lift.
Continue rotating until the forearm is parallel to the floor and pointing forward, with the dumbbell at the top of its arc.
Pause and hold the contraction for one second, keeping the upper arm completely still.
Slowly reverse the rotation, lowering the dumbbell back to the perpendicular start position; inhale as you lower.
Use light weight and a controlled tempo to protect the rotator cuff. Repeat for the prescribed reps, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a very slight incline, roughly 15 degrees off the floor, and grab a light dumbbell in each hand.
Lie chest-down (prone) on the bench so the pad supports your torso and your head clears the top; let your legs straddle the bench or rest your feet on the floor for balance.
Let both arms hang straight down with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and the elbows only slightly bent. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your neck neutral, and keep your chest pinned to the pad so you do not rock your torso to swing the weights.
Leading with the elbows, raise both dumbbells out to the sides in an arc until your elbows reach shoulder height and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor; exhale as you lift.
Keep your arms perpendicular to your torso and roughly straight, so the rear deltoids drive the movement rather than the elbows bending.
Avoid using momentum or shrugging the traps; keep the motion slow and the weight light.
Hold the top contraction for one second, squeezing the rear shoulders together.
Slowly lower both dumbbells back to the hanging start position, inhaling as you descend. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supination
instructions: Select a light dumbbell and lie on your side on a flat bench, holding the dumbbell in your top hand and resting your head on your other folded arm.
Tuck the working upper arm against your side so it stays parallel to the floor and aligned with your torso, elbow pinned to your ribs.
Bend the working elbow to 90 degrees so the forearm points straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso, palm facing down. This is your starting position.
Keep the upper arm completely stationary against your side; only the forearm should move during the exercise.
Keeping the 90 degree elbow bend, rotate the forearm upward (external rotation / supination) in a semicircle, raising the dumbbell toward the ceiling; exhale as you rotate.
Continue until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and pointing toward the ceiling, with the dumbbell at the top.
Pause and hold the contraction for one second, keeping the elbow tucked.
Slowly reverse the rotation, lowering the dumbbell back to the start where the forearm points forward; inhale as you lower.
Use light weight and strict control to protect the rotator cuff. Repeat for the prescribed reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: Dumbbell One-Arm Shoulder Press
instructions: Grab a single dumbbell and sit on an upright bench with back support (or stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart); rest the dumbbell on top of your thigh on the working side.
Use your thigh and a slight knee drive to clean the dumbbell up to shoulder height on the working side.
Rotate your wrist so the palm faces forward, with the dumbbell held just outside your shoulder and the elbow pointing down and slightly forward. This is your starting position.
Let your non-working hand rest at your waist or grip the bench or a fixed surface for stability, and press your lower back into the support.
Brace your core and keep your torso upright; do not lean away from the weight or arch excessively to help press it.
Press the dumbbell straight up overhead until your arm is fully extended and the weight is stacked over your shoulder; exhale as you press.
Avoid letting the dumbbell drift forward or out to the side; drive it in a controlled vertical path.
Pause for one second at the top with the arm locked out.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back down to shoulder height under control; inhale as you lower.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then switch the dumbbell to the other arm and repeat.

name: Dumbbell One-Arm Triceps Extension
instructions: Grab a single dumbbell and sit on a bench with back support (or stand tall); rest the dumbbell on your thigh on the working side.
Clean the dumbbell to shoulder height, then press and extend it overhead so the whole arm is vertical (perpendicular to the floor) and right next to your head, dumbbell above you.
Rotate your wrist so the palm faces forward and the pinkie points toward the ceiling. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arm fixed and vertical beside your head throughout; you can use your free hand to support the working upper arm or grip a fixed surface.
Brace your core and keep your torso upright, avoiding any back arch or shoulder swing.
Bend the elbow to slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping the upper arm stationary; inhale as you lower until your triceps are fully stretched.
Make sure only the forearm moves; the elbow should stay pointing up and not flare out to the sides.
Reverse the motion by extending the elbow and flexing the triceps to raise the dumbbell back overhead to full lockout; exhale as you press up.
Pause and squeeze the triceps at the top, then repeat for the prescribed reps before switching arms.

name: Dumbbell One-Arm Upright Row
instructions: Grab a single dumbbell and stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, back straight and chest up.
Let the working arm hang in front of you with the dumbbell resting against your thigh, palm facing your thigh and a slight bend in the elbow. This is your starting position.
Let your non-working hand rest at your waist or grip a fixed surface for balance, and brace your core.
Keeping the dumbbell close to your body, pull it straight up along the front of your torso by raising your elbow; exhale as you lift.
Drive the motion with the elbow, keeping it higher than your forearm and wrist throughout the pull.
Continue lifting until the dumbbell is nearly in line with your chin and your elbow is near shoulder height.
Keep your torso stationary and upright; do not lean back or use a hip swing to heave the weight up.
Pause for one second at the top, feeling the side shoulder and trap contract.
Lower the dumbbell back down slowly along the same path to the start; inhale as you lower. Repeat for the prescribed reps, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a moderate incline (around 45 degrees) and grab a dumbbell in each hand.
Lie face-down (prone) on the bench with your chest against the pad and your shoulders near the top edge; either rest your knees on the seat or straddle the bench with your feet on the floor.
Let both arms hang straight down in front of you, perpendicular to the floor, arms fully extended.
Turn your palms to face forward (supinated grip) and keep your elbows tucked in close to your sides. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your chest pressed into the pad so you cannot swing or use body english.
Curl the dumbbells up by contracting the biceps until your arms are fully flexed; exhale as you lift.
Keep the upper arms completely stationary and perpendicular to the floor, allowing only the forearms to move.
Pause and squeeze the biceps at the top of the curl.
Lower the dumbbells slowly and under control until your arms are fully extended again; inhale as you lower. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Dumbbell Raise
instructions: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, back straight and chest up.
Let your arms hang at your sides with a slight bend at the elbows; the dumbbells should rest near your thighs with palms facing back. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your torso upright and stationary throughout.
Using your side shoulders, lift both dumbbells out and up while keeping them close to the line of your body; exhale as you raise them.
Lead with your elbows, keeping each elbow slightly higher than the forearm and wrist as the weights rise.
Continue lifting until the dumbbells are nearly in line with your chin and your elbows reach about shoulder height.
Do not lean back, swing, or use momentum from the hips to drive the weight up.
Pause for one second at the top, feeling the deltoids and traps contract.
Lower the dumbbells back down slowly along the same path to the starting position; inhale as you lower. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Dumbbell Rear Lunge
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length by your sides, palms facing your thighs.
Set your feet about hip-width apart, brace your core, pull your shoulders back, and keep your torso upright. This is your starting position.
Take a controlled step backward with your right leg, roughly two feet behind the stationary left foot, landing on the ball of the rear foot.
Lower your body straight down by bending both knees until your back knee nearly touches the floor and your front thigh is about parallel to the ground; inhale as you descend.
Keep the front shin close to vertical and do not let the front knee drift past the toes, protecting the knee joint.
Keep your torso upright throughout; a longer step back emphasizes the glutes while a shorter step emphasizes the quads.
Drive back up to the standing start position by pushing through the front foot; exhale as you rise.
Push through the ball of the front foot to emphasize the quads, or through the heel to emphasize the glutes.
Keep the dumbbells steady and your core tight to maintain balance. Complete the reps on the right leg, then repeat stepping back with the left.

name: Dumbbell Scaption
instructions: Select a light dumbbell in each hand and stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, back straight and core braced.
Let your arms hang at your sides and rotate your grip so your thumbs point upward (palms facing roughly forward). This is your starting position.
Keep your arms fully extended with only a soft, unlocked elbow throughout the movement.
Raise both arms up and out in front of you at about a 30 degree angle from your body's midline, forming a wide V shape rather than straight ahead or straight to the sides; exhale as you lift.
Keep your thumbs pointing up and your shoulders down, away from your ears, to keep the work on the scapular stabilizers.
Continue raising until your arms reach about shoulder height, roughly parallel to the floor; do not raise above the shoulders.
Avoid shrugging, leaning back, or using momentum; this is a controlled corrective movement with light weight.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower your arms back to the starting position; inhale as you lower. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Dumbbell Seated Box Jump
instructions: Position a sturdy plyo box a couple of feet in front of a flat bench, and choose a manageable dumbbell.
Sit on the edge of the bench facing the box, holding the dumbbell against your chest with both hands.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor about shoulder-width apart with toes pointing forward. This is your starting position.
Lean your torso slightly forward and load the hips, keeping your chest up and core braced.
Explosively extend through the hips, knees, and ankles to jump up and forward off the bench toward the box, driving with the legs.
Land softly on top of the box with both feet at the same time, absorbing the impact by bending your hips and knees into a quarter-squat.
Keep the dumbbell snug against your chest throughout and maintain a stable, upright posture on landing rather than collapsing forward.
Stand fully upright on the box, then step down one foot at a time and return to a seated start position before the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Seated One-Leg Calf Raise
instructions: Place a sturdy block or low step on the floor about 12 inches in front of a flat bench, and select one dumbbell.
Sit upright on the bench and rest the dumbbell vertically on your left thigh, about 3 inches above the knee, holding it in place with your hand.
Place the ball of your left foot on the edge of the block with your heel hanging off, keeping your knee bent at roughly 90 degrees. This is your starting position.
Keep your torso upright and the dumbbell steady on the thigh to load the calf.
Press through the ball of your foot to raise your heel as high as possible, contracting the calf; exhale as you lift.
Pause and hold the peak contraction for one second at the top.
Slowly lower your heel back down, dropping it below the level of the block to get a full stretch in the calf; inhale as you lower.
Move through the full range on every rep without bouncing. Complete the prescribed reps on the left leg, then switch and repeat on the right.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a fully upright (90-degree) back position and sit firmly against the backrest with your glutes, upper back, and head supported. Plant both feet flat on the floor slightly wider than hip width for a stable base.
Pick up a dumbbell in each hand and rest them upright on top of your thighs, palms facing each other.

Kick each dumbbell up to shoulder height one at a time using a small thigh drive, then rotate your wrists so your palms face forward. The dumbbells should sit just outside and slightly above your shoulders with elbows pointing down and out at roughly 45 degrees.
Brace your core, press your lower back gently into the pad without overarching, and pull your shoulder blades back and down so they stay locked against the bench.

Take a breath and brace, then exhale as you press both dumbbells straight up and slightly inward in a controlled arc until your arms are nearly fully extended overhead. Stop just short of locking the elbows.
At the top the dumbbells should be almost touching directly over the crown of your head, wrists stacked over elbows. Do not clang them together hard or shrug your shoulders up to your ears.
Pause briefly at the top, then inhale as you lower the dumbbells slowly under control back to shoulder height, taking about 2 to 3 seconds on the way down.
Keep your forearms vertical throughout and avoid flaring the elbows too far behind your body, which stresses the shoulder joint. Repeat for the prescribed reps.
If you find yourself arching hard or using leg drive to grind out reps, reduce the weight so the movement stays strict and shoulder-driven.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip to shoulder width apart, knees soft, and a dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides with palms facing your thighs.
Set your posture: chest up, shoulders relaxed down, eyes forward, and a slight natural arch in the lower back. Brace your core to keep your torso rigid.
Let the dumbbells pull your shoulders down into a slight stretch at the bottom. Keep your arms completely straight and locked throughout the entire movement.
Exhale and shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible, leading with the traps. Imagine trying to touch your shoulders to your earlobes.
Squeeze and hold the top contraction hard for a full one to two seconds. Do not roll the shoulders forward or backward; the motion is purely vertical.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the fully stretched starting position under control, resisting gravity rather than dropping them.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid using your biceps to curl or your knees to bounce the weight up; only the shoulders should move.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, keeping the tempo controlled at the top and bottom.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet placed about shoulder width apart and toes pointing forward for a stable base.
Hold a single dumbbell in your left hand with your palm facing your torso, arm hanging straight down at your side. Place your right hand on your waist or behind your head.
Set your posture with your chest up, head neutral, and a tight core. Keep your hips and legs fixed and facing forward; they should not move during the exercise.
Inhale and bend slowly and only at the waist toward the loaded (left) side, lowering the dumbbell down the outside of your left thigh as far as is comfortable.
Keep your torso in one flat plane the whole time, as if pressed between two panes of glass. Do not lean forward or rotate; the bend is strictly side to side.
Feel the stretch on the right side of your waist at the bottom, then exhale and contract your obliques to pull your torso back up to fully upright.
Hold the top position briefly and keep tension on the working side rather than relaxing fully between reps.
Complete all the recommended repetitions on one side, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat to keep both obliques balanced.
Avoid using momentum or jerking; if you cannot control the bottom of the movement, lighten the dumbbell.

name: Dumbbell Squat
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down at your sides with palms facing the outside of your legs.
Position your feet about shoulder width apart with your toes turned out very slightly (about 10 to 20 degrees). This medium stance targets overall leg development.
Set your posture: chest up, shoulders back, head facing forward, and a natural arch in your lower back. Brace your core hard to protect your spine. This is your starting position.
Begin the descent by pushing your hips back and bending your knees at the same time, keeping your weight centered over your mid-foot and heels.
Inhale on the way down and continue lowering under control until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor, keeping your chest tall and back flat the whole time.
Track your knees out in line with your toes. They should travel roughly over your feet, not cave inward and not be forced excessively past your toes, which strains the knees.
Drive back up by pushing through your heels and mid-foot, exhaling as you straighten your hips and knees to return to the fully standing position.
Keep the dumbbells hanging straight down at your sides throughout; do not let them swing forward or pull you off balance.
Avoid looking down or rounding your back, as this shifts your weight and stresses your spine. Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Squat To A Bench
instructions: Set a flat bench directly behind you and stand up straight in front of it, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing the outside of your legs.
Position your feet about shoulder width apart with toes pointed slightly outward. The bench should be close enough that you can sit back and just graze it at the bottom of the squat.
Set your posture: chest up, shoulders back, head forward, lower back naturally arched, and core braced tight. This is your starting position.
Begin lowering by pushing your hips back toward the bench and bending your knees simultaneously, inhaling as you descend.
Continue down under control until your glutes lightly touch the top of the bench. Touch it gently to confirm depth, but do not flop down, relax, or rock backward onto it.
Keep your chest tall and your knees tracking in line with your toes throughout the descent; do not let the knees collapse inward or drift far past the toes.
Without bouncing off the bench, drive back up by pushing through your heels, exhaling as you extend your hips and knees to return to standing.
Keep the dumbbells hanging at your sides the whole time and your torso upright. The bench is only a depth target, not a resting seat.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, maintaining a controlled tempo on every rep.

name: Dumbbell Step Ups
instructions: Set a sturdy box, bench, or platform in front of you at a height where your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor when your foot is on top. A lower box is easier; a higher box is harder.
Stand tall facing the platform holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down at your sides with palms facing your legs.
Set your posture with chest up, shoulders back, core braced, and eyes forward. Keep the dumbbells hanging quietly and do not let them swing.
Place your entire right foot flat and firmly on top of the platform, with your heel well on the surface rather than hanging off the edge.
Exhale and drive up by pushing through the heel of your right foot, extending the right hip and knee to lift your body onto the platform. Avoid pushing off the floor with your back foot for momentum.
Bring your left foot up to stand fully on the platform, standing tall with both feet on top and the working leg fully but not harshly locked.
Inhale and step back down by lowering your left foot to the floor first, controlling the descent with the right leg rather than dropping quickly.
Return to the starting position with both feet on the ground, keeping the right foot as the working leg for the set.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward over the box. Complete the recommended reps with one leg, then switch to lead with the other leg.
If your knee caves inward as you drive up, consciously push it out in line with your toes and lower the dumbbell weight if needed.

name: Dumbbell Tricep Extension -Pronated Grip
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a flat bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor for stability and your head supported on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and press them up so your arms are fully extended straight above your shoulders, forming a 90-degree angle with the floor.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face forward (a pronated grip) and tuck your elbows in toward each other rather than letting them flare out. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms vertical and completely stationary, inhale and slowly bend only at the elbows, lowering the dumbbells down toward the sides of your head near your ears.
Lower under control until you feel a stretch in your triceps, keeping your elbows tucked and pointing toward the ceiling the entire time.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then exhale and contract your triceps to extend your forearms and press the dumbbells back up to the fully extended starting position.
Do not let your elbows drift apart or your upper arms swing back and forth; only your forearms should move, hinging at the elbow.
Keep your wrists firm and neutral so the dumbbells stay stable, and avoid lowering so fast that the weights pull your elbows out of position. Repeat for the recommended reps.

name: Dynamic Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, knees soft, chest up, and core lightly braced. This is your starting position.
Let your arms hang straight down in front of your thighs with palms facing back.
Keeping your arms straight, swing them forward and up in front of your body in a smooth, controlled arc, then back down to the start.
Repeat the swing 5 to 10 times, increasing the range of motion a little more each rep until your arms travel all the way up overhead.
Move at a steady, rhythmic pace rather than throwing the arms violently, and keep your torso upright without arching your lower back as the arms rise.
Breathe naturally throughout, exhaling as your arms swing up.

name: Dynamic Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width apart, knees soft, chest up, and core braced.
Bring your hands together in front of you with both arms extended straight out at shoulder height. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight and at shoulder height, sweep them open and back as far as possible, squeezing your shoulder blades together and opening across the chest.
Reverse the motion smoothly and bring your arms back together in front of you, like an exaggerated, wide clapping motion.
Repeat for 5 to 10 controlled repetitions, gradually increasing the speed and range as your chest and shoulders loosen up.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears and avoid arching your lower back as your arms travel behind you. Breathe steadily throughout.

name: Elbow Circles
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your feet slightly apart, chest up, and core lightly engaged.
Place your hands on top of your shoulders, fingertips resting on each shoulder, so your elbows are raised to about shoulder level and pointing out to the sides.
Keeping your hands fixed on your shoulders, begin drawing large, slow circles in the air with your elbows, moving from front to up to back to down.
Exhale as your elbows rise and sweep forward and up, and inhale as they travel back and down to complete each circle.
Make the circles as big and smooth as your shoulders comfortably allow, feeling the stretch through the shoulders and upper back.
Complete the desired number of circles in one direction, then reverse and circle the opposite way for the same count.
Keep your torso upright and still throughout; only the shoulders and elbows should move.

name: Elbow to Knee
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat. Bend your left knee and plant that foot, then cross your right ankle over the bent left knee.
Clasp your hands lightly behind your head with your elbows pointing out to the sides, and let your shoulder blades rest on the ground. This is your starting position.
Support your head with your hands but do not pull on your neck; your hands are only a cradle, and the work comes from your abs.
Exhale and flex your spine, curling your shoulders off the floor while rotating your torso to bring your left elbow toward your crossed right knee.
Squeeze your abs and obliques hard at the top of the twist where the elbow nears the knee, holding briefly.
Inhale and lower your torso back down under control to the starting position, returning your shoulder blades toward the floor.
Keep the movement slow and controlled, driving the rotation from your core rather than yanking with your arms or neck.
Complete all reps on this side, then switch your leg cross and bring the opposite elbow to the opposite knee.

name: Elbows Back
instructions: Stand up straight with your feet about hip width apart, chest up, and core lightly braced.
Place both hands on your lower back with your fingers pointing downward and your elbows bent and flared out to the sides.
Set your posture by keeping your shoulders down and your spine tall, avoiding any arching of the lower back.
Gently draw both elbows backward, aiming to bring them toward each other behind you as you open up across the chest and front of the shoulders.
Move into the stretch slowly until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders, then hold briefly.
Release back to the start under control and repeat, breathing steadily and never forcing the elbows past a comfortable range.

name: Elevated Back Lunge
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about shoulder height and load it with an appropriate weight. Place a short, stable raised platform on the floor just in front of the rack.
Step under the bar and position it across your upper back (on the traps or rear delts), gripping it firmly with hands a little wider than shoulder width.

Brace your core, set your back tight and arched, and unrack the bar by standing up. Carefully step both feet onto the raised platform and stand tall with feet about hip width apart. This is your starting position.
Take a controlled step backward off the platform with one leg, landing on the ball of that foot while keeping your torso upright.
Inhale and descend by bending both knees and your hips until your rear knee gently touches the floor, keeping your front shin roughly vertical and your front heel planted on the platform.
Because your front foot is elevated, you get a deeper range of motion, so control the descent and do not let the rear knee crash into the floor.
Pause at the bottom, then exhale and drive up through your front heel, extending the front hip and knee to bring the back leg forward and return to standing on the platform.
Keep your chest up and core braced throughout; do not let your torso pitch forward or your back round.
Alternate legs each rep or complete all reps on one side first as programmed. When finished, step off the platform carefully before re-racking the bar.

name: Elevated Cable Rows
instructions: At a seated cable row station, place a sturdy 4 to 6 inch platform (such as an aerobic step or calf-raise block) on top of the machine's seat to raise your hips. Attach a close-grip V-bar handle to the low cable.
Sit down on the elevated platform and brace your feet against the front footplate or crossbar with your knees slightly bent, never locked out.
Hinge forward from the hips while keeping the natural alignment of your spine, and grab the V-bar handle with both hands, palms facing each other.
Sit back so your arms are extended and your torso is roughly upright, with your back slightly arched and chest lifted. You should feel a stretch through your lats. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your torso stationary throughout; the elevated seat lets you pull the handle lower into your torso for a fuller lat contraction.
Exhale and pull the handle toward your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back close to your sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end.
Touch the handle to your lower abs and hold the peak contraction for a second, squeezing your back hard without leaning back excessively or jerking with momentum.
Inhale and slowly straighten your arms to return the handle forward under control, allowing your shoulder blades to spread and your lats to stretch at the front.
Avoid rounding your lower back at the stretched position or yanking the torso backward; keep the movement smooth and back-driven. Repeat for the recommended reps.

name: Elliptical Trainer
instructions: Step onto the elliptical pedals one foot at a time, placing each foot flat and centered on its pedal, and take hold of the stationary center rail or the moving handles.
Use the console to select a program or manual mode, and enter your age and weight if prompted so the machine can estimate calories and heart rate.
Stand tall with an upright posture, shoulders back, core lightly engaged, and a slight bend in the knees. Avoid leaning heavily on the handles to support your bodyweight.
Begin pedaling in a smooth, gliding motion, pushing the pedals through their full elliptical path with each stride and keeping your foot pressure spread across the whole foot.
If using the moving arm handles, drive and pull them in rhythm with your legs to involve the upper body; otherwise hold the center rail lightly for balance.
Adjust the resistance and incline or elevation settings to raise or lower the intensity so you stay in your target effort or heart rate zone.
Grip the metal contact sensors on the handles periodically if you want a heart rate reading, and adjust your pace to keep the intensity appropriate.
Maintain a steady cadence and controlled breathing for the duration of your session, and slow down gradually to cool off before stepping off carefully.

name: Exercise Ball Crunch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball, then walk your feet forward and lean back so the ball rolls up under your lower and mid back, supporting the natural curve of your lower spine.
Plant both feet flat on the floor about shoulder width apart with your knees bent at roughly 90 degrees for a stable, balanced base.
Let your upper torso hang back over the top of the ball so your abs are slightly stretched. Cross your arms over your chest or keep them at your sides to avoid pulling on your neck.
Set your starting position with your lower back in contact with the ball and your abs lengthened, head and neck neutral.
Keeping your hips still and the ball stationary, exhale and contract your abs to curl your shoulders and upper trunk up and forward toward your hips.
Crunch up only until you feel a strong contraction in the abdominals; your lower back should stay in contact with the ball rather than lifting fully off it.
Hold the top contraction for a second and squeeze your abs, keeping your neck relaxed and chin off your chest.
Inhale and slowly lower your torso back over the ball to the stretched starting position under control, feeling the abs lengthen again.
Keep your feet firmly planted and the ball steady throughout; if the ball rolls or you wobble, widen your feet for more stability. Repeat for the recommended reps.

name: Exercise Ball Pull-In
instructions: Place a stability ball on the floor in an open area and get into a high plank position in front of it, with your hands flat on the floor directly under your shoulders, fingers spread and pointing forward.
Walk your feet back and rest your lower shins and the tops of your ankles on top of the ball, so your legs are fully extended and your body forms a straight line from head to heels.

Set your shoulders directly over your wrists, brace your core, draw your shoulder blades down and back, and keep a flat back with hips level, neither sagging nor piking up. This is your starting position.
Exhale and contract your abs to pull your knees in toward your chest, letting the ball roll forward under your shins until it sits beneath your ankles or toes.
Keep your hips low and avoid letting them shoot up toward the ceiling; the movement should come from your abs flexing the hips and knees, not from rocking your shoulders.
Squeeze your abdominals hard at the top and hold for a one-count with your knees tucked under your torso.
Inhale and slowly straighten your legs, rolling the ball back out under control until your body returns to the straight-line plank position.
Maintain a stable, motionless upper body throughout and do not let your lower back arch as you extend; control the roll so the ball doesn't run away from you.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, keeping the tempo deliberate rather than rushing the pull-in.

name: Extended Range One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
instructions: Sit on the floor next to a kettlebell, grab the handle, and roll back onto your back while pulling the kettlebell into the racked position at the side of your chest with a neutral or slightly angled wrist.
Lie flat with your working-side forearm vertical, the kettlebell handle in your palm, and your wrist straight and stacked over the elbow so the bell rests against the back of your forearm.
Bend the leg on the same side as the pressing arm and cross that knee over toward the midline of your body to stabilize your torso; keep the opposite leg extended or planted for balance.
Plant your free hand and forearm out to the side on the floor for stability, brace your core, and keep your shoulder blade pulled down and back into the floor.
Set your elbow on the floor at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso, not flared straight out to the side; this is your starting position with the upper arm resting and the chest stretched.
Exhale and press the kettlebell straight up by extending the elbow and slightly adducting the arm so the bell finishes directly over your shoulder, locking out with a stacked wrist and elbow.
Pause briefly at the top with the kettlebell balanced over the joint, keeping the handle from rolling back into your wrist.
Inhale and lower the kettlebell under control until your upper arm and elbow gently touch the floor, allowing a full deep stretch through the chest at the bottom.
Keep the wrist firm and straight the entire time to avoid the bell snapping back, and let the floor cue the bottom of each rep rather than bouncing.
Complete all reps on one side, then carefully transfer the kettlebell and repeat with the other arm.

name: External Rotation
instructions: Lie on your side along a flat bench with a light dumbbell in your top hand and your bottom arm folded under your head as a cushion.
Keep your body stacked and stable, with the working arm on top and your torso square so you are not rolling forward or backward.
Bend the elbow of the dumbbell arm to 90 degrees and tuck the upper arm firmly against your side so the upper arm stays parallel to your torso throughout.
Let the forearm rest across the front of your abdomen with the dumbbell near your belly; the forearm should point across your body. This is your starting position.
Exhale and externally rotate the forearm, raising the dumbbell in a smooth arc upward while keeping the 90-degree elbow angle and pinning the upper arm to your side.
Continue rotating until the forearm points up toward the ceiling and the dumbbell is at the top of its arc; do not let the elbow drift away from your ribs.
Hold the contraction for a one-count, focusing on the back of the shoulder doing the work rather than the larger shoulder muscles.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back across your body to the starting position, resisting gravity the whole way down.
Use a light weight and a controlled tempo, since this trains small rotator-cuff muscles; momentum or a flaring elbow defeats the purpose.
Complete the reps, then sit up, switch sides, and repeat with the other arm.

name: External Rotation with Band
instructions: Anchor a resistance band around a sturdy post or rack at roughly elbow height, looping it so it is secure and won't slip.
Stand side-on to the anchor with the band on the side of your non-working arm, a couple of feet away so there is light tension when your hand is across your body.
Grasp the free end of the band with the hand farthest from the post, and bend that elbow to 90 degrees.
Pin the working upper arm tightly against your side; for best position, hold a rolled towel or foam pad between your elbow and ribs to keep the elbow locked in place.
Bring the working hand across the front of your torso so the band has tension; keep your wrist neutral and your shoulder blade set down and back. This is your starting position.
Stand tall with a braced core and squared hips, and avoid twisting your whole body to move the band.
Externally rotate the forearm outward in a backhand sweeping motion, keeping the elbow glued to your side and the 90-degree angle constant.
Rotate out as far as your shoulder comfortably allows, roughly until the forearm points straight ahead or slightly beyond your body line.
Pause and squeeze the back of the shoulder, then slowly return the hand across your body to the starting position under control.
Keep the movement isolated to rotation of the upper arm, do not let the elbow drift forward or the pad drop, and complete the reps before switching sides.

name: External Rotation with Cable
instructions: Set a single-handle attachment on an adjustable cable pulley and position the pulley at roughly elbow height.
Stand side-on to the machine with the cable on the side of your non-working arm, a couple of feet away so there is tension when your hand sits across your body.
Grasp the handle with the hand farthest from the machine and bend that elbow to 90 degrees, keeping your wrist neutral.
Press the working upper arm firmly against your side; hold a rolled towel or foam pad between your elbow and ribs to keep the elbow fixed in place.
Draw your hand across the front of your torso so the cable is loaded, set your shoulder blade down and back, and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Keeping the elbow pinned and the 90-degree angle constant, externally rotate the forearm outward in a backhand motion away from your body.
Rotate out as far as the shoulder allows, roughly to where the forearm points straight ahead, without letting the elbow lift off your side or your torso twist.
Pause and squeeze the rear shoulder at the end range of the rotation.
Slowly return the hand back across your body to the starting position, resisting the cable's pull the entire way.
Use a light load and controlled cadence, focus on isolating the rotation, and complete all reps before turning around to work the other arm.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
instructions: Load an EZ-curl bar and stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and core braced.
Grip the bar on the angled outer portions of the handles with your palms facing up and slightly tilted inward, following the natural bend of the bar to keep your wrists comfortable.
Pull your shoulders back and down, keep your chest up, and tuck your upper arms in against your sides so your elbows stay pinned. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the bar up by flexing only at the elbows, contracting the biceps.
Avoid swinging the bar or leaning back; the torso stays still and only the forearms should move.
Continue raising the bar until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar reaches roughly shoulder level.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top and hold the peak contraction for a moment.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control all the way back to full arm extension, resisting on the way down.
Do not let the elbows drift forward or the wrists curl excessively; keep the motion smooth and the tempo controlled.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher
instructions: Load an EZ-curl bar and sit on the end of a flat bench, then lie back so your head is near the end of the bench and your eyes are roughly under where the bar will travel.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor about hip-width apart and keep your glutes, upper back, and head in contact with the bench with a neutral spine.
Take a close grip on the inner angled portion of the bar with palms facing up, hands roughly shoulder-width or slightly narrower.

Press the bar up and bring your arms to vertical so they are perpendicular to the floor, then tuck your elbows in so they point toward the ceiling rather than flaring out. This is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and your elbows pointing up, inhale and lower the bar by bending only at the elbows.
Lower the bar in a controlled arc until it is just above your forehead or behind it toward the top of your head, feeling a stretch in the triceps; do not let the elbows flare wide.
Pause briefly at the bottom without resting the bar on your head.
Exhale and extend the elbows to drive the bar back up to the starting position over your shoulders, squeezing the triceps at lockout.
Keep the upper arms fixed throughout so the movement stays isolated to the triceps, and avoid pressing with the shoulders.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then carefully lower the bar to the floor or rack it.

name: Face Pull
instructions: Attach a rope to a cable pulley set at or slightly above head height and select a moderate, controllable weight.
Grip the rope with both hands using a neutral grip, palms facing each other, thumbs pointing back toward you.
Step back to take the tension, stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart in a slightly staggered stance for balance, and brace your core.
Extend your arms toward the pulley and let the weight draw your shoulders slightly forward; keep your chest up and shoulder blades set. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the rope directly toward your face, leading with your elbows and driving them high and back.
As you pull, separate your hands so the rope ends pass on either side of your face and your knuckles finish near your ears or temples.
Keep your upper arms roughly parallel to the floor and externally rotate so your hands end up high; squeeze your rear delts and the muscles between your shoulder blades.
Pause and hold the contraction briefly at the end range without shrugging your traps up toward your ears.
Inhale and slowly return the rope to the starting position with control, letting your shoulder blades protract slightly.
Use a deliberate tempo and avoid yanking or using body english; the focus is the rear delts and upper back, not heavy weight.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Farmer's Walk
instructions: Set up two heavy implements, dumbbells, or short loadable bars on the floor, spaced just outside hip width so you can stand between them.
Stand tall between the handles with your feet about hip-width apart and the weights centered alongside your feet.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower into a partial squat or deadlift position and grip both handles firmly with a full grip.
Set your back flat, chest up, shoulders pulled back and down, and brace your core hard before you lift. This is your starting position.
Drive through your heels and stand up to lift both implements, keeping your back straight, head up, and arms locked straight at your sides.
Stabilize at the top with the weights hanging at arm's length, shoulders packed, and torso upright and rigid.
Walk forward taking short, quick, controlled steps, keeping your trunk braced and avoiding any side-to-side sway or leaning.
Continue breathing in short bursts rather than holding your breath the entire way, and keep your grip crushing the handles.
Cover the prescribed distance, typically 50 to 100 feet, moving steadily and as fast as you can while staying upright and controlled.
At the finish, slow down, hinge at the hips with a flat back, and set the weights down on the floor under control rather than dropping them.

name: Fast Skipping
instructions: Stand tall in an open space with good footing, feet roughly hip-width apart and one leg positioned slightly forward in a relaxed athletic stance. This is your starting position.
Keep your posture upright with a tall chest, a braced core, and your arms bent at about 90 degrees ready to drive in rhythm with your legs.
Begin a skipping pattern using a step-hop rhythm, performing two quick contacts on one foot, then stepping to the other foot for two quick contacts, alternating side to side.
Coordinate your arms so the opposite arm drives forward as each leg comes up, keeping the motion fluid and rhythmic.
Emphasize speed by minimizing time on the ground and reducing air time, staying low and quick rather than skipping high.
Stay light on the balls of your feet and keep ground contacts short and snappy so each skip cycles rapidly.
Maintain a quick, consistent cadence and continue moving for the prescribed distance or time, keeping your form crisp as you fatigue.

name: Figure-Four Stretch
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with both knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh just above the knee so your legs form a figure-four shape, and gently flex the foot of the crossed leg to protect the ankle.
Reach both hands forward and clasp them behind the thigh of the supporting (bottom) leg, or grip the shin if your flexibility allows.
Keep your head, shoulders, and lower back relaxed on the floor and your tailbone down rather than rocking your pelvis.
Gently pull the supporting thigh toward your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch in the glute and outer hip of the crossed leg.
Use your crossed-leg elbow to lightly press the bent knee away from you to deepen the stretch if desired, without forcing it.
Hold the position and breathe slowly and evenly, keeping the stretch in a mild-to-moderate range with no sharp pain, for 20 to 30 seconds.
Release the pull, lower the leg back down, and repeat on the other side.

name: Finger Curls
instructions: Load a light barbell and either sit on the end of a bench with your forearms resting on your thighs or stand holding the bar in front of your hips.
Grip the bar with both hands palms facing up (supinated), hands about shoulder-width apart, and your wrists positioned just past your knees or in front of your thighs.
Plant your feet flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width for a stable base and keep your forearms supported and stationary. This is your starting position.
Open your hands and let the bar roll down out of your palms toward your fingertips, lowering it as far as possible while keeping control with the last joints of your fingers.
Let the bar settle against the final finger joints at the bottom for a full stretch through the fingers and forearm flexors.
Exhale and curl the bar back up by closing your fingers and rolling the bar up into your palms, contracting the forearms.
Squeeze and hold the top contraction briefly with the bar gripped firmly in your hands.
Keep the rest of your arms motionless so the work stays in the fingers and forearms, and avoid using wrist or arm movement.
Lower under control and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Flat Bench Cable Flyes
instructions: Position a flat bench centered between two low cable pulleys so that when you lie down, your chest lines up with the pulleys and you can reach a handle on each side.
Attach single handles to both low pulleys and set a light to moderate weight.
Lie back flat on the bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor, glutes and upper back on the bench, and a natural arch in your lower back.
Take a handle in each hand with a palms-up (neutral toward the ceiling) grip, having a partner hand them to you or grabbing them before lying down.

Extend your arms out to your sides and slightly toward the floor with a fixed slight bend in the elbows, arms roughly parallel to the floor. This is your starting position with a stretch across the chest.
Keeping the slight elbow bend constant, exhale and bring both handles up and together in a wide arcing, hugging motion over your chest.
Lead with your chest and bring the handles together directly above the middle of your chest until your hands nearly touch.
Squeeze your chest hard and hold the contraction for a one-count at the top.
Inhale and slowly reverse the arc, lowering the handles back out to your sides under control until you feel a stretch across the chest, without letting the elbows bend further.
Keep the elbows slightly bent throughout to protect the joints and keep tension on the chest rather than pressing, and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Flat Bench Leg Pull-In
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench (or lie on an exercise mat) and lower your torso back so your legs extend off the end with your knees and feet hanging.
Place your hands either palms-down under your glutes or gripping the sides of the bench to anchor your upper body and protect your lower back.
Extend your legs straight out in front of you, slightly above parallel, and brace your abs. This is your starting position.
Exhale and bend your knees while pulling your upper thighs in toward your midsection, contracting your lower abs.
Continue pulling until your knees are near your chest and your hips curl slightly off the bench, keeping the movement controlled.
Squeeze your abs and hold the contracted position for a one-count at the top.
Inhale and slowly straighten your legs back out to the starting position, keeping tension on the abs and not letting your feet drop or your lower back arch up.
Keep your upper body still and avoid using momentum; the pull should come from the abdominals, not from swinging the legs.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Flat Bench Lying Leg Raise
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a bench with your legs extended off the end and your head supported toward the opposite end.
Place your hands palms-down either under your glutes or gripping the edges of the bench beside your hips to stabilize your torso and protect your lower back.
Extend your legs straight out, keeping a slight but locked bend in the knees, and press your lower back gently into the bench. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise your legs upward as a unit, keeping them straight, until they reach roughly a 90-degree angle with your torso.
Lead the lift from your lower abs and avoid swinging or jerking the legs up.
Hold the top position for a one-count, keeping your abs contracted and your lower back supported.
Inhale and slowly lower your legs back down under control toward the starting position, stopping before your heels touch the floor to keep tension on the abs.
Do not let your lower back arch up off the bench as the legs lower; if it does, reduce the range or bend the knees slightly more.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Flexor Incline Dumbbell Curls
instructions: Set an incline bench to about a 45-degree angle and select a pair of dumbbells.
Grip each dumbbell shifted toward the outer (far) end of the handle so more weight sits on the inner side near your thumb, which increases the demand on the forearm flexors; do this for both hands.
Sit back against the incline bench with your back and head supported, feet flat on the floor, and let your arms hang straight down at your sides.
Keep your elbows tucked in close to your torso and turn your palms forward in a supinated grip with thumbs pointing slightly away from your body.

Cock your wrists back and maintain this wrist position and hand orientation throughout to keep stress off the wrists; there should be no twisting of the hands as you curl. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl both dumbbells up at the same time by flexing at the elbows until your biceps are fully contracted.
Keep your upper arms stationary against your sides and do not swing or use momentum; the motion comes only from the forearms.
Squeeze and hold the contracted position for a one-count at the top.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to full extension under control, maintaining the offset grip and cocked-back wrists.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, keeping a controlled tempo throughout.

name: Floor Glute-Ham Raise
instructions: Kneel on a padded mat or folded towel with your knees together and your upper legs, hips, and torso stacked in one straight vertical line. Padding under the knees is important since they bear pressure throughout.

Anchor your feet: either have a partner kneel behind you and press your heels firmly into the floor, or wedge your heels under a loaded barbell, the lip of a heavy bench, or a wall bar so they cannot lift.
Brace your core hard, squeeze your glutes, and tuck your pelvis slightly so your hips stay fully extended. Hold your hands up near your chest, ready to catch yourself. This is your starting position.

Keeping a rigid straight line from knees to head, slowly lower your torso toward the floor by extending only at the knee joint. Do NOT bend or fold at the hips; your hips must stay open the entire descent.
Control the descent with your hamstrings for a slow 3 to 4 second count, resisting gravity as long as possible. Inhale as you lower.
When you can no longer hold yourself, let your hands reach the floor and catch your bodyweight to avoid crashing down.
Use a light push from your hands off the floor to assist, then powerfully contract your hamstrings to pull your body back up to the upright kneeling start. Exhale as you rise.
Keep the hips locked in extension the whole way up; the most common mistake is bending at the hips to cheat the rep, which removes the hamstring load.
Use only the minimum hand assistance needed and reduce it over time as you build strength. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Floor Press
instructions: Set the j-hooks of a power rack low, so a loaded barbell sits roughly at arm's reach when you are lying on the floor with your head just past the rack uprights.
Lie flat on your back on the floor with your head near the bar, knees bent and feet flat, or legs extended straight out, whichever keeps you most stable and rooted.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with a full thumb-wrapped grip. Stack your wrists directly over your elbows and keep the bar weight centered over the heel of your palm.
Pull your shoulder blades down and together and press them into the floor to create a stable base. Take a deep breath into your belly and brace your core.
Unrack the bar by extending your arms, then move it forward so it is stacked directly over your shoulders. This is your starting position.

Lower the bar under control toward the bottom of your chest or upper stomach, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso, not flared out. Squeeze the bar hard as if trying to pull it apart.
Continue lowering until your upper arms and the backs of your triceps lightly touch the floor. Pause for a full second with no bouncing or slamming off the ground.
Drive the bar back up explosively, keeping the bar, wrists, and elbows stacked in a straight vertical line until your arms lock out.
Keep your elbows tucked through the whole press to bias the triceps and protect the shoulders. Exhale near the top, then reset your breath and brace before the next rep.

name: Floor Press with Chains
instructions: Set the j-hooks of a power rack low so a loaded barbell is at arm's reach while lying on the floor with your head just past the uprights.

Drape a chain over each end of the bar, hanging just inside the plates, so the links pile on the floor at the bottom and progressively lift off as you press, adding accommodating resistance at lockout.
Lie flat on your back with your head near the bar, knees bent and feet flat or legs extended straight for stability.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with a full thumb-wrapped grip, wrists stacked over elbows and the load centered over the heel of your palm.
Retract and depress your shoulder blades, pressing them into the floor. Take a big breath and brace your core hard.
Unrack the bar, then position it stacked directly over your shoulders. This is your starting position.

Lower the bar under control to the bottom of your chest or upper stomach, keeping elbows tucked around 45 degrees and squeezing the bar as if pulling it apart, until your triceps lightly touch the floor.
Pause for one full second on the floor with no bounce; the chains will be fully deloaded on the ground here.
Press the bar up as explosively as possible, keeping bar, wrists, and elbows in a vertical line; accelerate through the top to overcome the chain weight that lifts off as you rise.
Keep elbows tucked throughout to load the triceps and protect the shoulders. Reset your breath and brace before each rep.

name: Flutter Kicks
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench so your hips rest right at the edge and your legs hang off the end, torso fully supported along the bench.
Reach forward and grip the front edge or sides of the bench firmly with both hands to anchor your upper body and prevent rocking.
Squeeze your glutes and hamstrings and raise both straight legs until they are level with your hips, forming a straight line from torso to toes. This is your starting position.
Keeping both legs straight and the toes pointed, raise your left leg a bit higher while keeping the right at hip level.
Smoothly reverse, lowering the left leg as you simultaneously raise the right leg, in a slow scissoring flutter motion as if kicking in water.
Continue alternating in a steady, controlled rhythm; keep the movement small and tight rather than swinging the legs wildly.
Keep your glutes and hamstrings engaged throughout and avoid letting the legs drop below hip level, which removes tension and arches the lower back.
Breathe normally and evenly throughout. Continue alternating until you reach the prescribed number of kicks per leg.

name: Foot-SMR
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench with your shoes and socks removed and your feet flat on the floor. Place a foot roller, a tennis or lacrosse ball, or a short length of PVC pipe on the floor in front of you.
Set the arch of one bare foot on top of the roller so it sits between the ball of the foot and the heel. This is your starting position.
Press down with firm, tolerable pressure and slowly roll the roller forward and back along the length of your arch, from just behind the toes to the front of the heel.
When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the tissue to release.
Keep the pressure firm but never sharply painful; ease off slightly if it is too intense.
Cover the whole sole, working the inner and outer edges of the arch as well as the center.
Switch to the other foot and repeat for the same duration.

name: Forward Drag with Press
instructions: Load a weight sled with an appropriate weight and attach a dual-handle rope or chain harness to the front of the sled.

Stand facing away from the sled with the strap running between or beside your legs, and grip one handle in each hand at your sides. Walk forward until the slack is gone and you feel tension on the sled.
Set a strong athletic posture: chest up, core braced, and lean your torso slightly forward into the drag with the handles held near your hips. This is your starting position.
Step forward with one foot, driving hard through the leg and hip to pull the sled along behind you.

Once you have planted that step and are balanced, press both hands forward by extending the elbows until your arms are straight out in front of you, performing the chest press against the sled's resistance.
Return your hands to your hips, then take another forward step and repeat the press with each stride.
Keep your core tight and torso angle steady so power transfers through the legs into the press; avoid twisting or letting one side drift.
Continue stepping and pressing for the prescribed distance or time, maintaining controlled, deliberate steps.

name: Frankenstein Squat
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height, or clean it to your shoulders. This drill trains the bar and body positioning of the front squat.
Rest the bar across the front of your shoulders, high on the deltoids and lightly in contact with your throat or collarbone area.
Extend both arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor, and release your grip on the bar entirely so it balances only on your shoulder shelf. This forces an upright torso.
Push your shoulders forward to create a solid shelf for the bar, but only move the shoulder blades; do not round your upper back or let the thoracic spine flex.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes turned slightly out. Brace your core hard and take a big breath. This is your starting position.
Descend by bending at the knees and hips together, sitting straight down between your legs while keeping your torso vertical, arms up, and shoulders forward.
Continue down to full depth until your hamstrings reach your calves, keeping the bar perfectly still on your shoulders the entire time.
Keep the elbows and arms high throughout; if they drop, the bar will roll forward off your shoulders, so this is the key cue and the most common fault.
Drive up by pushing through the front of your heels and extending the knees and hips back to a tall standing position. Exhale near the top and repeat.

name: Freehand Jump Squat
instructions: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward.
Cross your arms over your chest, keep your head up and your back straight with a natural arch, and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Bend at the knees and hips and squat down under control until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and back straight. Inhale as you descend.
From the bottom, explode straight up by driving mainly through the balls of your feet, using your thighs like springs to jump as high as you can. Exhale forcefully as you jump.
Keep your torso upright and your eyes forward during flight; do not let the chest collapse forward.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately bend the knees and hips to absorb the impact, sinking right back into the squat position.
Without pausing, rebound into the next jump, keeping the contact time on the ground short and controlled.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, stopping if your landing form deteriorates.

name: Frog Hops
instructions: Stand with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and place your hands behind your head with elbows out.
Squat down into a deep position, keeping your torso as upright as possible, chest up, head up, and back straight. This is your starting position.
From the bottom of the squat, explosively jump forward several feet, extending through the hips, knees, and ankles, but avoid jumping unnecessarily high; the goal is horizontal distance.
As your feet contact the ground, land softly and immediately re-bend the knees and hips to absorb the impact and drop straight back into the deep squat.
Keep your hands behind your head and your torso upright the entire time; do not let the chest crash forward on landing.
Without a long pause, rebound out of the squat into the next forward hop.
Repeat the forward hops 5 to 10 times in a continuous controlled sequence.

name: Frog Sit-Ups
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor or an exercise mat with your legs extended straight out in front of you.
Bend both knees and let them drop out to the sides, lowering your outer thighs toward the floor while bringing the soles of your feet together so they touch.
Slide your heels in toward your body as close as is comfortable while keeping your outer thighs on or near the floor, so your legs form a diamond shape.
Cross your arms in front of your chest, each hand touching the opposite shoulder. This is your starting position.
Exhale and flatten your lower back into the floor as you curl your torso up off the ground, performing roughly the first quarter of a sit-up using your abs.
Hold the top contracted position for a one-second squeeze of the abdominals.
Inhale and slowly lower your torso back down to the starting position under control.
Keep the movement driven by the abs rather than momentum, and keep your knees splayed out the whole time. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Frog Stretch
instructions: Begin on all fours on a padded mat with your knees down, then widen your knees out to the sides as far as is comfortable.
Turn your shins out so they run roughly parallel behind you and flex your feet so the inner edges of the feet and ankles rest on the floor.
Lower yourself down onto your forearms, keeping your forearms and elbows under your shoulders to support your upper body.
Keep your spine long and neutral, hips, knees, and ankles roughly in line, so you feel the stretch in the inner thighs and groin.
Gently rock your hips backward toward your heels until you feel a comfortable stretch through the adductors, then ease slightly forward.
Hold a moderate stretch, breathing slowly and deeply, allowing the inner thighs to relax and open a little more with each exhale. Avoid forcing or bouncing.
Hold for the prescribed time, then slowly bring the knees back together to exit.

name: Front Barbell Squat
instructions: Set a barbell in a squat rack at about upper-chest height and load it. Step in close under the bar.
Bring both arms up under the bar and rest it across the front of your shoulders on top of the deltoids, keeping your elbows high so your upper arms are at or slightly above parallel to the floor.
Cross your arms over the bar and grasp it for total control, or use a clean grip with fingertips under the bar and elbows driven high; either way the bar sits on the shoulder shelf, not the hands.
Brace your core, take a deep breath, then lift the bar off the rack by pushing through your legs and straightening your torso at the same time.
Step back and set your feet at a shoulder-width medium stance with toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up and your back straight. This is your starting position.
Begin the descent by bending the knees and hips, keeping your torso as upright as possible and your elbows high so the bar does not roll forward. Inhale as you lower.
Continue down until the angle between your upper and lower leg is slightly less than 90 degrees, meaning your thighs are just below parallel to the floor.
Keep your knees tracking in line over your toes; do not let the knees collapse inward or shoot far past the toes, which stresses the joint.
Drive back up by pushing through the middle of your feet, straightening the legs and returning to the upright start position. Exhale as you rise.
Keep the elbows up and chest tall the entire time; dropping the elbows is the most common front squat fault and dumps the bar forward. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Front Barbell Squat To A Bench
instructions: Set a flat bench behind you positioned so that when you squat down your glutes will just touch it at the correct depth. Set a loaded barbell in a squat rack at about upper-chest height.
Step under the bar and rest it across the front of your shoulders on the deltoids, keeping your elbows high so your upper arms are at or slightly above parallel to the floor.
Cross your arms over the bar and grip it for full control, keeping the load on the shoulder shelf rather than the hands.
Brace your core, take a deep breath, and lift the bar off the rack by driving through your legs and straightening your torso together.
Step back into position over the bench and set your feet at a shoulder-width medium stance with toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up and back straight. This is your starting position.
Lower under control by bending the knees and hips, keeping the torso upright and elbows high, until your glutes lightly touch the bench. Inhale as you descend.
Do not relax or rock back onto the bench; simply tap it to confirm depth while staying braced and tight.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes and avoid letting them drift past the toes or cave inward.
Drive up by pushing through your heels, straightening the legs back to the upright start position. Exhale as you rise. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Front Box Jump
instructions: Place a sturdy plyo box of an appropriate height about 1 to 2 feet in front of you. Stand facing it with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Set an athletic stance with your weight balanced and core braced. This is your starting position.
Initiate by dipping into a short, quick quarter-squat while swinging both arms down and behind you to load the jump.
Explode out of the dip by extending powerfully through the hips, knees, and ankles, swinging both arms forward and up to drive momentum.
Jump up onto the top of the box and land softly with both feet flat, knees bent, hips back, and core tight to absorb the impact in an athletic quarter-squat.
Make sure to land fully on the box with the whole foot, not with the toes hanging off the edge, and stand fully upright to finish each rep.
Step down one foot at a time rather than jumping backward off the box to protect your joints from repeated landing impact.
Reset your stance in front of the box and repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Front Cable Raise
instructions: Set the pulley of a cable machine to the lowest position and attach a single-handle grip. Select an appropriate, light weight on the stack.
Grasp the handle with your left hand, then turn to face away from the machine so the cable runs behind you, between or beside your legs.

Stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, core braced, and let your working arm hang straight down with the handle in front of your thigh, palm facing back toward your thigh. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso completely still with no swinging or leaning, raise your left arm straight out in front of you with just a slight bend at the elbow, palm facing down.
