Continue lifting until your arm is slightly above parallel to the floor, leading with the wrist and feeling the front delt work. Exhale as you raise.
Pause for a second at the top in the contracted position without shrugging the shoulder up toward your ear.
Inhale and lower the arm slowly and under control back to the starting position in front of your thigh, resisting the cable the whole way.
Avoid using momentum or a backswing to fling the weight up; keep the rep strict and the delt under tension throughout.
Complete all prescribed reps with the left arm, then switch the handle to the right hand and repeat.

name: Front Cone Hops (or hurdle hops)
instructions: Set up a row of several cones, low hurdles, or small barriers in a straight line, spacing them a few feet apart.
Stand in front of the first cone with your feet about shoulder-width apart and core braced. This is your starting position.
Dip into a quick quarter-squat, swinging both arms back to load, then jump with both feet together up and forward over the first cone, swinging your arms forward to drive the jump.
Land softly on the balls of both feet just past the cone, bending your knees and hips to absorb the impact in a controlled athletic landing.
Use that landing as a rebound, immediately springing up and over the next cone with minimal ground-contact time.
Keep your chest up and torso stable throughout; jump just high enough to clear each barrier rather than wasting height.
Continue hopping over each cone in sequence until you have cleared the entire row, then reset and repeat as prescribed.

name: Front Dumbbell Raise
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart, knees softly unlocked, and your weight balanced through the middle of your feet. Hold a dumbbell in each hand resting against the front of your thighs with your palms facing your legs.
Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades down and slightly back, and keep your chest up so your torso stays rigid throughout the set. Avoid arching your lower back.

Rotate your wrists so your palms face down (overhand grip), with the dumbbells horizontal across the front of your thighs. Maintain a slight, fixed bend in your elbows. This is your starting position.

Keeping the torso completely still with no swinging or leaning back, lift the left dumbbell straight forward in a controlled arc, leading with the wrist and keeping the elbow only slightly bent. Exhale as you raise.
Continue raising until your arm is roughly parallel to the floor or just above shoulder height. Do not shrug the trap up or use momentum. Pause for one second and squeeze the front of the shoulder.
Lower the left dumbbell slowly back to your thigh over about two seconds as you inhale, and as it descends begin raising the right dumbbell in the same controlled manner.
Continue alternating arms, keeping each rep smooth and the hips and back motionless, until you have completed the prescribed repetitions for each arm.
Key cues: keep the movement strict, raise only to about shoulder height, and never let your body rock backward to throw the weight up. If you have to swing, the dumbbells are too heavy.

name: Front Incline Dumbbell Raise
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an incline between 30 and 60 degrees. A steeper angle increases the stretch on the front delts; pick one angle and keep it consistent for the set.
Sit back against the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, your head resting on the pad, your back flat against the bench, and your feet planted on the floor for stability.

Let your arms hang straight down in front of you with your palms facing down (overhand grip) and the dumbbells raised about an inch off your thighs. Keep your elbows nearly straight with only a slight fixed bend. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your head, shoulders, and back in firm contact with the bench so you cannot cheat with body english.
Exhale and raise both dumbbells straight up in front of you in a controlled arc, leading with your wrists and keeping your elbows locked in that slight bend.
Continue until the dumbbells are slightly above shoulder level, then pause and squeeze the front delts for one second.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly along the same path back to the starting position, resisting gravity the whole way and stopping just short of your thighs to keep tension on the muscle.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: keep your head down against the bench, do not let your hips or back lift off the pad, and avoid bending the elbows to turn it into a press.

name: Front Leg Raises
instructions: Stand tall beside a sturdy chair, wall, or rack and hold on lightly with one hand for balance. Keep your supporting leg straight but with a soft knee.
Set your posture tall: chest up, shoulders back, core braced, and hips square to the front so you do not rotate during the swing.
Keeping the working leg completely straight, swing it forward and upward in a smooth controlled motion, raising it only as high as your flexibility allows without rounding your lower back.
Without pausing long, reverse the motion and swing the same leg back and down, allowing it to travel behind you as far as your hip mobility permits while keeping the knee straight.
Keep the swing controlled and rhythmic rather than ballistic, and keep your torso upright the whole time instead of leaning to compensate.
Repeat the forward-and-back swing for 5 to 10 reps, then turn around or switch your supporting hand and perform the same number with the other leg.
Key cues: this is a dynamic mobility drill, so increase range gradually over the reps, never force the stretch, and keep your standing knee soft to absorb the motion.

name: Front Plate Raise
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip to shoulder width apart, knees slightly unlocked, and weight centered over your feet.
Hold a single weight plate with both hands gripping the edges at the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock positions, palms facing each other.

Let the plate hang at arm's length in front of your waist with your arms extended and your elbows holding a slight, fixed bend. Your arms stay in this position the entire set. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, pull your shoulders down and back, keep your chest up, and lock your torso in place so there is no swinging or leaning.
Exhale and slowly raise the plate straight up in front of you in a smooth arc until it is just above shoulder level. Keep the elbows fixed and do not bend them as you lift.
Pause and hold the contraction at the top for one second, feeling the front delts work.
Inhale and lower the plate slowly and under control back down to the starting position at your waist, resisting the descent.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: keep your torso stationary, do not use momentum or rock backward, and stop the lift at about shoulder height rather than swinging it overhead.

name: Front Raise And Pullover
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a flat bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor for a stable base and your head supported on the bench.
Grip a barbell with an overhand (palms-down) grip, hands roughly 15 inches apart, and rest the bar across your upper thighs.
Extend your arms straight up toward the ceiling and lock them with a slight, fixed bend at the elbows. Keep this arm angle constant throughout the entire movement. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your lower back in a natural position, pressed lightly toward the bench, so you do not over-arch when the weight goes overhead.

Inhale and lower the barbell in a wide semicircular arc over your face and back toward the floor behind your head, keeping your arms straight, until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor and your palms face the ceiling.
Feel the stretch across your chest and lats at the bottom, but do not drop below a comfortable shoulder range and keep the elbows from collapsing.
Exhale and reverse the same wide arc, pulling the bar back up and over until it returns above your thighs in the starting position. The bar travels roughly 180 degrees over the rep.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: keep the arc wide and the elbows fixed, control the eccentric, and use a moderate weight since the long lever places stress on the shoulders.

name: Front Squat (Clean Grip)
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack slightly below shoulder height. Step under the bar so it rests across the top of your front deltoids, pushing into your clavicles and lightly touching your throat.

Take a clean grip just outside shoulder width, then rotate your elbows up and forward so your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor. Let the bar roll back onto your fingertips, using your fingers only to keep it positioned against the shelf made by your delts.
Drive your elbows high and point them forward; high elbows create the shelf that keeps the bar from rolling off. Keep your chest tall and core braced.

Unrack the bar by pushing up with your legs while straightening your torso, then take one or two steps back. Set your feet about shoulder width apart with your toes turned out slightly. This is your starting position.
Take a big breath, brace your core, and begin the descent by bending at the knees and hips, sitting straight down between your legs while keeping your torso as upright as possible.
Push your knees out in line with your toes using your hips and abductors, and descend until your hamstrings cover your calves or as deep as you can keep an upright torso and neutral spine.
Keep your elbows and chest up the whole way down; if the elbows drop, the bar shifts forward and you will be pulled into a forward lean.
Drive back up by pushing through the middle of your foot and heel, extending the knees and hips together, and exhale as you near the top. Return to the upright starting position.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, keeping the bar racked on your shoulders and the torso vertical on every rep.

name: Front Squats With Two Kettlebells
instructions: Stand with two kettlebells on the floor between or just in front of your feet, with your feet about shoulder width apart and toes slightly turned out.

Clean both kettlebells to your shoulders at the same time: hinge to grip the handles, then extend explosively through your legs and hips and pull the bells up, rotating your wrists under as they reach the shoulders so the bell bodies rest on the backs of your forearms.

Settle into the rack position with your elbows tucked in front of your ribs, the kettlebells resting against your shoulders and forearms, your chest up, and your core braced. This is your starting position.
Look straight ahead, take a breath, and brace your trunk to support the front-loaded weight.
Descend by bending at the hips and knees, sitting down between your legs while keeping your torso upright and your elbows high so the bells stay racked.
Push your knees out in line with your toes as you lower, and squat as low as you can while keeping your head and chest up and your heels flat. Pause briefly at the bottom.
Drive back up through your heels, extending the hips and knees together until you are standing tall again.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: keep the elbows up and the torso vertical, do not let the bells pull you forward, and keep the weight in your heels rather than your toes.

name: Front Two-Dumbbell Raise
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart, knees softly unlocked, and weight balanced over the middle of your feet. Hold a dumbbell in each hand resting on the front of your thighs.
Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades down and back, and keep your chest up so your torso stays rigid for the entire set.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face down (overhand grip), with the dumbbells horizontal in front of your thighs and your elbows holding a slight fixed bend. This is your starting position.
Keeping the torso completely stationary with no swinging, exhale and raise both dumbbells straight forward together in a controlled arc, leading with your wrists.
Continue until both arms are slightly above parallel to the floor, around shoulder height. Do not shrug or use momentum.
Pause and squeeze the front delts for one second at the top.
Inhale and lower both dumbbells slowly back to the starting position over about two seconds, resisting gravity the whole way.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: keep both arms moving together and even, avoid rocking the hips back, and stop at shoulder height rather than swinging higher.

name: Full Range-Of-Motion Lat Pulldown
instructions: Set up at a cable station with two single stirrup handles attached to the high pulleys on each side. Adjust the pulleys high enough that your arms can extend fully overhead.

Stand between the pulleys or sit on a high bench positioned in the center, then grasp the handles with your arms crossed: take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand so the cables crisscross above you, palms facing forward.

Step or sit so there is tension on the cables with your arms extended overhead and slightly out to the sides. Keep your chest up and maintain a slight arch in your lower back. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and pull your shoulder blades down and together to initiate the movement rather than yanking with your arms.
Pull both handles down and outward in a wide arcing path, driving your elbows down and back as if performing a pulldown, exhaling as you pull.
As you pull, rotate your hands so that at the bottom your palms face each other; finish with the handles down near your shoulders or sides and squeeze your lats.
Inhale and return slowly along the same arc to full overhead extension, letting your lats stretch at the top without letting the weight stack slam down.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: lead with the elbows, keep the chest tall, and emphasize the long arcing path that gives this variation its full stretch and contraction.

name: Gironda Sternum Chins
instructions: Grasp a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width underhand (supinated) grip, palms facing you.

Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended, then immediately stick your chest out and lean your torso back away from the bar. You will stay leaned back throughout the entire movement. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and arch your spine, keeping your chest pushed forward and your head tilted back so it leads away from the bar.
Exhale and pull yourself up by driving your elbows down and back, keeping the spine arched and the torso leaning back as you rise.

Continue pulling until your collarbone passes the bar and the bar contacts your lower chest or sternum area. As you reach the top, your hips and legs angle to roughly 45 degrees to the floor and your head ends up near parallel to the floor.
Hold the peak contraction for one second, squeezing the lats and mid-back hard.
Inhale and lower yourself slowly and under control back to the full dead hang in the starting position, maintaining the arch and lean throughout the descent.

Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: keep leaning back and arching so the bar travels to your sternum rather than your chin, and control the negative; this is an advanced movement, so use assistance if you cannot reach sternum height cleanly.

name: Glute Bridge March
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor or a mat with your knees bent and your feet flat on the ground about hip width apart, positioned so your heels are a comfortable distance from your glutes.
Place your arms at your sides, palms down, for stability. Brace your core and tuck your pelvis slightly so your lower back is flat against the floor.
Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips up into a bridge until your shoulders, hips, and knees form a straight line. This is your starting position.
Keeping your hips fully raised and perfectly level, exhale and slowly lift one knee up toward your chest without letting that hip drop or rotate.
Pause briefly with the knee raised, keeping your glutes and core working hard to hold the bridge steady.
Lower that foot back to the floor under control, then repeat with the opposite leg, alternating like a slow march.
Continue alternating for the prescribed reps, keeping the pelvis level and the bridge height constant the entire time.
Key cues: the goal is anti-rotation stability, so do not let your hips sag or twist; if your hips drop, slow down and squeeze the glutes harder on the supporting side.

name: Glute Ham Raise
instructions: Adjust the glute-ham developer so the footplate and pads fit your body: your knees should rest just behind the large pad and your feet should brace firmly against the footplate between the rollers.
Position yourself face down with your feet anchored between the rollers against the footplate, your thighs on the pad, and your body able to pivot at the knees.
Brace your core and keep your back arched and your spine neutral. Start from the bottom with your torso hanging down and your body extended toward the floor.
Begin the raise by flexing your knees and driving your toes hard into the footplate to engage the hamstrings and calves.

Pull your torso up by curling at the knees, keeping your upper body straight and your hips extended, until your body rises to an upright position roughly perpendicular to the floor. Exhale as you raise.
Squeeze the hamstrings and glutes at the top, keeping the spine neutral rather than rounding.
Inhale and lower yourself slowly and under control back to the starting position, resisting the descent the whole way down.

Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: keep the movement smooth, do not let your hips pike or your back round, and control the eccentric; if the full raise is too hard, limit the range and build up over time.

name: Glute Kickback
instructions: Get onto an exercise mat on all fours in a kneeling position. Your hands should be under your shoulders, arms about shoulder width apart, and your knees under your hips.

Set your knees so there is a 90-degree bend between your hamstrings and calves, keep your back flat, your core braced, and your head looking forward or slightly down to keep your neck neutral. This is your starting position.
Exhale and lift your right leg backward and upward, keeping that 90-degree bend in the knee, until your thigh is in line with your back and parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glute hard at the top and hold for one second, with the upper leg parallel to the floor and the calf pointing toward the ceiling.
Inhale and lower your right leg slowly back to the starting position under control, keeping your hips square and your back flat throughout.
Repeat with the left leg, then continue alternating legs until you have performed all the prescribed repetitions for each side.
Key cues: drive the lift with your glute, not your lower back; do not arch or twist your spine to gain height, and keep your hips level rather than rotating toward the working side.

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your toes turned out slightly. Hold a kettlebell by the horns with both hands, cupping it vertically against your upper chest with your elbows tucked in.
Brace your core, keep your chest tall, shoulders down, and your back in a neutral arch. This is your starting position.
Take a breath and descend by bending at the hips and knees, sitting straight down between your legs while keeping your torso as upright as possible.
Push your knees out in line with your toes as you lower, and continue down until your hamstrings reach your calves or as deep as you can keep your heels flat and your spine neutral.
Pause at the bottom and use your elbows to gently press your knees outward, opening up the hips and reinforcing good knee tracking.
Drive back up through your heels, extending your hips and knees together, and exhale as you stand tall again, keeping the kettlebell snug against your chest the whole time.
Repeat for 10 to 20 repetitions. Key cues: keep the weight close to your body and your chest up; if your heels lift or your back rounds, reduce depth or load until you can stay upright.

name: Good Morning
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about shoulder height. Step under it and rack the bar across the rear of your shoulders on your upper traps, the same position as a low-bar power squat, not on top of your shoulders.

Grip the bar securely, pinch your shoulder blades together to create a stable shelf, keep your back tight, and unrack the bar. Step back and set your feet about shoulder width apart with a slight bend in your knees.
Brace your core hard, keep your chest up, and maintain a neutral, arched back with your neck in line with your spine. This is your starting position.
Take a breath and begin the movement by pushing your hips straight back, hinging at the hips while letting your knees stay softly bent.

Lower your torso by bending forward at the hips until your upper body is near parallel to the floor, or as far as you can go while keeping your back flat and feeling a stretch in your hamstrings. Do not round your spine.
Keep the bar path controlled and your weight in your heels and mid-foot; the hips travel backward as the chest travels down.
Reverse the motion by driving your hips forward and squeezing your glutes and hamstrings, extending until you return to the upright starting position. Exhale through the top.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: this is a hip hinge, not a squat or a back-rounding movement, so keep the spine rigid and use a conservative load to protect the lower back.

name: Good Morning off Pins
instructions: Set the safety pins or rack supports at about stomach height. Step under the bar and rack it across the rear of your shoulders on your upper traps, as in a low-bar power squat, not on top of your shoulders.
With the bar racked, bend over so your torso is near parallel to the floor while the bar rests on the pins. The pin height should match this bent-over starting position.

Set your feet about shoulder width apart with knees slightly bent, pinch your shoulder blades together, keep your back tight and arched, your core braced, and your neck in line with your spine. This is your starting position, with the bar dead-stopped on the pins.
Take a breath and brace hard. Begin the rep from this dead stop by driving your hips forward and extending through your glutes and hamstrings.
Continue raising your torso until you are standing fully upright with the weight, keeping your spine neutral and arched the whole way up. Exhale near the top.
Lower the weight slowly and under control back down the same hinge path until the bar settles back onto the pins, and let it come to a complete rest between reps.

Reset your brace and posture on the pins, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions. Key cues: starting from a dead stop removes the stretch reflex, so initiate with the hips and glutes, keep the back rigid, and avoid jerking the bar off the pins.

name: Gorilla Chin/Crunch
instructions: Set up under a fixed chin-up bar that you can reach with your arms extended overhead; the bar should be high enough that your feet clear the floor when you hang.
Grip the bar with a supinated (underhand) grip, palms facing toward you, hands set slightly wider than shoulder width.

Hang from the bar with arms fully extended, then bend your knees to roughly 90 degrees so your calves are parallel to the floor and your thighs hang straight down. Brace your core to stop your body from swinging. This is your starting position.
Exhale and simultaneously begin two movements: pull your chin toward the bar by flexing the biceps and lats while crunching your knees upward toward your chest.
Drive your knees up until they reach chest level, finishing the knee crunch at the exact moment your nose rises to the level of the bar.
Squeeze hard at the top, holding the contracted position briefly without swinging.
Inhale and lower under control, extending the arms and lowering the knees back to the 90-degree hang in one smooth, slow motion. Avoid dropping suddenly or letting momentum take over.
Keep the body from rocking front-to-back between reps; if you start to swing, pause and re-brace before the next rep.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Groin and Back Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with a tall, upright spine, knees bent and dropped out to the sides, and the soles of your feet pressed together close to your body in a butterfly position.
Interlock your fingers and place them behind your head, elbows pointing out to the sides. This is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly curl your torso downward, rounding forward and drawing your elbows toward the insides of your thighs while gently letting your knees press toward the floor.
Go only to the point of mild tension in the groin and lower back, never to sharp pain, and hold the bottom position for a brief pause.
Inhale and return to the starting position by lifting your head and chest and straightening your back to fully upright.
Move smoothly without bouncing or jerking, controlling both the descent and the return.
Repeat for 10 to 20 controlled repetitions.

name: Groiners
instructions: Begin in a high push-up (front plank) position: hands flat on the floor directly under your shoulders, arms straight, legs extended back, and body forming a straight line from head to heels. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your head up with your gaze slightly forward.
Push off with both feet and jump them forward together, landing flat with both feet planted just outside or next to your hands.
Land softly in a deep squat-like bottom position with hips low, chest up, and back flat, feeling a stretch through the groin and adductors.
Keep your hands planted on the floor throughout and your weight balanced so you do not topple forward.
Jump your feet back to the starting push-up position in one explosive motion, returning to a straight-body plank.
Immediately repeat the jump forward without resting, keeping a steady rhythm.
Continue for 10 to 20 repetitions, maintaining control on each landing to protect the knees and lower back.

name: Hack Squat
instructions: Step into the hack squat machine and place the entire back of your torso flat against the angled back pad, tucking your shoulders snugly under the shoulder pads.
Place your feet on the platform using a shoulder-width stance, toes pointed slightly outward, feet roughly centered on the platform so your knees track over your toes.

Grip the side handles, keep your head up and your back and hips pressed firmly against the pad, then disengage the safety stops by rotating the handles (usually from a front-facing to a diagonal position).
Straighten your legs to lift the carriage without locking the knees out hard. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and inhale as you slowly bend the knees and hips, lowering the carriage under control while keeping your back flat against the pad the entire time.
Descend until the angle between your thighs and calves is slightly less than 90 degrees, meaning your thighs drop just below parallel to the platform.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes; they should not collapse inward, and they should not shoot far past your toes, which would overload the knee joint.
Exhale and drive the carriage back up by pushing primarily through your heels and mid-foot, extending the legs back to the starting position without locking out hard at the top.
Maintain heel contact throughout; do not let your heels rise or your hips peel off the pad.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then re-engage the safety stops before stepping out.

name: Half Moon Pose
instructions: Begin standing, then shift your weight onto your right leg and place your right hand on the floor (or a yoga block) about a foot in front of and slightly outside your right foot.
As you hinge forward at the hips, lift your left leg back and up until it is parallel to the floor, foot flexed, forming a straight line from your head through your raised heel.
Stack your hips by rotating your left hip open toward the ceiling so your pelvis and chest face the side wall rather than the floor.
Keep your standing right leg strong with a micro-bend in the knee, pressing firmly through the foot for a stable base.
Extend your left arm straight up toward the ceiling, stacking the top shoulder over the bottom shoulder, and gaze forward or up toward your raised hand.
Engage your glutes, hamstrings, and core to hold the lifted leg level and resist wobbling.
Hold the balance steadily with smooth, even breathing for the prescribed time.
To exit, lower the raised leg and hand back to standing under control, then repeat balancing on the opposite leg.

name: Hammer Curls
instructions: Stand upright with feet about hip width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length by your sides.
Position the dumbbells with a neutral grip, palms facing your torso (thumbs pointing forward), and tuck your elbows close to your sides. This is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms stationary and pinned to your sides, your core braced, and your chest tall throughout the movement.
Exhale and curl one or both dumbbells upward by bending at the elbow only, keeping the palms facing inward (the neutral hammer position) the entire way.
Continue raising until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell reaches shoulder level.
Squeeze the biceps and forearms hard at the top and hold the contracted position for a brief moment.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position under full control, resisting gravity on the way down.
Do not swing the weights, rock your torso, or let your elbows drift forward; only the forearms should move.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Hammer Grip Incline DB Bench Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of roughly 30 to 45 degrees.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, palms facing each other, then lie back, using your thighs to kick the dumbbells up one at a time into position.
Bring the dumbbells to shoulder level on each side with a neutral (hammer) grip, palms facing each other.
Plant your feet flat on the floor, keep a slight natural arch in your lower back, and pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench. This is your starting position.
Position the dumbbells so the elbows are bent about 90 degrees with the upper arms tucked at a moderate angle rather than fully flared, palms still facing each other.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly and under control to the sides of your chest, keeping the neutral grip and feeling a stretch across the upper chest.
Exhale and press the dumbbells up and slightly inward using your chest, extending the arms until they are nearly locked out at the top while keeping the palms facing each other.
Hold the top contraction for a second, then lower again, taking roughly twice as long to descend as to press up.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows; do not let them bend back under the load.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then return the dumbbells to your thighs and set them down on the floor safely.

name: Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor with both legs extended.
Loop a belt, band, strap, or rope around the ball of one foot and hold an end in each hand.
Keeping the bottom leg flat on the floor, raise the strapped leg upward until the hip is at roughly 90 degrees, leg pointing toward the ceiling. This is your starting position.
Keep the raised leg as straight as comfortable, with only a slight bend in the knee if needed.
Gently pull on the strap to draw the leg slightly closer to your torso, creating tension through the hamstrings and calf.
Stop at the point of mild, comfortable stretch tension, not pain, and keep both hips flat on the floor.
Hold the stretch for 10 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly and relaxing into it.
Release the leg under control, then repeat with the other leg.

name: Hamstring-SMR
instructions: Sit on the floor and place a foam roller under the backs of your upper thighs (just below the glutes), legs extended out in front of you over the roller.
Place your hands flat on the floor behind or to the sides of your hips to support your weight. This is your starting position.
Press through your hands to lift your hips off the floor, shifting most of your body weight onto the roller; to increase pressure, stack one leg over the other and roll a single leg at a time.
Relax the hamstrings of the leg being rolled so the muscle can release into the roller.
Using your hands and supporting leg, slowly roll back and forth so the roller travels from just below the glute down to just above the back of the knee.
When you find a tight or tender spot, pause and hold pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly until the tension eases.
Avoid rolling directly over the back of the knee joint.
Switch and repeat the process on the other leg.

name: Handstand Push-Up
instructions: Face a sturdy wall and place both hands flat on the floor a few inches from the wall, slightly wider than shoulder width, with fingers spread for grip.
Kick up one leg at a time into a handstand so your heels rest lightly against the wall and your body is fully inverted, arms locked out.
Stack your wrists, elbows, and shoulders over your hands, brace your core and glutes, and keep your body in a straight, hollow line rather than arching the lower back.
Keep your head in neutral and your gaze toward the floor between your hands so you can spot your landing point. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower under control by bending the elbows, allowing them to travel slightly out and forward, until the top of your head lightly approaches the floor.
Descend slowly and deliberately to protect your head and neck; never crash down.
Exhale and press forcefully back up through your hands, extending the elbows until you return to a full lockout overhead.
Keep your heels lightly touching the wall for balance throughout and avoid excessive arching.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then bring one leg down at a time to exit the handstand under control. Use a spotter when learning.

name: Handstand Push-Ups
instructions: Stand with your back to a sturdy wall, bend forward at the waist, and place both hands flat on the floor at shoulder width, a few inches from the wall.
Kick up one leg at a time against the wall until you are inverted with arms and legs fully extended and your back toward the wall.
Keep your whole body as straight and rigid as possible, bracing the core and glutes, with your head facing the wall rather than looking straight down.
Stack your shoulders directly over your hands and lock the elbows. This is your starting position. Use a spotter if attempting this for the first time.
Inhale and slowly lower yourself toward the floor by bending the elbows until the top of your head almost touches the ground.
Control the descent carefully and deliberately to avoid any head injury; never let yourself drop.
Exhale and push yourself back up slowly through the hands until the elbows are nearly locked out.
Keep your body line straight and your heels resting lightly on the wall for balance throughout.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then lower one leg at a time to come down safely.

name: Hang Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip to shoulder width apart, the barbell held at mid-thigh with a double-overhand or hook grip set at roughly shoulder width.
Set your back flat and tight with the spine fully extended, chest up, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, and torso inclined slightly forward. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep the bar close to your thighs as you prepare to pull.
Aggressively extend through the hips, knees, and ankles in one explosive triple extension, driving the bar upward while keeping it close to your body.
As you reach full extension, violently shrug your shoulders up toward your ears to continue the bar's upward momentum.
Immediately pull yourself under the bar, whipping your elbows up and around fast so they point forward, and rack the bar across the front of your shoulders.
Receive the bar in a partial or full front-squat position, depending on how high it traveled, with the bar resting on your front delts and the hands relaxed.
Drive through your heels to stand fully upright, keeping the torso tall and elbows high, completing the clean.
Lower the bar back to the mid-thigh hang under control to begin the next rep.

name: Hang Clean - Below the Knees
instructions: Stand with feet about hip to shoulder width apart, gripping the barbell with a double-overhand or hook grip at roughly shoulder width.
Lower the bar to a hang position just below the knees by hinging at the hips and pushing them back, keeping a flat, tight back and the spine fully extended.
Keep your chest up, shoulders slightly over or in front of the bar, weight on mid-foot to heel, and the bar close to your shins. This is your starting position.
Brace hard, then aggressively extend through the hips, knees, and ankles, driving the bar upward while keeping it close to your legs.
As you reach full extension, transition into the final pull by violently shrugging the shoulders and flexing the arms with the elbows high and out.
At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down and rotate your elbows under and around the bar.

Receive the bar in a front-squat rack position with the bar on your protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat and the hands relaxed; continue descending into the bottom of the squat to absorb the load.
Drive through your heels to recover to a full standing position, keeping the torso upright and elbows high.
Lower the bar back to below the knees under control for the next repetition.

name: Hang Snatch
instructions: Set a wide (snatch) grip on the barbell with an overhand or hook grip, hands spaced so the bar would sit at your hip crease when standing tall.
Stand with feet directly below your hips, toes turned slightly out, knees slightly bent, and torso inclined forward with the bar resting at the hips.
Set your spine fully extended and flat, chest up, shoulders over the bar, and head facing forward. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, then aggressively extend through the legs and hips, driving the bar upward along the body in an explosive triple extension.
At peak extension, forcefully shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex up and out to the sides to keep the bar rising and close.
As the bar peaks, move your feet into the receiving stance and forcefully pull yourself down and under the bar while punching it overhead.
Receive the bar overhead with arms fully extended and locked, dropping into an overhead squat as low as possible to catch it, keeping the bar stacked over the mid-foot.
Stabilize the bar overhead with active shoulders, then stand up fully out of the overhead squat to complete the lift.
Lower the weight back to the hang position at the hips under control before the next rep.

name: Hang Snatch - Below Knees
instructions: Set a wide (snatch) grip on the barbell with an overhand or hook grip, hands spaced so the bar sits at the hip crease when standing tall.
Stand with feet directly below your hips, toes turned slightly out, then hinge to lower the bar to a hang just below the knees with knees slightly bent and torso inclined forward.
Keep your spine fully extended and flat, chest up, shoulders over the bar, weight on mid-foot, and head facing forward. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, then aggressively extend through the legs and hips, accelerating the bar upward and keeping it close to your body.
At peak extension, forcefully shrug the shoulders and let the elbows flex up and out to the sides to continue driving the bar.
As the bar peaks, move your feet into the receiving stance and forcefully pull yourself down and under the bar while punching it overhead.
Receive the bar overhead with arms fully extended and locked, dropping into an overhead squat as low as needed to catch it with the bar stacked over the mid-foot.
Stabilize the bar with active, locked-out shoulders, then stand up fully to complete the lift.
Return the weight to the hang below the knees under control before the next repetition.

name: Hanging Bar Good Morning
instructions: Set a barbell suspended from chains or straps in a rack at roughly stomach height, low enough that you can rack it across your rear delts when bent forward to parallel.
Step under the bar and rack it across the rear of your shoulders (over the rear delts and shoulder-blade shelf, not on top of the traps), as you would for a low-bar power squat.
Set your feet about hip to shoulder width apart, grip the bar firmly, pinch your shoulder blades together, and keep a slight bend in your knees.
Brace your core hard, arch your back, and keep your neck in line with your spine; at the proper bar height you should be close to parallel to the floor when bent over. This is your starting position.
Initiate the lift by driving your hips forward and squeezing your glutes and hamstrings, extending the hips to stand up with the weight.
Stand fully upright while keeping the back flat and the bar stable across the rear shoulders.
Slowly reverse the motion by pushing your hips back and hinging forward, lowering your torso under control until the bar is resting back on the chains or straps.
Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding the lower back at any point; the movement comes from the hips, not the spine.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, letting the chains support the bar at the bottom of each rep.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar and jump or step up to grip it with an overhand grip (palms facing away) set roughly shoulder-width apart; use a full grip with thumbs wrapped, or add straps if grip fatigues before your abs.
Hang at full arm extension with your shoulders pulled down and slightly back so they are not loose in the sockets, ribs tucked, and a slight engagement through your lats to keep you stable.

Bring your legs together and let them hang straight down, then tilt your pelvis slightly backward (posteriorly) so your lower back is not arched; this pre-tensions the abs and is your starting position.
Initiate the movement by curling your pelvis up and under, not by simply lifting the thighs at the hip; think of rolling the bottom of your spine toward your ribcage.
Continue pulling your knees up toward your chest as you exhale, raising the thighs to at least parallel or slightly above while keeping the knees bent at about 90 degrees.
Pause for a moment at the top and squeeze the abdominals hard, keeping your torso stable and avoiding any jerking.
Lower your knees slowly and under control as you inhale, resisting the descent until your legs are fully extended and the pelvis returns to neutral.
Keep the entire movement strict with no swinging or kipping; if your body starts to swing, slow the tempo and shorten the range rather than using momentum.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, maintaining a steady cadence of roughly one to two seconds up and two seconds down.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip (palms away) at a width between shoulder-width and slightly wider; wrap thumbs fully and consider lifting straps if grip is the limiting factor.
Hang at full arm extension with arms straight, then actively pull your shoulder blades down and engage your lats so you are not dead-hanging passively in the joints.
Bring your legs together with feet touching, let them hang straight down, and roll your pelvis slightly backward so the lower back flattens; this is your starting position.
Brace your core and, keeping your legs as straight as possible, raise them in front of you by curling the pelvis and lifting from the abs rather than just flexing the hips.
Continue lifting until your torso and legs form roughly a 90-degree angle (legs near parallel to the floor or higher), exhaling as you rise.
Hold the top contraction for about one second and squeeze the abdominals, keeping the knees only slightly soft to protect the joints.
Lower the legs slowly and with full control as you inhale, returning to the fully extended hanging position without letting them drop.
Avoid any swinging or momentum; if you cannot keep the legs straight, bend the knees slightly to reduce the lever, but never kip.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions with a controlled tempo throughout.

name: Hanging Pike
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip (palms facing away) set slightly wider than shoulder width, keeping your legs and feet together; wrist wraps or straps can help you hold on longer than your abs fatigue.
Hang at full arm extension with shoulders packed down and lats engaged so your torso is stable and not swinging.
Bend your knees to about 90 degrees and bring the upper legs forward so the thighs are roughly parallel to the floor while the calves hang perpendicular to the ground; this is your starting position.
Brace the abdominals and begin pulling your legs upward, simultaneously straightening them out so you fold at the hips into a pike shape.
Continue raising the legs as you exhale until your shins come up near the bar and your legs are as straight as your flexibility allows, aiming to almost touch the bar.
Squeeze the abs hard at the top and pause briefly, keeping the movement controlled rather than thrown.
Lower your legs as slowly as possible while inhaling, re-bending the knees on the way down until you return to the bent-knee starting position.
Keep the torso from swinging at all times by maintaining lat tension; do not use momentum to fling the legs up.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, prioritizing a slow eccentric and a full pike at the top.

name: Heaving Snatch Balance
instructions: Set a lightly loaded barbell across the back of your shoulders as in a high-bar back squat, then take a wide snatch grip on the bar with the hands far out toward the collars.
Set your feet roughly hip-width to slightly wider than hip width with the toes turned out, in the same stance you would use to squat; brace your core and keep the chest tall.
Establish a strong, rigid upper back and lock the bar tight against your traps; this is your starting position for the dip.
Dip straight down by bending the knees a few inches while keeping your torso vertical, like the dip of a push press, keeping weight in the mid-foot to heels.
Drive explosively upward through the legs to briefly unload and slightly elevate the bar off your shoulders, popping it just enough to punch under it.
As the bar floats, aggressively press your arms straight to lock the bar overhead while simultaneously pulling and dropping your body down into a full overhead squat.
Receive the bar locked out overhead with the head pushed slightly forward through the arms, the bar over the mid-foot, in the bottom of a deep squat with an upright torso.
Stabilize the overhead position in the bottom, keeping the elbows locked, lats active, and core braced so the bar does not drift forward or back.
Stand up out of the full squat to a tall finish, keeping the bar locked overhead the entire ascent.
Lower the bar back to the shoulders under control and reset before the next repetition; keep loads light since this is a technique drill for the snatch.

name: Heavy Bag Thrust
instructions: Stand next to a hanging heavy bag in an upright, athletic posture with your feet staggered, one foot forward and one back, and set fairly wide for a stable base.
Place both hands on the bag at about chest height, fingers pointing up or slightly inward, with your elbows bent and tucked, similar to the bottom of a push-up against the bag.
Brace your core, keep your chest up, and load slightly into your back leg; this is your starting position.
Initiate the thrust by rotating powerfully at the waist and driving through your back leg and hips, transferring force up into your arms.
Extend your arms explosively to push the bag forward and away from your body as hard and fast as possible, finishing with a strong triceps and chest contraction.
Exhale sharply at the moment of the push to maximize core bracing and power output.
Let the bag swing away, then receive it as it swings back by reversing the motion, absorbing it with bent elbows and a braced core.
Reload the back leg and waist rotation as the bag returns, and immediately thrust it forward again for the next repetition.
Repeat explosively for the prescribed reps or time, then switch your staggered stance to work the other side.

name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
instructions: Stand tall in an open, flat space with your feet together, posture upright, shoulders relaxed, and core lightly engaged.
Pick a fixed point at eye level straight ahead and keep your gaze on it to aid balance; let your arms hang relaxed or hold them out slightly for stability.
Step one foot directly forward and place its heel touching the toes of the back foot, so the feet line up along a single imaginary straight line.
Transfer your weight smoothly onto the front foot, keeping your hips level and core tight to avoid wobbling to either side.
Bring the back foot forward and place its heel directly against the toes of the now-front foot, continuing the straight-line tightrope pattern.
Move slowly and deliberately, pausing briefly on each step if needed to find your balance before taking the next.
Keep your steps in a perfectly straight line and resist the urge to widen your stance; the narrow base is what trains the stabilizers.
Continue walking heel-to-toe for the prescribed distance or number of steps, then turn carefully and repeat.

name: High Cable Curls
instructions: Set the pulleys on a dual cable station to a high position, near or just above shoulder height, and attach a single handle to each side.
Stand in the center between the two pulleys with your feet shoulder-width apart and your core braced, then grab one handle in each hand with a supinated grip (palms facing up toward you).
Raise and extend your arms out to the sides so your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, forming a T, with palms facing you; this is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms fixed in place and parallel to the floor, curl both handles toward you by bending only at the elbows.
Continue curling until the handles come up next to your ears, flexing the biceps hard and exhaling as you contract.
Hold the peak contraction for about one second and squeeze the biceps, making sure only the forearms have moved.
Slowly straighten your arms back to the extended T starting position as you inhale, resisting the cable on the way out.
Do not let your upper arms drift forward or drop; keep them locked in the horizontal plane the entire set.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, maintaining steady tension on the biceps throughout.

name: Hindu Push-Up
instructions: Begin on the floor in a downward-dog position: hands planted slightly wider than shoulder width, feet about hip-width apart, hips pushed high so your body forms an inverted V.
Straighten your arms and legs, press your chest back toward your thighs, and keep your head between your arms; this is your starting position.
Bend your elbows and swoop your chest down and forward in an arcing scooping motion, lowering your torso as if diving under a low bar.
Continue the arc by driving your chest forward and up while your hips drop toward the floor, transitioning your weight from your shoulders forward over your hands.
Finish in an upward-dog position with arms straight, chest lifted and open, hips low and close to the floor, and thighs off the ground, exhaling as you press up.
Keep the motion fluid and continuous, with the elbows tucking in close as you scoop through the bottom.
Reverse the path by lifting your hips back and pushing your body up and back, retracing the arc to return to the downward-dog start as you inhale.
Keep your core engaged the whole time to protect the lower back, especially in the upward-dog finish where over-arching is a common mistake.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, flowing smoothly between the two positions.

name: Hip Circles
instructions: Get on all fours on the floor with your hands stacked directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, shins and tops of the feet resting down.
Set a neutral spine with your back flat, head in line with your spine, and your core braced to prevent the lower back from sagging or rotating.
Shift a little weight onto the supporting limbs, then lift one knee out to the side, keeping that knee bent at about 90 degrees; this is your starting position.
Begin drawing a large circle in the air with the lifted knee, moving it forward, up and out, then around and back, opening and closing the hip through its full range.
Keep the movement coming from the hip joint while holding your torso and pelvis as still as possible, resisting any twisting through the spine.
Move slowly and deliberately, feeling the hip rotate through the top and bottom of each circle.
Complete the prescribed number of circles in one direction, then reverse and circle in the opposite direction for the same count.
Lower the leg, reset on all fours, and repeat the full set with the other leg.

name: Hip Circles (prone)
instructions: Position yourself on your hands and knees with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips.
Maintain good posture with a flat back, neutral neck, and a braced core so your spine stays stable throughout.
Keeping the knee bent at roughly 90 degrees, raise one leg off the ground out to the side; this is your starting position.
Rotate the thigh bone in an arc from the hip, attempting to trace as large a circle as possible with your knee while keeping the knee angle bent.
Drive the movement entirely from the hip joint, holding your torso and the opposite hip steady so you do not rock or twist the pelvis.
Perform the circles slowly and with control, feeling the abductors and adductors work as the leg opens and crosses.
Complete the prescribed repetitions in one direction, then reverse the circle direction for the same number.
Lower the leg, then repeat the full sequence on the other side.

name: Hip Extension with Bands
instructions: Anchor one end of a resistance band low on a sturdy post or rack, near floor level, and loop or attach the other end securely around one ankle.
Stand facing the anchor point so the band pulls your working leg forward, and step back far enough that there is tension on the band at the start.
Hold onto the post or rack with both hands to stabilize your upper body, keeping your head up, chest tall, and core braced.
Set your standing leg with a slight knee bend for balance, and shift your weight onto it; this is your starting position.
Keeping the working knee straight, drive that leg back behind you in a controlled arc against the band's resistance, leading with the heel.
Continue pressing the leg back as far as your hip extension allows, squeezing the glute hard at the end range and exhaling.
Avoid arching your lower back to gain extra range; the motion should come from the hip and glute, not the spine.
Hold the contracted position briefly, then return the leg slowly to the starting position as you inhale, controlling the band's pull.
Complete the prescribed repetitions, then switch the band to the other ankle and repeat.

name: Hip Flexion with Band
instructions: Anchor one end of a resistance band low on a sturdy post or rack near floor level, and attach the other end securely around one ankle.
Stand facing away from the anchor point so the band pulls your working leg backward, and step forward enough to create tension at the start.
Stand tall with your head and chest up, core braced, and hold a rack or wall lightly with one hand for balance if needed.
Set your standing leg with a slight knee bend and shift your weight onto it; this is your starting position.
Drive the working knee up and forward against the band's resistance, raising the thigh until the hip reaches about 90 degrees of flexion.
Pause at the top with the thigh roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your torso upright and avoiding any forward lean or rounding.
Exhale as you lift, and keep the movement controlled rather than swinging the leg up with momentum.
Lower the leg slowly back to the starting position as you inhale, resisting the band on the way down.
Complete the prescribed repetitions, then switch the band to the other ankle and repeat.

name: Hip Lift with Band
instructions: Choose an appropriately strong band and secure it across a power rack at hip height when lying down, anchoring it on pegs on both sides; if there are no pegs, pin each end under heavy dumbbells that will not shift.
Lie on your back in the middle of the rack so the band passes directly over the front of your hips, adjusting your position until it sits centered over the hip crease.
Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart, heels positioned so your shins will be roughly vertical at the top of the lift.
Rest your hands on the floor at your sides or hold the band in place over your hips, and keep your shoulders and upper back flat on the ground; this is your starting position.
Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips upward, pushing up into the band's resistance.
Raise your hips as high as you can until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees, squeezing your glutes hard and exhaling at the top.
Avoid arching your lower back to gain height; the lift should come from the glutes and hips finishing at full extension, not from the spine.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your hips slowly and under control back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, keeping the shoulders pinned to the floor throughout.

name: Hollow Body Hold
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended together and your arms reaching overhead on the floor.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor by tilting your pelvis posteriorly and engaging your abdominals; this contact must be maintained the entire hold.
Brace your core, then simultaneously lift your shoulder blades and head off the floor and raise your straight legs a few inches up.
Reach your extended arms back past your ears and point your toes, creating a long, dished banana shape with only your lower back and hips in contact with the floor.
The lower your arms and legs are to the floor, the harder the hold; raise them higher to make it easier if your lower back starts to lift.
Keep your ribs pulled down and avoid letting your lower back arch or pop off the floor, which is the most common mistake.
Hold the dished position steady while breathing in a shallow, controlled manner so your core stays braced.
Maintain the shape for the prescribed time, then lower your arms and legs down with control to finish.

name: Hollow Hold to Plank Shoulder Tap
instructions: Set up in a high plank with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms straight, and feet about hip-width apart for a stable base.
Form a straight line from head to heels by squeezing your glutes, bracing your abs, and keeping your hips level with your shoulders, not sagging or piking up.
Set your shoulder blades down and slightly apart, push the floor away to keep the upper back active, and grip the floor with your fingers; this is your starting position.
Shift your weight subtly and lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder, keeping your hips and torso completely square to the floor.
Resist the natural tendency for your hips to rotate or rock toward the supporting arm; widening your feet makes this easier and a narrower stance makes it harder.
Return the tapping hand to the floor under control, then repeat the tap with the other hand on the opposite shoulder.
Keep your breathing steady and your core braced throughout so the spine and pelvis stay rigid as a single unit.
Continue alternating shoulder taps at a slow, controlled pace for the prescribed time or repetitions.

name: Hollow Rock
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat and get into a hollow-body position with your arms extended overhead and your legs raised straight with toes pointed.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor by tilting the pelvis, then lift your shoulder blades and legs so only your lower back and hips contact the ground, forming a dished shape.
Brace your abs hard and keep your body rigid from fingertips to toes; this tight hollow shape is what you will rock on.
Initiate a gentle rocking motion by shifting your weight up toward your shoulders and then back toward your hips, rocking along your curved spine.
Move as a single solid unit, keeping your arms and legs in the same fixed position relative to your torso throughout the rock.
Keep your lower back pressed down so it stays the contact point; do not let the back arch or the shape break as you rock.
Use a small, controlled range driven by your core rather than flailing the limbs to generate momentum.
Continue rocking smoothly back and forth for the prescribed repetitions or time, maintaining the tight hollow shape the entire set.

name: Hug A Ball
instructions: Sit on the floor with an exercise ball positioned directly in front of you and a clear space around you so the ball cannot roll into anything.
Straddle the top of the ball so it sits between your thighs, then walk your feet outward and slowly lower your hips toward the floor, allowing your chest to drape forward over the ball.
Plant both feet flat on the floor, roughly hip-to-shoulder width apart, and adjust their position so your knees stack directly over your ankles for a stable base.
Wrap both arms around the ball and pull it gently into your chest and torso, hugging it firmly so it cannot roll away and tip you backward.
Let your lower back round gently over the curve of the ball and allow your spine to relax into a comfortable, supported flexion rather than forcing the stretch.
Breathe slowly and deeply, exhaling as you sink a little deeper into the hug, and feel a gentle stretch spread across the lower back and glutes.
Hold this relaxed position for 20 to 30 seconds, keeping a firm grip on the ball the entire time so it never slips out from under you.
To exit, walk your feet back in, press your hands into the ball, and slowly roll back up to a seated position under control.

name: Hug Knees To Chest
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat or other padded surface with your legs extended and arms resting at your sides.
Keep your head, shoulders, and the back of your pelvis relaxed and in contact with the floor to start in a neutral position.
Bend both knees and draw them up toward your chest, lifting your feet off the floor in a slow, controlled motion.
Reach your arms around your shins and clasp your hands underneath the knees rather than over the top of them, which protects the knee joints from excess compression.
Gently pull your knees in toward your shoulders and chest, feeling a comfortable stretch across the lower back and glutes.
Keep your tailbone heavy toward the floor and avoid yanking; the pull should be steady and gradual, never forceful or bouncy.
Breathe slowly and deeply, exhaling as you ease the knees a little closer, and let the lower back muscles soften and release.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then slowly lower your feet back to the floor and extend your legs to finish.

name: Hurdle Hops
instructions: Set up a row of low hurdles or small barriers in a straight line, spacing them roughly two to three feet apart, and choose a height you can clear comfortably and safely.
Stand facing the first hurdle with your feet about shoulder-width apart, weight balanced on the balls of your feet, and a small bend in your knees.
Bring your arms back and hinge slightly at the hips and knees into an athletic loaded position; this is your starting position.
Swing both arms forward and explode upward off both feet simultaneously, driving through the balls of your feet to jump over the first hurdle.
Tuck your knees up enough to clear the barrier and keep your feet level and together as you travel over it.
Land softly on the balls of both feet just past the hurdle, immediately bending your knees and hips to absorb the impact and protect your joints.
Minimize ground contact time by reacting quickly off the landing, using the rebound to spring straight into the next jump.
Continue jumping over each hurdle in succession with the same explosive, springy rhythm until you have cleared the entire row.
Keep your chest up and core braced throughout, and never let your knees cave inward on landing; reset and walk back to repeat for the prescribed sets.

name: Hyperextensions (Back Extensions)
instructions: Set up at a 45-degree or horizontal hyperextension bench and adjust the upper hip pad so its top edge sits just below your hip bones, allowing your torso to bend freely at the waist.
Lie face down and position the front of your thighs and hips flat against the pad, then hook your ankles securely under the footpads so your legs are anchored.
Straighten your body into a single line from head to heels and engage your glutes, hamstrings, and core to support the spine.
Cross your arms in front of your chest, or place your hands lightly behind your head, and keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor; this is your starting position.
For added resistance, hug a weight plate against your chest under your crossed arms.
Inhale and bend forward slowly at the waist, lowering your torso toward the floor while keeping your back flat and your spine long.
Continue down only as far as you can without rounding your lower back, stopping when you feel a comfortable stretch in the hamstrings.
Exhale and raise your torso back up by contracting the glutes and lower back until your body forms a straight line again.
Stop at the neutral straight-line position; do not arch or hyperextend past it, as this overloads the lumbar spine.
Move smoothly under control and never swing or jerk the torso, then repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Hyperextensions With No Hyperextension Bench
instructions: Position yourself face down on a flat bench and slide forward until your hips reach the edge and your entire upper body can hang off the end toward the floor.
Have a partner firmly hold your legs and ankles down, or anchor your feet under a heavy, secure object, so your lower body stays pinned to the bench.
Straighten your body so it forms one line from head to heels, and engage your glutes, hamstrings, and core to keep the spine stable.
Cross your arms over your chest, or place your hands behind your head, and keep your neck neutral; this is your starting position.
For extra resistance, hold a light weight plate against your chest under your crossed arms.
Inhale and bend forward slowly at the waist, lowering your torso toward the floor while keeping your back flat throughout.
Lower until your torso nearly touches the floor or you feel a good stretch in the hamstrings, whichever comes first, never allowing the lower back to round.
Exhale and raise your torso back up by contracting the glutes and lower back until your body is straight again.
Stop at the straight-line position without arching past it, and avoid any swinging or jerking to protect the spine.
Note the range of motion is shorter than on a dedicated hyperextension bench due to the bench height, then repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Iliotibial Tract-SMR
instructions: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie down on your side, positioning the roller under the outside of your bottom thigh between the hip and the knee.
Stack your body so your hip, shoulder, and the side of your leg are aligned, and prop yourself up on your bottom forearm and elbow for support.
Cross your top leg in front of you and plant that foot flat on the floor to help control how much pressure you apply, or stack the legs for more intensity.
Lower as much of your body weight as you can tolerate onto the bottom leg, and consciously relax the muscles of the leg being rolled.
Slowly roll along the outside of your thigh from just below the hip down toward just above the knee, using your supporting arm and top foot to drive the motion.
When you reach a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly until the tension eases.
Avoid rolling directly over the knee joint or the hip bone, keeping the work on the soft tissue of the outer thigh.
Continue rolling the full length for 30 to 60 seconds, then switch sides and repeat on the opposite leg.

name: Inchworm
instructions: Stand tall with your feet together or no more than hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides.
Keeping your legs as straight as possible, hinge at the hips and bend forward to place both hands flat on the floor directly in front of your feet; this is your starting position.
Begin walking your hands forward one at a time, alternating left and right, while keeping your legs straight and bending only at the hips.
Continue walking your hands out until your body is fully extended into a straight, parallel plank or push-up position.
Brace your core and keep your hips from sagging so your body stays in a rigid straight line at the top.
Now hold your hands in place and take small steps forward with your feet, moving only a few inches at a time, keeping your legs straight throughout.
Feel the stretch build in the hamstrings and calves as your feet creep closer and your hips rise.
Keep walking your feet in until they are as close to your hands as your flexibility allows, then either stand up to reset or walk your hands back out to repeat for the prescribed reps.
Move slowly and with control, breathing steadily, and never bounce or force the range of motion.

name: Incline Barbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an incline between 45 and 75 degrees and load a barbell, or use an EZ-bar for a more wrist-friendly grip.
Grip the bar with an overhand (palms-down) grip set slightly narrower than shoulder width, keeping the wrists firm and stacked.
Lie back against the incline bench with your head, upper back, and hips supported, and your feet planted for stability.
Press the bar up and bring it overhead so your arms are extended and roughly in line with your torso above your head, elbows tucked in; this is your starting position.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and close to your head, inhale and lower the bar in a semicircular arc behind your head by bending only at the elbows.
Continue lowering until your forearms approach your biceps and you feel a stretch in the triceps, allowing no movement at the shoulders.
Exhale and extend the elbows to drive the bar back to the starting position, squeezing the triceps hard at the top.
Hold the fully contracted position for a one-second count without locking out harshly or letting the elbows flare wide.
Move under control with a slow, deliberate lowering phase, and keep the elbows pointed forward, not flaring out, throughout.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then carefully bring the bar back to your thighs or rack it.

name: Incline Bench Pull
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to roughly a 30-degree incline and grab a dumbbell in each hand, or use a barbell positioned under the bench.
Lie face down (prone) on the bench so your chest and torso are fully supported and your head extends just past the top edge.
Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor with the dumbbells fully extended beneath you.
Rotate your wrists so you have a pronated, palms-down grip on the weights.
Flare your elbows out to the sides so your upper arms are positioned away from your ribs; this is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the dumbbells up like a reverse bench press, bending at the elbows and driving the upper arms upward while the forearms hang.
Continue pulling until your upper arms reach the level of your back and your torso and arms form a wide T shape, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Hold the contracted position at the top for a one-second count, focusing on the middle back and rear shoulders rather than the biceps.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly back to the fully extended starting position under control.
Keep your chest pinned to the bench and avoid jerking or using momentum, then repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Incline Cable Chest Press
instructions: Set the two cable pulleys to a low or mid-low position and attach a single handle to each, then select an appropriate weight on each stack.
Place an incline bench set to about 30 to 45 degrees between the two towers, or use the machine's seat, facing away from the pulleys.
Grasp a handle in each hand and sit back against the incline with your head and chest up and your feet planted firmly.
Position your upper arms at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso with your elbows bent to about 90 degrees and the handles near your chest; this is your starting position.
Retract and set your shoulder blades down and back, and brace your core to keep your torso stable against the bench.
Exhale and press the handles up and forward along an arc, extending through the elbows until your hands come together in front of your upper chest.
Squeeze your chest at full extension and pause briefly, keeping a slight bend in the elbows rather than harshly locking out.
Inhale and return the handles slowly to the starting position, keeping constant tension on the cables and not letting the weight stacks rest.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted throughout and avoid shrugging or letting the elbows drift too high, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Incline Cable Flye
instructions: Set both cable pulleys to the lowest position possible, below the level of your torso, and attach a single handle to each side.
Place an incline bench set to about 45 degrees centered between the two pulleys, and select an equal, moderate weight on each stack.
Grasp a handle in each hand, sit down, and lie back against the incline with your feet planted and your back firmly supported.
Press the handles up and bring your hands together at arm's length above your upper chest with a slight, fixed bend in your elbows; this is your starting position.
Set your shoulder blades back and down and brace your core to keep the torso stable.
Inhale and open your arms out and down in a wide arc to both sides, maintaining the same slight elbow bend, until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Keep the movement isolated to the shoulder joint only; the elbow angle should not change and the arms should not press.
Exhale and bring your arms back up along the exact same wide arc, squeezing the chest muscles together as the handles meet.
Hold the contracted position for a one-second count at the top, keeping constant tension from the low cables.
Avoid letting your elbows straighten or dropping the arms too far past a comfortable stretch, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench With Palms Facing In
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and select a pair of dumbbells.
Sit on the bench and rest a dumbbell on top of each thigh, holding them with your palms facing each other in a neutral grip.
Lie back against the incline while using your thighs to kick the dumbbells up one at a time until you can hold them at shoulder level.
Keep a neutral grip with palms facing each other, flare the elbows out so the upper arms are in line with the shoulders, and bend the elbows to about 90 degrees; this is your starting position.
Plant your feet firmly, set your shoulder blades back and down, and keep a natural arch in your lower back.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly down toward the sides of your upper chest, keeping the palms facing in and maintaining full control.
Lower until you feel a comfortable stretch across the chest without letting the shoulders roll forward.
Exhale and press the dumbbells back up using your chest, driving them up and slightly together until your arms are extended over the upper chest.
Hold the contracted position for a second at the top, then begin the next descent, aiming to lower roughly twice as slowly as you press.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then bring the dumbbells back to your thighs and set them down safely to finish.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of about 45 to 60 degrees and grab a dumbbell in each hand.
Sit back fully against the incline with your back supported, your head resting against the bench, and your feet planted on the floor.
Let your arms hang straight down at your sides so the dumbbells are at arm's length, and rotate your wrists so your palms face forward (supinated grip); this is your starting position.
Keep your upper arms pinned close to your torso and stationary; the elbows should stay behind the line of your body throughout because of the incline.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells upward by bending only at the elbows, contracting the biceps as you lift and keeping the upper arms still.
Continue curling until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells reach shoulder level, squeezing hard at the top.
Hold the peak contraction for a one-second count, feeling the stretch and tension that the incline position adds to the biceps.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly back to the fully extended starting position under control.
Avoid swinging the weights or letting the elbows drift forward, and do not let the dumbbells drop quickly, then repeat for the recommended repetitions.

name: Incline Dumbbell Flyes
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of no more than 30 degrees and grab a dumbbell in each hand.
Sit on the bench, rest the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and use your thighs to help bring them up to chest level.
Press the dumbbells up and extend your arms above you with a slight, fixed bend in the elbows.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face each other with the pinky fingers next to each other and the dumbbells nearly touching; this is your starting position.
Plant your feet, set your shoulder blades back and down, and brace your core for a stable base.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping the slight elbow bend fixed and rotating the wrists so the palms turn upward.
Continue until your arms are out to your sides level with the bench and you feel a comfortable stretch across the chest, with the palms facing the ceiling.
Exhale and bring the dumbbells back up along the same wide arc, rotating the wrists back so the pinky fingers come together again and squeezing the chest.
Keep all motion at the shoulder joint and wrists only, with no bending or straightening at the elbows during the rep.
Hold the squeeze briefly at the top, then repeat for the recommended repetitions and set the dumbbells down safely when finished.

name: Incline Dumbbell Flyes - With A Twist
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of no more than 30 degrees and grab a dumbbell in each hand.
Sit on the bench, rest the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and use your thighs to help bring them up to chest level.
Press the dumbbells up and extend your arms above you with a slight, fixed bend in the elbows.
