Rotate your wrists so your palms face you with the pinky fingers next to each other; this is your starting position.
Plant your feet, set your shoulder blades back and down, and brace your core for stability.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping the slight elbow bend fixed and rotating the wrists until the palms face each other and then turn upward at the bottom.
Continue until your arms are level with the bench and you feel a stretch across the chest, with the palms facing the ceiling.
Exhale and reverse the motion, bringing the dumbbells back up along the same arc while twisting the wrists so the pinky fingers come together again at the top.
Keep the movement isolated to the shoulder joint and wrists, with the elbow angle staying constant throughout, and squeeze the chest as the dumbbells meet.
Hold the contraction briefly, then repeat for the recommended repetitions and lower the dumbbells safely when done.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and select a pair of dumbbells.
Sit on the bench and rest a dumbbell on top of each thigh, holding them with your palms facing each other.
Lie back against the incline while using your thighs to kick the dumbbells up one at a time until you can hold them at shoulder width.

Rotate your wrists forward so your palms face away from you, then position the dumbbells at the sides of your upper chest with elbows bent and flared at about 45 degrees; this is your starting position.
Plant your feet firmly, set your shoulder blades back and down, and maintain a natural arch in your lower back.
Keeping full control of the weights, exhale and press the dumbbells straight up with your chest until your arms are extended over your upper chest.
Lock your arms at the top and hold the contraction for a one-second count, keeping the dumbbells from clanging together.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly back down toward the sides of your chest, aiming to take about twice as long lowering as you took pressing.
Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows and avoid letting the shoulders roll forward at the bottom.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then bring the dumbbells back to your thighs and set them on the floor safely to finish.

name: Incline Hammer Curls
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to roughly a 45 to 60 degree incline. Grab a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip, with your palms facing each other and your thumbs pointing forward.
Sit back against the bench so your head, upper back, and glutes are pressed firmly into the pad. Keep your feet flat on the floor for a stable base.

Let both arms hang straight down toward the floor at your sides, fully extended. The incline pulls your arms slightly behind your torso, which is what stretches the biceps and forearms in this variation. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, set your shoulders down and back, and keep your upper arms still and vertical throughout. Only your forearms should move.
Exhale and curl both dumbbells upward by flexing at the elbows, maintaining the neutral grip the entire way up so it looks like you are swinging a hammer.
Continue until your forearms are roughly vertical and the dumbbells are near your shoulders. Squeeze the biceps and brachialis hard at the top.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly and under control over about 2 to 3 seconds, resisting the weight back down to the full stretch.
Do not let your elbows drift forward or swing your upper arms; keeping them pinned to your sides isolates the biceps. Do not bounce out of the bottom.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Inner Biceps Curl
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to about a 45 to 60 degree incline. Take a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand (supinated) grip so your palms face forward, away from you.
Sit back and rest your head and upper back against the pad, with your feet planted flat on the floor for stability.

Let your arms hang straight down and slightly behind your torso, fully extended, palms facing forward. This deep stretch on the biceps is the point of the incline position. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your upper arms roughly fixed in line with your side deltoids; you will curl out and up rather than straight up the front.
Exhale and curl both dumbbells outward and upward in a wide arc, keeping your forearms tracking out to the sides in line with your shoulders.
Continue curling until the dumbbells reach shoulder height out to the sides of your delts; the finish position should resemble a front double-biceps pose.
Pause and squeeze the biceps hard at the top for a full second, focusing on the contraction of the inner (short) head.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly back along the exact same outward arc to the full stretch, controlling the weight the whole way.
Avoid letting the dumbbells drift in front of your body or using momentum; the wide path is what biases the inner biceps.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Incline Push-Up
instructions: Stand facing a bench, box, or other sturdy elevated platform. The higher the surface, the easier the exercise, so pick a height appropriate to your strength.
Place both hands on the front edge of the platform slightly wider than shoulder width, fingers pointing forward and arms straight.
Walk your feet back until your body forms one straight line from head to heels, weight on the balls of your feet. Arms should be roughly perpendicular to your torso. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips neither sag nor pike up. Keep your neck neutral, eyes down at the platform.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the edge of the platform, letting your elbows travel back at about a 45 degree angle to your torso rather than flaring straight out.
Lower until your chest is just above or lightly touches the edge, keeping your body rigid and straight the entire time.
Exhale and press through your palms to push your body back up until your arms are fully extended.
Keep the whole body locked as one unit; do not let your hips drop first or your lower back arch. Move at a controlled tempo.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Push-Up Close-Grip
instructions: Set a Smith machine bar or find a sturdy elevated bar or platform at an appropriate height; a higher bar makes the movement easier.
Place both hands on the bar close together, roughly shoulder width or narrower, with your hands nearly touching. A close grip shifts the emphasis onto the triceps.
Walk your feet back until your arms and body form one straight line from head to heels, weight on the balls of your feet, arms fully extended. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your torso rigid; do not let your hips sag or pike.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the bar, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides rather than flaring outward. Tucked elbows maximize triceps involvement.
Lower under control until your chest is at or just above the bar.
Exhale and forcefully extend your elbows to press yourself back up to the fully extended starting position.
Keep your body straight as a plank throughout and avoid letting the elbows flare wide, which would turn it into a chest exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Push-Up Depth Jump
instructions: Gather a box about 12 inches high and two thick mats or low aerobic steps. This is an advanced plyometric drill, so build a base of regular push-ups first.

Place the two steps on the floor just outside where your shoulders will be, and rest your feet up on the box so your body is in an elevated, incline push-up position with your hands on the floor just inside the steps.
Set your body in one straight line from head to heels, core braced and glutes tight, hands slightly wider than shoulders. This is your starting position.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor under control, loading the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
Explosively reverse direction and push hard enough that your hands leave the floor.
While airborne, quickly move your hands outward onto the raised steps and let your elbows bend to absorb the landing softly, like a shock absorber.
Without pausing, push off the steps explosively again and bring your hands back down inside onto the floor, again bending the elbows to cushion the impact.
Keep your torso rigid throughout each rep; never let your hips sag on landing, which strains the lower back. Land soft and controlled, not stiff.
Repeat the cycle for the desired number of explosive repetitions, stopping the set once you can no longer absorb landings cleanly.

name: Incline Push-Up Medium
instructions: Set a Smith machine bar or find a sturdy elevated bar or platform at an appropriate height; choose a higher bar to make the movement easier.
Place both hands on the bar about shoulder width apart, fingers wrapped over the bar, arms straight.
Walk your feet back until your arms and body form one straight line from head to heels, weight on the balls of your feet, arms fully extended. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips stay level with your shoulders; do not let them sag or pike.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the bar, letting the elbows travel back at about a 45 degree angle to your torso.
Lower under control until your chest is at or just above the bar.
Exhale and press through your palms to extend your elbows and push yourself back up to full arm extension.
Keep the whole body locked straight as one unit throughout and move at a steady, controlled tempo.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Push-Up Reverse Grip
instructions: Set a Smith machine bar or find a sturdy elevated bar at an appropriate height; a higher bar makes the movement easier.
Grip the bar with both hands palms up (an underhand, supinated grip), hands about shoulder width apart. The reverse grip increases emphasis on the upper and inner chest.
Walk your feet back until your arms and body form one straight line from head to heels, weight on the balls of your feet, arms fully extended. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your torso rigid and flat.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the bar under control, keeping your wrists stable and elbows tracking back, not flaring wide.
Lower until your chest is at or just above the bar.
Exhale and press through your hands to extend your elbows and return to the fully extended starting position.
Keep your body straight as a plank throughout; go gently at first as the reverse grip places more demand on the wrists and elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Incline Push-Up Wide
instructions: Set a Smith machine bar or find a sturdy elevated bar at an appropriate height; choose a higher bar to make it easier.
Place both hands on the bar wider than shoulder width. The wide grip increases stretch and emphasis on the outer chest.

Walk your feet back until your arms and body form one straight line from head to heels, weight on the balls of your feet, arms fully extended and roughly perpendicular to your torso. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips stay in line with your shoulders.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the bar, letting the elbows travel out and back as you descend.
Lower under control until your chest is at or just above the bar, feeling a stretch across the chest.
Exhale and press through your palms to extend your elbows and push back up to full arm extension.
Keep the body straight as one rigid unit throughout; avoid going so wide that your shoulders feel strained.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Intermediate Groin Stretch
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor with both legs extended straight. Loop a belt, rope, or resistance band around the arch of one foot, holding both ends in your hands.
Keep the opposite leg extended and relaxed flat on the floor as an anchor.
Keeping the strapped leg fairly straight, use the belt to guide that leg out to the side, lowering it toward the floor as far as your flexibility allows. This is your starting position.
Pull gently on the belt to increase the stretch, feeling tension along the inner thigh (groin) and hamstring of the strapped leg.
Keep both hips flat on the floor and the resting leg from rolling outward, so the stretch stays in the target leg rather than letting the whole pelvis twist.
Breathe slowly and hold the stretch for 10 to 20 seconds without bouncing.
Slowly bring the leg back to center, then repeat on the other side.

name: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended. Loop a rope, belt, or band around the arch of one foot and hold both ends over the same-side shoulder with both hands.
Rest your forehead or chin lightly on the floor and keep your hips square to the ground to start.
Bend the knee of the leg to be stretched, bringing your heel up toward your glutes, and use both hands to pull on the belt to draw the heel closer.

Continue pulling so that both your knee and that hip lift slightly off the floor, extending the hip back. You should feel a strong stretch through the front of the thigh (quadriceps) and the hip flexor.
Keep your lower back from over-arching and your hips from rotating; the stretch should come from hip extension and knee flexion, not from twisting.
Breathe slowly and hold the position for 10 to 20 seconds without bouncing.
Release gently, lower the leg, and repeat on the other leg.

name: Internal Rotation with Band
instructions: Anchor a resistance band around a sturdy post at about elbow height when standing. Stand with your right side facing the post, a couple of feet away so there is slight tension on the band.
Grasp the free end of the band with your right hand and pin your right elbow firmly against your side, bent to 90 degrees.
For better positioning, tuck a rolled towel or foam pad between your elbow and your ribs and squeeze it in place; this keeps the upper arm fixed and isolates the rotator cuff.
Start with your forearm rotated outward, away from your torso, so the band is stretched. Keep your wrist straight and your shoulder down and relaxed. This is your starting position.
Exhale and rotate your forearm inward across your body in a forehand motion, pulling the band toward your stomach while keeping the elbow glued to your side.
Continue rotating as far as you comfortably can, then pause and squeeze.
Inhale and slowly return your forearm back out to the starting position under control, resisting the band the whole way.
Keep your elbow pinned and your torso still throughout; do not let your shoulder hunch forward or your trunk twist to cheat the rotation.
Complete the desired reps, then turn around and repeat with the left arm.

name: Inverted Row
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack or use a Smith machine bar at about waist height. The lower the bar, the harder the exercise.
Lie on your back underneath the bar and take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width.

Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended, body straight from head to heels, and your heels on the floor. Bend your knees and plant your feet flat if you want an easier version. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a rigid, straight plank; your hips should not sag toward the floor.
Exhale and pull your chest toward the bar by bending your elbows, driving them down and back.
As you pull, retract and squeeze your shoulder blades together to engage the mid-back rather than just pulling with the arms.
Continue until your chest nearly touches the bar, then pause and hold the contraction briefly.
Inhale and lower yourself slowly and under control until your arms are fully extended again, maintaining the straight body line.
Keep your body rigid the entire set; avoid leading with your hips or letting your chin jut to reach the bar.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Inverted Row with Straps
instructions: Hang a pair of suspension straps or a rope from a rack, bar, or other stable overhead anchor so the handles sit at roughly waist to hip height.
Grasp one handle in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and walk your feet forward until you are hanging back beneath the anchor.
Extend your arms fully and set your body in a straight line from head to heels with your heels on the floor. Bend your knees and plant your feet for an easier version. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body stays rigid and straight; the straps will let your hands rotate, so keep your shoulders set and stable.
Exhale and pull your chest up toward your hands by bending your elbows and driving them down and back.
Retract and squeeze your shoulder blades together at the same time to load the mid-back and lats rather than just the arms.
Continue until your chest reaches your hands, pause, and squeeze the back hard.
Inhale and lower yourself slowly under control until your arms are fully extended, keeping the body line straight the whole time.
Do not let your hips sag or use a jerking motion; control the unstable straps throughout each rep.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Iron Cross
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet about shoulder width apart, knees slightly soft. This is a dynamic, full-body coordination drill, so start with light dumbbells.
Brace your core and keep your chest up, spine neutral, and gaze forward. This is your starting position.

In one coordinated motion, swing both arms out to your sides and up to shoulder height so your body forms a cross or T shape, while simultaneously squatting down by sitting your hips back and bending your knees.
Keep your arms roughly straight as they rise and let your shoulder blades set; the dumbbells should reach about shoulder level at the bottom of the squat.
Keep your weight in your mid-foot and heels and your knees tracking over your toes as you descend; do not let your lower back round.
Reverse the motion smoothly, lowering your arms back to your sides as you stand up out of the squat to return to the start.
Coordinate the arms and legs so they begin and finish together, moving at a controlled tempo rather than flinging the weights.
Keep the dumbbells light enough to maintain control of both the arm raise and the squat throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Iron Crosses (stretch)
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended and your arms stretched straight out to the sides at shoulder level, palms pressed flat to the floor.
Keep your chest and palms anchored to the floor; they will act as your stable base throughout. This is your starting position.
Bend one knee and rotate at the hip to swing that leg across the back of your body, reaching the foot toward the floor near the opposite hand.
Allow your hips to twist while keeping your upper body and palms pinned down, feeling a stretch through the lower back, hip, and front of the thigh.
Promptly return that leg to the starting position, then repeat immediately with the other leg, swinging it across toward the opposite hand.
Move in a smooth, controlled rhythm rather than forcing the range; this is a dynamic mobility drill, not a held static stretch.
Continue alternating sides for 10 to 20 total repetitions.

name: Isometric Chest Squeezes
instructions: Stand or sit tall with a neutral spine, chest up, and shoulders relaxed down and back.
Bend both arms to about a 90 degree angle and bring your hands together in front of the middle of your chest.
Open your hands and press the palms flat together, with your fingers pointing forward (perpendicular to your torso) so your forearms are roughly level. This is your starting position.
Begin pressing your palms firmly against each other while actively contracting your chest muscles, as if trying to crush something between your hands.
Start with gentle tension and gradually build to a maximal squeeze; keep breathing normally throughout rather than holding your breath.
Hold the peak contraction for the recommended number of seconds, focusing on squeezing the chest rather than just the hands.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears and your elbows up so the tension stays in the chest.
Slowly release the tension, rest for the recommended time, and repeat for the desired number of holds.

name: Isometric Neck Exercise - Front And Back
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your spine neutral, shoulders relaxed and down, and your head erect facing straight forward with your chin level (not tucked or jutting).
Interlace your fingers or place both palms flat against your forehead with your elbows pointing forward and slightly down.
Brace your neck and gently begin pushing your head forward into your hands while your hands resist, so your head does not actually move at all.
Build tension gradually over two to three seconds until you reach a moderate, controlled effort, never a sudden maximal jerk that could strain the neck.
Continue breathing normally throughout, do not hold your breath, and keep your jaw and shoulders relaxed.
Hold the steady contraction for the prescribed time, keeping the head perfectly still.
Release the tension slowly over a couple of seconds rather than letting it snap off.
Rest as prescribed, then move your hands to the back of your head and reverse the action, pushing your head backward into your hands while your hands resist so the head stays motionless.
Build, hold, and release with the same slow control, keeping the chin level and avoiding any backward head tilt.

name: Isometric Neck Exercise - Sides
instructions: Sit or stand tall with a neutral spine, shoulders relaxed and pulled down, and your head erect facing straight forward with the chin level.
Place your left palm flat against the left side of your head, just above and forward of the ear, with the elbow lifted out to the side.
Brace your neck and gently begin pressing your head sideways into your left hand while the hand resists, so your head does not move or tilt.
Increase the tension gradually over two to three seconds to a moderate, controlled level, avoiding any sudden or maximal push.
Keep breathing normally and keep both shoulders level and relaxed, resisting the urge to hike the shoulder up toward the ear.
Hold the steady contraction for the prescribed time with the head perfectly still and the neck straight.
Release the tension slowly and under control.
Rest as prescribed, then place your right palm on the right side of your head and repeat, pressing the head into the right hand while resisting so the head stays motionless.
Build, hold, and release with the same slow control, keeping the head from tilting toward either shoulder.

name: Isometric Wipers
instructions: Set up in a high push-up position with your hands flat on the floor just outside shoulder width and your fingers spread and pointing forward.
Position your feet about hip width apart on the balls of your feet, and form a straight line from your heels through your hips to the crown of your head.
Brace your abs, squeeze your glutes, and tuck your pelvis slightly so your hips neither sag toward the floor nor pike upward.
Keeping the plank rigid, shift your bodyweight toward one side, allowing the elbow on that side to bend as your chest lowers down and over that hand.
Inhale as you lower, descending under control while keeping the opposite arm relatively straight and the whole torso moving as one solid unit.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the shift without letting your hips twist or your lower back collapse.
Exhale and press through the bent arm to push your body back up and across toward the other side, bending that elbow as you lower into it.
Continue wiping smoothly from side to side, keeping the core tight so the motion comes from the shoulders and arms rather than from sagging hips.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, counting one rep per side or per pair as programmed.

name: IT Band and Glute Stretch
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat with both legs extended and your spine neutral.
Loop a belt, strap, rope, or resistance band around the arch of one foot and hold an end in each hand.
Keeping that leg straight, raise it a short way off the floor, then guide it across your body toward the opposite side using the strap.
Let the leg travel across as far as is comfortable while keeping it extended and your foot off the floor, feeling the stretch along the outer hip, glute, and IT band.
Keep your opposite shoulder and hip anchored to the floor so the stretch comes from the hip and not from rolling your whole torso over.
Gently pull on the strap to draw the toes up and increase the stretch, breathing slowly and relaxing into it.
Hold for ten to twenty seconds without bouncing, then ease the leg back to center and lower it.
Repeat the stretch on the other side for the same duration.

name: Jackknife Sit-Up
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor or an exercise mat with your legs fully extended and together.
Stretch your arms straight overhead on the floor behind you so your body forms one long line from fingertips to toes; this is your starting position.
Brace your core and exhale as you simultaneously lift your legs and your arms and torso off the floor.
Raise the legs to roughly a thirty-five to forty-five degree angle while curling your upper back up, reaching your hands toward your feet to meet in a folded jackknife position.
Keep the legs straight and the arms extended and parallel to the legs at the top, balancing on your hips for a brief squeeze.
Avoid yanking with your arms or throwing your head forward; the lift should come from the abs contracting.
Inhale and lower your arms and legs back down under control to the fully extended starting position without letting your heels or hands slam the floor.
Keep continuous tension in the abs and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Janda Sit-Up
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor in the basic sit-up position with your knees bent to about ninety degrees and your feet flat on the floor.
Cross your arms over your chest or rest them at your sides, and keep your spine neutral with your lower back in light contact with the floor.

Before moving, firmly contract your glutes and dig your heels gently into the floor to engage your hamstrings; this co-contraction switches off the hip flexors through reciprocal inhibition so the abs do the work.
Maintaining that glute and hamstring tension the entire time, inhale to fill your lungs, then begin curling up slowly.
Exhale steadily as you rise, taking a deliberate three to six second count and rounding the spine up one segment at a time using only your abdominals.
Expect a much shorter range of motion than a normal sit-up; you may only come part way up, which is correct since the hip flexors are no longer assisting.
Keep the glutes and hamstrings squeezed at the top and avoid pulling on your neck or jerking forward.
Inhale and lower back down slowly and under full control to the starting position.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, keeping the glutes engaged throughout.

name: Jefferson Curl
instructions: Stand tall on a raised platform or bench with your feet hip width apart and your toes near the edge so a light weight can hang below foot level.
Hold a light dumbbell, kettlebell, or barbell with both hands in front of your thighs using an overhand grip, arms hanging straight and relaxed.
Set your legs straight with knees soft but essentially locked, since keeping the knees straight is what loads and stretches the hamstrings.
Begin by tucking your chin to your chest, then roll your spine down one vertebra at a time, segment by segment, starting from the neck and working down through the upper, mid, and lower back.
Let the weight pull your hands toward and past your toes as you continue rounding, keeping the weight close to your legs and exhaling as you descend.
Go only as far as your flexibility allows while keeping the legs straight, feeling a deep stretch through the hamstrings and lower back, and never force the bottom range.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then reverse by stacking your spine back up one vertebra at a time from the base of the back, with the head coming up last.
Move slowly and with control throughout, treating this as a loaded mobility drill rather than a fast lift, and use a very light load.
Return to a tall standing position and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Jefferson Squats
instructions: Place a loaded barbell on the floor and straddle it so it runs between your legs, standing midway along its length with the bar against your inner thighs.
Set your feet wider than shoulder width, staggered so one foot is in front of the bar and one behind it, with your toes turned out slightly.
Bend at the knees and hips with a flat back, lowering until you can reach the bar with your back kept upright and tight.
Grasp the bar in front of you with one hand using a neutral grip and grasp the bar behind you with the other hand, also neutral, so your torso sits centered between the two hands.
Check that the bar is balanced, with the distance from your torso to the front hand equal to the distance from your torso to the rear hand.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and back straight, drive through both feet, and stand fully upright to lift the bar to the starting position with arms hanging straight.
Inhale and descend by bending the knees and sitting down until your upper thighs are about parallel to the floor, keeping your back as vertical as possible and your head up.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes and do not let them collapse inward or shoot far past your toes.
Exhale and drive back up through your feet to the standing position, letting your arms act only as hooks and doing all the lifting with your legs.
Complete the set, then switch the front and rear hand positions on a subsequent set to balance the asymmetric loading.

name: Jerk Balance
instructions: Set up with a barbell racked across the front of your shoulders in the jerk rack position, shoulders pushed forward to create a shelf, torso upright, and the bar lightly touching the throat or collarbone.

Take a slightly split stance with one foot a touch in front of the other and your weight centered, keeping the torso vertical; this drill teaches you to drive under the bar and stops you from drifting backward.
Brace your core, keep your eyes forward, and take a steady breath before initiating.
Begin a controlled dip by bending only at the knees, keeping the torso perfectly vertical and the bar over your midfoot, without letting the hips shift backward.
Keep the dip shallow and balanced, then reverse forcefully by driving straight up through your legs.
Use the leg drive and the resulting momentum to elevate the bar, punching it overhead without pressing it up with your arms.
Keep the rear foot planted and use it to drive your body forward as you split, stepping the front foot forward into a full split position as you punch under the bar.
Lock the bar out overhead with the arms straight and the head pushing through, stabilizing it directly over your shoulders and hips.
Recover by stepping the front foot back, then the rear foot up, standing tall with the bar locked overhead before lowering it back to the rack position.

name: Jerk Dip Squat
instructions: Rack a barbell across the front of your shoulders in the jerk position, pushing your shoulders forward to create a supporting shelf so the bar lightly contacts your throat.
Set your feet directly under your hips with your toes turned out as comfortable, and stand tall with the torso vertical and core braced.
Take a breath and tighten your midsection to keep the trunk rigid before you dip.
Dip straight down by flexing only at the knees, letting them travel slightly forward while keeping the torso perfectly vertical and the bar over your midfoot.
Do not push your hips backward or fold at the waist; the chest and bar must stay upright so the bar tracks straight down.
Keep the dip shallow and controlled, descending only a short distance rather than into a deep squat.
Without pausing long, reverse by driving forcefully through your whole foot, extending the knees explosively to return to the standing start.
Stay tall at the top with the bar still racked on the shoulders, reset your breath and brace, and repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: JM Press
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor and a slight natural arch in your lower back, eyes roughly under the bar.
Take a close grip on the barbell with your hands about shoulder width apart, similar to a close grip bench press.

Unrack the bar and hold it at arm's length with your elbows tucked in, but position the bar in a direct line above your upper chest rather than perpendicular to the torso; this is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar like a lying triceps extension, letting the elbows bend and travel so the bar drops back toward the upper chest and chin area.

At about the halfway point, let the bar roll back about one inch by bringing your upper arms forward toward your legs until they are roughly perpendicular to the torso, keeping the elbow bend constant during this transition.
Lower the bar until it is near your upper chest or chin with the forearms close to the upper arms, feeling a strong stretch in the triceps.
Exhale and press the bar back up by extending the elbows, using the triceps as if finishing a close grip bench press.
Lock back out to the starting position over the upper chest with the elbows in, keeping the wrists stacked and the bar path tight.
Reset and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, using a controlled, moderate load since this is an intense triceps movement.

name: Jogging, Treadmill
instructions: Step onto the treadmill deck, standing on the side rails or holding the handrails before starting the belt.
Select your program from the console, using either a manual setting or a preset, and enter your age and weight if prompted to estimate calories.
Set the elevation, starting at a one to two percent incline to better simulate outdoor running, and adjust higher to increase intensity.
Begin at a slow walking speed, step onto the moving belt, and gradually increase the pace until you reach a comfortable jogging speed.
Maintain an upright posture with your chest tall, shoulders relaxed, and a slight forward lean from the ankles, looking ahead rather than down at your feet.
Let your arms swing naturally at about ninety degrees and land with a midfoot strike under your hips, breathing in a steady rhythm.
Avoid gripping the handrails while jogging, since holding on alters your gait and reduces the workout; only use them when dismounting or briefly checking your heart rate.
Continue for the desired duration, then gradually reduce the speed to a walk to cool down before stopping the belt and stepping off.

name: Jump Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, toes pointed slightly out, and your weight balanced over your midfoot.
Set your chest up, brace your core, and let your arms hang ready to swing back for momentum.
Inhale and lower into a quarter to half squat by bending the hips and knees, keeping your back straight and your knees tracking over your toes.
Without pausing at the bottom, explode upward by forcefully extending your hips, knees, and ankles, driving the balls of your feet into the floor.
Swing your arms up as you jump to add momentum and leave the ground fully, exhaling as you extend.
Reach full extension in the air with your body straight, then prepare your legs to absorb the landing.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, then your heels, immediately bending the hips and knees to cushion the impact and protect your joints.
Flow straight from the soft landing into the next descent and repeat explosively for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Keg Load
instructions: Set up the course by placing the kegs a set distance, typically thirty to fifty feet, from the loading platform.
Approach the first keg, set your feet about shoulder width apart, push your hips back, and bend your knees to get low with a flat, braced back.
Grab the near handle, tilt the keg onto its side, and reach across to grab the opposite bottom edge of the keg with your other hand.
Brace your core hard and lift the keg by driving through your legs and hips, hugging it tightly into your chest as you stand.
Carry the keg as high against your chest as you can, since a higher carry position lets you move faster, and keep a firm grip the entire way.
Move quickly toward the platform with the keg secured, keeping your chest up and core tight, and note that shouldering the keg is usually not allowed.
At the platform, dip slightly and then extend explosively through your hips, knees, and ankles to drive the keg up and onto the platform.
Return to the starting area to collect the next keg and repeat the lift and carry until all kegs are loaded or the event time ends.

name: Kettlebell Arnold Press
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width apart, knees soft, and core braced.

Clean a kettlebell up to your shoulder by hiking it back and extending through the legs and hips, catching it in the rack with your palm facing inward toward your chest and the bell resting on the back of your forearm.
Set the elbow in front of your body with the forearm vertical, shoulder packed down, and your gaze straight ahead.
Brace your abs and glutes so your ribcage stays down and you do not lean back as you press.
Press the kettlebell up and out, and as it rises rotate your wrist and forearm so the palm turns from facing inward to facing forward.
Continue pressing until the arm is fully locked out overhead with the palm facing forward and the bell stacked over the shoulder.
Exhale through the press and keep the wrist firm so the bell stays balanced over your forearm rather than bending the wrist back.
Lower under control along the same path, rotating the palm back inward as the elbow returns to the racked starting position.
Complete the prescribed repetitions, then switch arms, or alternate as programmed.

name: Kettlebell Dead Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and place the kettlebell on the floor centered between your feet.
Push your hips back, bend your knees, and reach down to grip the kettlebell handle with one hand, keeping your back flat and chest up while looking straight ahead.
Set your shoulders down and back, brace your core, and take the slack out of the arm so you are loaded over the bell; this is your starting position.
Drive explosively through your legs and hips, extending the knees and hips to accelerate the kettlebell upward in a vertical path close to your body.

Guide the bell up toward your shoulder and, as it rises, rotate your wrist around the bell and punch your hand through so it lands softly on the back of the forearm in the rack position rather than crashing onto the wrist.
Receive the kettlebell in the rack with the elbow tucked, forearm vertical, and the trunk upright and braced.
Reverse the path by hinging at the hips and pushing your butt back as you guide the bell down, keeping your back straight and the hamstrings loaded.
Let the kettlebell come to a dead stop on the floor between your feet, resetting fully since each rep starts from a dead stop.
Re-establish your grip and bracing, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions before switching hands.

name: Kettlebell Figure 8
instructions: Set a single kettlebell on the floor directly between your feet. Take a stance wider than shoulder width with your toes pointed slightly outward.
Hinge at the hips by pushing your butt back and bending your knees, keeping your spine flat and chest up rather than rounding your lower back.
Brace your core and grip the kettlebell handle with one hand from the front of your legs. The non-working hand waits behind the same-side thigh, ready to receive.
Pass the kettlebell backward between your legs, handing it off to the receiving hand which reaches in from behind that thigh.
Swing the kettlebell around the outside of that leg toward the front, then loop it back between your legs to the original hand, tracing a continuous figure-8 pattern around and between your legs.
Keep the hips hinged and the back flat throughout. Do not stand fully upright between passes; stay in the loaded athletic position.
Exhale on the effort of each pass and keep the movement smooth and controlled rather than jerky.
Keep your head up and eyes forward to help maintain a neutral spine. Continue tracing figure-8s for the desired number of repetitions, then switch initiating direction.

name: Kettlebell Hang Clean
instructions: Place the kettlebell on the floor between your feet, which should be roughly shoulder-width apart with toes pointed slightly out.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your butt back and bending the knees, keeping a flat back and chest up, and grip the kettlebell handle with one hand.
Stand up to a hanging start position with the kettlebell hanging between your thighs at arm's length, shoulder packed down, core braced, and eyes straight ahead.
Initiate the clean by hinging slightly and then explosively extending through the legs and hips, driving the kettlebell upward close to the body.
As the kettlebell rises, pull your elbow up and back and rotate your wrist so the bell flips around to rest on the outside of your forearm in the rack position at the shoulder.
Spear your hand through the handle smoothly so the kettlebell settles gently against your forearm rather than banging the wrist. The bell should land in the rack with elbow tucked.
Pause briefly in the rack position with the kettlebell resting on the forearm, shoulder packed, and torso upright.
Lower the kettlebell back down by hinging at the hips, letting it swing into the hanging position between your legs while keeping the hamstrings loaded and the back flat.
Exhale as you drive up and inhale on the descent. Keep your head up at all times. Complete the reps, then switch hands.

name: Kettlebell One-Legged Deadlift
instructions: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in one hand with your arm hanging straight down at your side.
Stand on the leg on the same side as the kettlebell, with a slight soft bend in that supporting knee. The opposite (free) leg stays close to start.
Set your shoulders back and down, brace your core, and fix your gaze a few feet ahead on the floor to keep your spine neutral.
Begin the movement by hinging at the hip of the standing leg, pushing your hips back and lowering your torso toward the floor.
Simultaneously extend your free leg straight behind you, in line with your torso, to act as a counterbalance. Your body should form a straight line from head to heel like a seesaw.
Keep the kettlebell close to your standing leg as it lowers, and keep your hips square to the floor rather than letting the trailing hip open up to the side.
Continue lowering until your torso and free leg are roughly parallel to the ground, feeling a strong stretch in the standing-leg hamstring.
Drive through the heel of the standing leg and squeeze the glute to return to the upright position, bringing the free leg back down.
Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand. Move slowly and avoid bending the standing knee excessively. Complete the reps, then switch sides.

name: Kettlebell Pass Between The Legs
instructions: Place one kettlebell on the floor between your legs and adopt a comfortable stance roughly shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips by pushing your butt out and bending your knees, keeping your back flat and chest up rather than rounding the spine.
Brace your core and grip the kettlebell handle with one hand from the front.
Pass the kettlebell backward between your legs to your other hand, which receives it from behind the thighs.
Bring that hand forward around the front and pass it back between the legs again to the first hand, tracing a 'W' or zig-zag pattern in front of and between the legs.
Keep the hips hinged and back flat throughout; stay down in the athletic position rather than standing up between passes.
Move smoothly and under control, exhaling on each pass.
Keep your head up and eyes forward to maintain a neutral spine. Continue for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Kettlebell Pirate Ships
instructions: Take a wide stance, feet noticeably wider than shoulder width with toes turned slightly out for a stable base.
Hold a single kettlebell with both hands gripping the handle, and let it hang at waist level with your arms extended straight down. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your chest up, and maintain a tall spine.
Initiate the movement by rotating your torso to one side and swinging the kettlebell up and across to head height on that side, keeping the arms relatively straight.
Pivot the trailing foot slightly to allow the hips to rotate and avoid straining the knees as you turn.
Pause briefly at the top with the kettlebell at head height.
Let the kettlebell drop back down across your body as you rotate toward the opposite side, again swinging it up to head height there.
Keep the movement controlled and driven by hip and torso rotation rather than just the arms, and keep your core tight to protect the lower back.
Exhale as you swing up each side. Repeat side to side for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Kettlebell Pistol Squat
instructions: Pick up a kettlebell with both hands and hold it by the horns (the sides of the handle) at chest height, close to your body, to act as a counterbalance.
Stand on one leg, with your weight planted firmly through the foot. Extend the other leg out in front of you, held off the floor.
Set your shoulders back, brace your core, and keep your chest tall with eyes forward.
Begin the descent by bending the standing knee and sitting your hips back and down, keeping the kettlebell up in front of you for balance.
Allow the non-working leg to extend forward and rise as you lower, keeping it off the floor throughout.
Continue lowering as far as your mobility allows, ideally until the hamstring of the standing leg meets the calf at the bottom, keeping the heel flat on the floor.
Hold the bottom position for a second, keeping your head and chest up and your knee tracking in line with your foot.
Reverse the motion by driving through the heel of the standing leg, extending the knee and hip to return to standing.
Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand. Keep the kettlebell steady throughout. Complete the reps, then switch legs.

name: Kettlebell Seated Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with your torso tall and spread your legs out comfortably in front of you for a stable base.
Position the kettlebell beside one hip, then clean it up to the rack position at your shoulder, rotating the wrist so the bell rests on the outside of your forearm.
Settle into the rack with the elbow tucked, the kettlebell against the forearm, and your wrist straight, not bent back.
Brace your core hard and sit tall, keeping your lower back from arching since the floor removes the leg drive you would have when standing.
Press the kettlebell straight up and slightly out, extending the elbow until the arm is locked out directly overhead with the bell stacked over the shoulder.
As the bell passes the head, allow your wrist to rotate so the palm finishes facing forward and the kettlebell is balanced over the shoulder joint.
Exhale as you press up and keep the shoulder packed; do not shrug excessively.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position at the shoulder under control, inhaling on the way down. Complete the reps, then switch arms.

name: Kettlebell Seesaw Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and two kettlebells on the floor between or just outside your feet.
Clean both kettlebells to the rack position at your shoulders, rotating the wrists so each bell rests on the outside of the forearm with elbows tucked.
Set your stance, brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep a tall, neutral spine with both kettlebells racked. This is the start position.
Press one kettlebell straight overhead, extending the elbow to lockout while the other stays racked at the shoulder.
As you lower that kettlebell back to the rack, simultaneously begin pressing the other kettlebell overhead, so the bells alternate in a continuous seesaw rhythm.
Keep your torso upright and resist leaning to either side; the core works hard to stay stable against the uneven load.
Exhale on each press and keep the wrist straight with the bell balanced over the shoulder at lockout.
Continue alternating, making sure to perform the same number of reps on both sides. Lower both kettlebells back to the rack and down when finished.

name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
instructions: Place a kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Set a wide sumo stance, feet well outside shoulder width with toes turned out about 30 to 45 degrees.
Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to lower down, gripping the kettlebell handle with both hands, palms facing you.
Set your hips back as far as possible while keeping your chest and head up, back flat, and arms straight. Brace your core. This is the starting position.
Drive the movement by explosively extending your hips and knees, standing up tall and pushing the floor away.
As your lower body extends, pull the kettlebell up toward your shoulders, leading with your elbows so they rise up and out to the sides above the bell.
Finish with the kettlebell near collarbone height, elbows high, torso upright, and hips fully extended.
Keep the kettlebell close to your body during the pull and let the leg and hip drive do most of the work, not the arms alone.
Exhale as you extend and pull. Reverse the motion smoothly, lowering the bell back down as you hinge the hips back to the starting position. Repeat for reps.

name: Kettlebell Thruster
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and two kettlebells set on the floor between or just outside your feet.

Clean both kettlebells to the rack position at your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips, rotating the wrists so each bell rests on the outside of the forearm. This is your starting position.
Set your stance, brace your core, keep your chest up, and hold the kettlebells in the rack with elbows tucked.
Begin the squat by hinging the hips back and bending the knees, lowering your hips down between your legs while keeping an upright torso and flat back.
Descend as low as you comfortably can, keeping your heels flat and knees tracking over your toes.
Reverse direction by driving through your heels and extending the knees and hips powerfully to stand up.
Use the upward momentum from the squat to help press both kettlebells overhead, extending your arms straight up until they lock out with the bells stacked over the shoulders.
Time the press so the leg drive flows directly into the overhead lockout in one fluid motion.
Inhale as you squat down, exhale as you drive up and press. Lower the kettlebells back to the rack as you begin the next squat. Repeat for reps.

name: Kettlebell Turkish Get-Up (Lunge style)
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor. Position a kettlebell beside one shoulder, roll into it, and press it up with both hands, then release the free hand so the working arm holds it locked out straight above your shoulder.

Bend the knee on the same side as the kettlebell and plant that foot flat on the floor. Extend the opposite leg straight out at about a 45-degree angle, and place your free arm on the floor out to the side.
Keeping the kettlebell locked out and your eyes fixed on it, press through the planted foot and your free hand to roll up onto your free forearm, then onto your free hand.
Drive your hips up off the floor into a high bridge, keeping the kettlebell stacked over your shoulder.
Sweep the straight (free) leg back underneath your body and place that knee on the floor, coming into a kneeling position with the free hand still supporting.
Lift the free hand off the floor and come up tall into a half-kneeling lunge position, torso vertical, kettlebell still locked out overhead.
Drive through the front foot to stand up out of the lunge into a full standing position, keeping the kettlebell locked overhead and your gaze on it.
To reverse, step back into the lunge, lower the back knee, plant the free hand, sweep the leg through to seated, lower to the forearm and back flat, reversing every step in order.
Move slowly and deliberately throughout, keeping the working arm vertical and shoulder packed at all times. Complete reps on one side before switching.

name: Kettlebell Turkish Get-Up (Squat style)
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor. Position a kettlebell beside one shoulder, roll into it, and press it up with both hands, then release the free hand so the working arm holds it locked out straight above your shoulder.
Bend the knee on the same side as the kettlebell and plant that foot flat. Extend the opposite leg straight out at about 45 degrees, and place your free arm on the floor out to the side.
Keeping the kettlebell locked out and your eyes on it, press through the planted foot and free hand to come up onto your free forearm, then onto your free hand.
Drive your hips up into a high bridge, then sweep the free leg back under you and bring both feet underneath your body.
Instead of kneeling, bring your free hand off the floor and rise straight up into a deep squat with both feet planted and the kettlebell locked overhead.
Stand up out of the squat by driving through both heels, keeping your chest up and the kettlebell stacked over your shoulder, eyes on the bell.
Reverse the motion by squatting back down, lowering your hands and hips back to the seated bridge, then back onto the forearm and flat to the floor, reversing each step.
Keep the working arm vertical with the shoulder packed throughout, and move under control. Complete reps on one side before switching.

name: Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Place the kettlebell on the floor just in front of your lead foot. Clean and press it overhead with the arm opposite to your lead leg, rotating the wrist so the palm faces forward and locking the elbow out overhead.
Set your feet so they point at about a 45-degree angle away from the side of the raised kettlebell. The kettlebell-side leg is the lead leg.
With the kettlebell locked out overhead and your gaze fixed on it, push your hips out to the side in the direction of the raised kettlebell.
Keeping that overhead arm vertical and the shoulder packed, begin bending sideways at the hips, sticking your butt out and keeping your legs relatively straight.
Slowly lower your torso, letting your free hand slide down the inside of your front leg toward the floor as you fold to the side.
Continue until your free hand can touch the floor, keeping your eyes on the overhead kettlebell the entire time and your spine long rather than rounded.
Keep the overhead arm locked and stacked over the shoulder throughout; the movement comes from the hips bending sideways, not from the arm.
Pause for a second at the bottom, then reverse the motion by driving the hips back under you and standing tall to the starting position.
Inhale as you lower, exhale as you rise. Complete the reps on one side, then switch.

name: Kipping Muscle Up
instructions: Set up under a pair of gymnastic rings hung at a height where you can hang fully extended without your feet touching the floor.

Establish a false grip on each ring by placing the base of your palm (heel of the hand) on top of the ring so your wrist sits over the ring, with fingers wrapped underneath. This shortens the distance you must pull and sets up the transition.
Hang from the rings with the false grip, arms extended, shoulders active, and core braced. This is the starting position.
Initiate the kip by swinging your legs backward slightly and pressing the rings away to load the swing.
Reverse by swinging your legs forward and up while throwing your chin and chest back, using that momentum to pull explosively with both arms.

As you reach the top of the pull, drive the rings down to your armpits and roll your shoulders forward, letting your elbows travel straight back behind you. This is the critical transition into the dip.
From the bottom of the dip with the rings at your chest, press down and extend through your elbows to lock the arms out straight above the rings, finishing in the support position.
Stabilize at the top with rings turned out and arms locked.
Lower yourself under control by reversing the dip and transition, then descend back to the hang. Take care not to drop suddenly, especially as fatigue sets in.

name: Knee Across The Body
instructions: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your right leg straight and extended.
Bend your left knee and lower that leg across your body to the right, rotating from the spine.
Reach across with your right hand and gently hold the left knee down toward the floor. The knee does not need to touch the floor if you feel tight.
Extend your left arm out comfortably to the side along the floor and turn your head to look to the left, opposite the bent knee, to deepen the rotation.
Imagine a weight tied to your tailbone: let the tailbone and hip fall back toward the floor while your chest and left shoulder reach in the opposite direction, lengthening the lower back.
Keep both shoulders in contact with the floor as much as possible and breathe slowly and deeply, relaxing further into the stretch with each exhale.
Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds without bouncing, then slowly return to the start and switch sides.

name: Knee Circles
instructions: Stand with your feet and legs together and place your hands on your knees or at your waist.
Bend your knees slightly into a partial squat so your knees are soft and mobile.
Slowly move your knees in a smooth circular motion, tracing a circle while keeping your feet flat on the floor.
Keep the movement gentle and controlled, breathing normally as a warm-up rather than forcing range of motion.
Complete the desired number of circles in one direction, then reverse and circle in the opposite direction for an equal count.

name: Knee Tuck Jump
instructions: Stand tall on a flat, non-slip surface with your feet roughly hip-width apart and your toes pointing straight ahead. Allow a soft, slight bend in your knees rather than locking them.
Hold both hands out in front of you at about chest or upper-abdomen height, palms facing down and fingertips lightly touching. These hands act as a target for your knees during the jump.
Brace your core, keep your chest up and your eyes looking forward at a fixed point to maintain balance.

Initiate the jump by rapidly dipping down into a quarter squat: push your hips back, let your knees bend to about 45 degrees and swing your arms slightly back. This loading phase should be quick and shallow, not a deep squat.
Immediately reverse and explode straight up, driving through the balls of your feet to extend your hips, knees and ankles powerfully.

At the top of the jump, snap both knees up toward your chest, aiming to lightly tap your knees against your downturned palms. Keep your torso as upright as possible rather than folding forward to meet the knees.
Exhale sharply as you jump and tuck.
Quickly re-extend your legs underneath you so your feet are beneath your hips for landing.
Land softly on the balls of your feet then the whole foot, immediately re-bending your knees and hips to absorb the impact like a spring. Avoid landing with stiff, straight legs.
Reset to a tall standing position, take a breath, and repeat. Keep each rep crisp and explosive; stop the set when your jumps lose height or your landings become sloppy.

name: Knee/Hip Raise On Parallel Bars
instructions: Step up onto the vertical leg raise station (captain's chair) and place your forearms flat on the two padded arm rests, gripping the handles in front of them.
Press your forearms down into the pads and grip firmly so your bodyweight hangs from your upper arms, with your elbows bent at roughly 90 degrees.

Press your entire back, especially your lower back, flat against the vertical back pad. Let your legs hang straight down toward the floor with your toes pointed lightly down. This is your starting position.
Brace your abs hard and posteriorly tilt your pelvis (think of tucking your tailbone) before you move, so the movement comes from your abdominals rather than your hip flexors.

Exhale and lift your legs upward by curling your pelvis and bringing your knees and hips up. For the easier knee-raise version bend the knees as you lift; for the harder straight-leg version keep the legs extended.
Continue raising until your thighs are at or just above parallel to the floor, focusing on rolling your hips up and crunching your lower abs at the top.
Pause and squeeze the contraction for a full second at the top.
Inhale and lower your legs slowly and under control back to the fully hanging starting position. Do not let them drop.
Keep your torso still throughout. Do not swing or use momentum, and do not let your shoulders shrug up into your ears.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Kneeling Arm Drill
instructions: Kneel into a half-kneeling position on a mat: your left foot planted flat on the floor in front of you with the knee bent about 90 degrees, and your right knee down on the mat behind you.
Drive pressure through the heel of your front (left) foot to engage your glutes and hamstrings, and keep your torso tall and upright with a braced core.
Set your shoulders down and back, look straight ahead, and bend your elbows to roughly 90 degrees as in a running posture.
Begin with slow, long pendulum-like swings of the arms front to back from the shoulder joint, keeping the elbows fixed at about 90 degrees and the hands relaxed.
Gradually close and tighten the arm angle and increase the cadence, mimicking the arm action of a jog, then a run, then a full sprint.
Swing the arms straight forward and back, not across the body, with the hands traveling from roughly cheek height down to just past the hip.
As soon as each hand passes the hip on the backswing, accelerate it forward as fast as possible to train explosive, efficient arm drive.
Keep your hips square, your trunk stable, and avoid rocking or twisting your shoulders as your arm speed increases.
Perform the drill for the prescribed time or rep count, then switch so the right foot is forward and the left knee is down, and repeat.

name: Kneeling Cable Crunch With Alternating Oblique Twists
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a high pulley and select an appropriate weight. Place a mat on the floor directly in front of the machine.
Grab one end of the rope in each hand and kneel on the mat roughly two feet back from the tower so there is tension on the cable.
Pull the rope down and position your hands beside your ears, with the rope running behind your head. Keep your hips extended (sitting tall, not back on your heels) so the work stays in your abs.
Set your spine in a slight forward lean with tension already on the cable. Lock your hands in place by your ears for the entire set; they should not move relative to your head.

For a straight crunch, exhale and contract your abs to curl your torso downward, rounding your spine and driving your elbows toward your knees until you feel a deep ab contraction. Keep your hips fixed and bend only at the waist.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then inhale and rise back up slowly and under control to the starting position, resisting the cable the whole way.
On the next rep, crunch down until you are about halfway, then begin rotating so you drive one elbow toward the opposite knee, twisting through the obliques.
Pause and squeeze at the bottom of the twist, then return slowly to the start.
Repeat the crunch-and-twist, this time rotating the other elbow toward its opposite knee, alternating sides each rep.
Maintain steady tension, avoid yanking with your arms or using momentum, and continue the series until you reach failure or your target reps.

name: Kneeling Cable Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and select an appropriate weight. Place a flat bench sideways on the floor in front of the machine, a couple of feet from the tower.
Grab the straight bar with an overhand grip, hands about 6 inches apart and palms facing down.
Turn to face away from the machine and kneel on the floor behind the bench.

Lower your torso so you rest your head and the backs of your upper arms on the bench. Your upper arms should be roughly parallel and your elbows bent, with your forearms angled up toward the high pulley. This is your starting position.
Pin your upper arms firmly against the bench and keep them stationary and close to your head throughout; only your forearms should move.
Exhale and press the bar out in a smooth arc by extending your elbows until your arms are nearly straight and roughly parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your triceps hard at full extension and hold for a second without locking out aggressively.
Inhale and slowly bend your elbows to return the bar along the same arc back to the starting position, keeping the resistance under control.
Avoid flaring your elbows out or letting your upper arms drift; keeping them tucked targets the triceps properly.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Kneeling Forearm Stretch
instructions: Kneel down on a mat in an upright kneeling position, with your knees roughly hip-width apart.
Place both palms flat on the floor in front of your knees with your fingers pointing back toward your body (toward your knees) and your thumbs out.
Keep your elbows straight but not locked, and keep your palms pressed fully flat against the floor.
Slowly lean your weight backward, shifting your hips toward your heels, until you feel a gentle stretch through the underside of your wrists and forearms.
Stop at the point of a mild, comfortable stretch; never push into sharp pain. Keep your palms down the whole time.
Breathe slowly and hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds, then ease forward to release.
Repeat for an additional round if desired.

name: Kneeling High Pulley Row
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley set above head height and select an appropriate weight.
Grab one end of the rope in each hand and kneel on the floor a couple of feet back from the cable tower so there is tension on the line. A mat under your knees adds comfort.

Sit tall with your hips extended, brace your core, set your chest up and pull your shoulder blades slightly back. Extend both arms up and out toward the pulley so the rope is taut. This is your starting position.
Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows down and back, leading with the elbows rather than the hands.
Pull the rope toward your upper chest, allowing your elbows to flare out to the sides, and squeeze your lats and mid-back hard at the end of the movement.
Keep your torso upright and stationary; do not lean back or rock to generate force.
Pause briefly in the fully contracted position.
Slowly return your arms to full extension overhead under control, feeling a stretch in the lats, and reach slightly to complete the range of motion.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, keeping the motion smooth and the lats engaged throughout.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor
instructions: Kneel on a mat on both knees in an upright position.
Bring your right leg forward and plant the right foot flat on the floor, with the knee bent about 90 degrees and stacked over the ankle.
Extend your left leg back behind you so the top of your left foot rests on the floor and your left thigh points down toward the mat.
Tuck your pelvis slightly under and keep your torso tall and upright with your core gently braced; avoid arching your lower back.
Slowly shift your weight forward by pushing your hips toward the front foot until you feel a stretch across the front of your left hip and thigh.
Stop at a comfortable, moderate stretch and hold for about 15 seconds while breathing slowly.
Ease back, switch so the left foot is forward and the right leg extends behind, and repeat on the other side.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Set up in a half-kneeling position on a mat: one knee down on the floor behind you and the opposite foot planted flat in front, with that front knee bent about 90 degrees over the ankle.
Stack your torso upright over your hips, draw your shoulders back and gently brace your core.
Tuck your pelvis under by squeezing the glute of the down (rear) leg and rotating your tailbone toward the floor. This posterior tilt is what makes the stretch effective.
Keeping the pelvic tuck, slowly shift your weight forward over the front foot until you feel a stretch across the front of the hip and upper thigh of the rear leg.
Keep your torso tall and avoid letting your lower back arch or your front knee collapse inward.
Hold the stretch for the desired time while breathing slowly and steadily.
Release, switch the position of your legs, and repeat on the other side.

name: Kneeling Jump Squat
instructions: Set up inside a power rack with the safety pins or supports at a height that lets you rack a barbell across your upper back while kneeling, which makes unracking easier. Pad your knees with a mat.

Kneel upright on the mat and position the barbell across the back of your shoulders (on the traps, not the neck), gripping it firmly with both hands and retracting your shoulder blades so the bar sits tight. Alternatively, perform this with bodyweight only.
Unrack the bar and kneel tall with your hips fully extended, core braced, chest up and eyes forward. Your knees and lower legs are on the mat with feet behind you. This is your starting position.
Sit back by bending at the hips and lowering your glutes toward your heels, keeping your head and chest up and your back flat.
When your glutes lightly touch your feet, immediately and explosively drive your hips forward and up, generating maximal power to launch your body upward off your knees.
As you rise, swing your feet forward underneath you and land with both feet flat on the floor in a squat or partial-squat stance.
Absorb the landing by bending your knees and hips, keeping the bar tight and your torso upright.
Continue the motion by driving through your heels and extending your knees and hips to stand fully upright.
Carefully reset to the kneeling start between reps. Keep every rep explosive and controlled, and stop if your landing position becomes unstable.

name: Kneeling Single-Arm High Pulley Row
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high pulley set above head height and select an appropriate weight.
Kneel on the floor a couple of feet in front of the cable tower, using a mat for knee comfort. Sit tall with hips extended and core braced.

Take the handle in one hand and extend that arm up and out toward the pulley so the cable is taut, with your palm facing forward. Let your shoulder reach slightly toward the pulley for a full stretch. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso upright and square, initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blade and driving your elbow down and back.
Pull the handle down toward the side of your torso, and as you do, rotate your wrist so your palm finishes facing toward you (a supinated finish).
Squeeze your lat and mid-back hard at the bottom of the pull.
Avoid twisting or leaning your torso to help move the weight; keep the trunk stable and let the working side do the work.
Pause briefly, then slowly return the handle to the fully extended starting position, reversing the wrist rotation back to palm-forward.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch the handle to the other hand and repeat.

name: Kneeling Squat
instructions: Set the barbell on the pins or J-hooks of a power rack at about the height of your shoulders when you are kneeling. Place a mat down to pad your knees.
Kneel upright behind the bar and slide under it, racking the bar across the back of your shoulders (on the upper traps, not the neck). Grip the bar with both hands a bit wider than shoulder-width.
Retract your shoulder blades and pull the bar tight across your back, brace your core, lift your chest and keep your head facing forward. Unrack the bar by extending your hips to kneel tall.
Establish your starting position kneeling fully upright with hips extended, knees about hip-width apart on the mat, and torso vertical.
Keeping your head looking forward and your back flat, sit back by bending at the hips and lowering your glutes toward your calves.
Descend under control until your glutes touch or nearly touch your calves, maintaining a braced core and neutral spine throughout.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to reverse the motion, returning your torso to the fully upright kneeling position.
Do not let your lower back round or your torso pitch forward; keep the movement hip-driven and the spine neutral.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then carefully re-rack the bar.

name: L-Sit
instructions: Set up on a pair of parallettes, parallel bars, or place your hands flat on the floor at your sides. Sit between or behind your hand supports with your legs extended in front of you.
Grip the parallettes (or press your palms into the floor) and lock your elbows completely straight, with your arms vertical and directly under your shoulders.
Actively depress your shoulders by pushing down through your hands and pulling your shoulders away from your ears; this scapular depression is essential to lifting your body off the ground.
Brace your core hard, tilt your pelvis slightly under, and engage your quads and hip flexors.
Press down through your arms to lift your hips and seat off the floor, then raise both legs straight out in front of you so your body forms an L shape, with legs parallel to the floor.
Keep your legs perfectly straight, your knees locked, and your toes pointed.
Maintain a tall, depressed-shoulder position and avoid letting your hips sag or your shoulders shrug up.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, breathing steadily, then lower your feet under control to release.
If holding straight legs is too difficult, bend the knees into a tuck position to scale the hold.

name: Landmine 180's
instructions: Insert one end of a barbell into a landmine anchor or wedge it securely into a corner so it cannot slip. Load the free end with an appropriate weight.
Stand facing the loaded end of the bar and lift it off the floor with both hands, bringing it to about shoulder height with your arms extended out in front of you.
Adopt a wide, athletic stance with your feet wider than shoulder-width, knees slightly bent, and core braced. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight throughout, rotate your trunk and hips together to swing the bar in a wide arc down to one side, pivoting your back foot and turning the hips as the weight travels.
Control the descent and let the weight finish low and to the side; do not let it crash down or pull you off balance.
Reverse the motion powerfully, rotating your trunk and hips to swing the bar back up, across the front, and all the way down to the opposite side.
Keep your arms in a fixed, extended position; the rotation must come from your hips and torso, not from bending the arms.
Keep your core tight and exhale as you swing through each side to protect your lower back.
Alternate swinging the weight from side to side in a smooth, controlled arc until the set is complete.

name: Landmine Linear Jammer
instructions: Insert one end of a barbell into a landmine anchor or wedge it securely into a corner. Load the free end and, if available, fit a double-handle (jammer) attachment over the loaded end.
Face the bar and lift it off the floor, bringing the handles up to shoulder height so they rest at the front of your shoulders.

Set your feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart in an athletic stance, knees and hips slightly bent, chest up, core braced, with your elbows flexed and the handles near your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Lower into a partial squat by flexing your knees and sitting your hips back, keeping your arms flexed and the handles held at your shoulders.
Explode out of the squat by powerfully extending your hips, knees, and ankles all at once (triple extension), driving your bodyweight up and forward.
At the same time, press the handles forward and up by extending your elbows, transferring the leg drive into a powerful arm press in a single, fluid motion.
Finish at full extension with your legs straight and arms extended forward and slightly up. Perform the whole movement as explosively as possible.
Exhale forcefully through the drive, and keep your core tight so the power transfers efficiently without your lower back overarching.
Return under control to the starting position with the handles back at your shoulders and repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Lateral Bound
instructions: Stand on a flat, non-slip surface. Turn your body so you are facing 90 degrees away from your intended direction of travel; you will be jumping sideways.
Drop into a half-squat athletic position, with your knees and hips bent, chest up, and your weight balanced over your feet. This is your starting position.
Shift your weight onto your outside leg (the leg furthest from the direction you want to bound), loading it like a spring, while your lead leg performs a slight countermovement inward.
Brace your core and swing your arms to assist the jump.
Push off explosively from the outside leg and extend your hip, knee, and ankle to bound as far as possible to the side toward your direction of travel.
Land on the opposite (lead) leg in a soft, controlled single-leg half-squat, absorbing the impact by bending the knee and hip and keeping the knee tracking over the toes.
Stabilize for a moment if needed, then immediately push off that leg in the opposite direction to bound back to your original starting spot.
Keep your chest up and avoid letting your landing knee cave inward; control each landing before launching the next bound.
Continue bounding back and forth from side to side for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Lateral Box Jump
instructions: Select a sturdy plyo box roughly knee-height or lower to start; only progress higher once you can land cleanly and quietly. Place it on a flat, non-slip surface with clear space on both sides.
Stand to one side of the box with your feet about hip-width apart, the side of your body facing the box. Position yourself so the box is squarely beside you, not in front.
Set your posture: chest up, eyes forward at the box, core braced, and a slight bend in the knees and hips. Let your arms hang ready to swing.
Initiate the jump by dipping quickly into a quarter squat, hinging at the hips and bending the knees while swinging both arms back to load the stretch reflex.
