Immediately reverse the dip and explode laterally, driving through both feet and swinging your arms up and across in the direction of the box to generate sideways height.
Pull your knees up high so your feet clear the top of the box comfortably; do not drag your trailing foot or clip the edge.

Land softly in the center of the box on the balls of your feet first, then the whole foot, with knees tracking over your toes and hips sinking into a quarter squat to absorb the impact. Land quietly with both feet at once.
Stabilize for a moment in a balanced athletic stance before the next rep. Avoid landing with stiff, locked knees as this jars the joints.
Step or hop down carefully to the opposite side, reset your stance, and repeat the jump back across, continuing to alternate sides for the prescribed reps.
Keep the contact time short and the movement athletic; quality and clean landings matter more than speed. Stop the set if your landings become sloppy.

name: Lateral Cone Hops
instructions: Set up a row of low cones (or markers) spaced one to two feet apart in a straight line on a flat, non-slip surface.
Stand beside the first cone with your body turned 90 degrees to the line of cones, so you will be hopping sideways over them. Place your feet about hip-width apart.
Adopt an athletic ready position: knees and hips slightly bent, chest up, core braced, weight on the balls of your feet, and arms ready to swing.
Begin by dipping quickly with the knees and hips while swinging your arms back to load the stretch reflex.
Immediately reverse and push explosively off both feet, jumping up and sideways to clear the first cone, swinging your arms in the direction of travel for momentum.
Lift your knees enough to clear the cone cleanly without clipping it; keep your feet together and the movement compact.
Land softly on the balls of both feet with knees slightly bent and tracking over the toes, absorbing the impact rather than landing flat-footed and stiff.
Rebound immediately into the next hop, using a short ground-contact time to bounce over each successive cone down the row.
Keep your torso upright and facing forward throughout; resist twisting toward the cones. Move with control and reset if your landings get sloppy.

name: Lateral Raise - With Bands
instructions: Attach handles to a resistance band, or use a looped band, and stand on the middle of it with both feet so tension begins when your arms hang at your sides.

Stand with feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart for a stable base, knees soft, and grip one handle in each hand with a pronated grip (palms facing your thighs), hands slightly narrower than shoulder width.
Set your posture: stand tall with a straight back, chest up, shoulders down and back, and core braced. The handles rest against the outsides of your thighs.
Maintain a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout. This is your starting position.
Leading with your elbows and using your side (lateral) deltoids, raise both handles out to the sides as you exhale, keeping arms nearly straight and that fixed elbow bend.
As you lift, slightly tilt your hands as if pouring water from a pitcher (pinkies a touch higher than thumbs) to better target the side delts.
Continue until your upper arms reach about shoulder height (handles slightly above parallel to the floor). Keep your torso stationary and do not shrug or use momentum.
Pause for a one-count at the top, feeling the contraction in your side delts.
Lower the handles slowly and under control back to the starting position as you inhale, resisting the band the whole way down.
Repeat for the prescribed reps. Avoid swinging the body or letting the band snap your arms down; control both directions.

name: Latissimus Dorsi-SMR
instructions: Lie down on the floor on your side and place a foam roller on the ground perpendicular to your body, positioned just behind your armpit on the side you want to release.
Roll onto the roller so it sits under the upper-outer portion of your back (the lats), just below the armpit, on one side.
Extend the arm of the side being worked overhead and slightly behind you, thumb pointing up, to open up the lat and expose the muscle to the roller. This is your starting position.
Shift your body weight onto the roller and the targeted lat, keeping your upper body off the ground and using your free hand or bottom leg for balance and control.
Slowly roll a few inches up and down the lat between the armpit and the lower edge of the muscle, searching for tender spots.
When you find a tight or tender spot, pause and hold steady pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the tissue to relax.
Keep the movements slow and controlled; never roll quickly or grind aggressively, and avoid rolling directly on the spine or bony areas.
Switch to the other side and repeat for an equal duration.

name: Leg Extensions
instructions: Select your weight on the leg extension machine, then sit fully back into the seat so your back is supported and your hips and knees are at roughly 90 degrees.
Adjust the back pad (if available) so the backs of your knees rest at the edge of the seat, aligning your knee joint with the machine's pivot point.
Adjust the ankle (shin) pad so it rests on the front of your lower legs just above the tops of your feet, with your feet pointed forward.

Position your legs under the pad so the angle between your upper and lower leg is about 90 degrees. If the machine forces a deeper bend that puts your knees past your toes, adjust the start so you do not descend below 90 degrees, to avoid undue knee stress.
Grip the side handles to anchor your torso, keep your back against the pad, and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Using your quadriceps, extend your legs upward to full (but not violently locked) extension as you exhale, keeping the rest of your body still on the seat.
Squeeze your quads and pause for a one-count at the top contracted position.
Slowly lower the weight back down under control as you inhale, stopping at the 90-degree starting angle rather than letting the plates crash down.
Keep your hips and glutes planted and avoid swinging or using momentum; the movement comes only from the knees.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Leg Lift
instructions: Stand up tall with both feet next to each other at about shoulder width, near a sturdy support such as a squat rack upright or the back of a chair.
Grasp the support with one or both hands to brace yourself and maintain balance throughout the movement.
Set your posture: stand tall, chest up, hips square to the front, and core lightly braced. Optionally wear an ankle weight for added resistance.
Keep your supporting leg straight with a soft knee and your foot planted firmly. This is your starting position.
Squeezing your glute, lift one leg straight back behind you, hinging slightly at the hip while keeping that knee mostly straight, as you exhale.
Raise the leg only as far as you can without arching your lower back or rotating your hips; keep the torso upright and stable.
Pause and squeeze the glute at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the leg back to the floor under control as you inhale, resisting the urge to let it drop.
Complete all prescribed reps on one leg, focusing on the glute doing the work rather than swinging the leg.
Switch sides and repeat with the opposite leg for the same number of reps.

name: Leg Press
instructions: Load an appropriate weight on the leg press sled, then sit fully into the seat with your back and head flat against the pad and your hips set into the seat.

Place your feet on the platform about shoulder-width apart, feet flat and roughly mid-platform, toes pointed slightly out. (This medium stance targets overall development; a higher stance emphasizes glutes and hamstrings, a lower stance the quads.)
Grip the side handles, brace your core, and press the platform up enough to release and rotate the safety stops out of the way.
Extend your legs to press the platform up until they are nearly straight, but do not lock your knees out hard; keep a slight bend. This is your starting position.
As you inhale, slowly bend your knees and lower the platform under control until your upper and lower legs reach about a 90-degree angle.
Keep your lower back and hips pressed into the seat throughout; do not let your hips round or lift off the pad at the bottom, so reduce range of motion before that happens.
Drive the platform back up by pushing mainly through your heels and using your quads, exhaling as you extend back to the starting position.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes the entire time and avoid letting them cave inward.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, keeping each rep controlled rather than bouncing at the bottom.
When finished, rotate the safety stops back into place before lowering the sled and exiting, so the loaded platform is securely supported.

name: Leg Pull-In
instructions: Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with your legs extended straight out in front of you.
Place your hands either palms-down flat on the floor beside your hips, or tucked under your glutes to support your lower back. This is your starting position.
Press your lower back gently toward the floor and brace your abs to remove any excessive arch before you begin.
Keeping your core tight, bend your knees and pull your upper thighs in toward your midsection as you exhale.
Continue curling your knees up until they reach roughly chest level, contracting your abs hard at the top.
Keep your lower legs (calves) parallel to the floor throughout the movement to maintain tension on the abdominals.
Hold the contracted position for a one-count, squeezing your abs.
Slowly extend your legs back out to the starting position as you inhale, controlling the descent and keeping your lower back from arching up off the mat.
Avoid using momentum or yanking with the hip flexors; let the abs draw the legs in. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Leg-Over Floor Press
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with one kettlebell positioned beside your working-side shoulder. Roll toward it and grip the handle securely, then bring it to rest on your chest.
Press the kettlebell up so it sits stacked over your shoulder, gripping the handle with your wrist straight and knuckles toward the ceiling.
Cross the leg on your working side over the top of your non-working leg, which helps anchor and stabilize your hips on the floor.
Extend your free arm out to the side along the floor for support and balance. Brace your core and keep your shoulder blade pulled down and back. This is your starting position.
Press the kettlebell up by extending your elbow until your arm is locked out directly over your shoulder, exhaling as you push.
Keep your wrist neutral and the kettlebell balanced over the forearm so the weight stays controlled and does not tip toward your face.
Lower the weight slowly and under control as you inhale until your upper arm (elbow) touches the floor, keeping the elbow tucked at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso.
Let the floor stop the descent gently rather than bouncing your elbow off it; pause briefly with the kettlebell still stacked above the elbow.
Press back up and repeat for the prescribed reps, then carefully bring the kettlebell down and switch sides.

name: Leg-Up Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat. Bend one knee and place that foot flat on the floor to stabilize your pelvis and protect your lower back.
Raise the other leg straight up into the air; if your hamstrings are tight you will not be able to fully straighten it, which is fine.
Extend the knee as much as comfortable so the sole of the lifted foot faces the ceiling (or as close to that as you can manage), with a slight flex in the ankle.
Keeping your hips and head relaxed on the floor, slowly straighten the raised leg as much as possible.
Gently pull the straightened leg toward your nose, using your hands clasped behind the thigh or calf, until you feel a comfortable stretch in the back of the thigh.
Hold the stretch without bouncing, breathing slowly and deeply, and let the muscle relax for 20 to 30 seconds.
Avoid pulling so hard that you feel pain or that your lower back lifts off the floor; ease back if the stretch is sharp.
Lower the leg under control and switch to the other side, repeating for an equal hold.

name: Leverage Chest Press
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the machine's pins, then adjust the seat height so that when seated, the handles line up near the bottom to middle of your pectorals.
Sit down with your back flat against the back pad, head up, and feet planted firmly on the floor for a stable base.
Grip the handles with a full, secure grip. Pull your shoulder blades down and back and pin them against the pad. Keep your chest up. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and press the handles forward by extending through the elbows, driving with your chest, until your arms are nearly straight but not locked hard.
Exhale as you press; keep your wrists straight and your shoulders retracted, not rolling forward at the top.
Squeeze your chest briefly at the top of the press.
Return the handles under control toward your chest as you inhale, but stop just before the weight stack returns to the stops to keep tension on the muscles.
Keep your back and head against the pad throughout; do not flare your elbows excessively or arch off the seat to move more weight.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, only letting the weight rest on the stops once the set is complete.

name: Leverage Deadlift
instructions: Load the machine's pins to an appropriate weight and stand on the platform directly between the two handles, positioned so the load is centered on you.
Set your feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart, flat and stable, with your weight balanced through your mid-foot and heels.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower into position and grasp the handles with a comfortable, secure grip, arms straight.

Set your spine: chest up, look forward, shoulders slightly in front of or over the handles, lower back flat and braced rather than rounded. Take a breath and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Drive the movement by pushing your feet through the platform and extending your hips and knees together, standing up tall as you lift the handles.
Keep your arms straight (they are just hooks), the load close to your body, and your back flat throughout; exhale near the top as you reach full, upright lockout with hips extended.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without leaning back or overextending your spine.
Reverse the motion by hinging at the hips first and then bending the knees, lowering the handles back to the starting position under control as you inhale.
Keep your core braced and back flat on the way down; avoid letting the lower back round. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Leverage Decline Chest Press
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the machine's pins, then adjust the seat height so the handles sit near the lower portion of your pectorals when seated.
Sit down with your back and head flat against the pad and your feet planted firmly on the floor or footrests for stability.
Grip the handles securely, pull your shoulder blades down and back against the pad, and keep your chest up. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and press the handles forward and slightly downward along the machine's path by extending through the elbows, driving with your lower chest.
Exhale as you press to a near-full extension without harshly locking the elbows, keeping your wrists straight.
Squeeze your lower chest briefly at the top of the press.
Return the handles under control as you inhale, stopping just short of the weight returning to the stops to maintain tension on the muscles.
Keep your shoulders retracted and your back against the pad throughout; do not let the shoulders roll forward at the top.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, resting the weight on the stops only after the set is finished.

name: Leverage High Row
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the machine's pins and adjust the seat height so that, when seated, you can just reach the handles positioned above and in front of you with arms extended.
Adjust the knee or thigh pad so it holds you firmly down in the seat and prevents your body from lifting during the pull.

Sit with your chest against the chest pad (if equipped), torso upright, and feet planted. Grasp the handles with a pronated (overhand, palms-down) grip, arms fully extended overhead. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your chest up, and begin the pull by driving your elbows down and back, leading with the elbows rather than the hands.
Pull the handles toward your upper torso while retracting and squeezing your shoulder blades together as you flex the elbows, exhaling through the effort.
Pause and squeeze your back at the bottom of the motion, keeping your chest tall and shoulders down rather than shrugged toward your ears.
Slowly return the handles to the overhead starting position under control as you inhale, letting your shoulder blades protract slightly at the top to fully stretch the lats and mid-back.
Keep your torso stationary; avoid yanking with momentum or leaning back to move the weight.
For multiple reps, stop just short of letting the weight touch the stops to keep continuous tension on the muscles. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Leverage Incline Chest Press
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the machine's pins, then adjust the seat height so the handles line up near the top of your pectorals (just below the collarbone) when seated.
Sit down with your back and head flat against the inclined back pad and your feet planted firmly for stability.
Grip the handles securely, pull your shoulder blades down and back against the pad, and keep your chest up. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and press the handles forward and upward along the machine's path by extending through the elbows, driving with your upper chest.
Exhale as you press to a near-full extension without harshly locking out the elbows, keeping your wrists straight.
Squeeze your upper chest briefly at the top of the press.
Return the handles under control as you inhale, stopping just short of the weight returning to the stops to keep tension on the muscles.
Keep your shoulders retracted and back against the pad throughout; avoid letting the shoulders roll forward or shrug up at the top.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, letting the weight rest on the stops only once the set is complete.

name: Leverage Iso Row
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the machine's pins and adjust the seat height so that the handles sit at about chest level when you are seated.
Sit down with your chest against the chest pad, torso upright, feet planted, and core braced.
Grasp the handles with either a neutral (palms facing each other) or pronated (palms-down) grip, arms fully extended forward. This is your starting position.
Begin the pull by driving your elbows back and retracting your shoulder blades, leading with the elbows rather than yanking with the hands.
Pull the handles toward your torso as you flex the elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades together, exhaling through the effort.
Keep your chest pressed against the pad and your torso stationary; do not lean back or use momentum to move the weight.
Pause and squeeze your back muscles at the bottom (fully contracted) position, keeping your shoulders down rather than shrugged.
Slowly return the handles to the extended starting position under control as you inhale, allowing a slight stretch in the lats and mid-back at the top.
For multiple reps, avoid letting the weight settle fully onto the stops to keep tension on the working muscles. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Leverage Shoulder Press
instructions: Load the desired weight onto the pin and sit fully back into the seat so your back, including your lower spine, is flat against the pad.
Adjust the seat height so that the handles sit at roughly shoulder height when your arms are relaxed; the handles should be level with or just below the top of your shoulders at the start.
Grip the vertical handles with a pronated (palms-facing-forward) grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder width so your forearms are vertical.
Plant your feet flat on the floor about hip width apart, lift your chest, keep your head neutral, and brace your core to lock your torso against the backrest.
Take a breath and exhale as you press the handles straight up by extending through the elbows, driving toward the ceiling along a smooth vertical path.
Stop just short of full elbow lockout to keep tension on the shoulders, and pause briefly at the top without shrugging the traps.
Inhale as you lower the handles under control back to just above shoulder height, feeling a stretch across the front of the shoulders.
Do not let the weight stack rest on the stops between reps until the set is finished, so the delts stay loaded the whole time.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows throughout, and avoid arching your lower back off the pad as you press.

name: Leverage Shrug
instructions: Load the desired weight onto the pin of the leverage shrug machine and stand directly between the two side handles, feet flat and about hip width apart.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower yourself, grasp the top handles with a neutral (palms-facing-in) grip, and take a breath.
Set your spine neutral with chest up and eyes forward, then drive through your heels to extend the hips and knees and rise to a fully standing position holding the weight.
Stand tall with arms hanging straight, shoulders back, and a slight squeeze in your core; let the weight pull your shoulders down for a full stretch in the traps. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms completely straight, exhale and shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears in a vertical line.
Do not roll the shoulders or bend the elbows; the only movement should be the shoulder girdle rising and falling.
Squeeze and pause hard at the top for one second to maximally contract the traps.
Inhale and lower the weight slowly and under control back to the starting position, allowing the shoulders to drop into a full stretch before the next rep.

name: Linear 3-Part Start Technique
instructions: Find a line on the ground or any visible marker to start from, and stand with both feet on the line facing the direction you want to sprint.
Place your left foot so its toe sits next to your right ankle, then set your right foot 4 to 6 inches behind the left, staggering your stance.
Lower into a crouch by squatting down and leaning forward, loading most of your weight onto the front (left) leg.
Place your right hand on the line and bring your nose down close to your left knee so your head is lower than your hips.
Raise your left arm up and back so it is roughly parallel to the ground, pointing behind you, and hold this loaded, leaning starting position.
When ready, explode forward by driving violently off the front leg, punching the right arm forward and the left arm back to initiate the sprint.
Keep your body leaning forward through the first several steps, gradually rising as you accelerate rather than popping upright immediately.
Drive the knees aggressively and stay low so your force is directed forward, not vertically, for maximum acceleration out of the start.

name: Linear Acceleration Wall Drill
instructions: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away and place both hands flat on the wall at shoulder height.
Walk your feet back and lean your whole body into a straight line at roughly a 45-degree angle to the ground, weight on the balls of your feet.
Bring your feet together, contract your glutes, and keep your spine, hips, and head in one rigid line with no sag at the hips or piking at the waist.
Quickly lift your right knee up to about hip height, keeping the toe dorsiflexed (pulled up) and the ankle locked, then pause to hold the position.
Drive that right foot straight down and back into the ground forcefully, striking under your hip, and return to the tall double-support position.
Switch legs by raising the left knee, pausing, then hammering it straight down into the ground in the same manner.
Repeat once more with the right leg, then as soon as that foot strikes the ground, begin alternating left and right as fast as you can while keeping the body line rigid.
Maintain the forward lean and contracted glutes the entire time; do not let the hips drop or the chest rise toward vertical.

name: Linear Depth Jump
instructions: Set up two sturdy boxes or benches of similar height a few feet apart, far enough that you can comfortably jump from one to the other.
Stand on top of the first box facing the second platform, feet about hip to shoulder width apart and core braced.
Initiate the drop by stepping off the front edge so you fall straight down to the ground between the two platforms rather than jumping out.
Land softly on the balls of both feet, allowing your knees, hips, and ankles to flex and absorb the impact for a brief instant.
Immediately reverse direction as quickly as possible, minimizing ground contact time, and explode upward and forward by extending through the hips, knees, and ankles.
Drive your arms upward to add momentum as you jump onto the second platform.
Land softly on top of the second box with bent knees and hips to absorb the landing, finishing in a controlled athletic stance.

Focus on spending as little time on the ground as possible between the drop and the jump, as the reactive ground contact is the point of the drill; step down and reset before each rep rather than jumping down.

name: Lizard Pose
instructions: Start in a low lunge with your right foot forward, knee bent over the ankle, and your left leg extended straight back with the knee on or just off the floor.
Walk your right foot slightly outward and place both hands on the floor on the inside of your right (front) foot.
Keep your back leg active by pressing through the ball of the left foot, or lower the left knee to the mat for a gentler version.
Sink your hips down and forward, letting your weight settle to open the hip and stretch the front of the left hip and inner thigh.
If comfortable, lower down onto your forearms, walking the front foot wider if needed, and continue sinking the hips toward the floor.
Keep your chest lifted and spine long rather than rounding the upper back, and breathe slowly and deeply into the stretch.
Hold the position for 20 to 60 seconds, relaxing deeper on each exhale without bouncing.
Press back up to your hands, step the front foot back to a lunge, and switch sides to repeat with the left foot forward.

name: Log Lift
instructions: Stand with the log on the floor directly in front of your shins, feet about hip width apart, and roll the log so the neutral handles are positioned correctly under your grip.
Bend at the hips and knees, set a flat neutral back with chest up, and grasp the handles firmly with a neutral grip.
Begin the clean by driving through the legs and extending the hips explosively, pulling the log up your body and into your lap, then onto your chest as high as possible.
Drop your elbows underneath and roll the log up so it rests on the shelf of your chest and front of the shoulders; push your head back to clear a path.
Stand tall, brace your core hard, and look up to keep the log supported on your chest shelf in the starting press position.
Initiate the press with a dip by flexing slightly at the knees, then reverse explosively into a leg drive (push press) to launch the log upward.
As the log passes your face, push your head and chest through the window and finish by extending the elbows to lock the log overhead.
Hold the log locked out and stable overhead with the body straight, then control it back down to the chest and reset for the next rep.
Lower the log under control back to the floor by bending the hips and knees with a flat back; use whatever efficient technique suits you, as there are no strict form rules.
Keep your core braced throughout to protect your lower back, and never press with a soft, unbraced midsection.

name: London Bridges
instructions: Securely attach a thick climbing rope to a high, strong beam or cross member so it hangs down to roughly chest height.
Beneath the rope, lock a Smith machine bar in place with its safeties so it cannot move, or set up a solid, stable box to stand on as an alternative.
Stand on top of the locked bar and grasp the rope with both hands, using it to balance and support yourself in a tall standing position.
Set your feet so they stay planted on the bar throughout, brace your core, and keep your entire body straight from head to heels. This is your starting position.
Keeping your body rigid and straight, lean back and slowly lower yourself by moving hand over hand down the rope, letting your body angle away from vertical.
Continue descending hand over hand until your body is roughly perpendicular to the ground (parallel to the floor), feeling the lats and back working to control the descent.
Reverse the motion by pulling hand over hand back up the rope, keeping the body straight and core tight, until you return to the upright starting position.
Move smoothly and under control the whole time; do not let the body bend at the hips or jerk between hand placements.

name: Looking At Ceiling
instructions: Kneel on the floor on both knees, sitting your hips back so you are resting toward your heels.
Reach back and hold one heel in each hand to anchor your arms and support the position.
Brace your core gently to protect your lower back before moving.
Lift your buttocks up and forward, pushing the hips toward the front while squeezing the glutes.
At the same time, drop your head back and look up at the ceiling, creating a gentle backward arch through the spine.
Open the chest and stretch through the front of the thighs and abdomen, keeping the movement smooth and controlled.
Hold the stretched position briefly, breathing steadily, then lower the hips back down to the kneeling start.
Avoid forcing the neck or cranking the lower back; move only as far as feels comfortable and pain-free.

name: Low Cable Crossover
instructions: Set both pulleys to the lowest position on the cable column and select an equal, moderate resistance on each side.
Grasp a single handle in each hand and stand in the center between the two stacks.
Take a step forward to lift the weight off the stack and create tension, then stagger your feet slightly for balance with knees soft.
Let your arms hang down and slightly out to your sides with palms facing forward and hands below your waist; keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, lift your chest, and keep a slight forward lean from the hips with your back flat.
Exhale and draw both hands upward and inward in a scooping arc toward the midline of your body, leading with the pinkies.
Bring your hands together in front of the upper chest with palms facing up, squeezing the chest hard at the top.
Keep the elbow bend constant throughout so the movement comes from the shoulders, not from bending and straightening the arms like a press.
Pause briefly at the peak contraction, then inhale and lower your arms slowly back out and down along the same arc to the stretched starting position.

name: Low Cable Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a rope to the low pulley of a seated row machine or low cable station and select the desired weight.
Lie face up on the bench with your head pointing toward the cable attachment, so the rope feeds down toward the top of your head.
Reach back and grab the outside of each rope end with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Position your upper arms so they point straight up to the ceiling and your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees, with the forearms angled back toward the pulley behind your head.
Tuck your elbows in close and keep your upper arms perpendicular to your torso; this is your starting position and the elbows stay fixed here throughout.
Exhale and extend your forearms by straightening the elbows until your arms are straight and vertical, pointing the rope ends toward the ceiling.
Keep the upper arms and elbows completely stationary so only the forearms move; squeeze the triceps hard for one second at full extension.
Inhale and slowly lower the forearms back to the bent 90-degree starting position under control, feeling the stretch in the triceps.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, never letting the elbows flare out or drift toward your feet.

name: Low Pulley Row To Neck
instructions: Attach a rope to the low pulley of a seated row machine and select an appropriate weight.
Sit on the bench facing the pulley, place your feet on the platform with knees slightly bent, and sit up tall with a straight, nearly vertical back.

Grab the ends of the rope with a pronated (palms-down) grip and extend your arms fully out in front of you, allowing the weight to pull your shoulders into a slight stretch. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso completely still and upright, exhale as you lift your elbows up and out and bend them, pulling the rope toward your neck.
Throughout the pull keep your upper arms parallel to the floor and your elbows flaring out wide, away from your sides, to target the rear delts.
Continue pulling until your hands are almost beside your ears; the forearms will angle slightly upward at the end rather than staying parallel to the floor.
Squeeze the rear delts and upper back at the contracted position for about a second.
Inhale and slowly extend your arms back out to the fully stretched starting position under control.
Do not lean back, swing, or use momentum at any point; keep the movement strict and torso fixed throughout.

name: Lower Back Curl
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your legs extended straight behind you and the tops of your feet resting down.
Stretch your arms out to your sides at shoulder level, palms down, so the arms cannot be used to push.
Rest your forehead lightly toward the floor and relax your neck into a neutral position. This is your starting position.
Brace your core gently, then use your lower back muscles to extend your spine and lift your chest and head off the ground.
Keep your head in line with your spine and your gaze slightly forward as you rise, without throwing the head back.
Lift only as high as your lower back can take you on its own, without pressing through the arms or hands.
Pause and squeeze the lower back muscles briefly at the top of the lift.
Lower your chest slowly and under control back to the floor, then repeat for 10 to 20 controlled repetitions, avoiding any jerking or bouncing.

name: Lower Back-SMR
instructions: Sit on the floor and place a foam roller on the ground behind your hips, positioned to sit just under your lower back.
Lean back so the roller contacts your lower back, then cross your arms in front of your chest and round (protract) your shoulders forward.
Raise your hips off the floor so your bodyweight presses down onto the roller through your lower back. This is your starting position.
Shift your weight slightly to one side so the pressure rolls onto the muscles beside the spine rather than directly on the bony spine itself.
Slowly roll back and forth a few inches over the muscles of your lower back, searching for tight or tender points.
When you find a tender spot, pause and hold steady pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds until the tension eases.
Keep your weight off the center of the spine at all times and breathe steadily rather than holding your breath.
Repeat the process on the other side of the lower back, holding tension points as needed.

name: Lunge Pass Through
instructions: Stand tall with your torso upright, feet about hip width apart, holding a kettlebell by the handle in your right hand at your side. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and step forward with your left foot into a lunge stance, keeping your upper body vertical.
Lower straight down by bending the front hip and knee, dropping your back (right) knee until it nearly touches the floor; keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
At the bottom of the lunge, pass the kettlebell underneath your front (left) thigh from your right hand into your left hand.
Take a fresh, secure grip with the left hand before continuing so you do not drop the bell.
Press through the heel of your front foot to drive back up to the upright standing starting position.
On the next rep step forward with the opposite foot and pass the kettlebell back under the new front leg, alternating legs each repetition.
Keep your chest up and core tight throughout, and avoid letting the front knee cave inward or the torso pitch forward.

name: Lunge Sprint
instructions: Set the bar in a Smith machine to about upper-chest height and load an appropriate, manageable weight since this is an explosive movement.
Step under the bar and rack it across the upper back of your shoulders (the traps), not on your neck, gripping it slightly wider than shoulder width.
Rotate the hooks to unrack the bar, then split your stance by stepping one foot forward and the other foot back into a lunge position. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, keep your torso upright and chest tall, and set your weight evenly between both legs.
Lower your back knee toward the ground by flexing both knees and dropping your hips straight down.
At the bottom of the descent, immediately and explosively reverse direction, driving hard through the heel of the front foot with light assistance from the back foot.
Jump up off the floor and switch the position of your legs in the air so the front and back feet swap.
Land softly in a lunge with bent knees to absorb the impact, then immediately descend into the next rep and repeat, alternating legs each jump.

name: Lying Bent Leg Groin
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your spine neutral and your head resting comfortably on the floor.
Bend both knees and bring the soles of your feet together, then let your knees fall open to the sides so your legs form a diamond shape; slide your heels in toward your groin as comfort allows.
Relax your arms at your sides, keep your lower back lightly pressed to the floor, and breathe normally to settle into the position.
Have your partner kneel at your feet or beside you and place their hands gently on the inside of your knees; this is the starting position.
Inhale, then attempt to squeeze your knees together toward the midline while your partner resists so that no actual movement occurs, creating an isometric contraction of the adductors.
Hold this gentle contraction at roughly 20 to 30 percent effort for 10 to 20 seconds, breathing steadily rather than holding your breath.
Stop pushing and fully relax your inner thighs as you exhale, allowing your partner to slowly and gently press your knees toward the floor to deepen the stretch.
Hold the deeper stretch, feeling a mild pulling sensation in the inner thighs but never sharp pain, and tell your partner immediately when the stretch is adequate to avoid overstretching or injury.

name: Lying Cable Curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar or E-Z bar to the low pulley of a cable machine and set a light starting weight on the stack.
Lie flat on your back on a mat on the floor directly in front of the low pulley, facing up, with the crown of your head pointing toward the machine.
Place the soles of your feet flat against the base or frame of the pulley machine and keep your legs straight to anchor your body and prevent sliding.
Grab the bar with both hands using an underhand (supinated, palms-up) grip about shoulder-width apart.
Straighten your arms toward the pulley so the cable is taut, then pin your elbows close to your sides and put a slight bend in the arms; this is the starting position.
Brace your core and keep your upper arms locked stationary against the floor throughout the movement.
Exhale and curl the bar in a smooth arc up toward your chest by bending only at the elbows, squeezing the biceps hard as the bar rises.
Hold the fully contracted position for one second at the top, keeping your wrists straight rather than letting them roll back.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back along the same arc to the starting position over about two to three seconds, resisting the cable's pull.
Keep the upper arms motionless and avoid using your shoulders or jerking the bar; only the forearms should move. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Cambered Barbell Row
instructions: Load a cambered (bent) barbell with a moderate weight and place it on the floor directly underneath a flat exercise bench so the bar can hang below the bench surface.
Lie face down (prone) on the bench with your chest and stomach supported, positioning yourself so your head extends slightly past the end of the bench and your arms can hang straight down to the bar.
Let your legs straddle or rest alongside the bench for stability and keep your feet in contact with the floor or footrests.
Reach down and grab the bar with a pronated (palms-down) grip slightly wider than shoulder width, letting your arms hang fully extended toward the floor; this is the starting position.
Set your shoulder blades, brace your core, and keep your chest pressed into the bench so your torso stays completely still throughout the lift.

Exhale and row the bar straight up by driving your elbows up and back, keeping them fairly close to your body, pulling toward your upper chest to emphasize the upper mid-back or toward your lower stomach to emphasize the lats.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold the top contracted position for one second without letting your torso lift off the bench.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control back to the fully extended starting position, feeling a stretch across the back.
Avoid jerking the weight with your whole body; let the bench eliminate momentum so the back muscles do the work. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Close-Grip Bar Curl On High Pulley
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the high pulley of a lat pulldown or cable station and select a light starting weight.
Position a flat bench directly in front of and below the high pulley, lined up so the cable runs straight down toward where your shoulders will be.
Grasp the bar with an underhand (supinated, palms-up) grip about shoulder-width apart before lying down, or have a spotter hand it to you.
Lie back on the bench with your head near the end closest to the pulley so the cable is in line with your shoulders.
Extend your arms straight up above your shoulders so your torso and arms form a 90-degree angle, keeping your elbows tucked in and pointing toward the ceiling; this is the starting position.
Brace your core, keep your upper arms vertical and stationary, and fix your elbows in place pointing upward.
Exhale and curl the bar down in a semicircular arc toward your chin by bending only at the elbows until the bar lightly reaches your chin or forehead, squeezing the biceps hard.
Hold the peak contraction for one second, making sure the upper arms have not moved or drifted.
Inhale and slowly return the bar to the fully extended starting position above your shoulders, controlling the cable's pull.
Keep only the forearms moving and the upper arms perpendicular throughout; do not let the elbows flare or swing. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Close-Grip Barbell Triceps Extension Behind The Head
instructions: Load a light barbell or E-Z curl bar; if using a straight bar take a shoulder-width grip, if using an E-Z bar grip the inner angled handles, both with a pronated (palms-forward) grip.
Sit on the end of a flat bench holding the bar, then lie back so your head is near the end of the bench, feet planted on the floor and back flat.
Brace your core, then press the bar up and extend your arms in front of you.
Keeping your arms straight, slowly lower them back in a semicircular motion until they are overhead and parallel to the floor; this is the starting position with elbows tucked in.
Inhale and lower the bar by bending only at the elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary and angled back, until your forearms are perpendicular to the floor and the bar is near or behind your head.
Keep your elbows pointing away from your body and tucked in rather than flaring out as you lower.
Exhale and push the bar back up in a semicircular motion by extending the elbows until your forearms are once again parallel to the floor.
Contract the triceps hard for one second at the top, making sure the upper arms have stayed fixed in place.
Move only the forearms throughout; keep the upper arms angled overhead and motionless to keep tension on the triceps. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Close-Grip Barbell Triceps Press To Chin
instructions: Load a light E-Z curl bar or barbell and grip it with a pronated, palms-forward grip; on an E-Z bar use the inner angled handles, on a straight bar use a shoulder-width grip.
Lie back on a flat bench positioned so your head is right at or just off the end of the bench, keeping your back flat and feet planted on the floor.
Press the bar up and extend your arms so it is held directly over your chest with the arms perpendicular to your torso at a 90-degree angle; this is the starting position.
Brace your core and keep your upper arms vertical and fixed in place throughout.
Inhale and lower the bar in a semicircular motion by bending at the elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary and elbows tucked in, until the bar lightly touches your chin.
Control the descent so the bar travels back toward your chin rather than straight down to your chest, which keeps tension on the triceps.
Exhale and press the bar back up along the same arc by extending the elbows until your arms are straight over your chest again.
Squeeze the triceps hard for one second at the top, ensuring the upper arms have not drifted.
Keep only the forearms moving and the upper arms motionless; use a controlled tempo and avoid letting the bar bang into your chin. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Crossover
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with both legs extended straight and your arms out to your sides for stability.
Keep your shoulders and upper back flat on the floor throughout to isolate the stretch to the hip and outer thigh.
Bend one knee and lift that leg, then cross it over your body toward the opposite side, lowering the knee toward the floor on the far side while keeping the same-side shoulder down.
Have your partner kneel beside you and hold that shoulder down with one hand while their other hand controls the crossed leg; this is the starting position.
Inhale, then attempt to raise the bent knee back up and away from the floor while your partner resists so no actual movement occurs, creating an isometric contraction in the outer hip and abductors.
Hold this gentle contraction at low effort for 10 to 20 seconds, breathing steadily.
Stop pushing and fully relax the leg as you exhale, allowing your partner to gently press the knee farther toward the floor to deepen the stretch through the outer hip and glute.
Hold the deeper stretch while keeping your opposite shoulder pinned down, then switch and repeat on the other side. Tell your partner when the stretch is adequate to avoid overstretching.

name: Lying Dumbbell Tricep Extension
instructions: Select two light dumbbells and sit on the end of a flat bench, then lie back flat with your head supported and feet planted firmly on the floor.
Press the dumbbells up so your arms are fully extended and perpendicular to your torso and the floor, holding them directly over your shoulders.
Rotate your wrists so your palms face each other (neutral grip) and tuck your elbows in toward each other rather than letting them flare out; this is the starting position.
Brace your core and keep your upper arms vertical and stationary throughout the movement.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells by bending only at the elbows, bringing them down toward the sides of your head until they are near your ears.
Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing toward the ceiling so the upper arms do not drift back or splay out.
Exhale and use the triceps to extend the elbows and press the dumbbells back up to the starting position over your shoulders.
Squeeze the triceps hard for one second at the top without snapping the elbows into a hard lockout.
Move only the forearms and keep the upper arms fixed; control the weights to protect the elbows. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Face Down Plate Neck Resistance
instructions: Select a light weight plate and lie face down (prone) on a flat bench with your whole body straight and your legs extended behind you.
Position yourself so your shoulders are just past the end of the bench, allowing your upper chest, neck, and face to hang off the edge.
Anchor your body by gripping the sides of the bench or letting your toes rest on the floor for stability so only your head moves.
Place the weight plate flat against the back of your head and hold it securely in place with both hands; this is the starting position with your neck in a neutral, slightly extended position.
Inhale and slowly lower your head by tucking your chin toward your chest in a nodding (yes) motion, moving only at the neck and controlling the plate's weight.
Lower under control through a comfortable range without forcing it, keeping the rest of your body still.
Exhale and raise your head back up in a smooth semicircular motion until your neck returns to the starting position.
Hold the top contraction for one second, then continue with slow, controlled reps and never jerk the neck. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Face Up Plate Neck Resistance
instructions: Select a light weight plate and lie face up (supine) on a flat bench with your whole body straight and your back flat against the bench.
Position yourself so your shoulders are just past the end of the bench, allowing your traps, neck, and head to hang off the edge.
Plant your feet on the floor and grip the bench or keep your body braced so only your head moves during the exercise.
Place the weight plate on your forehead and hold it securely with both hands; this is the starting position with your neck in a neutral position.
Inhale and slowly lower your head backward in a controlled semicircular motion, letting the neck extend through a comfortable range while supporting the plate.
Keep the movement smooth and avoid letting the head drop, controlling the plate's weight at all times.
Exhale and raise your head back up by flexing the neck forward in a semicircular motion until you return to the starting position.
Hold the contraction for one second at the top, then continue with slow, deliberate reps and never use momentum. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Glute
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with both legs extended and your upper body relaxed against the floor.
Have your partner kneel beside you on the side of the leg you will stretch first.
Flex the hip of one leg and raise it off the floor, then rotate it across your body so the foot crosses over toward the opposite hip and the lower leg is roughly perpendicular to your torso.
Let your partner hold the bent knee and the ankle to support and control the leg; keep your opposite leg flat and your back on the floor. This is the starting position.
Inhale, then attempt to push your bent leg back toward your partner, away from your chest, while they resist so no movement occurs, creating an isometric contraction in the glute.
Hold this gentle contraction at low effort for 10 to 20 seconds, breathing steadily throughout.
Stop pushing and completely relax as you exhale, allowing your partner to gently press the ankle and knee toward your chest to deepen the stretch in the glute and outer hip.
Hold the deeper stretch, then switch sides. Tell your partner when the stretch is adequate to avoid overstretching or injury.

name: Lying Hamstring
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with both legs extended and your upper body relaxed against the floor.
Have your partner kneel beside you near the leg you will stretch first.
Keeping your knee straight, raise one leg up toward the ceiling as far as is comfortable while the other leg stays flat on the floor with a neutral foot.
Have your partner hold your raised ankle and brace your leg against their shoulder if needed to keep it in place; this is the starting position.

Inhale, then attempt to push your raised leg back down toward the floor, contracting the hamstrings, while your partner resists so no movement occurs, holding the isometric contraction for 10 to 20 seconds.
Breathe steadily during the contraction and keep your raised knee straight and your hips on the floor.
Stop pushing and fully relax your leg as you exhale, allowing your partner to gently push the straight leg farther toward your head to deepen the hamstring and calf stretch.
Hold the deeper stretch, feeling a pull along the back of the thigh and calf but never sharp pain, then switch sides. Tell your partner when the stretch is adequate to avoid overstretching.

name: Lying High Bench Barbell Curl
instructions: Load a light barbell or E-Z bar; on a straight bar take a shoulder-width grip, on an E-Z bar use the inner angled handles, with a supinated (palms-up) grip.
Lie face down (prone) on a tall flat bench positioned high enough that your hanging arms clear the floor.

Position your body so your upper chest is just over the end of the bench and the barbell hangs straight down in front of you with your arms fully extended and perpendicular to the floor; this is the starting position.
Press your chest into the bench, brace your core, and pin your upper arms stationary so they do not swing.
Exhale and curl the barbell up in a semicircular arc by bending only at the elbows, squeezing the biceps as the bar rises toward your shoulders.
Keep your elbows tucked in and your upper arms fixed against the bench edge so only the forearms move.
Hold the top contracted position for one second, getting a strong biceps squeeze.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back along the same arc to the fully extended starting position, maintaining full control.
Avoid any swinging or using body momentum; the strict prone position eliminates cheating. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Leg Curls
instructions: Set up at a lying leg curl machine, ideally an angled (cambered) one, and adjust the leg pad so it rests on the back of your legs just a few inches below the calves, around the lower Achilles area.
Select an appropriate weight and lie face down on the machine with your torso flat against the pad and your kneecaps positioned just off the edge of the bench.
Hook the back of your lower legs under the roller pad and grab the side handles to keep your torso anchored.
Fully extend your legs so the hamstrings are stretched, and set your toes pointing straight, or angled in or out for variation; this is the starting position.
Exhale and curl your legs up by flexing at the knees, bringing your heels toward your glutes as far as possible without lifting your thighs or hips off the pad.
Squeeze the hamstrings hard and hold the fully contracted position for one second at the top.
Inhale and slowly lower the weight back down under control to the fully extended starting position, resisting the descent.
Keep your hips pressed down and avoid jerking or arching your lower back to lift the weight; let the hamstrings do the work. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Machine Squat
instructions: Adjust the lying (horizontal hack-style) leg machine so that when you lie in it your knees are bent and your thighs sit slightly below parallel to the foot platform.
Select your weight, then position yourself face up inside the machine with your back and head resting against the backrest and your shoulders pressed firmly under the shoulder pads.
Place your feet flat on the platform at about shoulder width with toes pointed slightly outward, ensuring your knees track over your toes and do not extend past them.
Bend your knees so your thighs start slightly below parallel, making the angle between your hamstrings and calves slightly less than 90 degrees; grasp the handles. This is the starting position.
Brace your core and keep your back and head in contact with the pad throughout.

Exhale and press through the balls of your feet to straighten your legs and extend your whole body, squeezing the quads at the top; you may push lightly on your thighs with your hands to assist out of the deep start on the first rep.
Hold the contracted, near-locked position for one second without snapping the knees.

Inhale and slowly squat down under control, but stop once your thighs reach parallel to the platform (a 90-degree angle between hamstrings and calves) rather than going all the way back to the deep start.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes and avoid letting them cave inward. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying One-Arm Lateral Raise
instructions: Select a light dumbbell and lie chest-down (prone) on a flat bench, or lie on your side with the working shoulder on top, holding the dumbbell in one hand hanging down toward the floor.
Use your free hand to grip the leg or edge of the bench for stability and to keep your torso fixed.
Turn the palm of the working hand to face your torso (neutral grip) and keep that arm extended down with only a slight bend at the elbow; this is the starting position.
Brace your core and keep your shoulder, back, and torso still so the movement comes only from the shoulder joint.
Exhale and raise the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc until your elbow reaches shoulder height and your arm is roughly parallel to the floor, keeping the arm perpendicular to your torso.
Lead with the elbow and keep the slight elbow bend constant rather than bending or straightening the arm during the lift.
Hold the top contracted position for one second, feeling the side delt engage.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back along the same arc to the starting position under full control.
Avoid swinging or using momentum; use a light weight so the side deltoid does the work. Complete all reps, then switch arms. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Prone Quadriceps
instructions: Lie face down (prone) on a flat, padded surface or the floor with your legs extended straight behind you, hips pressed flat into the ground, and forehead resting on your folded arms or the mat so your spine stays neutral.
Have your partner kneel beside your hips on the side of the leg you intend to stretch first.
Bend one knee and lift that foot toward your glutes, bringing the heel as close to the buttock as is comfortable; this is your starting position.
Have your partner place one hand on the back of your bent knee to keep the thigh down on the ground and the other hand cupped around your ankle or the top of your foot.

Push your foot away from your glutes (attempting to straighten the knee) against your partner's resistance, building to about 70 percent effort while your partner holds the leg completely still so no movement occurs; breathe steadily and never hold your breath.
Maintain this isometric contraction for 10 to 20 seconds, keeping your hips pinned flat to avoid arching your lower back.

Relax the leg fully and exhale as your partner gently guides your foot closer toward your glutes, easing into a deeper stretch through the quadriceps and hip flexors until you feel mild tension, not pain.
Hold the deepened stretch for 10 to 20 seconds while keeping the front of the hip and pelvis in contact with the ground so the stretch targets the quads rather than the lower back.
Carefully lower the leg back to the floor, then repeat the contract-relax sequence on the opposite leg.

name: Lying Rear Delt Raise
instructions: Set a flat bench and grab a light dumbbell in each hand, since the rear delts respond to control rather than heavy load.
Lie face down (prone) on the bench so your chest and stomach are supported, your head extends just past the top edge, and your legs straddle the bench or rest on the floor for stability.
Let both arms hang straight down toward the floor and position the dumbbells with a neutral grip, palms facing each other and in toward your torso.
Keep your elbows only slightly bent and lock that angle for the entire set, then brace your core and squeeze your shoulder blades lightly together; this is your starting position.
Exhale and raise both arms out to the sides in a wide arc, leading with the elbows, until your upper arms reach shoulder height and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Keep your arms perpendicular to your torso throughout and focus on driving the movement with the rear delts and upper back rather than shrugging or swinging the weights up.
Hold the contracted position for a one-second squeeze, keeping the neck relaxed and the chest down on the bench.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the hanging starting position under full control, resisting the weight the whole way down.
Avoid using momentum or letting the elbows straighten; if you cannot keep the arc smooth, reduce the weight, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying Spinal Twist
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended straight and your arms resting at your sides.
Bend one knee and draw that thigh up toward your chest while keeping the opposite leg long on the floor.
Use your opposite hand to gently guide the bent knee across the midline of your body and toward the floor on the other side, letting your hips and lower spine rotate.
Extend the same-side arm (the arm on the side of the bent leg) straight out to the side at shoulder height, palm up, and turn your head to gaze toward that extended hand.
Keep both shoulder blades reaching toward the floor so you feel a gentle twist through the lower back, glutes, and chest rather than forcing the knee down.
Breathe slowly and deeply, allowing the knee to settle a little closer to the floor with each exhale, never pushing into pain.
Hold the position for 20 to 30 seconds, keeping the movement relaxed and the spine long.
Return the knee to center, extend the leg, and repeat the twist on the opposite side.

name: Lying Supine Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Select a pair of light-to-moderate dumbbells, since the lengthened position of this curl is demanding on the biceps.
Lie face up (supine) on a flat bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor on either side and a dumbbell resting on top of each thigh.
Let both arms hang straight down off the sides of the bench toward the floor, with a neutral grip so the palms face in toward your thighs and the elbows are only slightly bent.
Pin your upper arms in this hanging position close to your torso; this fully stretched bottom position is your starting position and your elbows must stay fixed here throughout.
Exhale and slowly curl both dumbbells upward, simultaneously rotating (supinating) your wrists so the palms turn to face up as you lift.
Continue curling until the biceps are fully contracted, then squeeze hard at the top for a one-second hold.
Keep only the forearms moving; the upper arms and elbows should remain stationary and tucked in, with no swinging from the shoulders.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells very slowly back to the deep stretched starting position, resisting gravity the entire way.
Avoid letting the elbows drift forward or the shoulders take over; if you cannot control the descent, lighten the load, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Lying T-Bar Row
instructions: Load the lying (chest-supported) T-bar row machine with your desired weight plates on the loading pin.
Adjust the leg height or platform step so that when you lie down, your upper chest sits right at the top edge of the angled pad and your arms can hang fully without the plates touching the floor.
Lie face down on the pad with your chest and stomach supported, feet braced on the platform or floor for stability.

Reach down and grip the handles using your chosen grip: a pronated (palms-down) wide grip emphasizes the upper back and rear delts, while a neutral or supinated grip shifts work toward the lats and lower lats.
Lift the bar slightly to unrack it and let your arms extend straight down; brace your core, retract your shoulder blades to set them, and this is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the handles up toward the pad by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together, leading with the elbows rather than the hands.
Keep the upper arms relatively close to your torso and concentrate on contracting the back muscles, not yanking with the biceps.
Hold the peak contraction for a one-second squeeze at the top without letting your chest or hips rise off the pad.
Inhale and lower the weight slowly and under control back to the fully extended starting position, feeling the stretch across your back.
Keep your body flat on the pad the entire set to protect your lower back, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions before carefully re-racking the bar.

name: Lying Triceps Press
instructions: Place a loaded E-Z curl bar (preferred for wrist comfort) or straight bar on the floor just behind the head end of a flat bench.
Lie face up on the bench with your feet flat on the floor and your head near the end closest to the bar.
Reach back overhead and grasp the bar with a medium-width overhand (pronated) grip, hands roughly shoulder-width on the angled portions of the E-Z bar.

Press the bar up and bring it forward so it is held at arm's length over your upper chest, with your arms perpendicular to both the torso and the floor and your elbows tucked in; this is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar by bending only at the elbows, keeping the upper arms fixed in place, until the bar lightly touches or nearly touches your forehead.
Keep your elbows pointed roughly toward your knees and tucked in rather than flaring out to the sides, which maximizes triceps involvement and protects the elbows.
Without bouncing the bar off your head, exhale and use the triceps to press the weight back up to the locked-out starting position.
Keep the upper arms stationary throughout so only the forearms move, and maintain a controlled tempo on both the descent and the press.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then carefully lower the bar back to the floor behind your head.

name: Machine Bench Press
instructions: Adjust the seat of the chest press machine so that the handles align with the middle of your chest when seated, then select your desired weight on the stack.
Sit down with your back flat against the back pad, your feet planted firmly on the floor, and your shoulder blades pinned back and down for a stable base.
If the machine has a foot lever, step on it to bring the handles forward within reach so you do not have to strain your shoulders to grab them.
Grip the handles with a palms-down (pronated) grip and position your upper arms so they are roughly parallel to the floor out to the sides of your torso, with forearms pointing forward.
Release the foot lever and press the handles out until your arms are fully extended; this is your starting position.

Inhale and slowly bring the handles back toward your chest under control, keeping your elbows at roughly a 75 to 90 degree angle to your torso and stopping when you feel a comfortable stretch across the chest.
Exhale and push the handles away from you by flexing your pecs, driving until your arms are extended without harshly locking the elbows.
Hold the contraction for a second at the top, keeping your back against the pad and avoiding any shrugging of the shoulders.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then step on the foot lever again to safely return the handles to their resting position.

name: Machine Bicep Curl
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that when you sit, the back of your upper arms rest flat and fully along the angled arm pad, with your armpits resting near the top edge of the pad.
Select your desired weight on the stack and sit down with your chest against the support, your torso upright, and your feet flat on the floor.
Place the backs of your upper arms firmly against the pad and grasp the handles with an underhand (supinated) grip, palms facing up.
Keep your shoulders down and back and your upper arms pressed into the pad; this is your starting position.
Curl the handles upward by flexing at the elbows, bringing your lower arms toward your upper arms while keeping the upper arms motionless on the pad.
Exhale as you lift and squeeze the biceps hard, then pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the weight back down under control, resisting the descent rather than letting the stack drop.
Stop just short of letting the weight plates touch the stack at the bottom so constant tension stays on the biceps, and avoid leaning back or using your body to heave the weight.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, only resting the weight on the stops once the set is complete.

name: Machine Preacher Curls
instructions: Adjust the seat of the preacher curl machine so that when seated, your armpits rest comfortably over the top of the angled pad and your upper arms lie flat against it, then select your weight.
Sit down with your chest against the support and your feet flat on the floor for a stable base.
Lay the backs of your upper arms (your triceps) flat on the preacher pad and grasp the handles with an underhand (supinated) grip, palms facing up.
Keep your elbows tucked in and roughly shoulder-width apart on the pad rather than letting them flare outward; this is your starting position.
Exhale and curl the handles upward by contracting the biceps, bringing your forearms toward your upper arms.
Hold the peak contraction for a one-second squeeze at the top, keeping the upper arms flat and stationary on the pad at all times.
Inhale and lower the handles slowly back toward the starting position, controlling the descent and feeling the stretch in the biceps.
Stop just short of full lockout at the bottom to keep tension on the muscle and protect the elbow joint, and never let the weight drop quickly.
Keep only the forearms moving throughout, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Machine Shoulder (Military) Press
instructions: Adjust the seat of the shoulder press machine so that the handles sit at about shoulder height when you are seated, then select your desired weight.
Sit down with your back flat against the back pad, your feet planted firmly on the floor, and your core braced to keep your torso upright.

Grasp the handles to the sides of your shoulders with a palms-forward (pronated) grip, keeping your elbows bent and roughly in line with or just in front of your torso; this is your starting position.
Exhale and press the handles upward by extending your arms fully overhead, driving through the shoulders and triceps.
Stop just short of harshly locking out the elbows and hold the contraction at the top for a second.
Keep your back against the pad and avoid arching your lower back or shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears as you press.
Inhale and lower the handles slowly back down to the starting position, controlling the weight until your hands are at about shoulder height.
Maintain a smooth, controlled tempo and keep your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows throughout, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Machine Triceps Extension
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that when seated, the backs of your upper arms rest flat and fully along the arm pad with your elbows aligned to the machine's pivot point, then select your weight.
Sit down with your chest against the support, your torso upright, and your feet flat on the floor for stability.
Place the backs of your upper arms firmly against the pad and grasp the handles with your chosen grip, keeping your wrists neutral and firm.
Keep your shoulders down and your upper arms pressed into the pad; this is your starting position.
Perform the movement by extending the elbows, driving your lower arms away from your upper arms until your arms are nearly straight.
Exhale as you extend and squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom of the movement, keeping the upper arms motionless on the pad.
Pause briefly at full extension without harshly locking out, then inhale and slowly return the weight under control as the elbows bend back.
Stop just short of letting the weight plates rest on the stack so tension stays on the triceps, and avoid using your shoulders or leaning forward to force the weight.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, only resting the weight on the stops once the set is complete.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
instructions: Select a medicine ball of a weight you can throw explosively while still controlling it, and find a partner standing several feet in front of you; if you have no partner, stand facing a solid wall instead.
Stand with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart in an athletic stance, knees slightly bent and core braced.
Hold the ball with both hands at chest height, fingers spread around the sides and elbows pointing out and down; this is your starting position.
Pull the ball in slightly toward your chest to load the movement.
Explosively extend through both elbows and push the ball away from your chest toward your partner or the wall, snapping the wrists at release for maximum power.
For sports applications, you may take a step forward as you throw to add lower-body drive into the pass.
Keep your core tight and avoid arching your lower back as you generate force through the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
Receive the return throw or rebound with both hands at chest height, absorbing the impact by bending the elbows and bringing the ball back to your chest.
Reset to the starting position and repeat for the prescribed repetitions, keeping each throw crisp and controlled.

name: Medicine Ball Full Twist
instructions: Select a medicine ball you can pass quickly and stand back to back with a partner, spaced about 2 to 3 feet apart.
Stand with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and core braced; have one partner hold the ball in front of the trunk to begin. This is your starting position.
The partner with the ball rotates the torso to one side, opening the hips and turning the shoulders together while the other partner rotates in the same direction to meet them.
Agree on a consistent direction (for example, both rotating counter-clockwise) so the ball travels a full circle around the pair.
Pass the ball to your partner at the point where you both meet behind your backs, keeping your arms extended and the ball close to waist height.
Immediately reverse and both twist in the opposite direction to bring the ball back around and repeat the hand-off.
Keep the movement controlled and rhythmic, rotating from the trunk and hips rather than just the arms, and keep your spine tall throughout.
Continue passing back and forth for the prescribed repetitions or time, then reverse direction to balance both sides.

name: Medicine Ball Scoop Throw
instructions: Select a medicine ball and stand in an open area with plenty of clearance behind you, since the ball will travel backward and overhead.
Assume a semi-squat stance with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart, hips back, and knees bent.
Hold the ball in both hands with your arms hanging down between your legs so the ball is near your feet; this is your starting position.
Initiate the throw by explosively thrusting your hips forward and extending powerfully through the knees and ankles, jumping upward.
As you extend, swing both arms upward and overhead in a scooping arc, keeping the arms long and extended.
Release the ball at the peak of your upward movement, aiming to throw it as far as possible behind and over your head.
Keep your core braced and your chest up throughout to transfer force efficiently from the legs through the trunk to the arms.
Retrieve the ball, reset to the semi-squat starting position, and repeat each throw with maximal explosive effort for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Middle Back Shrug
instructions: Set an incline bench to roughly a 30 to 45 degree angle and select a pair of light-to-moderate dumbbells.
Lie face down (prone) on the incline bench with your chest and stomach supported and your head extending just past the top edge.
Let both arms hang straight down toward the floor with a neutral grip, palms facing each other; this is your starting position.
Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together and slightly down, retracting them as if performing the reverse of a hug, while keeping the arms long and the elbows only slightly bent.
Drive the movement entirely from the shoulder blades and mid-back rather than bending the elbows or curling the weight up.
Hold the retracted contraction for a full second, feeling the squeeze across the rhomboids and mid-traps.
Inhale and slowly let the shoulder blades spread apart again, lowering the dumbbells back to the hanging starting position under control.
Keep your chest on the bench and avoid jerking the weights; if you cannot isolate the shoulder blades, reduce the load, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Middle Back Stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly soft.
Place your hands on your hips and brace your core lightly to protect your lower back.
Keeping your hips and feet facing forward and relatively still, slowly rotate your torso to one side at the waist until you feel a gentle stretch through your mid-back and obliques.
Keep your shoulders down and your spine tall, breathing slowly and avoiding any forced or bouncing motion.
Hold the stretch for 10 to 15 seconds at the point of mild tension, not pain.
Return slowly to center, then rotate to the opposite side and hold for the same duration to stretch both sides evenly.

name: Mixed Grip Chin
instructions: Stand under a fixed pull-up bar and reach up to grip it with your hands about one to two inches wider than shoulder-width apart. Take a mixed (alternating) grip: one palm facing toward you (supinated) and the other palm facing away (pronated).
Wrap your thumbs fully around the bar and grip firmly. Let your body hang with arms fully extended, ankles crossed behind you and a slight bend in the knees so your feet clear the floor.
Set your shoulders by pulling your shoulder blades down and back out of your ears, brace your core, and keep a slight hollow-body position with the ribs tucked rather than swinging.

Take a breath, then pull yourself up by driving your elbows down toward your ribs. With the supinated (palm-up) arm, focus on squeezing the back and biceps while keeping that elbow tight to your torso; with the pronated (palm-away) arm, drive through the lat with the elbow flared slightly but in line with your torso.
Exhale as you rise and continue until your collarbone or chin clears the bar and your chest is near the bar.
Pause for one second at the top and consciously squeeze your shoulder blades together, avoiding any kipping or kicking of the legs.
Inhale and lower yourself slowly and under control over about two to three seconds until your arms are fully extended and shoulder blades reset at the bottom.
