Keeping your spine tall and ribs down without arching the lower back, gently attempt to extend the arm straight up while your partner holds it in place so it does not move, in an isometric contraction.
Hold this gentle effort for 10 to 20 seconds while breathing steadily.
Relax the arm completely and exhale, then let your partner apply slow, gentle pressure to the wrist to ease the hand further down your back and deepen the triceps stretch.
Hold the deepened stretch for 10 to 20 seconds, staying relaxed and never pushing into pain.
Lower the arm, then switch and repeat the same sequence on the other side.
Common mistakes: arching the lower back to gain range, forcing past mild tension, and the partner pulling too hard or too fast.

name: Pallof Press
instructions: Attach a single handle to an adjustable cable column and set it to about chest height (a low pulley works if no adjustment is available), selecting a light to moderate weight.
Stand side-on to the machine, then grab the handle with both hands, interlocking your fingers around it, and draw it to the center of your chest.
Step away from the column until your arms are roughly arm's length and there is constant tension on the cable trying to rotate your torso toward the machine.
Set your feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, hips and shoulders squared straight ahead, and brace your core hard; this is your starting position.
Exhale and slowly press the handle straight out from your chest until both arms are fully extended in front of your sternum.
Resist the cable's pull to rotate you, keeping your hips and shoulders facing forward and your spine stacked, fighting the anti-rotation challenge with your core.
Hold the fully pressed position for two to three seconds, keeping the handle on the centerline of your body.
Bring the handle back to the center of your chest slowly and under control without letting your torso twist toward the machine.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then turn around so your other side faces the column and perform the same number to work both sides.
Common mistakes: letting the torso rotate or lean toward the cable, holding your breath instead of bracing, and pressing the handle off to one side rather than straight down the midline.

name: Pallof Press With Rotation
instructions: Attach a single handle to an adjustable cable column and set it to about shoulder or chest height, selecting a light to moderate weight.
Stand side-on to the machine and grab the handle with the hand nearest the column, then step away so your outstretched arm aligns with the cable and there is tension on it.
Set your feet hip-width apart with knees slightly bent, then pull the handle in toward your chest and place your other hand on it so both hands grip the handle.
Square your hips and shoulders straight ahead, brace your core hard, and keep your spine stacked; this is your starting position.
Facing forward, exhale and press the handle straight out from your chest until both arms are fully extended in front of your sternum.
Keeping your hips fixed and facing forward, slowly rotate your torso away from the column until you reach about a quarter turn, moving from the trunk rather than the arms.
Maintain straight arms and a rigid stance, then rotate back to the neutral forward position in a slow, controlled manner with arms still extended.
While the side tension keeps engaging your core, draw the handle back to the center of your chest, then immediately press it out again to full extension; this completes one rep.
Repeat for the prescribed reps or to controlled failure, then reposition so the opposite side faces the column and perform the same series on the other side.
Common mistakes: rotating from the hips instead of stabilizing them, letting the arms bend during the twist, and losing core tension so the cable pulls you off balance.

name: Palms-Down Dumbbell Wrist Curl Over A Bench
instructions: Place two light dumbbells on the floor at one end of a flat bench, within easy reach.
Kneel on the floor on both knees facing the long side of the bench, so the bench top sits at roughly mid-thigh to waist height in front of you.
Grip a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip (palms facing down, knuckles up), holding the handles toward the base of your fingers rather than buried deep in the palm.

Lay both forearms flat along the top of the bench, parallel to each other, so your wrists and hands hang off the near edge with nothing supporting them. Press your forearms firmly down so they cannot move.

Set your torso so your chest is close to the bench, back flat, core braced, and elbows roughly shoulder-width apart. Let your wrists drop fully so the dumbbells lower toward the floor and you feel a stretch along the top of your forearms. This is the start position.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward by extending them, lifting the backs of your hands toward you while keeping your forearms pinned flat to the bench. Move only at the wrist joint.
Squeeze the top of your forearms (the extensors) for a brief moment at the top of the range without letting your elbows or forearms lift off the bench.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly under control back to the fully stretched bottom position, taking about two seconds on the way down.
Keep the weight light and the tempo controlled; do not swing the body or use momentum, since the forearm extensors are small and easily strained. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Palms-Down Wrist Curl Over A Bench
instructions: Load a barbell lightly and rest it on the floor at one end of a flat bench, within easy reach.
Kneel on the floor on both knees facing the long side of the bench, so the bench top sits at about mid-thigh to waist height in front of you.
Grip the bar with both hands using a pronated grip (palms facing down, knuckles up), hands roughly shoulder-width apart, holding the bar in your fingers rather than deep in the palms.

Lay both forearms flat along the top of the bench, parallel and roughly shoulder-width apart, so your wrists and hands hang off the near edge unsupported. Press the forearms firmly into the bench so they stay locked in place.

Set your torso close to the bench with a flat back and braced core. Let your wrists relax and drop so the bar lowers toward the floor and you feel a stretch across the top of your forearms. This is the start position.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward by extending them, raising the backs of your hands toward you while keeping the forearms glued to the bench. Move only at the wrist.
Pause and squeeze the forearm extensors at the top without letting your elbows or forearms lift.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control back to the fully stretched bottom position, taking about two seconds.
Use a light load and strict form; avoid any swinging or jerking, as the forearm extensors are small and prone to strain. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Palms-Up Barbell Wrist Curl Over A Bench
instructions: Load a barbell lightly and set it on the floor at one end of a flat bench, within easy reach.
Kneel on the floor on both knees facing the long side of the bench, so the bench top is about mid-thigh to waist height in front of you.
Grip the bar with both hands using a supinated grip (palms facing up), hands roughly shoulder-width apart, letting the bar roll down into your fingers at the bottom of each rep for full range.

Lay both forearms flat along the top of the bench, parallel and roughly shoulder-width apart, so your wrists and hands hang off the near edge unsupported. Press your forearms firmly into the bench so they cannot move.

Set your torso close to the bench with a flat back and braced core, elbows roughly shoulder-width. Let your wrists open and the bar roll toward your fingertips so you feel a stretch through the underside of your forearms. This is the start position.
Exhale and curl your wrists upward by flexing them, rolling the bar back into your palms and lifting it as high as possible while keeping the forearms pinned to the bench. Move only at the wrist.
Squeeze the forearm flexors hard at the top for a brief moment without letting your elbows or forearms rise off the bench.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly under control back to the fully stretched bottom position, letting it roll down to the fingers again over about two seconds.
Keep the weight controlled and avoid swinging or using the biceps; the movement should be felt entirely in the front of the forearms. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Palms-Up Dumbbell Wrist Curl Over A Bench
instructions: Place two light dumbbells on the floor at one end of a flat bench, within easy reach.
Kneel on the floor on both knees facing the long side of the bench, so the bench top sits at about mid-thigh to waist height in front of you.
Grip a dumbbell in each hand with a supinated grip (palms facing up), letting the handles roll down toward your fingers at the bottom of each rep for a full stretch.

Lay both forearms flat along the top of the bench, parallel and roughly shoulder-width apart, so your wrists and hands hang off the near edge unsupported. Press your forearms firmly into the bench so they remain stationary.

Set your torso close to the bench with a flat back, braced core, and elbows roughly shoulder-width. Let your wrists open so the dumbbells roll toward your fingertips and you feel a stretch under your forearms. This is the start position.

Exhale and curl your wrists upward by flexing them, rolling the dumbbells back into your palms and lifting them as high as possible while keeping your forearms pinned to the bench. Move only at the wrist.
Squeeze the forearm flexors at the top for a moment without letting your elbows or forearms lift off the bench.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly under control back to the fully stretched bottom position over about two seconds.
Keep the load light and the tempo strict; do not swing the body or recruit the biceps. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Parallel Bar Dip
instructions: Set up at a parallel dip station where the bars are roughly shoulder-width apart; bars slightly wider than the shoulders work for a chest emphasis, closer for a triceps emphasis.
Grip a bar in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), wrists straight and stacked over the bars.
Press down through your hands and jump or step up to support your bodyweight at the top with arms fully extended and elbows locked out. This is the start position.

Set your posture: pull your shoulders down and back away from your ears, brace your core, and keep your chest up. For a triceps focus stay as upright as possible; for a chest focus lean your torso slightly forward.
Cross your ankles and bend your knees behind you to keep your legs from swinging, keeping your body still and controlled.

Inhale and lower yourself by bending the elbows under control, descending until your upper arms reach roughly parallel to the floor (about 90 degrees at the elbow). Avoid going so deep that you feel shoulder strain.
Keep your elbows tracking back rather than flaring wide, and do not let your shoulders shrug up toward your ears at the bottom.
Exhale and press back up by extending the elbows, driving through your hands until your arms are fully locked out again at the top.
Maintain a steady, swing-free tempo throughout, and stop the set if you feel any sharp pain in the front of the shoulder. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Pelvic Tilt Into Bridge
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, heels positioned directly under your knees.
Rest your arms at your sides, palms down, and let your shoulders and head relax into the floor.

Begin the pelvic tilt by gently drawing your navel in toward your spine and flattening your lower back against the floor, tilting only your pelvis so your tailbone curls slightly up toward the ceiling. Do not lift your hips off the floor yet.
Feel the small stretch and engagement in your lower back and lower abdominals as you hold the tilt for a moment, breathing steadily.
From the tilted position, exhale and continue by lifting your hips off the floor, peeling your spine up one vertebra at a time from the tailbone upward.
Rise until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders, keeping your neck and head relaxed on the floor and not pushing your chin into your chest.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and keep your core braced; avoid overarching your lower back or letting your knees splay outward.
Inhale and lower back down slowly and smoothly, setting the spine down one segment at a time from the upper back to the tailbone until you return to the start. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Peroneals Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor or a mat with one leg extended straight in front of you and the other leg comfortably bent or resting to the side.
Loop a belt, rope, or resistance band around the ball and arch of the extended foot, holding both ends in your hands.
Sit tall with a long spine and keep the extended leg straight, lifting the heel slightly off the ground so the ankle can move freely. This is the start position.
Gently pull on the belt to invert the foot, drawing the inner edge of the foot up and toward you while the sole turns inward.
Increase the pull slowly until you feel a stretch along the outside of the lower leg and ankle (the peroneal muscles), staying just short of any sharp pain.
Keep the stretch steady and breathe normally; do not bounce or yank on the band.
Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then release slowly and switch to the other leg, repeating for the desired number of rounds.

name: Peroneals-SMR
instructions: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie on your side next to it, supporting your upper body on your forearm with the elbow under the shoulder.
Position the foam roller crossways under the outside of your lower leg, just below the knee, so it contacts the muscles along the outer shin and calf (the peroneals).

Stack or cross your top leg: either rest the upper leg directly on top of the bottom leg, or cross it in front with the foot flat on the floor for extra support and control. This is the start position.
Brace your core and lift your hips off the floor so your bodyweight presses the outside of your lower leg into the roller.
Slowly roll along the length of the lower leg, moving from just below the knee down to just above the ankle, using your supporting arm and top foot to control the speed.
When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the muscle to release.
Keep the pressure on muscle tissue and avoid rolling directly over the bony shin or the ankle joint.
Repeat the rolling and pausing as needed, then switch to the other leg.

name: Physioball Hip Bridge
instructions: Position an exercise ball on the floor and sit on it, then walk your feet forward as you slide down so your upper back and shoulders come to rest on the ball.
Settle into the start position with only your upper back supported on the ball, your hips unsupported and lowered, and your head and neck relaxed and supported by the ball.
Plant both feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart or slightly wider, with your shins roughly vertical and your knees bent about 90 degrees.
Rest your arms across your chest or out to your sides for balance, and brace your core to keep the ball stable.
Exhale and extend your hips by squeezing your glutes and hamstrings, driving your hips upward until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders, parallel to the floor.
Keep your weight balanced through your feet and avoid letting the ball roll or your hips twist to one side; keep the movement slow and controlled.
Pause and squeeze your glutes hard at the top without overarching your lower back.
Inhale and lower your hips back down under control to the start position, then repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Pigeon Pose
instructions: Start on all fours in a tabletop position with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.

Slide your right knee forward toward your right wrist, then angle the right shin across your body so the right foot moves toward your left hand; the more parallel the shin is to the front of the mat, the deeper the stretch.
Extend your left leg straight back behind you, resting the top of the foot and the front of the thigh on the floor, and square your hips so they face forward evenly.
Keep the toes of the back foot pointing straight back and the back leg in line with the hip, not splayed out to the side.
Inhale and lengthen your spine, lifting your chest tall over the front shin to set the foundation of the stretch in the right glute and hip.
Exhale and slowly fold your torso forward over the front leg, walking your hands out in front of you and lowering down onto your forearms or fully toward the floor as far as is comfortable.
Keep your hips level and avoid collapsing all your weight onto one side; place a folded towel or block under the front hip if it does not reach the floor.
Hold the position for the desired time while breathing slowly and deeply, then press back up to all fours and repeat on the other side.

name: Pike Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a push-up position with your hands flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width and feet together.
Walk your feet in toward your hands and lift your hips high toward the ceiling so your body forms an inverted V (a downward-dog position), with straight arms and legs.
Set your hands with fingers spread and pointing forward, and angle your torso so it is as vertical as possible to shift more load onto the shoulders.
Brace your core, keep your back flat, and let your head hang in line between your arms looking back toward your feet. This is the start position.
Inhale and bend your elbows to lower the crown of your head toward the floor between your hands, keeping your hips high and your elbows tracking back and slightly out.
Lower under control until your head lightly approaches or just touches the floor, maintaining the V shape rather than letting your hips drop.
Exhale and press firmly through your hands to extend your elbows and push your body back up to the start position.
Keep the movement slow and stable; do not let your lower back sag or your elbows flare straight out to the sides. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Pin Presses
instructions: Set a flat bench inside a power rack and set the safety pins or rails to the desired point in your range of motion, such as a few inches off the chest or near lockout, so the bar rests on the pins at that height.
Rest a loaded barbell on the pins, positioned so it sits directly above your usual bench-press contact point on your chest when you lie down.

Lie back on the bench and set your eyes under the bar. Plant your feet firmly and pull them slightly back under you, then arch your upper back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, pressing your traps down into the bench.
Grip the bar with your preferred width: about a standard bench grip for more chest, or closer to shoulder-width to emphasize the triceps. Keep your wrists stacked straight over your elbows.

Squeeze the bar hard as if trying to pull it apart, keeping your whole body tight, glutes engaged, and feet driving into the floor. The bar rests on the pins with no weight in your hands at the start, since there is no lowering phase.
Take a deep breath and brace, then drive the bar up off the pins explosively with as much force as you can generate from a dead stop.
Keep your elbows tucked toward your sides as you press, and extend your arms until the bar is locked out fully overhead.
Lower the bar under control back down to rest fully on the pins, then release the tension and let the bar settle completely.
Reset your tightness, take a fresh breath, and pause on the pins before initiating the next rep, since each rep begins from a dead stop. Repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Piriformis-SMR
instructions: Sit on top of a foam roller placed on the floor, with the roller under your buttocks and your hands on the floor behind you for support.
Bend both knees with feet flat, then cross one leg over the other so that the ankle of the crossed leg rests on top of the opposite knee, opening the hip. This is the start position.
Shift your weight toward the side of the crossed leg, leaning onto that glute so the roller presses into the upper, outer portion of the buttock where the piriformis lies.
Use your supporting hands and feet to control the pressure, and slowly roll over the glute to explore the area for tight spots.
To deepen the release, gently pull the bent crossed knee toward your opposite shoulder with one hand while keeping pressure on the roller.
When you reach a tender spot, hold steady pressure on it for 10 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly and allowing the muscle to relax.
Avoid rolling directly on the tailbone or hip bone; keep the pressure on the muscle. Switch sides and repeat for the other glute.

name: Pistol Squat
instructions: Stand tall on one leg with your feet, core, and posture set, holding your arms out in front of you at roughly shoulder height for balance and counterweight.
Lift the non-working leg off the floor and extend it straight out in front of you, keeping the knee fairly straight and the foot off the ground throughout. This is the start position.
Set the standing foot flat and stable, finding your balance with weight slightly toward the heel and midfoot rather than the toes.
Brace your core and keep your chest up, then begin descending by simultaneously sitting your hips back and down while bending the standing knee.
Lower slowly under control, allowing your torso to lean forward to stay balanced and keeping the extended leg raised and straight, until your hamstring meets your calf at the bottom.
Keep the standing knee tracking in line over the foot and avoid letting it cave inward or your heel lift off the floor.
Drive forcefully through the heel and midfoot of the standing leg to extend the hip and knee, pressing back up to standing while keeping the other leg out in front.
Stand fully tall to finish the rep, maintaining balance and an upright finish. Complete all reps on one leg, then switch sides.

name: Plank
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat, then prop yourself up onto your forearms with your elbows directly beneath your shoulders and your forearms flat and parallel, pointing forward.
Tuck your toes under and lift your knees and hips off the floor so your weight is supported only on your forearms and toes.
Set your body in one straight line from the crown of your head through your hips to your heels, with feet about hip-width apart.
Brace your core by drawing your navel toward your spine, and squeeze your glutes to keep the hips from sagging or piking up.
Keep your shoulders pressed down away from your ears, push the floor away slightly through your forearms, and hold your neck neutral with your gaze just in front of your hands.
Breathe steadily and evenly throughout rather than holding your breath, keeping the body rigid and still.

Hold this straight position for the prescribed time or as long as you can maintain perfect form; stop once your hips begin to drop or rise. To increase difficulty, raise one arm or one leg while keeping the rest of the body braced and level.

name: Plate Pinch
instructions: Select two wide-rimmed weight plates and stand them together so their smooth (machined) sides face outward and the lettered or ridged sides face each other in the middle.
Stand tall with the plates positioned next to your thigh, feet about hip-width apart and core braced.

Grip the pair of plates by pinching: place your four fingers flat against the smooth outer face on one side and your thumb against the smooth outer face on the other side, so your grip alone holds the plates together.
Lift the plates off the rack or floor and let them hang at your side at arm's length, keeping your shoulder packed down and wrist straight. This is the start position.
Squeeze the plates as hard as you can between your fingers and thumb to keep them from slipping, keeping your arm relaxed and the plates from rotating.
Hold the pinch for as long as you can maintain a secure grip, breathing normally throughout.
Lower the plates under control to the floor before your grip fully fails so they do not drop. Rest, then repeat for the prescribed number of holds.
Switch to the other hand and repeat the same number of holds to train both sides evenly.

name: Plate Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor or a mat with your knees bent and feet flat, then lean your torso back to roughly a 45-degree angle so your abs are engaged and your spine stays long, not rounded.
Grab a weight plate by its sides with both hands, holding it just in front of your stomach with your elbows slightly bent and your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
Brace your core hard, lift your feet a few inches off the floor and either cross your ankles or keep your shins parallel; keep your knees softly bent. This is your starting position.
Keeping your hips square and your back flat, rotate your torso to the left, leading with the plate, and lightly tap the plate to the floor beside your hip while exhaling.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then rotate back through center under control as you inhale.
Without resting at center, rotate to the right and tap the plate to the floor on that side while exhaling.
Move slowly and deliberately, driving the twist from your obliques rather than swinging the arms; jerky momentum shifts the load to your lower back.
Keep your chest lifted and avoid letting your shoulders round forward as you fatigue.
Continue alternating sides for the recommended number of repetitions, counting one rep as a tap to each side.

name: Platform Hamstring Slides
instructions: Find a smooth floor (hardwood, tile, or laminate). Lie flat on your back with your legs fully extended and your arms resting at your sides for stability.
Place a folded gym towel, a furniture slider, or a light plate under one heel so that foot can glide easily across the floor.
Press the towel-loaded heel firmly into the floor and brace your core so your lower back stays in light contact with the ground. This is your starting position.
Drive your heel down into the floor and flex that knee, sliding the heel toward your glutes while keeping the opposite leg straight and still.
Continue sliding the heel as close to your buttocks as your hamstring will allow, feeling the hamstring contract; exhale through this phase.
Keep your hips level and avoid letting them hike or rotate toward the working side.
Slowly reverse the motion, sliding the heel back out to full leg extension while keeping constant downward pressure into the floor; inhale as you extend.
Maintain heel pressure throughout so the hamstring stays loaded; releasing pressure makes the slide too easy.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch the towel to the other heel and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Plie Dumbbell Squat
instructions: Stand tall and take a wide stance, feet noticeably wider than shoulder width, and rotate your toes out to roughly 45 degrees so your knees can track over them.
Hold a single dumbbell vertically by one end with both hands cupped under the top plate, letting it hang at arm's length in front of your hips.
Set your posture: chest up, shoulders back, core braced, and a slight natural arch in your lower back. Your arms stay straight and stationary throughout. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower into the squat by bending your knees and pushing them outward in line with your toes, sinking straight down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Keep your torso upright and vertical rather than leaning forward, and let the dumbbell travel straight down between your legs without your back rounding.
Make sure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward; driving the knees out keeps tension on the inner thighs and glutes.
Drive back up by pressing through your heels and squeezing your glutes, extending the knees and hips to return to standing while exhaling.
Avoid bouncing out of the bottom; control the descent and stand up with a smooth, deliberate effort.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Plyo Kettlebell Pushups
instructions: Place a single kettlebell on the floor where your chest will be at the bottom of a pushup.

Set up in a high plank pushup position on your toes with one hand flat on the floor and the other hand gripping the top of the kettlebell handle; hands are roughly shoulder-width apart with arms fully extended.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms one straight line from head to heels, with no sag in the hips or pike at the waist. This is your starting position.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending both elbows, descending as deep as you can while keeping your back flat and elbows tucked at roughly 45 degrees.
Explosively push up off both hands as hard as possible so your upper body leaves the floor, propelling yourself laterally over the kettlebell.
While airborne, swap your hands so the hand that was on the floor lands on the kettlebell and the hand that was on the kettlebell lands on the floor on the other side.
Land softly with bent elbows to absorb the impact, immediately sinking into the next descent without pausing.
Keep your hips level and core tight throughout; letting the hips twist or sag wastes power and strains the lower back.
Continue pressing explosively back and forth over the kettlebell for the recommended number of repetitions or time.

name: Plyo Push-up
instructions: Get into a prone plank position on the floor, supporting your weight on your hands and toes with your hands placed about shoulder-width apart.
Fully extend your arms and brace your core and glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. This is your starting position.
Lower yourself by bending at the elbows, bringing your chest toward the ground while keeping your body rigid and elbows tucked at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
At the bottom, reverse direction explosively, driving through your palms and extending your elbows as fast as possible to launch your upper body off the floor.
Push hard enough that your hands leave the ground at the top of the drive; keep your body straight while airborne rather than piking at the hips.
Land with soft, slightly bent elbows to absorb the impact, immediately controlling the descent into the next rep.
Keep your neck neutral and avoid letting your hips sag or your lower back hyperextend on landing.
For added difficulty, add a clap while your hands are off the ground.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, resetting your position if your form breaks down.

name: Posterior Tibialis Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor or a mat with one leg extended straight out in front of you.
Loop a belt, rope, or resistance band around the ball of the extended foot, holding one end in each hand.
Lift the heel slightly off the ground and keep the knee straight. This is your starting position.
Gently pull on the strap to evert the foot, drawing the outer edge of the foot up and toward you so you feel a stretch along the inside of the ankle and lower shin.
Hold the stretched position for 10 to 20 seconds, breathing steadily and keeping the pull gentle rather than forcing the ankle.
Release slowly, then switch the strap to the other foot and repeat.

name: Power Clean
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart with toes turned out slightly, positioning the loaded barbell over the balls of your feet so it sits about an inch from your shins.
Squat down and grip the bar with a closed, pronated (overhand) grip just outside your knees, hands roughly shoulder-width apart, with arms fully straight and elbows pointed out.

Set your back flat or slightly arched, chest up and out, shoulder blades retracted, shoulders positioned slightly in front of and over the bar, and your head neutral with eyes forward. Inhale and brace. This is your starting position.

Begin the first pull by forcefully extending your hips and knees together, keeping your back angle constant and the bar dragging close to your shins; do not let your hips shoot up faster than your shoulders.
As the bar passes your knees, drive your hips forward into the bar (the scoop), keeping your arms straight and the bar against your thighs.

Explode into the second pull by violently extending your hips, knees, and ankles, rising onto the balls of your feet as if jumping, keeping the bar close to your body and your shoulders over it as long as possible.
At full extension, shrug your shoulders hard upward, then pull your body under the bar by sharply bending the elbows and driving them up and out to the sides.
Drop into a quarter squat as you whip your elbows around and under the bar, racking it across the front of your shoulders and collarbones with the upper arms parallel to the floor.
Catch the bar with a tall, tight torso, neutral head, and flat feet, then stand fully erect by extending the hips and knees. Exhale at the top.
Throughout the lift keep the bar tracking in a near-vertical line close to your body; letting it swing away forward kills power and strains the back.
Lower the bar under control to your thighs, bend the hips and knees to cushion it, then guide it down to the floor and reset before the next repetition.

name: Power Clean from Blocks
instructions: Set the loaded barbell on blocks or boxes at the desired height (typically around knee or mid-thigh level) and stand with your feet about hip-width apart under the bar.

Take a closed, pronated grip just outside your legs, then lower your hips with your weight over your heels, back flat, chest up, head facing forward, and your shoulders positioned just in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through your heels and extending your knees, keeping your back angle constant and your arms straight as the bar rises along your thighs.
As the bar reaches mid-thigh, begin extending aggressively through the hips, keeping the bar close to your body.

Explode into the second pull with a jumping action, extending your hips, knees, and ankles fully so the bar accelerates upward; at peak extension your body is fully stretched and leaning slightly back with arms still straight.
Transition into the third pull by shrugging hard and pulling yourself under the bar, driving your elbows up and out and rotating them around and under the bar.
Rack the bar onto your protracted shoulders so it lightly touches your throat with your hands relaxed, catching it in a partial squat with the elbows high.
Recover by driving through your heels with the torso upright and elbows up until you stand fully erect.
Return the bar to the blocks under control and reset your position for the next repetition.

name: Power Jerk
instructions: Begin with the barbell racked across the front of your shoulders, elbows up, hands just outside shoulder width, and your feet directly under your hips.
Stand tall with a braced core, chest up, and the bar resting on your shoulders and throat; take a breath and tighten your whole torso. This is your starting position.
Initiate the dip by bending your knees straight down a short distance while keeping your torso completely vertical and your hips directly over your feet; do not let the hips drift backward.
Reverse the dip explosively, driving through your heels to extend your legs as fast and forcefully as possible to propel the bar upward off your shoulders.
As the bar leaves your shoulders, pull your head back slightly out of the bar's path so it can travel straight up.

At the moment your drive is complete and the bar is moving up, quickly punch your arms straight and push yourself down under the bar, jumping your feet out to a slightly wider stance with knees partially bent.
Receive the bar with your arms fully locked out overhead, the bar stacked directly over the middle of your feet, with a solid, braced torso.
Stabilize the overhead position, then stand fully erect by extending your knees and hips, bringing your feet back in line if needed.
Keep the bar path vertical throughout; pressing the bar forward or letting your torso lean during the dip will cause you to miss the lift.

name: Power Partials
instructions: Stand tall with your torso upright, core braced, and feet about shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length with your elbows close to your torso and palms facing your body.
Keep your shoulders down and back and your arms nearly straight with just a slight bend at the elbow. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso stationary and arms straight, raise both dumbbells out to your sides through a short partial range, lifting only until they are about shoulder height while exhaling.
As you lift, tilt your wrists so the little finger is slightly higher than the thumb, as if pouring out a pitcher, to concentrate tension on the side delts.
Squeeze the shoulders at the top for a brief moment without shrugging your traps up toward your ears.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control while inhaling, resisting the weight on the way down.
Avoid swinging or using momentum from the hips; keep the movement strict and driven by the shoulders.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, performing fast, continuous partial reps if training for endurance.

name: Power Snatch
instructions: Place a loaded barbell on the floor close to or touching your shins, with your feet directly below your hips and toes turned out as needed.
Take a wide (snatch) grip on the bar, hands set so the bar would land at your hip crease when standing; use a hook grip for security.
Lower your hips into the start with your chest up, head looking forward, back flat, arms straight, and your shoulders positioned just in front of the bar. This is your starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through the front of your heels to raise the bar from the floor, keeping your back angle constant until the bar passes your knees.
Transition into the second pull by extending explosively through your hips, knees, and ankles, keeping the bar close to your body as it accelerates upward.
At peak extension, shrug your shoulders hard and let your elbows bend out to the sides, beginning to pull yourself under the bar.
Jump your feet out to a slightly wider receiving stance and pull yourself down under the bar while punching it overhead, receiving it in a partial (power) squat.
Lock the bar out directly overhead with the bar stacked over the middle of your feet and your arms fully straight.
Stand fully erect with the weight held overhead, then lower the bar under control to reset.
Keep the bar traveling in a tight vertical path close to your body throughout; any forward swing will pull you off balance and you will miss in front.

name: Power Snatch from Blocks
instructions: Set the loaded barbell on boxes or stands at the desired height and stand with your feet directly below your hips, toes turned out as needed.
Take a wide snatch grip on the bar, ideally with a hook grip, and set your hands so the bar would land at your hip crease when standing.
Lower your hips with your chest up, head looking forward, back flat, shoulders just in front of the bar, and elbows pointed out to the sides. This is your starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through the front of your heels to lift the bar off the boxes, keeping your back angle constant and arms straight.
Transition into the second pull by extending explosively through your hips, knees, and ankles, keeping the bar close to your body as it accelerates upward.
At peak extension, shrug forcefully and let the elbows flex out to the sides, then pull yourself down under the bar.
Jump your feet to just outside your hips, turned out as necessary, and forcefully pull yourself below the bar while punching it overhead.
Receive the bar locked out overhead in a partial squat with arms fully extended and the bar stacked over the middle of your feet.
Keeping the bar aligned over the front of your heels with your head and chest up, drive through your heels to stand fully erect.
Carefully return the bar to the boxes under control and reset for the next repetition.

name: Power Stairs
instructions: Position the implement (a strongman implement, tire, or weighted box for training) on the ground directly in front of a sturdy staircase, typically with steps about 16 to 18 inches high.
Set your feet in a wide stance close to the implement, then hinge down and grip it firmly with both hands.
Set your back flat, chest and head up, core braced, and your weight over your heels. This is your starting position.
Drive through the ground with your heels, extending your knees and hips powerfully to break the implement off the floor while keeping your back rigid.
As you reach extension, lean back slightly and swing the implement upward, using your legs and hips to help push and guide it onto the next step.
Settle the implement securely onto the stair, keeping control so it does not tip back toward you.
Maintain a flat back throughout and let your legs and hips do the lifting; rounding the back under this load risks serious injury.
Move as fast as possible while staying controlled, repeating for 3 to 5 repetitions or until the implement reaches the top, then progress to a heavier implement.

name: Preacher Curl
instructions: Set up at a preacher bench and adjust the seat so that when you sit, the top edge of the angled pad rests just under your armpits.

Take an underhand (supinated) grip on an E-Z curl bar at the inner angled handles so your palms face up and are tilted slightly inward; have a partner hand you the bar or lift it from the bench's bar rest.
Sit with your chest against the pad and the backs of your upper arms flat against the angled surface, holding the bar at shoulder height with biceps contracted. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar by extending your elbows until your arms are nearly straight and your biceps are fully stretched.
Do not let your elbows lift off the pad or fully lock out the joint at the bottom under heavy load; keep a slight bend to protect the elbow and maintain tension.
Exhale and curl the bar back up by contracting your biceps until the bar reaches shoulder height and your biceps are fully squeezed.
Hold the top contraction for a second, focusing on squeezing the biceps rather than swinging the weight.
Keep your upper arms pinned to the pad and avoid leaning back or using momentum to move the bar.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Preacher Hammer Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Set up at a preacher bench and adjust it so the top of the angled pad sits just below your armpits when seated.
Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and rest the backs of your upper arms flat against the angled pad with your chest against it.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with biceps contracted and your wrists in line with your forearms. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells by extending your elbows until your arms are nearly straight and your biceps and forearms are fully stretched, keeping the neutral grip throughout.
Keep your upper arms flat against the pad and avoid bouncing or fully locking the elbows at the bottom.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells back up by contracting the biceps until they reach shoulder height, maintaining the hammer (neutral) hand position to emphasize the brachialis and forearms.
Squeeze hard at the top for a second, keeping your elbows pinned to the pad.
Avoid letting your wrists rotate or your torso lean back to assist the lift; keep the motion strict.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Press Sit-Up
instructions: Lie back on a flat or decline abdominal bench and secure your feet under the foot pads or rollers so your lower body is anchored.
Take a barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip and rest it across your upper chest, keeping your elbows tucked and wrists stacked under the bar.
Set your starting position lying back with the bar held on your chest, your abs and glutes ready to brace.
Tighten your abdominals and glutes, then curl your torso up off the bench into a sit-up while simultaneously beginning to press the barbell upward; exhale through the effort.
As you reach the top of the sit-up, press the barbell to a fully locked-out overhead position, using your arms to push the bar up while keeping the work focused on the abs.
Reverse the movement by bending the elbows to bring the barbell back to your chest as you lower your torso back down to the bench under control; inhale as you descend.
Move smoothly and avoid jerking the bar or yanking with your hip flexors; let the abs drive the torso flexion.
Keep the bar path controlled so it does not drift forward over your face as you press and lower.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Prone Manual Hamstring
instructions: Lie face down on a padded floor or bench with your legs fully extended, hips pressed flat, and toes pointed. Rest your forehead on your folded arms or turn your head to one side so your neck stays relaxed.
Position your training partner kneeling beside or behind your working leg, within easy reach of your heel. Brief them to apply pressure against the back of your heel, not your foot or ankle joint.
Brace your abdominals and squeeze your glutes lightly to keep your pelvis pinned to the surface. This prevents your hips from rising and isolates the hamstring.
Have your partner cup the back of your heel with their palm and apply a light, steady resistance as you begin.
Curl your heel toward your buttocks by flexing the knee, driving smoothly against your partner's resistance. Exhale as you lift and take roughly two seconds to reach the top.
Tell your partner to increase pressure gradually as the leg curls higher, where the hamstring is strongest, so you meet near-maximal resistance through the full range.
Pause and squeeze the hamstring hard for a moment at the top, getting the heel as close to the glute as your flexibility allows without lifting the hip off the surface.
Lower the leg back to straight over three to four seconds while your partner now resists the downward motion, giving you an eccentric overload. Inhale on the way down.

Keep your hips flat the entire time; if your pelvis pops up or you arch your lower back, the resistance is too heavy or your core is loose. Communicate constantly so the pressure stays matched to your effort.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch sides.

name: Prowler Sprint
instructions: Load the prowler sled on a flat, firm surface with enough room to sprint at least 10 to 20 meters. Choose a weight that lets you accelerate and move fast; it should slow you slightly but never reduce you to a grind.

Decide between the tall upright posts or the low handles. Upright handles keep you more vertical for speed; low handles put you in a deeper drive angle. For sprinting, the upright posts are usually preferred.
Grip the posts or handles firmly with arms fully extended and step back so your body forms a long, leaning line angled forward into the sled, weight on the balls of your feet.
Set a flat back, neutral spine, and braced core, with your head in line with your torso and eyes a few feet ahead on the ground. Do not round your upper back or let your hips pike up.
Begin by driving one foot hard into the ground, extending the hip, knee, and ankle to push the sled forward as you fire the opposite knee up.
Take short, powerful, choppy steps with high turnover, landing on the balls of your feet and never letting your heels settle. Stay low and leaned for the first several steps to accelerate.
Drive your arms isometrically into the sled and keep constant forward lean so all of your force goes into horizontal propulsion.
Breathe in short, sharp bursts; do not hold your breath. Sprint the full distance at maximum effort, then decelerate smoothly.
Keep the back flat and hips low the whole way; rising up tall or letting the hips shoot up bleeds off power. Reset, turn the sled, and repeat for the prescribed distance or rounds.

name: Pseudo Planche Lean
instructions: Start on the floor in a high plank with your hands flat, shoulders stacked directly over your wrists, and feet together or hip-width apart on your toes.

Rotate your hands outward so your fingers point back toward your feet, or at least out to the sides. This wrist position lets you lean forward without jamming the wrists; warm up the wrists first if they are stiff.
Set a hollow body: brace your abs, tuck your pelvis slightly, squeeze your glutes and quads, and keep your legs straight so your body is one rigid line from heels to head.
Push the floor away strongly and protract your shoulder blades, rounding the upper back slightly so your chest spreads. Keep this active protraction throughout.

Slowly lean your entire body forward as a unit, shifting your shoulders out ahead of your hands. Move from the ankles and shoulders, keeping the body straight; do not pike at the hips or let them sag.
Lean only as far as you can hold with control. The further your shoulders travel past your hands, the harder your front delts work and the more weight loads onto your wrists.
Keep your arms locked straight and elbows pointing back, not flaring out to the sides.
Hold the lean isometrically, breathing steadily and shallowly, maintaining the straight line and protracted shoulders for the prescribed time, then ease back to start.

name: Pseudo Planche Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a push-up position with hands flat on the floor and feet on your toes, body in one straight line.
Turn your hands so the fingers point backward toward your feet, or at least angled out to the sides, to keep your wrists comfortable as you lean. Warm up the wrists beforehand.
Set a hollow-body brace: squeeze the abs, glutes, and quads, tuck the pelvis slightly, and lock the legs so the whole body stays rigid.

Protract your shoulder blades by pushing the floor away, then lean forward so your shoulders travel well in front of your hands. This forward shoulder position is the starting point and what makes the movement load the front delts.
Keeping the forward lean and straight body, lower yourself by bending the elbows. Let the elbows stay relatively close to your sides and travel back, not flare wide.
Descend under control over two to three seconds until your chest nears the floor, maintaining the leaned shoulder position the entire way down. Inhale as you lower.
Press back up by extending the elbows while actively keeping your shoulders pushed forward past your hands; exhale through the press.
Do not let your hips sag or pike or your shoulders slide back behind your hands; keep the lean constant so tension stays on the delts. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Pull Through
instructions: Attach a rope handle to the low pulley of a cable machine and set the pulley to its lowest position.
Face away from the machine and straddle the cable so it runs between your legs. Reach down between your legs and grab the rope with both hands, palms facing each other.
Step forward a few feet until you feel tension on the cable, then set your feet slightly wider than shoulder width with toes pointed slightly out.
Set a neutral spine with your chest up and shoulders back, brace your core, and keep your arms straight; your arms act only as hooks and should not pull.
Begin by hinging at the hips, pushing your buttocks back toward the machine and letting the rope travel back between your legs. Keep your knees softly bent and your shins fairly vertical.
Hinge back until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings and glutes and your torso is near parallel to the floor; keep your back flat, never rounded, and inhale on the way down.
Reverse by driving your hips forward and squeezing your glutes hard, standing tall as the rope pulls through. Exhale as you finish and lock out by fully extending the hips.
Finish standing upright with glutes squeezed; do not lean back or hyperextend the lower back at the top.
Keep all the motion in the hips, not the arms or shoulders, and avoid squatting down by bending the knees too much. Repeat for the prescribed reps under control.

name: Pull-Up Negative
instructions: Set up at a pull-up bar with a box or bench beneath it if needed. Use an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, palms facing away.
Jump, step off the box, or use the bar's support to get your chin above the bar with your elbows fully bent, the top position of a pull-up.

Set your starting position at the top: pull your shoulder blades down and back, keep your chest up toward the bar, brace your core, and squeeze your glutes so your body stays rigid and does not swing.
Begin lowering yourself as slowly as you can by gradually straightening your arms, controlling the descent with your lats and biceps. Aim for three to five seconds.
Keep tension throughout: resist the bar the whole way rather than dropping, and keep the shoulders pulled down rather than letting them shrug up to your ears too early.
Continue lowering smoothly until your arms are fully extended and you reach a complete dead hang with shoulders active, not slumped. Inhale through the descent.
Once at the bottom, let go or reset by stepping or jumping back to the top rather than trying to pull up from the hang.
Avoid kipping, swinging, or jerking; the value of the negative is the slow, controlled eccentric. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Pullups
instructions: Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip, palms facing away from you. Choose your width: wider than shoulders for a wide grip, about shoulder-width for a medium grip, or narrower than shoulders for a close grip.
Hang from the bar with arms fully extended, then set your shoulders by pulling the blades down and slightly back so you are not hanging passively.

Lean your torso back roughly 30 degrees, create a slight arch in your lower back, and stick your chest out toward the bar. Brace your core and keep your legs together; you may cross your ankles or bend the knees. This is the starting position.
Pull your torso up by driving your elbows down and back and squeezing your shoulder blades together, leading with your chest toward the bar. Exhale as you rise.
Continue until your upper chest nears or touches the bar and your chin is clearly over it. Squeeze your back muscles hard at the top.
Keep your torso relatively stationary so only your arms move through space; let your back do the work and let your forearms only grip, not pull.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower yourself slowly and under control until your arms are fully extended and your lats are fully stretched. Inhale as you descend.
Avoid kipping, swinging, or using momentum, and do not let your shoulders shrug up to your ears at the bottom. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Push Press
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about upper-chest height and load it. Grip the bar with hands just outside shoulder width, palms facing forward.
Step under the bar and rack it across the front of your shoulders, resting it on the meat of your delts with elbows pointing forward and slightly down. Your wrists should be stacked under the bar.
Unrack and step back. Set your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart with toes pointed slightly out, brace your core hard, and keep your chest up with a neutral spine.
Take a breath and brace, keeping the bar tight to your shoulders and your torso vertical. This is the starting position.
Initiate the dip: bend your knees and drop straight down a few inches, keeping your torso upright and your weight on your mid-foot to heels. Do not push your hips back; the dip is shallow and quick.
Reverse explosively, driving through your legs and extending your hips and knees to launch the bar upward with leg power.
As the bar leaves your shoulders from the leg drive, press it the rest of the way overhead with your arms, moving your head slightly back out of the bar's path then forward as the bar passes.
Lock the bar out directly over the crown of your head with arms straight, shoulders shrugged up, and the bar stacked over your mid-foot. Exhale at the top.
Lower the bar under control back to your shoulders, absorbing it by softening your knees. Reset your brace and breath before the next rep.
Keep the dip vertical and the bar path straight up and down; leaning forward or dipping too deep kills the drive. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Push Press - Behind the Neck
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about shoulder height and load it. Grip the bar wider than shoulder width, palms facing forward.
Step under the bar and rack it across your upper traps and rear delts behind your neck, as in a high-bar squat, with elbows pointing down. Keep your wrists firm and the bar secure.
Unrack and step back. Set your feet directly under your hips, toes slightly out, brace your core, and keep your torso tall with a neutral spine and head looking forward.
Take a breath, brace hard, and keep the bar tight against your traps. This is the starting position.
Dip by flexing your knees and dropping straight down only slightly, keeping your hips under you and not pushing them backward, weight on your heels. Keep the torso vertical.
Reverse direction as powerfully and quickly as possible, driving through your heels to generate maximum upward speed and force on the bar in a vertical path.
Using that momentum, press the bar the rest of the way overhead by extending your arms until it locks out above and slightly behind your head.
Lock out with arms straight and the bar stacked over the back of your neck and mid-foot, shoulders shrugged up. Exhale at the top.
Lower the bar under control back to your traps, bending the knees to absorb the impact softly.

Keep the bar path vertical and the dip shallow and upright; this lift demands good shoulder mobility, so only use it if you can hold the behind-the-neck rack comfortably. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Push Up to Side Plank
instructions: Get into a push-up position on your toes with your hands flat on the floor just outside shoulder width, arms straight, and your body in one straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips level so your body does not sag or pike. This is the starting position.
Lower into a push-up by bending your elbows and letting them travel back at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso, descending until your chest nearly touches the floor. Inhale on the way down.
Press back up to full arm extension by driving through your palms, exhaling as you rise.
At the top of the push-up, shift your weight onto your left hand and the outside edge of your left foot, then rotate your whole body open to the right into a side plank.
As you rotate, reach your right arm straight up toward the ceiling, stacking your shoulders and hips and keeping your body in a straight line. Look up at your top hand.
Hold the side plank briefly with your hips lifted and your core tight, then rotate back down and return your right hand to the floor.
Perform another push-up, then rotate to the opposite side, reaching your left arm to the ceiling.
Keep your hips from sagging during the side plank and move with control rather than flopping over. Alternate sides for the prescribed reps.

name: Push-Up Wide
instructions: Get onto the floor and place your hands flat, noticeably wider than shoulder width, fingers pointing forward or slightly out.
Extend your legs back and support yourself on your toes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Straighten your arms, brace your core, and squeeze your glutes so your hips neither sag nor pike. Keep your head neutral, eyes on the floor. This is the starting position.
Lower yourself by bending the elbows out to the sides, descending until your chest nearly touches the floor. Inhale as you lower.
Keep your body rigid and straight throughout; do not let your lower back arch or your hips drop.
Press your upper body back up to the starting position by driving through your palms and extending the elbows, using your chest muscles. Exhale as you push.
The wide hand placement shifts more emphasis onto the chest and reduces triceps involvement, so focus on squeezing the pecs at the top.
Pause briefly at the top with arms straight, then repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Push-Ups - Close Triceps Position
instructions: Get onto the floor face down and place your hands flat, closer than shoulder width so your palms are near the center of your chest, fingers pointing forward.
Extend your legs and support yourself on your toes, then straighten your arms so your torso is held up at arm's length in one straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag or pike, and keep your head neutral. This is the starting position.
Lower yourself by bending the elbows, keeping them tucked in close to your sides rather than flaring out, until your chest almost touches the floor. Inhale on the way down.
Keeping the elbows hugged to your ribs is what shifts the load onto the triceps; letting them flare turns it into a chest push-up.
Press your upper body back up to the starting position using primarily your triceps with assistance from the chest, extending the elbows fully. Exhale as you press.
Squeeze your triceps and chest at the top and pause for a second.
Keep the body rigid and the elbows tracking back, not out, and repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Push-Ups With Feet Elevated
instructions: Place a flat bench or sturdy raised platform behind where you will set up. The higher the surface, the harder the exercise and the more it targets the upper chest and shoulders.
Get into push-up position with your hands flat on the floor about shoulder-width to slightly wider apart, arms straight, fingers pointing forward.
Place your toes on top of the bench so your feet are elevated and your body forms a straight, downward-angled line from your heels to your head.
Brace your core hard and squeeze your glutes so your hips stay in line and do not sag or pike; the elevated position makes sagging more likely, so stay tight. This is the starting position.
Lower yourself by bending the elbows until your chest almost touches the floor. Inhale as you descend.
Keep your elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso and maintain the straight body line throughout.
Press your upper body back up to the starting position by extending the elbows and driving through your palms, squeezing your chest. Exhale as you push.
Pause briefly at the top with arms straight, then repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Push-Ups With Feet On An Exercise Ball
instructions: Position a stability ball behind you. Kneel in front of it, place your hands on the floor, and walk your hands out as you lay your shins or feet onto the ball.
Set your hands flat on the floor about shoulder-width to slightly wider apart, arms straight, fingers pointing forward, with your toes or lower shins balanced on top of the ball.

Establish a straight line from your feet to your head, then brace your core hard and squeeze your glutes; the unstable ball forces your trunk and shoulders to work to keep you steady. This is the starting position.
Lower yourself by bending the elbows until your chest almost touches the floor, keeping the ball still and your body rigid. Inhale on the way down.
Resist any rocking or rolling of the ball by keeping your core tight and your hips level; do not let your hips sag or your feet wobble side to side.
Press your upper body back up to the starting position by extending the elbows and driving through your palms, squeezing your chest. Exhale as you press.
Pause briefly at the top with arms straight, maintaining balance, then repeat for the prescribed reps.
If balancing is too difficult at first, rest more of your shins on the ball for a longer, more stable base.

name: Pushups
instructions: Get onto the floor face down and place your hands flat about shoulder-width to slightly wider apart, fingers pointing forward.
Extend your legs back and support yourself on your toes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.

Straighten your arms to hold your torso up at arm's length, brace your core, and squeeze your glutes so your hips neither sag nor pike. Keep your head neutral, eyes down. This is the starting position.
Lower yourself by bending the elbows, letting them travel back at roughly 45 degrees from your torso, until your chest almost touches the floor. Inhale as you lower.
Keep your whole body rigid and straight throughout; do not let your lower back arch or your hips drop or rise.
Press your upper body back up to the starting position by extending the elbows and driving through your palms, squeezing your chest as you reach the top. Exhale as you push.
Pause briefly at the top with arms straight, then lower again under control.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Pushups (Close and Wide Hand Positions)
instructions: Get onto the floor face down on your toes with your body straight, ready to alternate between two hand positions: wide, with hands set wider than shoulder width, and close, with hands set closer than shoulder width.
Begin with the wide position: place your hands flat, well wider than your shoulders, arms straight, and your body in one line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips stay level. This is the starting position.

Lower yourself by bending the elbows until your chest almost touches the floor, inhaling on the way down, then press back up by extending the elbows and squeezing your chest, exhaling as you push. The wide hands emphasize the chest.
For the close-position reps, set your hands closer than shoulder width near the center of your chest and keep your elbows tucked closer to your sides; this shifts more load onto the triceps.
Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor, then press back up to full arm extension with the same controlled tempo and breathing.
Keep your body rigid and straight in both positions, never letting your hips sag or pike.
Alternate between wide and close sets, or as prescribed, repeating for the required reps.

name: Pyramid
instructions: Choose an exercise ball sized for your height; when seated on it your knees should sit at roughly 90 degrees. Place it on a non-slip surface with clear space around you.
Kneel in front of the ball and drape your torso over the top of it, then roll forward so the ball moves under your hips and lower abdomen until your hips become the highest point of your body.
Walk your hands forward on the floor until your palms are flat and shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing ahead, supporting your upper body in a near push-up position.
Let your legs trail behind with the balls of your feet or toes resting on the floor about hip-width apart, so your weight is shared between hands and feet.
Set your spine in a long, neutral line from the crown of your head to your heels, forming an inverted-V or pyramid shape with the hips peaked. Do not let the lower back sag or the upper back round.
Gently brace your core and lightly engage your lower back and glutes so the spine stays supported rather than collapsing onto the ball.
Keep your shoulders set down and back with the shoulder blades engaged to stabilize the position; the arms and legs may be slightly bent or straight depending on ball size and your flexibility.
Breathe slowly and evenly, holding this balanced position to build stabilizing strength through the torso and shoulders.
Hold for the prescribed time, then walk your hands back toward the ball and carefully roll off to dismount under control.

name: Quad Stretch
instructions: Lie on your side on a mat with your body in a straight line, your bottom arm extended overhead or bent to cushion your head, and your legs stacked on top of one another.
Loop a belt, rope, or band around the top foot (the leg facing the ceiling), securing it around the midfoot or ankle so it will not slip.
Hold the free ends of the belt in your top hand and bend the top knee, drawing the heel back toward your glutes.
Extend the top hip slightly so the thigh moves in line with or just behind your torso rather than drifting forward; this targets the quadriceps and hip flexors. This is your starting position.
Keeping your core lightly braced and your spine neutral, gently pull the belt over your shoulder or overhead to draw the heel closer to the glute, increasing the stretch along the front of the thigh.
Pull only to a moderate, tolerable stretch, never sharp pain, and keep the knees stacked together rather than letting the top knee splay forward.
Breathe slowly and relax the quadriceps as you hold the stretch for 10 to 20 seconds.
Release the tension gradually, unloop the belt, roll over to the other side, and repeat with the opposite leg.

name: Quadriceps-SMR
instructions: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie face down with your forearms on the ground, elbows under or slightly ahead of your shoulders to support your upper-body weight in a plank-like position.
Position the foam roller underneath the front of one thigh, roughly mid-thigh, and keep that foot lifted off the ground.
Let the leg being rolled stay as relaxed as possible while your forearms and the opposite leg control how much weight presses into the roller. This is your starting position.
Keep your core engaged and spine neutral so your lower back does not sag while you support yourself.
Slowly roll your body forward and back so the roller travels along the quadriceps from just above the knee up to just below the hip, moving an inch or two per second.

When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 10 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly until the tension eases. Avoid rolling directly over the kneecap or the hip bone.
Adjust how much weight you shift onto the working leg to keep the pressure firm but tolerable, never sharply painful.
After covering the whole quadriceps, switch the roller to the other leg and repeat.

name: Quick Leap
instructions: Select a sturdy plyometric box at a height you can land on safely with control and clear the area around it. This is a power and reactive-strength drill.
Stand facing the box about one to two feet from its edge, feet hip-width apart and weight balanced over the midfoot.
Set an athletic posture: soft knees, chest up, core braced, and arms ready to swing.
Dip into a quarter-squat by hinging the hips back and bending the knees, swinging your arms behind you to load for the jump.
Drive explosively through your hips, knees, and ankles while swinging your arms forward and up to hop onto the box.
Land softly on both feet at once with your feet flat and knees bent to absorb the impact, keeping the knees tracking over the toes rather than caving inward.
Immediately upon landing, reverse the motion: fully extend through hips, knees, and ankles and swing your arms overhead to explode straight up off the box.
Land back on the ground with bent knees to absorb the impact, reset your stance, and repeat for the prescribed reps, prioritizing speed and quality over height.
Step down rather than jump down between reps if you are fatigued, to protect your knees and ankles.

name: Rack Delivery
instructions: This drill teaches racking a barbell on the shoulders, a key part of the clean. Use a light barbell while learning the pattern.
Set your feet about hip-width apart, knees soft, core braced, and stand tall with a neutral spine.
Hold the bar in the scarecrow position: upper arms raised parallel to the floor and out to the sides, with the forearms hanging straight down and the bar near the front of the shoulders.
Take a hook grip on the bar, wrapping your fingers over your thumbs, with hands roughly shoulder-width apart.
Begin the delivery by whipping your elbows around and under the bar, rotating them forward and up so the bar travels to rest across the front of your shoulders.
As the elbows come forward, relax and open your grip so the fingers give way and the bar settles into the rack rather than being gripped tightly.
Protract your shoulders and lift the elbows high to create a stable shelf across the front delts, letting the bar lightly contact the base of your throat.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout, because with heavier loads any gap will cause the bar to crash into you on the way to the rack.
Lower the bar back to the scarecrow position under control and repeat, only increasing speed and load once the motion is smooth.

name: Rack Pull with Bands
instructions: Set a barbell on the safety pins inside a power rack, placing the pins at the desired start height: just below the knees, just above the knees, or at mid-thigh.
Anchor resistance bands to the base of the rack or secure them under heavy dumbbells, then loop the other ends over the bar; choke the bands if needed so they have tension from the bottom.
Step up so the bar sits over your midfoot with your feet about hip-width apart and shins close to the bar.
Hinge at the hips and grip the bar just outside your legs at about shoulder width; because the load is usually heavy, use a mixed grip, hook grip, or lifting straps.
Set your back flat and arched, push your hips back to load the hamstrings, lift your chest, and brace your core hard. Keep your head looking forward.
Take a breath, then drive through your heels and extend the hips and knees together, pulling the bar up and slightly back toward your body against the increasing band tension.
Finish by standing fully tall at lockout, squeezing the glutes and pulling the shoulder blades back; do not lean back or hyperextend the lower back.
Lower the bar under control back down to the pins, letting it settle and the bands relax, reset your position, and repeat.

name: Rack Pulls
instructions: Set a barbell on the safety pins inside a power rack at the desired height: just below the knees, just above the knees, or at mid-thigh depending on the range you want to train.
Position yourself so the bar is over your midfoot, feet about hip-width apart with your shins near the bar.
Hinge at the hips and take a shoulder-width grip just outside your legs; since rack pulls are typically loaded heavy, use a mixed grip, hook grip, or straps to secure the bar.
Set a flat, arched back, push your hips back to engage the hamstrings, raise your chest, and brace your core tightly. Keep your head facing forward.
Take a breath, then drive through your heels and extend powerfully through the hips and knees, pulling the bar up and back close to your body.
Keep the bar dragging close to your thighs throughout; do not let it swing out away from you.
Finish standing tall at lockout, pulling your shoulder blades back and squeezing the glutes without leaning back or overextending the lower spine.
Lower the bar under control back onto the pins, let it fully settle, reset your brace and position, and repeat.

name: Rear Leg Raises
instructions: Get onto your hands and knees on an exercise mat in a quadruped position.
Place your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, with the bend of the knees creating a 90-degree angle between your hamstrings and calves.
Set a neutral spine with your head looking forward or slightly down, and lightly brace your core so your lower back does not sag. This is your starting position.
Keeping the core tight, extend one leg up and back behind you, opening both the hip and the knee until the leg is roughly in line with your torso.
Squeeze the glute and the front of the thigh at the top, keeping your hips level and square to the floor rather than rotating open.
Avoid arching or twisting the lower back to gain extra height; control the range with the working muscles instead.
Lower the leg back under control to the starting position without letting the knee crash to the floor.
Repeat for 5 to 10 repetitions, then switch and perform the same number with the other leg.

name: Recumbent Bike
instructions: Sit back into the seat of the recumbent bike so your back rests against the support and your hips are settled into the seat.
Adjust the seat distance so that with a foot on the forward pedal your knee keeps a slight bend at full extension and is never locked out, then secure your feet under the pedal straps.
Place your hands on the side or front handles to keep your torso stable and relaxed.
Wake the console by beginning to pedal, then select either the manual setting or a preset program from the menu.
If prompted, enter your age and weight so the machine can estimate calories burned, and set a starting resistance level.
Begin pedaling at a smooth, steady cadence, keeping your core lightly engaged and your upper body relaxed against the backrest.
Adjust the resistance up or down throughout the session to control intensity, and grip the heart-rate handles periodically to keep your effort in your target zone.
Maintain even, controlled pedal strokes for the duration of your workout, then gradually reduce resistance and cadence to cool down before stopping.
Recumbent cycling provides low-impact cardiovascular work; a 150 lb person burns roughly 230 calories over 30 minutes at a moderate pace.

name: Return Push from Stance
instructions: This is a partner-based reactive throwing drill, so position a partner several feet in front of you with a medicine ball.
Set up in an athletic two-point or three-point stance: feet roughly shoulder-width apart, knees bent, hips loaded back, chest up, and weight on the balls of your feet ready to move.
Stay alert with your eyes on your partner and your hands ready to react.
On your partner's signal, push off explosively and move into position to receive the pass, keeping your base wide and athletic.
Catch the medicine ball with both hands, absorbing it slightly into your chest while keeping your core braced and elbows in.
Immediately and explosively chest-pass or push the ball straight back to your partner, driving from the legs and extending the arms.
Reset back into your athletic stance and repeat each repetition with maximum speed and control.
Vary the drill by running different routes or directions before receiving the pass to add a movement and reaction challenge.

name: Reverse Band Bench Press
instructions: Position a flat bench inside a power rack and set the bar at the correct height in the supports for benching.

Anchor resistance bands to the band pegs or the top of the rack so they hang down over the bar path, then attach the lower ends to the barbell sleeves; the bands should assist most at the chest and least at lockout.
Lie back on the bench so your eyes are roughly under the bar, tuck your feet back underneath you, and plant them firmly to create a strong arch in your upper back.
Pull your shoulder blades down and together and drive your traps into the bench, lifting your chest while keeping your glutes on the bench. Maintain this tight, arched position throughout.
Grip the bar so that whatever width you choose your hands cover the ring markings, and squeeze the bar hard while trying to bend or pull it apart.
Unrack the bar without losing your shoulder set or protracting your shoulders, and bring it to a stable position over your chest with arms locked.
