Lower until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor to keep tension on the shoulders without overstressing the joints.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Seated Flat Bench Leg Pull-In
instructions: Sit lengthwise on the end of a flat bench and grip the sides of the bench just behind your hips with both hands for support.
Extend your legs out straight in front of you and hold them slightly below parallel, keeping them together and just off the bench.
Lean your torso back to about a 45-degree angle, keeping your chest up and core engaged. This is your starting position.
Exhale and simultaneously bend your knees, pulling them in toward your chest while crunching your torso forward to meet them.
Contract your abdominals hard at the point where your knees and chest are closest together.
Hold the squeezed position for a one second pause, focusing on the abs rather than the hip flexors.
Inhale and slowly reverse the motion, extending your legs and leaning your torso back to the starting position with your legs hovering just below parallel.
Move smoothly and avoid dropping your legs onto the bench or using momentum to swing them.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Seated Floor Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit on a mat with good upright posture and extend your right leg straight out in front of you with the toes pointing up.
Bend your left knee and place the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh so the leg falls open to the side.
Keep your back long and your chest lifted rather than rounding forward through the upper spine.
Hinge forward from your hips and reach toward your right ankle or foot, walking your hands down the leg until you feel a moderate stretch along the back of the right thigh.
Hold the position for 15 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and easing slightly deeper on each exhale without bouncing.
Release gently, switch the position of your legs, and repeat the stretch on the other side.

name: Seated Forward Fold
instructions: Sit on a mat with both legs extended straight out in front of you, feet together and toes pointing up toward the ceiling.
Sit up tall, lengthening your spine and engaging your core, with your hands resting on your thighs.
Inhale to lengthen, then exhale and hinge forward from your hips, keeping your back long and your chest reaching toward your feet rather than rounding your shoulders.
Reach your hands toward your shins, ankles, or feet, going only as far as you can while maintaining a flat back, until you feel a stretch through the hamstrings and lower back.
Relax your neck and shoulders and hold the position, breathing deeply and sinking slightly deeper with each exhale.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then slowly roll up to a tall seated position to release.

name: Seated Front Deltoid
instructions: Sit upright on the floor with your legs bent and your partner standing close behind you.
Extend both arms straight out to your sides at shoulder height with your palms facing down toward the ground.
Move your arms as far behind your body as you comfortably can while your partner takes hold of your wrists. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows straight and your torso upright, gently attempt to pull your arms forward while your partner resists, allowing no actual movement.
Maintain this steady isometric contraction for 10 to 20 seconds while breathing normally.
Relax your arm and shoulder muscles completely, then let your partner slowly and gently draw your arms further back to deepen the stretch across the front delts and chest.
Hold the increased stretch for 10 to 20 seconds, never forcing past mild tension, then release slowly.

name: Seated Glute
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, and have your partner stand close behind you.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee so the shin forms a figure-four and the bent-leg knee falls outward.
Lean your torso forward over your legs while your partner places their hands on your shoulders to brace you. This is your starting position.
Gently attempt to push your torso backward against your partner's hands while they resist, allowing no actual movement.
Hold this steady isometric effort for 10 to 20 seconds while breathing normally.
Relax your muscles completely, then let your partner gently press your torso further forward to increase the stretch deep in the glute and hip.
Hold the deepened stretch for 10 to 20 seconds, then release slowly and repeat with the other leg crossed.

name: Seated Good Mornings
instructions: Set up a flat box or bench inside a power rack and set the safety pins at roughly the height your torso will reach at the bottom of the movement, about parallel.
Position the barbell in the rack at upper-chest height and step under it, placing the bar across the rear of your shoulders and your upper traps rather than on your neck.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward to create a solid shelf of muscle, then grip the bar firmly to lock it in place.
Unrack the bar, brace your core, and create a tight arch in your lower back with your head facing forward.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to sit down onto the box, keeping the arch and your weight balanced. This is your starting position.
Keeping your back tight and arched, hinge forward at the hips, lowering your torso toward the pins while maintaining a neutral spine.
Descend until your torso is just above the pins, feeling a strong stretch in the hamstrings and lower back, without rounding your back.
Pause just above the pins, then drive your torso back up by contracting your lower back and glutes until you are seated fully upright.
Keep the movement controlled and never let your spine round forward under the load.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then re-rack the bar carefully.

name: Seated Hamstring
instructions: Sit on the floor with both legs extended straight out in front of you and your toes pointing up, with your partner standing close behind you.
Sit up tall and lean your torso forward over your legs while your partner places their hands on your shoulders to brace you. This is your starting position.
Gently attempt to push your torso backward against your partner's hands while they resist, allowing no actual movement.
Hold this steady isometric contraction for 10 to 20 seconds while breathing normally.
Relax your muscles completely, then let your partner gently press your torso further forward to deepen the stretch along the hamstrings.
Hold the increased stretch for 10 to 20 seconds, keeping your back long and never forcing past mild tension, then release slowly.

name: Seated Hamstring and Calf Stretch
instructions: Loop a belt, rope, or resistance band securely around the ball of one foot and hold an end in each hand.
Sit on the floor with both legs extended straight out in front of you, sitting tall with your chest up. This is your starting position.
Keep the working leg straight and lean forward slightly from the hips while gently pulling on the belt to draw your toes back toward your shin.
Increase the pull until you feel a stretch through both the back of the thigh and the calf of the working leg.
Hold the position for 10 to 20 seconds, breathing slowly and avoiding any bouncing.
Release gently and repeat the stretch with the belt looped around the other foot.

name: Seated Head Harness Neck Resistance
instructions: Place a head harness with its attached weights on the floor at the end of a flat bench.
Sit on the end of the bench with your feet planted wider than shoulder width and your toes pointed outward for a stable base.

Lean your torso forward until it is nearly parallel to the floor and use both hands to securely fasten the harness around your head, keeping the weights resting on the floor to avoid straining your neck.
Grasp the weight with both hands and slowly raise your torso back up until it is nearly perpendicular to the floor, keeping your head and torso tilted slightly forward.
Rest both hands on top of your knees so your neck supports the load on its own. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly lower your head forward and down until your chin nears the top of your chest, controlling the descent against the weight.
Exhale and slowly raise your head back up to the starting position by extending your neck.
Keep the movement slow and smooth at all times, never jerking the head, and use a light weight to protect the cervical spine.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, then lean forward to set the weights down before removing the harness.

name: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Adjust the seated leg curl machine so the seat depth places the backs of your knees right at the edge of the seat, and set the lever pad to fit your lower legs.
Sit down with your back flat against the back support pad and your buttocks pushed all the way into the seat.
Place the backs of your lower legs on top of the padded lever, positioning the pad a few inches below your calves near the ankles.
Bring the lap pad down and secure it snugly against your thighs just above the knees to lock your legs in place.
Grasp the side handles, point your toes straight ahead, and start with your legs fully extended out in front of you. This is your starting position.
Exhale and pull the lever down and back by flexing at the knees, curling your heels toward the backs of your thighs as far as the range allows.
Keep your torso stationary against the pad and your thighs pinned under the lap pad throughout, moving only at the knee joint.
Squeeze the hamstrings hard and hold the fully contracted position for one second.
Inhale and slowly return the lever to the starting position over two to three seconds, resisting the weight until your legs are fully extended.
Avoid lifting your hips or jerking the weight up; keep the motion smooth and controlled.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Seated Leg Tucks
instructions: Sit sideways on the long edge of a flat bench so you are balanced on your glutes near the front edge, with your legs extended out in front of you and held together.
Grip the sides of the bench just behind your hips with both hands; this anchors your upper body and gives you a stable base to balance on.

Lean your torso back to roughly a 45-degree angle and lift your feet a few inches off the floor so your legs hover slightly below parallel. Your body should now form a wide V shape with the bench at the point. Brace your core. This is your starting position.
Exhale and simultaneously draw your knees in toward your chest while crunching your torso forward to meet them, folding your body closed at the hips and waist.
Squeeze your abs hard at the top where your knees and chest are closest together, and hold the contraction for one second.
Inhale and slowly reverse the motion, extending your legs back out and leaning your torso back until you return to the V-shaped starting position. Keep your feet from touching the floor between reps.
Move with control rather than momentum, and keep tension on the abs throughout instead of resting at the open position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Seated One-arm Cable Pulley Rows
instructions: Set up a seated cable row station with a single D-handle attached to the low pulley. Sit on the platform facing the machine with your knees slightly bent and your feet planted firmly on the foot plate or crossbar; do not lock your knees out.
Grasp the single handle with your left hand using a palms-down (pronated) grip, leaning forward from the hips to reach it while keeping the natural arch in your lower back.

Sit back until your torso is upright and roughly 90 degrees from your thighs, your left arm fully extended and your left lat feeling a stretch. Keep your chest up and a slight arch in your back. Rest your right hand on your waist or thigh. This is your starting position.

Keeping your torso stationary, pull the handle back toward your abdomen, driving your elbow back and keeping it close to your side. As you pull, rotate your wrist so your palm finishes facing your torso (neutral grip) by the time the handle reaches your midsection.
Exhale through the pull and squeeze your back and shoulder blade hard at the end of the movement; let the working shoulder draw back rather than rounding forward.
Hold the contraction for one second, then inhale and slowly return the handle along the same path, rotating your wrist back to palm-down and allowing your arm to fully extend and your lat to stretch.
Avoid twisting your torso or using your lower back to heave the weight; keep the motion isolated to your arm and shoulder blade.
Complete the recommended number of repetitions, then switch the handle to your right hand and repeat.

name: Seated One-Arm Dumbbell Palms-Down Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench holding a single dumbbell in your right hand.
Plant both feet flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width to create a stable base.
Lean forward and lay your right forearm along the top of your right thigh, palm facing down, so that the back of your wrist and hand hang just past your kneecap with the dumbbell free to move.
Press your forearm firmly into your thigh so it cannot move, and let the dumbbell roll the wrist down. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell as far as possible by letting your wrist extend down, opening your fingers slightly if needed, while keeping a tight grip so the weight does not slip.
Exhale and curl the dumbbell upward as high as you can by extending the wrist (knuckles toward the ceiling), contracting the back of the forearm.
Hold the top contraction for one second, then lower under control. Only your wrist should move; keep your forearm pinned to your thigh throughout.
Complete the recommended number of repetitions, then switch the dumbbell to your left hand and repeat.

name: Seated One-Arm Dumbbell Palms-Up Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench holding a single dumbbell in your right hand.
Plant both feet flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width to create a stable base.
Lean forward and lay your right forearm along the top of your right thigh, palm facing up, so that the front of your wrist and hand extend just past your kneecap with the dumbbell free to move.
Press your forearm firmly into your thigh so it stays fixed, letting the dumbbell hang and the wrist drop down. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell as far as possible by letting your wrist roll down, allowing the fingers to open slightly if needed, but keeping a tight grip so the weight does not fall.
Exhale and curl the dumbbell up toward you as high as possible by flexing the wrist and contracting the underside of the forearm.
Hold the peak contraction for one second, then lower slowly. Keep the movement isolated to the wrist; your forearm must stay pressed against your thigh.
Complete the recommended number of repetitions, then switch the dumbbell to your left hand and repeat.

name: Seated Overhead Stretch
instructions: Sit up tall on an exercise mat with your spine long and your shoulders relaxed.
Bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall open, positioning your feet about six to eight inches in front of your hips.
Place your right hand flat on the floor beside your hip for support, and bring your left hand behind your head.
Reach your left elbow up toward the ceiling and lengthen your torso, then gently incline your upper body to the right, opening up the left side of your waist and ribcage.
Keep both sit bones grounded so you bend sideways rather than leaning forward, and breathe slowly and steadily into the stretch.
Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, feeling a comfortable stretch along your side, then return to upright and switch hands to repeat on the other side.

name: Seated Palm-Up Barbell Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench and hold a barbell with both hands using a palms-up (supinated) grip, hands spaced about shoulder width apart.
Plant both feet flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width for a stable base.
Lean forward and lay both forearms along the tops of your thighs, palms up, so the front of each wrist rests just over your kneecaps and the bar hangs freely past your knees.
Press your forearms firmly into your thighs so they cannot move, and let the bar roll the wrists down. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar as far as possible by letting your wrists extend down, allowing your fingers to open slightly, but keeping a tight enough grip that the bar does not slip from your hands.
Exhale and curl the bar up as high as possible by flexing both wrists and contracting the underside of your forearms.
Hold the top contraction for one second, then lower under control. Only your wrists should move; keep your forearms pinned to your thighs throughout.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Seated Palms-Down Barbell Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench and hold a barbell with both hands using a palms-down (pronated) grip, hands spaced about shoulder width apart.
Plant both feet flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width for a stable base.
Lean forward and lay both forearms along the tops of your thighs, palms down, so the backs of your wrists rest just over your kneecaps and the bar hangs freely past your knees.
Press your forearms firmly into your thighs so they stay fixed, and let the bar roll the wrists down. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar as far as possible by letting your wrists drop, while keeping a tight grip so the bar stays in your hands.
Exhale and curl the bar upward as high as possible by extending both wrists (knuckles toward the ceiling) and contracting the tops of your forearms.
Hold the contraction at the top for one second, then lower slowly. Keep the motion isolated to the wrists; your forearms must remain pressed to your thighs.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions, using a lighter weight than the palms-up version since the wrist extensors are weaker.

name: Seated Side Lateral Raise
instructions: Select a pair of light dumbbells and sit on the end of a flat bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor and your torso upright.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length down at your sides, palms facing in toward your body. Keep your back straight and your core braced. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso completely still with no swinging or leaning, raise both dumbbells out to your sides with a slight bend in your elbows.
As you lift, tilt your hands slightly forward so the front of each dumbbell is a touch lower than the back, as if pouring water from a pitcher; this keeps the tension on the side delts.
Continue raising until your arms reach roughly parallel to the floor, leading with your elbows rather than your hands. Exhale as you lift and pause for one second at the top.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly back to your sides under control, resisting the descent rather than letting them drop.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears or using momentum; keep your neck and traps relaxed throughout.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Seated Spinal Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor or a mat with both legs extended straight out in front of you and your spine tall.

Bend your right knee and cross your right foot over your left leg, planting the right foot flat on the floor beside the outside of your left knee. You can keep the left leg straight or bend it so the left foot rests near your right hip.
Place your right hand flat on the floor just behind your hips for support, sitting up as tall as possible to lengthen your spine.
Bring your left elbow to the outside of your bent right knee, using it to gently brace and deepen the twist.
Inhale to lengthen the spine, then exhale and rotate your torso to the right, turning from the base of the spine upward and gazing over your right shoulder.
Keep both sit bones grounded and your chest lifted so the rotation comes from the spine rather than from leaning back. Hold and breathe steadily for the desired time.
Slowly unwind back to center, then switch sides by crossing the left foot over and twisting to the left.

name: Seated Triceps Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a fully upright (90-degree) back support and sit with your back flat against it and feet planted firmly on the floor.

Grasp a single dumbbell with both hands, cupping one of the inner weight plates so the handle runs vertically and your palms press up under the top plate with your thumbs wrapped around. Have a partner hand it to you if it is heavy.
Press the dumbbell straight overhead to full arm extension, palms facing up toward the ceiling. Keep your upper arms close to your head and pointing straight up. This is your starting position.

Keeping your upper arms stationary, vertical, and tucked close to your head, inhale and lower the dumbbell in a smooth arc behind your head by bending only at the elbows, until your forearms reach your biceps.
Keep your core tight and your back against the pad so your torso does not arch or sway as the weight travels behind you.
Exhale and extend your elbows to press the dumbbell back up to the starting position, contracting your triceps at the top without locking out aggressively.
Only your forearms should move; flaring your elbows out wide shifts the work off the triceps, so keep them pointing forward.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Seated Two-Arm Palms-Up Low-Pulley Wrist Curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar or EZ-curl bar to a low pulley cable and place a flat bench in front of the machine, facing it.
Position the bench far enough from the pulley that when you bring the bar to the top of your thighs, the cable is taut and the weight stack is slightly lifted, creating constant tension.
Grasp the bar with both hands using a palms-up (supinated) grip, hands about shoulder width apart, then step back and sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor about shoulder width apart.
Lean forward and lay your forearms along the tops of your thighs, palms up, so the backs of your wrists rest just over your knees and the bar hangs freely. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar as far as possible by letting your wrists roll down, keeping a tight grip so the bar does not slip while the cable maintains tension.
Exhale and curl the bar up as high as possible by flexing both wrists and contracting the underside of your forearms.
Hold the contraction at the top for one second, then lower slowly under control. Only your wrists should move; keep your forearms pressed firmly to your thighs.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: See-Saw Press (Alternating Side Press)
instructions: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and stand upright with your feet about shoulder width apart and your core braced.
Clean the dumbbells up to shoulder height, then rotate your wrists so your palms face you, as if setting up for an Arnold press. This is your starting position.

Press your left arm overhead while rotating that wrist so the palm faces forward as the arm extends; at the same time, let your left elbow travel out and up and bend your torso laterally to the right, away from the pressing arm.
Performed correctly, it should look as though your left arm is reaching for something high on your right side. Exhale as you press up and keep the lowered right dumbbell racked at your shoulder.
Inhale at the top with the left arm fully locked overhead and your body leaned to the right, then reverse the motion to bring the left dumbbell back to your shoulder as you return upright.
Immediately begin pressing the right arm overhead while bending your torso to the left, mirroring the same rotating, reaching, side-bending action.
Keep your core tight throughout to control the side bend and protect your lower back; the dumbbells alternate up and down like a see-saw.
Continue alternating sides for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Shotgun Row
instructions: Attach a single D-handle to the low pulley of a cable machine and select an appropriate weight.
Grasp the handle with one hand and step back a couple of feet, setting up in a wide split stance with the leg opposite your working arm forward for balance.

Extend your working arm fully toward the pulley and allow that shoulder to roll forward, feeling a stretch through your lat. Keep your torso upright and your core braced. This is your starting position.
Pull the handle toward your hip by first retracting your shoulder blade and then flexing your elbow, driving the elbow back and down along your side.
As you pull, supinate your wrist so your palm rotates to face upward by the time the handle reaches your hip, which increases the lat and biceps contraction.
Squeeze your back and pause briefly at the fully contracted position with your shoulder blade drawn back.
Slowly reverse the movement, rotating the wrist back to neutral and letting the arm extend and the shoulder roll forward to the starting stretch.
Keep your hips and torso stable rather than rotating with the weight, and complete the recommended reps before switching arms.

name: Shoulder Circles
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart, or sit upright, with your shoulders relaxed and your arms hanging loosely at your sides or resting in your lap.
Keeping your arms loose, lift both shoulders up toward your ears, then roll them forward, then down, then back, tracing a smooth circular path with the shoulders.
Move slowly and deliberately through the full range, exaggerating each part of the circle without tensing your neck or arms.
Complete several controlled circles in the forward direction.
Reverse the direction, rolling your shoulders up, back, down, and forward for the same number of circles.
You can circle both shoulders together or alternate one at a time; keep your breathing relaxed throughout.

name: Shoulder Dislocates
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart and hold a resistance band, dowel, or broomstick in front of your thighs with a very wide overhand grip, wider than shoulder width.
Keep your arms completely straight, your chest up, and your core braced throughout the movement.
Keeping the elbows locked out, raise the band or stick in a wide arc up and overhead.
Continue the arc back and down behind your body, allowing the implement to pass behind your head until it reaches your glutes or lower back, going only as far as your shoulders comfortably allow.
Move slowly and smoothly; if you feel a pinch or cannot keep your arms straight, widen your grip to reduce the demand on the shoulders.
Reverse the motion under control, raising the band back overhead and down to the front of your thighs to complete one repetition.
Keep the movement gentle and never force the range; the goal is to mobilize the shoulders, not to strain them.

name: Shoulder Press - With Bands
instructions: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with both feet about shoulder width apart so the band is anchored under your feet and tension begins at arm's length.
Grasp a handle in each hand and bring them up to shoulder height, one on each side, so your hands are level with the tops of your shoulders.

Rotate your wrists so your palms face forward, with your elbows bent and pointing down and out, and your upper arms and forearms roughly in line with your torso. Keep your core braced and your back straight. This is your starting position.
Exhale and press the handles straight up overhead until your arms are fully extended, bringing your hands close together near the top.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows and avoid arching your lower back as you press; the band resistance increases as you near lockout.
Pause briefly at the top with your arms extended, then inhale and lower the handles under control back to shoulder height in the starting position.
Resist the band on the way down rather than letting it snap your arms back, and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Shoulder Raise
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, knees soft, and weight balanced evenly over the middle of both feet.
Let your arms hang relaxed and straight down at your sides, palms facing your thighs, with no tension in your hands or grip.
Set your posture before moving: chest open, spine neutral, and gaze forward. Keep your jaw and neck loose throughout.
Inhale, then actively shrug both shoulders straight up toward your ears, lifting as high as you comfortably can while keeping your arms hanging passively.
Pause for a one-count at the top and squeeze the muscles at the base of your neck and the tops of your shoulders.
Exhale and lower your shoulders back down slowly and fully, allowing them to settle into a relaxed, depressed position below the start.
Move only at the shoulders, not the head: avoid jutting your chin forward or tilting your head back as you shrug.
Keep your arms straight and still the whole time. This is a controlled mobility and tension exercise, not a swinging motion. Repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand or sit tall with your feet hip-width apart, shoulders relaxed, and spine long. Drop your shoulders down away from your ears.
Bring your left arm straight across the front of your chest at roughly shoulder height, keeping it long and extended.
Place your right hand or forearm against the back of your left upper arm, just above the elbow.
Gently draw the left arm closer toward your chest using your right arm, feeling a stretch through the back of the left shoulder.
Keep your left arm straight and avoid bending it or letting the elbow drift. Do not pull on the elbow joint itself.
Keep both shoulders down and level: resist the urge to shrug the stretching shoulder up toward your ear.
Breathe slowly and hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds without bouncing, easing deeper only as the muscle relaxes.
Release slowly, then repeat on the right side by reaching the right arm across your body.

name: Shrimp Squat
instructions: Stand tall on one leg with your supporting foot flat and firmly planted, weight centered over the midfoot, and your standing knee soft.
Bend your trailing (non-working) leg back so the shin points behind you, then reach the same-side hand back and grab the top of that foot near the toes.
Hold the foot snug against your glute so the trailing knee points down toward the floor. This is your starting position.
Brace your core, lift your chest, and extend your free arm forward as a counterbalance to help maintain balance.
Inhale and slowly descend by bending the standing knee and hips, lowering under control until your trailing knee lightly touches the floor.
Keep your torso fairly upright and your standing knee tracking in line with your toes, not caving inward.
Touch the trailing knee to the ground without crashing into it, then pause briefly at the bottom while maintaining balance.
Exhale and drive forcefully up through the heel and midfoot of the standing leg to return fully to standing.
Move slowly and stay tight throughout. If balance is difficult, lightly touch a wall or rail with your free hand. Complete all reps, then switch legs.

name: Side Bridge
instructions: Lie on your side on a mat with your legs straight and stacked one directly on top of the other, feet together.
Prop yourself up on your bottom forearm, placing the elbow directly underneath your shoulder and the forearm flat on the floor pointing forward.
Stack your top arm along your side or place that hand on your top hip. Keep your head in line with your spine, gaze forward.
Brace your abs and glutes, then lift your hips off the floor until your body forms one straight line from your ankles through your hips to your head.
Press firmly through the bottom forearm and the outside edge of your bottom foot to support your weight.
Hold this position with your hips high: do not let them sag toward the floor or pike up too far.
Keep your shoulders, hips, and ankles aligned and avoid rotating your chest toward the ground or rolling backward.
Breathe steadily and hold for the prescribed time, keeping your core tight the entire duration.
Lower your hips down under control, then roll over and repeat on the other side for equal time.

name: Side Hop-Sprint
instructions: Set up a low cone, hurdle, or line as your obstacle and stand to one side of it with your feet about hip-width apart.
Adopt an athletic stance: knees and hips slightly bent, chest up, weight on the balls of your feet, and arms ready to swing.
Brace your core and load slightly by dipping at the hips and knees to prepare for an explosive lateral push.
Explode off both feet sideways, clearing the obstacle, and use your arms to drive the movement across.
Land softly on both feet on the far side, absorbing impact through bent knees and hips. Stay balanced and tall.
Immediately rebound out of the landing and hop back over the obstacle to your starting side, minimizing ground contact time.
Continue hopping side to side over the obstacle as quickly as possible for the prescribed number of repetitions.
On your final hop, land and immediately transition into a short forward sprint, accelerating hard for several yards.
Keep your landings quiet and controlled and your core braced throughout to protect your knees and stay reactive.

name: Side Jackknife
instructions: Lie on your side on a mat with your legs straight and stacked directly on top of one another, body in a straight line.
Place your bottom arm across your torso or on the floor in front of you for light support and stability.
Bring your top hand up to the side of your head, elbow pointing up toward the ceiling. This is your starting position.
Brace your obliques on the down side, then simultaneously raise both stacked legs up toward the ceiling while crunching your top elbow down toward your hip.
Exhale as you contract, drawing your ribcage and pelvis together on the top side and squeezing the side of your waist.
Pause for a moment at the top of the contraction where your elbow and legs are closest together.
Inhale and lower your legs and torso back down slowly and under control to the starting position without fully relaxing.
Keep the movement smooth and avoid using momentum or pushing off the floor with your bottom arm.
Complete all reps on one side, then roll over and repeat on the other side.

name: Side Lateral Raise
instructions: Select a pair of light-to-moderate dumbbells and stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold the dumbbells at arm's length by your sides with your palms facing in toward your thighs and a slight bend in your elbows.
Set your posture: brace your core, keep your torso upright and stationary, and keep your shoulders down and back. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise both dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, leading with your elbows and keeping the slight elbow bend fixed.
Tilt your hands slightly forward as you lift, as if pouring water from two pitchers, so your pinkies stay slightly higher than your thumbs.
Continue lifting until your arms are roughly parallel to the floor at shoulder height, then pause and squeeze for one second.
Do not shrug your shoulders up toward your ears or swing your torso. Keep the work in the side delts, not the traps.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells back down slowly and under control to the starting position, resisting on the way down.
Avoid using momentum or bouncing at the bottom. Keep the tempo controlled and repeat for the prescribed repetitions.

name: Side Laterals to Front Raise
instructions: Select a pair of light dumbbells and stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Hold the dumbbells at your sides with palms facing your body and a slight bend maintained in both elbows. Brace your core and keep your torso upright. This is your starting position.
For the first phase, exhale and raise both dumbbells directly out to your sides in a wide arc to shoulder height, leading with your elbows.
At the top, with arms extended out to the sides, sweep the dumbbells around to the front of your body, keeping them at shoulder height and arms long.
Inhale and lower the weights down to your sides under control to complete one repetition.
On the next repetition, reverse the order: raise the dumbbells straight in front of you to shoulder height first.
At the top of the front raise, sweep the weights laterally out to your sides, keeping arms extended at shoulder height.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.
Throughout, keep your torso stationary with no swinging or leaning, and keep your shoulders down rather than shrugging.
Continue alternating which movement comes first, keeping the tempo slow and controlled for the prescribed reps.

name: Side Leg Raises
instructions: Stand upright beside a sturdy chair, wall, or rail and rest one hand lightly on it for balance and support.
Shift your weight onto your outside leg, keeping that knee soft and your foot flat. Stand tall with your core engaged. This is your starting position.
Keeping your inside (working) leg straight, swing it out to the side, away from the chair, as far as is comfortable.
Swing the leg back down and across the front of your standing leg, letting it cross over toward the chair side.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled, driven by your hip rather than by jerking or throwing the leg.
Keep your torso upright and stable: avoid leaning or twisting your trunk to gain extra range.
Repeat this swinging motion for 5 to 10 reps, gradually increasing the range of motion as the hip loosens.
Turn around and repeat with the other leg for the same number of reps.

name: Side Lying Groin Stretch
instructions: Lie down on your right side on a mat with your body extended in a straight line.
Bend your right knee and bring it forward in front of you to create a stable base and keep your torso from rolling.
Rest your head on your right hand, forearm, or shoulder so your neck stays relaxed and supported.
Reach down with your left hand and grasp your left leg, either behind the knee for an easier stretch or at the foot for a deeper one.
Lift your left leg upward, drawing your left knee in toward your left shoulder while keeping control of the leg.
Simultaneously press your foot or knee gently down toward the floor, feeling the stretch deep in your inner thigh and groin.
To intensify the stretch, slowly straighten your left leg while maintaining the downward pressure.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20 to 30 seconds without bouncing, keeping your hips stacked and torso stable.
Release under control, then roll over and repeat the stretch on the other side.

name: Side Neck Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your spine long, chest open, and shoulders relaxed and dropped down away from your ears.
Let your arms hang at your sides and keep your gaze facing straight forward to start in a neutral position.
Slowly and gently tilt your head sideways, lowering your right ear toward your right shoulder without lifting the shoulder up.
Keep the opposite (left) shoulder pressed down to deepen the stretch along the left side of your neck.
For a gentle assist, rest your right hand lightly on the left side of your head and apply only mild, slow pressure.
Do not yank or force the stretch: use minimal hand pressure and let gravity and relaxation do most of the work.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20 to 30 seconds, feeling a comfortable stretch but never any sharp pain.
Return your head to center slowly, then repeat on the opposite side.

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on your side on a mat with your legs straight and stacked one on top of the other, feet together.
Set your bottom elbow directly beneath your shoulder with your forearm flat on the floor pointing forward.
Stack your top hand on your top hip or extend that arm straight up toward the ceiling. Keep your head in line with your spine.
Brace your core and obliques, then press through your forearm and the side of your bottom foot to lift your hips off the floor.
Raise your hips until your body forms one straight line from your ankles through your hips to your head.
Keep your hips high and square: do not let them sag toward the floor or rotate your chest toward the ground.
Engage your glutes and keep your shoulder packed down, away from your ear, to protect the joint.
Breathe steadily and hold the position for the prescribed time, maintaining full-body tension.
Lower your hips under control, then roll to the other side and repeat for equal time.

name: Side Standing Long Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart in an athletic stance, head and chest up, with your knees and hips slightly bent.
Set your weight on the balls of your feet and let your arms hang ready to swing. This is your starting position.
Load the movement by leaning toward your right, dipping at the hips and knees and swinging your arms back to coil for the jump.
Explosively extend through your hips, knees, and ankles, driving your arms forward and up to leap as far to the right as you can.
Travel sideways through the air, keeping your chest up and your body facing the same forward direction throughout the jump.
Land softly on both feet about hip-width apart, absorbing the impact by sinking into bent knees and hips and sitting your weight back.
Stick the landing with control and balance, avoiding any knee collapse inward or stumbling.
Reset to your athletic stance and repeat for the prescribed reps, then perform the jumps leaning and leaping to your left.

name: Side to Side Box Shuffle
instructions: Position a sturdy plyo box and stand to one side of it. Rest your left foot flat on the middle of the box top with your right foot on the floor.
Set an athletic posture: chest up, core braced, knees and hips slightly bent, and arms ready to swing.
Push off the floor with your right foot and the box with your left foot to jump up and laterally over the box.
Swing your arms across in the direction of travel to drive and aid the movement.
Land on the opposite side with your right foot now planted on top of the box and your left foot on the floor, knees soft to absorb the impact.
Immediately rebound and reverse direction, jumping back across so the feet switch positions again.
Keep your foot contacts quick and your knees tracking over your toes, staying light and reactive on the balls of your feet.
Continue shuffling back and forth across the box for the prescribed time or reps, keeping your core tight throughout.

name: Side To Side Chins
instructions: Grab a pull-up bar with both palms facing forward (overhand grip) using a wide grip, hands set wider than your shoulders.
Hang at full arm extension with your arms straight, then lean your torso back about 30 degrees, arch your lower back slightly, and stick your chest out. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and set your shoulders down and back to take tension off the joints before pulling.
Exhale and pull your torso up while leaning toward your left hand, drawing that side of your chest up toward the bar until it nearly touches your upper chest.
Initiate the pull by driving your shoulders and elbows down and back, and squeeze your back muscles hard at the top.
Keep your forearms doing nothing but holding the bar, and avoid swinging the lower body. Only your arms and torso should move.
Inhale and lower yourself back to the starting hang under control after a one-second squeeze.
Repeat the pull to the right side, leaning toward your right hand until your upper chest nears the bar, again squeezing your back at the top.
Lower back down under control, then continue alternating sides for the prescribed reps per side.

name: Side Wrist Pull
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, core engaged, and shoulders relaxed and down. This stretch works best standing.
Cross your left arm down and across the midline of your body so your left hand rests near the front of your right hip.
Reach over with your right hand and grasp your left wrist, starting with your left arm slightly bent.
Slowly straighten your left arm and pull it gently across and up, lifting it toward shoulder height on the opposite side.
Feel the stretch originate through the upper back and side, not in the shoulder joint itself.
Pull only as far as is comfortable and avoid yanking hard on the shoulder. Keep the motion smooth and gradual.
Keep both shoulders down and your torso facing forward, resisting the urge to twist or shrug.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then release and repeat on the opposite side.

name: Side-Lying Floor Stretch
instructions: Lie down on your left side on a mat, stacking your body so your shoulders, hips, and ankles are roughly in line.
Bend your left knee and bring it forward in front of your torso to create a stable base; let it rest on the floor so you cannot roll backward.
Straighten your right (top) leg and place the right foot flat on the floor behind your left leg, using it as an additional anchor to keep your hips from rotating.
Brace your abdominal muscles gently to hold your torso upright and prevent your trunk from collapsing forward or back.
Extend your right arm up and over your head, reaching long so you feel a line of tension run from your right hip up through your right lat and ribs.
With your left hand, gently grasp your right wrist and apply light traction, pulling the arm slightly further overhead to deepen the stretch through the right lat and side of the torso.
Breathe slowly and deeply; on each exhale, let the right side relax and lengthen a little more without forcing.
Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds, keeping the movement static and pain-free, never bouncing.
Release the wrist, roll over to your right side, and repeat the entire sequence on the opposite side for equal time.

name: Single Dumbbell Raise
instructions: Select one moderate dumbbell and stand tall with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width for a stable base.
Grasp the dumbbell with both hands by cupping one end (the top head), interlacing or stacking your fingers and palms underneath so the weight hangs vertically.
Let your arms hang fully extended down in front of your body so the dumbbell rests against your upper thighs; this is your starting position.
Set your posture: chest up, shoulders down and back, core braced, and a slight bend in the knees, keeping your spine neutral.
Keeping your arms straight (only a soft, fixed bend at the elbows), exhale and raise the dumbbell forward and up in a smooth arc.
Lift until the dumbbell is at or just above shoulder/eye level, leading with the weight and keeping your wrists firm.
Throughout the raise keep your torso and hips completely stationary; do not lean back or use a leg drive to swing the weight up.
Pause briefly at the top, feeling the front and middle deltoids working under tension.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell under control along the same path back to the starting position against your thighs.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, avoiding any jerking or momentum on each rep.

name: Single Leg Butt Kick
instructions: Stand tall on one leg in an athletic posture with your chest up, eyes forward, and core braced; let your arms hang ready to swing.
Lift the opposite (non-working) knee so its thigh is roughly parallel to the floor; hold it there for the entire drill so only the grounded leg works.
Set a slight bend in the standing knee and hip to load the leg; this is your starting position.
Perform a quick countermovement by dipping slightly at the hip, knee, and ankle, then immediately reverse to explode upward.
Jump off the ground by powerfully extending the hip, knee, and ankle of the standing leg, swinging your arms up to add lift.
As soon as you leave the ground, snap the heel of your jumping leg up toward your glutes by quickly flexing that knee.
Aim to lightly touch or nearly touch your butt with your heel at the peak of the jump.
Bring the jumping leg back down to a partially bent position directly underneath your hips to prepare for landing.
Land softly on the ball of the same foot, absorbing the impact by bending the hip, knee, and ankle to cushion the landing.
Keep the opposite leg in its raised position throughout, complete the reps, then switch legs and repeat.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and both feet flat on the floor, heels positioned about a hand's length from your glutes.
Place your arms at your sides, palms down, for stability, and gently brace your core so your lower back is in a neutral position.
Lift one leg off the floor and draw that knee toward your chest, or extend it straight out in line with the opposite thigh, keeping the working foot planted.
This is your starting position; the weight of your lower body is now supported by the single planted foot.
Drive through the heel of the planted foot, squeezing your glute to extend your hip and lift your pelvis off the ground.
Raise your hips until your body forms a straight line from the working knee through the hip to the shoulders, avoiding overarching the lower back.
At the top, exhale and forcefully contract the glute of the working leg, keeping your hips level and not letting the raised-leg side drop.
Pause for one second at full extension to maximize the glute contraction.
Inhale and lower your hips under control back toward the floor without letting them fully rest, keeping tension on the glute.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch the working leg and repeat, keeping the pelvis square throughout.

name: Single Leg Push-off
instructions: Set a sturdy plyometric box of moderate height in front of you; choose a height that lets you maintain control.
Stand facing the box with one foot resting on top of it near the front edge, heel close to the edge, and the other foot flat on the ground.
Set an athletic posture: chest up, eyes forward, core braced, and arms ready to swing; this is your starting position.
Drive forcefully through the foot on top of the box, extending the hip, knee, and ankle of that top leg to propel yourself upward.
Swing your arms upward in time with the push-off to generate maximum height, treating each rep as an explosive jump.
The goal is height, not forward travel, so jump as vertically as possible off the elevated leg.
While airborne, prepare to land by placing the same (top) foot back onto the box and bringing your other foot down to the ground.
Land softly, absorbing impact by bending the hip, knee, and ankle, returning to the starting position with the same foot on top.
Reset your balance, then immediately repeat for the prescribed reps before switching to the opposite leg.

name: Single-Arm Cable Crossover
instructions: Set both pulleys on a dual cable station to the high position, above head height, and select a light to moderate resistance.
Attach a single-grip handle to one pulley (you will work one side at a time), and stand in the center between the two uprights.
Grasp the handle and step forward in front of the pulley so there is constant tension on the cable, then assume a staggered stance with one foot ahead of the other for stability.
Lean your torso slightly forward from the hips with your chest and head up, core braced, and a fixed, slight bend in the working elbow.
Bring the working hand in toward the midline of your body at roughly chest height; this is your starting position.
Keeping the elbow bend constant, let the working arm open outward and back in a wide arc until it is roughly perpendicular to your body at about shoulder level, feeling the chest stretch.
Inhale as the arm travels out and back, controlling the resistance and not letting your shoulder shrug up toward your ear.
Exhale and pull the handle back across your body to the midline in a hugging motion, driving with the chest rather than the arm.
Squeeze the pecs at the midline and hold for a second.
Complete the prescribed reps on this side, then switch the handle to the other pulley and repeat with the opposite arm, keeping the torso stable throughout.

name: Single-Arm Linear Jammer
instructions: Insert one end of a barbell into a landmine attachment, or wedge it securely into a corner so it cannot slip; load the free end with an appropriate weight.
Stand facing the loaded end and lift the bar up to one shoulder, cupping the end of the sleeve with your working hand near the front of that shoulder.
Adopt a wide, athletic stance with feet roughly shoulder-width or slightly wider, knees and hips slightly bent, and brace your core hard.
Position your body so you are slightly behind and below the bar, ready to drive it up and away at an angle; this is your starting position.
Initiate the movement explosively by extending your hips, knees, and ankles in a triple extension to drive force up through the body.
Simultaneously press the bar forward and upward by extending the working elbow, transferring the leg power into the press.
Exhale forcefully as you punch the bar out and up to full arm extension, keeping your wrist firm and your core tight.
Move with intent and speed on every rep to develop power, keeping the rest of your body controlled.
Inhale and return the bar under control back down to the starting position at your shoulder, re-bending the hips and knees to reset.
Complete the reps on this arm, then switch the bar to the opposite shoulder and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Push-Up
instructions: Begin lying prone (face down) on the floor and press up into a push-up position supported on your toes and both hands.
Spread your feet considerably wider than a standard push-up to create a broad, stable base that resists rotation.
Shift your weight onto one arm, placing that hand flat on the floor directly under, or slightly outside, the shoulder of the working side, arm fully extended.
Place your free hand behind your lower back or rest it along your side so it cannot assist; this is your starting position.
Set your posture by bracing your core, squeezing your glutes, and keeping your body in a rigid straight line from head to heels with no sag or pike.
Lower yourself slowly by bending the working elbow, allowing it to travel back and slightly out, while keeping your torso square to the floor and resisting the urge to twist.
Descend under control until your chest or shoulder is just above or lightly touching the ground.
Inhale on the way down and keep your hips level, fighting any rotation toward the working arm.
Exhale and reverse the motion by powerfully extending the working arm to press your body back up to the starting position.
Maintain the wide foot base and rigid trunk throughout, complete the reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: Single-Cone Sprint Drill
instructions: Place a single cone on the ground and stand close beside it in an athletic sprinter's posture with knees soft and chest up.
Set your arms in a running position, one arm forward and one arm back, elbows bent at about 90 degrees; this is your starting position.
Begin chopping your feet as rapidly as possible, taking very short, quick steps so your feet barely leave the ground.
Drive your arms in a sharp blocking action in sync with your feet to reinforce fast, coordinated turnover.
Keep your knees up and your foot contacts violent and quick, staying on the balls of your feet for maximum cadence.
Maintain the rapid foot action as you move in a tight circle around the cone, keeping the cone close to your body.
Stay low in an athletic stance with a tall chest, never standing fully upright, and keep the steps short and choppy the whole way around.
Complete three full trips around the cone at maximal foot speed, then rest before repeating.
Focus on quick feet and crisp arm action rather than covering distance.

name: Single-Leg Balance Reach
instructions: Stand tall on one leg with a soft, slightly bent knee on the standing leg and your core gently braced for stability.
Fix your gaze on a point ahead and keep your chest up and hips level; this is your starting position.
Imagine a clock on the floor around you with your standing foot at the center.
Slowly reach the opposite (free) foot forward toward 12 o'clock, lightly tapping or hovering the toe without shifting weight onto it.
Control the reach by hinging slightly at the standing hip and bending the standing knee, keeping your balance over the planted foot.
Return the free foot to the center next to the standing foot to re-establish balance.
Reach the same free foot out to the side toward 3 or 9 o'clock, then return to center, staying tall and controlled.
Reach the free foot behind you toward 6 o'clock, hinging at the hips as needed, then return to center.
Keep movements slow and deliberate, resisting any wobble by engaging the standing-side glute.
Complete the set of reaches, then switch to balance on the opposite leg and repeat.

name: Single-Leg Box Squat
instructions: Position a box or bench behind you at a height that lets your working thigh reach about parallel when seated; stand facing away from it.
Balance on one leg a short step in front of the box, with the free leg held out in front of you, slightly off the floor.
Set your posture: chest up, core braced, arms extended forward as a counterbalance, and weight centered over the mid-foot of the standing leg.
Begin by pushing your hips back and bending the standing knee, sitting back and down toward the box under control.
Keep your standing knee tracking in line with your toes and your torso upright, lowering slowly rather than dropping.
Lightly touch your glutes to the box without fully relaxing or rocking back onto it, maintaining tension in the working leg.
Drive forcefully through the heel of the standing foot to stand back up, extending the hip and knee to the start.
Exhale as you rise and squeeze the glute at the top, keeping the free leg from touching down.
Complete the prescribed reps on this leg, then switch and repeat on the opposite leg.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
instructions: Stand upright on one foot, optionally resting one hand lightly on a wall, rail, or post for balance without bearing weight on it.
Lift the non-working foot off the floor by bending that knee, keeping it relaxed behind or beside you.
Set your posture tall with your core braced and the standing leg straight or with only a slight knee bend; this is your starting position.
For a greater range, stand with the ball of the working foot on the edge of a step so the heel can drop below it.
Exhale and rise straight up onto the ball of your foot, pushing through the big toe and lifting your heel as high as possible.
Pause at the top and squeeze the calf hard for a moment, keeping your ankle stable and not rolling outward.
Inhale and lower your heel slowly under control to the floor, or below the step edge for a full stretch.
Avoid bouncing at the bottom; control each repetition through the full range of motion.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch to the other foot and repeat.

name: Single-Leg High Box Squat
instructions: Place a box of an appropriate height inside a power rack, and secure a band, rope, or strap to the rack above the box for balance support.
Stand in front of the box and take hold of the band or rope with light tension to assist your balance, not to pull yourself up.
Place one foot fully on top of the box, positioning the whole foot flat with the heel down, and let the other leg hang free.
Set your posture: chest up, core braced, and weight loaded over the heel of the foot on the box; this is your starting position.
Drive through the heel of the foot on the box and extend the hip and knee to step up to a full standing position on top.
Keep the working knee tracking over the toes and the trailing leg unsupported, letting it hang rather than pushing off the floor.
Stand fully tall at the top, squeezing the glute, using the band only for light balance.
Lower yourself slowly and under control by bending the working hip and knee, stepping the free leg back down toward the floor.
Continue stepping up and down on the same leg for the prescribed reps, then switch to the opposite leg and repeat.

name: Single-Leg Hop Progression
instructions: Arrange a straight line of small cones or low hurdles evenly spaced in front of you, with spacing matched to your ability.
Stand in a relaxed athletic posture balanced on one leg, with a soft bend in that knee.
Raise the opposite knee so the thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and hold it there; this is your starting position.
Initiate each hop with a quick countermovement by dipping slightly at the hip, knee, and ankle of the standing leg.
Explode upward and forward off the standing leg, swinging your arms to clear the first cone with the same leg.
Land softly on the same leg, absorbing the impact by bending the hip, knee, and ankle, and immediately stabilize.
Use the absorption of each landing to spring directly into the next hop, hopping cone to cone on the same leg.
Keep your torso upright and the raised opposite knee up throughout, controlling your balance on every landing.
At the end of the line, turn around and hop back over the cones on the opposite leg.
Focus on soft, controlled landings and quick reactive take-offs rather than maximum distance.

name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop
instructions: Place a single cone or low hurdle on the ground and stand to one side of it.
Balance on the leg nearest the cone with a slight bend in that knee, lifting the other foot off the floor.
Set an athletic posture: chest up, core braced, and arms ready to assist with balance and drive; this is your starting position.
Begin with a quick countermovement dip at the hip, knee, and ankle of the standing leg to load it.
Explode sideways off the standing leg, hopping laterally over the cone and clearing it with the same leg.
Land softly on that same (jumping) leg on the far side, absorbing the impact by bending the hip, knee, and ankle.
Immediately rebound out of the landing, hopping back sideways over the cone to the starting side.
Keep your hops quick and reactive, minimizing ground contact time while staying balanced and controlled.
Maintain an upright torso and keep the non-working foot off the ground throughout.
Continue hopping back and forth for the prescribed reps, then switch to the opposite leg and repeat.

name: Single-Leg Leg Extension
instructions: Sit down in the leg extension machine with your back flat against the backrest and your glutes pushed fully into the seat.
Adjust the seat depth so the back of your knees rest at the front edge of the seat and the machine's pivot point lines up with your knee joint.
Set the shin pad so it rests against the lower part of your shin just above the ankle, but not touching the ankle bone itself.
Select an appropriate weight for single-leg work, then place one foot behind the pad and let the other leg hang relaxed off to the side.
Grip the side handles, sit tall with good posture, and brace your core; this is your starting position.
Exhale and extend the working leg by straightening the knee, raising the pad in a smooth, controlled arc until the leg is fully straight.
Pause at the top and squeeze the quadriceps hard for a moment, keeping your hips and torso pressed into the seat.
Inhale and lower the weight slowly back toward the start, resisting the descent and not letting the stack slam down.
Stop just before the weight plates rest fully to keep continuous tension on the muscle, then begin the next rep.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch and repeat with the other leg for balanced development.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight)
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides, and shift your full bodyweight onto one leg. This is your stance leg.
Soften the knee of your stance leg to roughly a 15-20 degree bend and keep it fixed there throughout; the knee should not bend further as you descend.
Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades down and back, and set a long neutral spine from your head through your tailbone.
Initiate the movement by hinging at the hip, pushing your hips straight back as if closing a car door with your butt, while the free leg extends straight behind you.
Allow your torso to tip forward toward the floor as a single rigid unit; your torso and rear leg should move together like a seesaw, staying roughly in line.
Reach your hands down toward the floor and lower until your torso is roughly parallel to the ground or until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstring of your stance leg, whichever comes first.
Keep your hips level and square to the floor; do not let the hip of the free leg rotate open toward the ceiling. Inhale as you descend.
Drive through the heel and mid-foot of your stance leg and squeeze the glute to pull your hips forward and return to standing, exhaling as you rise.
Stand fully tall and balanced before beginning the next rep; for a harder version avoid letting the rear toe tap down for balance.
Complete all prescribed reps on one leg, then switch sides. Common mistakes: rounding the lower back, bending the stance knee too much (turning it into a squat), and rushing the descent.

name: Single-Leg Stand
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart on a firm, flat surface, weight evenly distributed and arms relaxed at your sides.
Brace your core lightly, lengthen your spine, and pull your shoulders back and down to set a stable, upright posture.
Shift your weight fully onto one foot, spreading your toes and gripping the floor slightly to create a stable tripod through the heel and the ball of the foot.
Lift the opposite foot off the ground and either hover it just above the floor or raise the knee toward hip height, depending on the balance level you are working at.
Keep a soft, slightly bent knee on your standing leg; do not lock it out, since a locked knee reduces the stabilizing work and makes balance harder to control.
Fix your gaze on a single stationary point at eye level a few meters ahead to give your balance system a visual anchor.
Hold the position still, making small constant adjustments through the ankle and foot rather than swinging the arms wildly. Breathe normally throughout.
Hold for the prescribed time, then lower the foot and switch to the other leg.
To progress, close your eyes, stand on an unstable surface such as a foam pad, or add slow head turns. Common mistake: holding your breath or stiffening up, which actually makes balance worse.

name: Single-Leg Stride Jump
instructions: Set up a sturdy plyometric box, roughly knee height, and stand to one side of it with your inside foot (the foot nearest the box) placed flat on top, close to the near edge.
Position your outside foot on the floor beside the box so your hips are square and your weight is split between the two feet.
Set an athletic posture: chest up, eyes forward, core braced, and bring your arms back behind you ready to swing.
Begin by aggressively swinging both arms upward and forward as you forcefully extend the hip, knee, and ankle of the top (inside) leg, exploding straight up.
Drive the opposite knee upward toward your chest to add momentum and reach as high as possible at the top of the jump.
Reach full extension through the pushing leg in the air, fully straightening the hip and knee for maximum height.
Land softly back in the same position you started from, with the inside foot returning to the top of the box and the outside foot to the floor.
Absorb the landing by bending the inside leg's hip, knee, and ankle to decelerate the impact quietly and under control; avoid landing on a stiff, straight leg.

Reset your balance and posture briefly, then repeat for the prescribed reps before switching sides. Key cue: explode up fast but land soft, and keep the knee tracking over the toes rather than caving inward.

name: Sissy Squat
instructions: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and hold onto a sturdy support such as a squat rack upright, pole, or bench with one hand for balance.
Rise up onto the balls of your feet so your heels lift off the floor, and keep your weight on the forefoot throughout the movement.
Brace your core and keep your hips, torso, and head in a straight line, squeezing your glutes to lock the hips so they do not pike or bend.
Begin lowering by bending only at the knees, allowing your knees to travel forward over and past your toes while you simultaneously lean your torso backward.
Keep a straight line from your knees through your hips to your shoulders, like a leaning plank, so the stretch loads the quadriceps directly. Inhale as you lower.
Descend as low as you comfortably can, ideally until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor and you feel a deep stretch through the front of the thighs, without any knee pain.
Pause briefly at the bottom, keeping tension in the quads and avoiding any bounce.
Reverse the movement by powerfully contracting your quadriceps to extend the knees and pull yourself back up to the starting tall position, exhaling as you rise.

Maintain the straight hip-to-shoulder line the whole way up; do not break at the hips. Common mistakes: bending at the hips instead of keeping a rigid torso, dropping the heels, and going too deep before the knees are conditioned.

name: Sit Squats
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward, and weight balanced across your whole foot. This is your starting position.
Set your posture: chest up, shoulders back, core braced, and a neutral spine. Let your arms hang or extend them forward for counterbalance.
Begin the movement by simultaneously flexing your knees and hips, sitting your hips back and down as if reaching for a low chair behind you.
Keep your weight centered over your mid-foot and heels, and let your knees track in line with your toes rather than caving inward.
Descend partway down, stopping while your thighs are still above parallel to the floor (a shorter, controlled range than a full squat). Inhale as you lower.
Keep your chest lifted and back flat throughout; avoid rounding your lower back or letting your torso collapse forward.
Quickly but under control, reverse the motion by driving through your heels and extending the hips and knees to return to the standing start position, exhaling as you rise.
Squeeze your glutes briefly at the top, then immediately flow into the next rep. Aim for a smooth, rhythmic cadence for 5-10 repetitions.
Common mistakes: letting the knees collapse inward, lifting the heels, and squatting too deep when the goal is the partial above-parallel range.

name: Sit-Up
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent to roughly 90 degrees and your feet flat on the floor.
Anchor your feet by hooking them under a sturdy immovable object or having a partner hold them down so they stay planted throughout.
Place your hands lightly behind your head and interlace your fingers, keeping your elbows wide; alternatively cross your arms over your chest for less neck strain. This is the starting position.
Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly toward your chest before you begin, keeping your lower back in contact with the floor at the start.

Curl and lift your upper body off the floor by contracting your abdominals, sequentially peeling your spine up until your torso approaches your thighs, forming a V shape with them. Exhale as you rise.
Avoid yanking on your head or neck with your hands; let your abs do the work and use your hands only as a light cradle.
Pause and squeeze your abdominals for a one-count at the top.
Lower your upper body back down slowly and under control to the starting position, inhaling as you descend, and lightly touch your shoulders to the floor before the next rep.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions. Common mistakes: pulling on the neck, using momentum to fling the torso up, and dropping back down with no control.

name: Skating
instructions: Put on properly fitted roller or inline skates and full protective gear: a helmet, plus wrist guards, knee pads, and elbow pads to prevent injury from falls.
Before moving, learn the basics on a flat, smooth, open surface free of traffic and obstacles. Practice standing balance with your feet in a slight V-shape.
Adopt an athletic ready stance: knees bent, hips back, chest up, and core braced, keeping your weight centered low for stability.
Start gliding by pushing one skate diagonally out and back, transferring your weight onto the gliding foot, then repeating with the other side in a smooth striding rhythm.
Practice and master stopping (using a heel brake, T-stop, or plow stop) and turning before attempting any speed, since these are essential safety skills.
For a steady cardio session, skate at a comfortable, conversational pace for about 30 minutes of continuous movement, keeping your strides relaxed and even.
For an interval challenge, alternate within each five-minute block: speed skate hard for two minutes, then skate easy for the remaining three minutes to recover, and repeat.
Maintain good posture throughout: avoid hunching forward at the waist, keep your gaze up and ahead rather than down at your feet, and keep movements smooth.
Cool down with a few minutes of easy gliding. As a reference, a 150 lb person burns roughly 175 calories in 30 minutes at a comfortable pace, similar to brisk walking.

name: Skin the Cat
instructions: Reach up and grip a pull-up bar or set of rings with an overhand (pronated) grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart, and hang at full arm extension.
Engage your shoulders by pulling them down and away from your ears, and brace your core to control the body; do not hang fully passive.
Begin by tucking your knees up toward your chest, lifting your hips, and starting to rotate backward, letting your legs lead the way up between and through your arms.
Continue rotating backward, keeping a tight tuck and your hands fixed on the bar, allowing your shoulders to rotate as your hips pass overhead.
Pass your legs through and behind the line of the bar until your body is inverted and your torso is below and behind the bar, then slowly extend your legs straight down toward the floor.

Reach the bottom of the inverted, fully extended hang where you feel a deep stretch through the shoulders and lats; go only as far as your shoulder mobility comfortably allows. Inhale during the lowering.
Hold the stretched position briefly under control, keeping the arms straight and shoulders active rather than dumping all the load onto loose joints.
Reverse the movement smoothly: re-tuck the knees, rotate your hips back up and through your arms, and return to the front hanging position, exhaling as you come back up.

Move slowly and never throw yourself through the rotation. Key cues: keep the grip secure, control the speed throughout, and progress range of motion gradually to protect the shoulders. Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain.

name: Sled Drag - Harness
instructions: Load the sled with your desired weight and fasten a body harness snugly around your hips and torso, then clip the pulling strap from the harness to the sled.
Step forward to take up the slack in the strap until the line is taut and you feel the sled's resistance, with the harness load centered on your hips.
Set an athletic stance: feet hip-width, knees slightly bent, chest up, core braced, and lean your whole body forward in the direction you intend to travel.
Keep your spine neutral and your weight forward over the balls of your feet so the sled load drives you to push the ground behind you.
Drive forward by taking powerful, deliberate steps, extending hard through the hips, knees, and ankles of each leg with every stride.
Maintain the forward lean and steady forward pressure throughout; keep the strap taut so the resistance is continuous rather than jerky.
Take short, strong, choppy steps for a strength emphasis, or longer driving strides for a power and conditioning emphasis. Breathe in a steady rhythm with your steps.
Drag the sled for the prescribed distance or time, keeping your posture tall and stable rather than letting your torso collapse forward as you tire.

To work the quads and reverse muscles, you can also face the sled and walk backward, leaning back and extending through the legs. Common mistakes: rounding the lower back, taking timid steps, and letting the line go slack between strides.

name: Sled Overhead Backward Walk
instructions: Attach dual handles to a sled using a rope or chain and load the sled to a light weight, since the overhead position greatly reduces how much you can handle.
Stand facing the sled and take a handle in each hand, then back up until you have taken the slack out of the line and feel light tension.
Press both hands directly overhead with your elbows fully extended and locked, palms facing each other or forward, framing your head with your arms.
Set your posture: ribs down, core braced hard, glutes tight, and a neutral spine; do not let your lower back arch as the overhead load tries to pull you backward. This is your starting position.
Begin walking backward with small, controlled steps, keeping your arms locked straight overhead and rigid the entire time.
Keep the line under steady tension and your torso stacked tall, with shoulders pulled away from your ears and biceps near your ears.

Move smoothly and avoid any jerky steps or arm dips, as the long lever overhead makes the shoulders and core vulnerable to sudden load shifts. Breathe in a controlled rhythm without letting the brace fully release.
Continue walking backward for the prescribed distance, then carefully lower the handles. Common mistakes: arching the lower back, bending the elbows under fatigue, and using too much weight.

name: Sled Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach dual handles to a sled with a chain or rope and load the sled to a light, appropriate weight, since the overhead triceps position handles relatively little load.
Face away from the sled, take a handle in each hand, and step forward until the line is taut and you feel tension pulling back behind you.

Raise both hands overhead and bring them close together, palms facing each other, with your upper arms pointing up alongside your head and your elbows bent so your hands sit behind your head. This is the starting position.
Brace your core hard, tuck your ribs, and keep a tall neutral spine so your lower back does not arch against the overhead pull. You may stagger your feet for a stable base.

Keeping your upper arms locked in place and pointing straight up, extend through the elbows to straighten your arms and press the handles up and forward against the sled's resistance. Exhale as you extend.
Drive to full elbow extension, feeling the triceps contract; the only joint that moves should be the elbow, so keep the upper arms from flaring or dropping.
Once your arms are fully extended, take a step forward to remove the slack from the line and re-establish tension for the next rep.
Lower under control by bending the elbows to bring your hands back behind your head to the start, inhaling as you do.
Repeat for the prescribed reps. Common mistakes: letting the elbows drift forward or flare out, arching the lower back, and moving the upper arms instead of isolating the elbow.

name: Sled Push
instructions: Load the pushing sled (prowler) with your desired weight on a surface that allows it to slide, such as turf or rubber flooring.
