Step up to the sled and grip the vertical or horizontal posts; use the high handles for a more upright push or the low handles for a stronger forward-leaning drive.
Take an athletic staggered stance behind the sled, lean your body forward into it with your arms fully extended, and set a straight line from your head through your hips to your heels.
Brace your core hard, keep your spine neutral and chest down, and pull your shoulders away from your ears so your whole body is rigid like a plank.
Drive your feet into the ground and push the sled forward as forcefully as possible, focusing on powerfully extending your hips, knees, and ankles with each step.
Take aggressive driving steps, fully extending the rear leg behind you on each push and keeping your weight forward into the sled so it moves continuously.
Maintain the forward body lean and rigid torso throughout; do not let your hips pike up or your back round as you fatigue.
Breathe in short forceful bursts and keep your effort high, pushing for the prescribed distance or time.
Slow and stop under control. Common mistakes: standing too upright (losing leg drive), short shuffling steps instead of full leg extension, and letting the lower back round when pushing heavy.

name: Sled Reverse Flye
instructions: Attach dual handles to a sled connected by a rope or chain and load the sled to a light weight, since reverse flyes use the smaller rear delt muscles.
Face the sled, take a handle in each hand, and back up until the line has light tension and your arms are extended out in front of you at about waist level.
Bend your knees slightly into an athletic stance, hinge a touch at the hips, and keep your chest up, head neutral, and core braced. This is your starting position.
Keeping your elbows nearly straight with just a fixed soft bend, sweep both arms upward and apart in a wide arc, performing a reverse fly out to your sides.
Add a slight external rotation as you pull so your palms rotate to face forward and your thumbs point up at the end of the movement.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end range and feel the contraction in the rear delts and upper back; do not let the elbows bend to turn it into a row.
Lead with the back of the hands and keep the movement smooth against the sled's steady resistance rather than jerking. Exhale as you pull the handles apart.
Return your arms to the extended front position under control, then take a step or two backward to take the slack out of the line and reset tension for the next rep.
Repeat for the prescribed reps. Common mistakes: bending the elbows (rowing instead of flying), shrugging the traps up toward the ears, and using too heavy a load that forces body english.

name: Sled Row
instructions: Attach dual handles to a sled connected by a rope or chain, load the sled to an appropriate weight, and face the sled, backing up until the line has light tension.
Take a handle in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other, and start with your arms fully extended out in front of you.
Set your stance: feet shoulder-width or slightly staggered, knees bent, hips hinged back so your torso leans slightly forward, with chest and head up and core braced.
Keep a flat, neutral spine and your shoulders pulled back; resist the sled's pull without letting it round your upper back or yank you forward.
Initiate the row by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows back along your sides, pulling the handles toward your lower ribs or waist. Exhale as you pull.
Pull until your hands reach the front of your torso and your shoulder blades are fully squeezed together, feeling the contraction in the mid-back and lats.
Keep your torso angle steady and your elbows tracking close to the body; do not jerk with your lower back or stand up to heave the weight.
Extend your arms back out under control to the starting position, letting the shoulder blades protract slightly while keeping tension. Inhale as you reach.

Take a step or two backward to remove the slack and re-tension the line, then repeat for the prescribed reps. Common mistakes: rounding the back, flaring the elbows wide, and using momentum instead of a controlled pull.

name: Sledgehammer Swings
instructions: Set up a large tire on the ground and pick up a sledgehammer of an appropriate weight. Stand about two feet in front of the tire in a staggered athletic stance, knees slightly bent.
Take your grip on the handle. For a right-handed swing, place your left (bottom) hand near the end of the handle and your right (top) hand choked up higher, closer to the head.
Brace your core, keep your back flat, and hold the hammer ready at one side with your eyes on the spot you intend to strike.
Raise the sledgehammer up and back over your shoulder, sliding your top (right) hand up the handle toward the head as you lift, building height and momentum.

Swing the hammer down forcefully toward the tire, letting your top hand slide back down the handle to meet your bottom hand at the end of the handle just before impact, creating a whip-like acceleration.
Drive the swing with your hips, core, and lats rotating together rather than just your arms, and exhale sharply as you slam the head down as hard as you can onto the tire.
Keep your spine braced and avoid rounding your back at the bottom; absorb and control the rebound of the hammer bouncing off the tire instead of letting it whip uncontrolled.
Reset to the starting stance and repeat for reps on this side, then switch your hand positions and stance to swing from the other side so both sides are trained evenly.
Common mistakes: swinging only with the arms instead of the hips and core, gripping too rigidly so the hand cannot slide, and losing control of the bounce.

name: Smith Incline Shoulder Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a moderate incline (around 30-45 degrees) directly underneath the Smith machine bar.
Set the bar at a height you can reach while lying back with your arms almost fully extended, then load the desired weight and position the safety stops sensibly.
Lie back on the incline bench and position yourself so your shoulders sit directly under the bar, feet planted firmly on the floor, with a slight natural arch and your core braced.

Take a pronated (palms-forward) grip on the bar at about shoulder width, rotate the bar to unhook it from the rack, and hold it straight above you with a slight bend in the elbows. This is your starting position.

Keeping your elbows fixed at that slight bend and your wrists firm, press the bar straight up by protracting and elevating your shoulders, pushing the bar a short distance toward the ceiling. Exhale as you lift.
Focus the effort on the shoulder girdle: this is a short-range shoulder elevation and protraction, so the bar travels only a few inches and you should feel the contraction around the shoulders.
Pause for a one-count at the top with the shoulders fully extended upward.
Lower the bar back down to the starting position under control by retracting and depressing the shoulders, inhaling as you descend.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, keeping the elbow angle constant the whole time.

When finished, return the bar to the rack and rotate the hooks to lock it. Common mistakes: bending the elbows to turn it into a press, using too much weight, and arching the lower back off the bench.

name: Smith Machine Behind the Back Shrug
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to roughly mid-thigh height and load it with an appropriate weight; stand with your back to the bar so it sits directly behind your glutes and upper hamstrings.
Position your feet hip-to-shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward, with the bar lightly touching the backs of your legs.
Reach back and grip the bar with a pronated (palms-facing-back) grip just outside shoulder width, then rotate your wrists to unhook the bar from the safety catches.
Stand fully upright with your chest up, head neutral, shoulders pulled back, and arms hanging straight down behind you; brace your core. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms completely straight, elevate the bar by shrugging your shoulders straight up toward your ears as you exhale; drive the traps as high as possible.
Do not bend the elbows, flex the wrists, or roll the shoulders forward or backward, the motion is a pure vertical shrug.
Squeeze the traps hard and hold the top contraction for a one-second pause.
Lower the bar slowly under control as you inhale, allowing the shoulders to fully depress and gently stretch the traps at the bottom.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then return to the standing position and rotate the bar to re-engage the safety hooks before stepping away.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
instructions: Place a flat bench centered under the Smith machine so the bar path crosses over your mid-chest when you lie down; load the bar with an appropriate weight.
Set the bar height so that with your arms nearly fully extended you can reach and unrack it comfortably while lying flat.

Lie back on the bench with your eyes roughly under the bar, plant your feet flat on the floor, and drive your shoulder blades down and back into the bench to create a slight natural arch in your lower back.

Grip the bar with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width so that at the bottom your forearms are vertical, then rotate the bar to unrack it and hold it locked out directly over your mid-chest. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control, keeping your elbows tucked to roughly a 45 to 75-degree angle from your torso, until the bar lightly touches your mid-chest.
Pause briefly at the chest without bouncing, keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows and your shoulder blades retracted.
Exhale and press the bar back up by driving through your chest until your arms are fully locked out over your mid-chest; the descent should take about twice as long as the press.
Hold the contracted lockout for a moment, then begin the next slow descent.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then rotate the bar back into the rack hooks to lock it before sitting up.

name: Smith Machine Bent Over Row
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to a height roughly two inches below your knees and load it with an appropriate weight.
Stand close to the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointing forward, positioning your shins near the bar.

Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, pushing your hips back and lowering your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor while keeping your back flat and your head in a neutral position.

Grasp the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip slightly wider than shoulder width and rotate it to unhook it from the rack, letting it hang at arm's length straight down, perpendicular to the floor. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and, keeping your torso completely still, exhale and pull the bar up toward your lower ribs or upper abdomen, driving your elbows up and back close to your body.
Keep the work in your back and biceps, your forearms should only hold the bar, not curl it.
At the top, squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold the contraction for one second.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly under control back to the fully extended starting position without rounding your back or jerking the torso upward.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, then re-engage the rack hooks to secure the bar before standing fully upright.

name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
instructions: Place a sturdy block or thick weight plate on the floor directly beneath the Smith machine bar to elevate the balls of your feet.
Set the bar height so it will rest across your upper traps and the back of your shoulders when you stand on the block; load an appropriate weight.
Step onto the block with the balls of both feet, letting your heels hang off the back edge, feet about hip-width apart and toes pointing forward.
Duck under the bar and position it across the back of your shoulders (not on your neck), gripping it with both hands facing forward, then rotate the bar to unrack it. This is your starting position.
Keeping your knees straight (only the slightest soft bend) and your torso upright, exhale and push up through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Flex and squeeze your calves hard at the very top and hold the peak contraction for one second.
Inhale and lower your heels slowly under control, dropping them below the level of the block to feel a deep stretch in the calves.
Keep the motion controlled and the knees fixed throughout, do not bounce out of the bottom.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, then re-rack the bar by rotating it into the hooks.

name: Smith Machine Close-Grip Bench Press
instructions: Center a flat bench under the Smith machine so the bar crosses over your lower chest when lying down; load the bar with an appropriate weight.
Set the bar height so you can reach and unrack it with your arms nearly fully extended while lying flat.
Lie back with your eyes under the bar, feet planted flat on the floor, and your shoulder blades pulled down and back into the bench.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip at about shoulder width, hands close together; rotate the bar to unrack it and hold it locked out over your lower chest. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly, keeping your elbows tucked tight to your torso the entire time to maximize triceps involvement, until the bar lightly touches your lower chest.
Pause briefly without flaring the elbows outward, your elbows should stay close to your sides rather than pointing out.
Exhale and press the bar back up by extending through your triceps until your arms are fully locked out; take about twice as long lowering as pressing.
Squeeze the triceps at the top lockout and hold for a moment before the next rep.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then rotate the bar back into the rack hooks to lock it.

name: Smith Machine Decline Press
instructions: Position a decline bench inside the Smith machine so that the bar path lines up over your lower chest when you are lying down; secure your feet under the leg or ankle pads.
Set the bar height so it can be unracked with arms nearly extended, and load an appropriate weight.
Lie back on the decline bench, hook your legs in, and drive your shoulder blades down and back so your upper back is set and your chest is slightly arched.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width, then rotate it to unhook it and lock your arms out directly above your lower chest. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly under control, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45 to 60-degree angle from your torso, until the bar lightly touches your lower chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom, keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows and your shoulder blades retracted.
Exhale and press the bar back up by driving through your lower chest until your arms are fully extended over your lower chest.
Hold the contracted lockout for a moment, focusing tension in the chest, then begin the next controlled descent.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then rotate the bar to re-rack it on the hooks before unhooking your legs and sitting up.

name: Smith Machine Hang Power Clean
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to about knee height and load it with an appropriate, controllable weight; this is a fast, technical movement, so do not overload it.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart under the bar, toes forward, and take a pronated grip just outside shoulder width.
Unhook the bar and stand tall with arms fully extended, chest up, shoulders pulled back and down, and elbows pointed out to the sides.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your butt back to lower the bar to just above the knees while keeping your back flat and the weight loaded into your hamstrings. This is your starting (hang) position.

Initiate the pull by forcefully and explosively extending your hips and knees, accelerating the bar upward; keep your arms straight during this drive, the power comes from the legs and hips, not the arms.
At full extension, shrug and let the momentum carry the bar upward, then rapidly re-bend your hips and knees to drop your body under the bar into a partial squat.
As you drop under, whip your elbows up and around the bar to catch it racked across the front of your shoulders, keeping your elbows high and torso upright.
Stabilize the catch, then stand up fully by extending your hips and knees to finish with the bar racked on your shoulders.
Lower the bar back to the hang position under control and repeat for the desired repetitions; re-engage the hooks to rack the bar when finished.

name: Smith Machine Hip Raise
instructions: Position a flat bench under the Smith machine, oriented so you can lie on it with your feet pointing up toward the bar; load the bar with a light, appropriate weight.
Lie back on the bench and place the soles of your feet flat against the underside of the bar, knees bent.
Rotate the bar to unhook it and press it up by extending your legs until your feet support the bar overhead with a slight bend remaining in your knees; use your hands to assist if needed.
Grasp the sides of the Smith machine frame or the bench for stability and set your lower back flat against the bench. This is your starting position.
Initiate the movement by curling your pelvis upward, contracting your abs to flex your spine and roll your hips up off the bench toward the bar.
Drive through the abdominals rather than pushing with your legs; maintain the slight knee bend throughout so the work stays in the core.
Hold the top contraction briefly, squeezing your abs.
Lower your hips slowly and under control back down to the bench.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then carefully bring the bar back down and rotate it into the hooks to rack it.

name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
instructions: Set an incline bench (about 30 to 45 degrees) under the Smith machine so the bar path crosses over your upper chest when lying back; load an appropriate weight.
Set the bar height so you can reach and unrack it with arms nearly fully extended.
Sit back on the incline bench with your upper chest aligned beneath the bar, plant your feet flat on the floor, and drive your shoulder blades down and back into the pad.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width, then rotate it to unrack it and hold it locked out directly over your upper chest. This is your starting position.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly under control, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45 to 60-degree angle from your torso, until the bar lightly touches your upper chest just below the collarbones.
Pause briefly without bouncing, keeping your shoulder blades retracted and wrists stacked over your elbows.
Exhale and press the bar back up by driving through your upper chest until your arms are fully locked out; the descent should take about twice as long as the press.
Hold the lockout for a moment, then begin the next slow controlled descent.
Repeat for the prescribed repetitions, then rotate the bar back into the rack hooks to lock it before sitting up.

name: Smith Machine Leg Press
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar a couple of feet off the ground, resting on the safety catches, and load it with an appropriate weight.
Lie on your back on the floor directly underneath the bar, positioning yourself so the bar lines up over your feet.
Place the middle of both feet flat against the bar, about hip to shoulder width apart, and tuck your knees in toward your chest.
Brace your core and keep your lower back flat against the floor. This is your starting position.
Drive through the middle of your feet to push the bar upward, extending your hips and knees, exhale as you press.
Stop just short of full lockout, do not snap your knees straight, to keep tension on the quads and protect the joints.
Pause briefly at the top, then inhale and lower the bar slowly under control, allowing your knees to bend back toward your chest.
Keep your feet flat and your hips and lower back stable throughout; do not let your back round or lift off the floor.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then carefully lower the bar back onto the safety catches.

name: Smith Machine One-Arm Upright Row
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to about thigh height and load it with an appropriate, lighter weight; stand facing the bar with feet shoulder-width apart, toes forward.
Grip the bar with one hand using a pronated grip near the center of the bar, then rotate it to unhook the weight and remove your other hand.
Stand fully upright with your chest up, head neutral, shoulders back, and the working arm hanging straight down holding the bar. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso still and avoiding any swinging, exhale and pull the bar straight up by driving your elbow up and out to the side, leading with the elbow.
Continue raising until your upper arm reaches roughly parallel to the floor (elbow at about shoulder height); keep the bar close to your body.
Do not let the elbow drop below the wrist or shrug excessively, the elbow should always stay higher than the hand to keep tension on the side delt and traps.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the shoulder.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly under control back to the fully extended starting position.
Complete the desired repetitions on one side, switch hands and repeat, then re-engage the hooks to rack the weight.

name: Smith Machine Overhead Shoulder Press
instructions: Position a bench, preferably one with an upright back support set near vertical, under the Smith machine so the bar path passes just in front of your face when seated.
Set the bar height so that when seated, your arms must be nearly fully extended overhead to reach it; load an appropriate weight.
Sit on the bench just behind the bar so there is an imaginary straight vertical line from the tip of your nose to the bar; plant your feet firmly and keep them stationary.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width, rotate it to unrack it, and press it up until your arms are fully extended overhead. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your back against the support; inhale and lower the bar slowly under control until it reaches about chin level.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows and avoid letting the elbows flare excessively behind the bar.
Exhale and press the bar back up powerfully through your shoulders until your arms are fully locked out overhead.
Pause briefly at the top, then begin the next controlled descent.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, then rotate the bar back into the rack hooks to secure it.

name: Smith Machine Pistol Squat
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to a height that matches the top of your shoulders so you can step under it comfortably; load lightly or start with just the bar.
Step under the bar and position it across the back of your shoulders (on the upper traps, not the neck), gripping it with both hands facing forward.
Unrack the bar by extending your legs and lifting it off the hooks; keep your chest up and core braced.
Step one foot forward about 12 inches in front of the bar line, then extend your other leg straight out in front of you and hold it off the ground. This is your starting position.
Look forward and maintain a neutral or slightly arched spine, keeping the non-working leg lifted throughout.
Lower yourself slowly by bending the working knee and hip, descending as far as your flexibility and balance allow while keeping the raised leg out in front and your heel planted.
Keep your knee tracking over your foot and avoid letting it collapse inward.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive up through the heel of the working foot, extending the knee and hip to return to standing.
Complete the desired repetitions on one leg, then switch legs; re-rack the bar by rotating it into the hooks when finished.

name: Smith Machine Reverse Calf Raises
instructions: Place a raised platform or block directly under the Smith machine bar, positioned so you can stand on it with your heels on top and the balls of your feet hanging off the front.
Set the bar to a height that lets it rest across the back of your shoulders when you stand on the platform; load an appropriate weight (mainly for balance).
Stand on the platform with your heels secured on top of it and the balls of your feet extending off the front edge, feet about shoulder-width apart with toes pointing forward.

Duck under the bar, position it across the back of your shoulders, then push up by extending your hips and knees until your torso is upright, keeping a slight bend in the knees, never locked. This is your starting position.
Exhale and raise the balls of your feet and toes as high as possible, dorsiflexing your ankles to flex the front of your shins.
Keep your knees stationary throughout, the movement happens only at the ankles, with no bending of the legs.
Hold the top contraction for one second, squeezing the front-of-shin muscles.
Inhale and slowly lower the balls of your feet and toes back down under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, then re-rack the bar by rotating it into the hooks.

name: Smith Machine Squat
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to about upper-chest or shoulder height so you can step under it comfortably; load an appropriate weight.
Step under the bar and position it across the back of your shoulders slightly below the neck, resting on the upper traps; grip the bar with both hands facing forward just outside shoulder width.
Push up with your legs while straightening your torso to unrack the bar by rotating it off the hooks.

Position your feet about shoulder-width apart with toes pointed slightly outward; because the Smith bar is on a fixed track you may set your feet slightly forward of the bar to keep balance. Keep your head up, chest tall, and back straight. This is your starting position.

Brace your core, inhale, and lower yourself slowly by bending at the knees and hips, sitting down and back until your upper legs are at least parallel to the floor (the angle between thigh and calf slightly less than 90 degrees).
Keep your weight on your heels and mid-foot and your knees tracking in line with your toes; avoid letting the knees cave inward.
Maintain a straight, upright back with your head up throughout the descent.
Exhale and drive back up by pushing through your heels and extending your knees and hips until you return to the standing starting position.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, then rotate the bar into the hooks to rack it.

name: Smith Machine Stiff-Legged Deadlift
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to about mid-thigh height and load it with an appropriate weight; consider wrist wraps if using heavier loads.
Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly narrower, toes pointing forward and shins close to the bar.
Grasp the bar with a pronated (palms-back) grip at about shoulder width, then rotate it to unhook it and lift it by fully extending your arms.
Stand tall with your torso straight, arms hanging the bar against your upper thighs, and only a slight, fixed bend in your knees. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and keep your back flat; inhale and lower the bar by hinging at the hips, pushing your butt back while keeping your knees in their fixed slightly-bent position.

Let the bar travel down close to the front of your legs toward the tops of your feet, continuing until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings; keep your back straight the entire time, never rounding.
Keep your shoulders pulled back and the bar close to your body to protect your lower back.
Drive your hips forward and extend at the waist to bring your torso back up to the upright starting position, exhaling as you rise.
Repeat for the recommended repetitions, then rotate the bar into the hooks to rack it.

name: Smith Machine Upright Row
instructions: Set the bar on the Smith machine to roughly mid-thigh height and load it with a moderate weight, then stand directly underneath so the bar tracks straight up your body.
Position your feet hip-to-shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward, knees soft, with your weight centered over your midfoot.
Grasp the bar with a pronated (palms-facing-you) grip at roughly shoulder width; a slightly narrower grip emphasizes the traps more, while wrist wraps help if loading heavy.
Rotate the bar to unlock it from the safety hooks, then stand tall with arms fully extended, a slight bend in the elbows, chest up, shoulders back, and core braced. This is your starting position.
Brace your abs and keep your torso completely stationary; do not lean back or swing to generate momentum.
Exhale and pull the bar straight up the front of your body by driving your elbows up and out to the sides, keeping the bar close to your torso.
Lead with the elbows so they always stay higher than your forearms and wrists; continue until the bar reaches roughly upper-chest or collarbone height.
Pause for a one-count at the top and squeeze your traps and side delts without shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control along the same path back to full arm extension.
Avoid jerking the weight or raising the bar past your chin if it causes shoulder discomfort, and repeat for the prescribed reps before re-racking by twisting the bar back onto the hooks.

name: Smith Single-Leg Split Squat
instructions: Place a flat bench 2 to 3 feet behind the Smith machine, then set the bar at roughly upper-chest height and load it appropriately.
Step under the bar and rest it across your upper traps and rear delts, slightly below the base of your neck, never on the bony part of your spine.
Grip the bar with both hands just outside shoulder width, palms facing forward, then unlock it by rotating and lift it off the hooks by extending your legs and straightening your torso.
Step one foot forward so it sits directly under the bar, then extend the other leg back and rest the top of that foot's laces on the bench behind you.
Set your front foot far enough forward that when you descend, your shin stays close to vertical and your knee tracks over your foot rather than far past your toes.
Stand tall with your chest up, head facing forward, core braced, and the majority of your weight loaded onto the front foot's heel and midfoot. This is your starting position.
Inhale and slowly bend your front knee and hip to lower straight down, keeping your torso upright and the rear leg relaxed as a balance point.
Descend until your front thigh is at or just below parallel and the angle behind your front knee is slightly under 90 degrees, keeping your front knee tracking over your toes.
Exhale and drive up by pushing through the heel and midfoot of your front leg, straightening the knee and hip to return to the start without locking out aggressively.
Keep the rear leg light and avoid pushing off it, then complete all reps on one leg before switching the front foot and repeating for the other side.

name: Snatch
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out, with the barbell over the balls of your feet so it sits close to your shins.
Take a wide (snatch) grip, hands set roughly so the bar reaches your hip crease when standing; a hook grip (thumb wrapped under the fingers) is strongly recommended for security.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower into the start, keeping your back flat, chest up, arms straight, shoulders slightly in front of or over the bar, and hips above knee level.
Brace your core, set your lats, and take a breath. This is your starting position.
Begin the first pull by pushing the floor away with your legs, raising the bar smoothly while keeping it close to your shins and your back angle constant until the bar clears the knees.
Transition into the second pull: as the bar reaches mid-thigh, violently extend your hips, knees, and ankles in one explosive jump, keeping the bar brushing close to your body.
At full extension shrug your shoulders upward and let your elbows pull high and out to the sides, staying above the bar as long as possible to keep it traveling vertically.
Quickly pull yourself down and under the bar, punching your arms to lock out overhead as your feet jump out into a squat-width receiving stance.
Receive the bar with arms fully locked directly overhead and shoulders active, catching it as you drop into a full overhead squat with your torso upright.
Stand up out of the squat in one controlled motion to finish with feet in line, arms fully extended, and the bar stacked over your midfoot, then return it under control.

name: Snatch Balance
instructions: Set up with your feet in your pulling stance, about hip-width apart, and rack the loaded bar across the back of your shoulders on your upper traps.
Take a wide snatch grip on the bar with a hook grip, and set your wrists so you can punch directly overhead.
Brace your core, set a tall, vertical torso, and keep your weight balanced over your midfoot. This is your starting position.
Pop the bar off your shoulders with a short, abrupt dip and drive of the knees and hips, giving the bar just enough upward momentum to clear your head.
The instant the bar leaves your shoulders, aggressively drive your body straight down underneath it while punching your arms to lock out overhead.
Simultaneously jump your feet out into your squat receiving stance and meet the bar with arms fully extended and locked overhead near the bottom of the squat.
Keep your torso vertical and lower your hips down between your legs, with the bar stacked directly over the back of your head and midfoot.
Continue descending to full squat depth under control, maintaining an active overhead lockout, then stand up to a fully erect position before carefully lowering the weight.

name: Snatch Deadlift
instructions: Place the loaded barbell on the platform over the balls of your feet, with your feet directly under your hips and your toes turned slightly out.
Take a wide snatch grip with a hook grip (thumb wrapped under the fingers), hands set so the bar would reach your hip crease at standing.
Squat down to the bar keeping your back in full, hard extension, chest up, head facing forward, and your shoulders slightly in front of the bar with arms straight.
Brace your core, engage your lats to pull the bar in toward your shins, and take a breath. This is your starting position.
Initiate the lift by driving through your heels and pushing the floor away, raising your hips and the bar together at the same rate.
Keep your back angle constant and the bar dragging close to your legs until it passes your knees; do not let your hips shoot up faster than your shoulders.
Once the bar clears the knees, drive your hips forward into the bar and stand tall, finishing with a slight lay-back at full extension.

Reverse the motion under control by pushing your hips back and bending the knees, keeping the bar close, and return it to the platform with a flat back. Move slower and heavier than a full snatch to build first-pull strength.

name: Snatch from Blocks
instructions: Set the loaded barbell on boxes or blocks at your desired height (typically knee or above-knee level), and stand so the bar sits over the balls of your feet, feet directly under your hips with toes slightly out.
Take a wide snatch grip with a hook grip, hands set to reach your hip crease at standing height.
Lower your hips into position with your chest up, head looking forward, back flat and tight, shoulders just in front of or over the bar, and elbows pointed out to the sides.
Brace your core and set your lats so the bar is pulled in close. This is your starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through the front of your heels and pushing the floor away, lifting the bar smoothly off the blocks while keeping it close to your body.
Transition into the second pull: explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, driving the bar upward as fast as possible while keeping it brushing close to your thighs.
At peak extension, shrug your shoulders and let your elbows bend high and out to the sides, keeping them above the bar to guide it straight up.
Forcefully pull yourself down and under the bar as you punch your arms to lock out overhead, jumping your feet out to just outside hip width with toes turned out.
Receive the bar with arms fully locked overhead in as deep a squat as you can control, keeping the bar aligned over the back of your heels and your chest and head up.
Drive through your heels to stand to full extension, then carefully return the bar to the blocks under control.

name: Snatch Pull
instructions: Place the loaded barbell on the floor close to your shins, with your feet about hip-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
Take a wide snatch grip with a hook grip (thumb wrapped under the fingers) for security under heavier loads.
Lower your hips with your weight balanced over your heels and midfoot, back straight and tight, chest up, head facing forward, and shoulders positioned just in front of the bar.
Brace your core, engage your lats, and pull the bar in toward your shins. This is your starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through your heels and extending your knees, keeping your back angle constant and arms straight as you move the bar with control up to above the knees.
Once the bar passes mid-thigh, begin the second pull by explosively extending your hips in a jumping motion, accelerating the bar with your hips, knees, and ankles.
Let the speed come from your legs and hips rather than actively bending the arms; keep the bar close to your body throughout.

Finish with a full, violent, abrupt extension of the body, leaning slightly back at the top, then control the bar back down without dragging out the finish or letting the bar drift away. Snatch pulls can be loaded heavier than full snatches, but keep the bar speed crisp.

name: Snatch Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, toes slightly turned out, holding a loaded barbell at the mid-thigh hang position.
Take a wide snatch grip using either an overhand or hook grip, with your arms hanging straight down and your wrists relaxed.
Set your back straight and tight, chest up, and incline your torso slightly forward from the hips, weight balanced over your midfoot. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, exhale and shrug your shoulders forcefully straight up toward your ears, elevating the bar a few inches purely through trap contraction.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the traps without bending the elbows or using a leg drive that turns it into a pull.
Inhale and lower the bar back to the start under control, allowing the shoulders to fully depress.
Although you can load this heavier than a snatch, avoid going so heavy that the bar speed slows or your elbows start to bend, and repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Speed Band Overhead Triceps
instructions: Anchor a resistance band to a low, secure point near the floor (such as the base of an incline bench) so it runs upward behind you, or stand on the band with both feet.
Stand or sit facing away from the anchor with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your core braced.
Grasp the band with both hands using a pronated (palms-forward) grip and bring it up behind your head, elbows pointing forward and up, upper arms close to your ears.
Set your torso tall, brace your abs, and keep your upper arms fixed in place. This is your starting position.
Exhale and explosively extend through your elbows to straighten your arms overhead, driving against the band's resistance as fast as possible while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Keep the movement isolated to the elbow joint; do not let your shoulders or upper arms drift forward or your lower back arch.
Pause at full extension and feel the triceps fully contract, then return under control to the starting position behind your head and repeat for the prescribed reps with an emphasis on speed each rep.

name: Speed Box Squat
instructions: Attach resistance bands to each end of the barbell and securely anchor them near the ground, choking the bands as needed to get adequate tension at the top.

Position a box of appropriate height behind you so that sitting on it puts your hips at or just below parallel; load the bar to roughly 50 to 70 percent of your one-rep max so speed is not compromised.
Set the bar across your upper back, pull your shoulder blades together and down, arch your back, and brace everything from head to toe.
Unrack the bar, step back, and set your stance slightly wider than shoulder width with toes turned slightly out, positioning yourself just in front of the box. This is your starting position.
Take a breath, brace hard, and sit back with your hips (not straight down), pushing your knees out as you descend under control toward the box.
Sit fully onto the box softly without crashing, keeping your shins close to vertical and your back tight; relax the hip flexors only briefly while staying braced.
Pause for a brief moment to eliminate momentum, then explode off the box by driving your hips forward and pushing the floor away, extending through the hips and knees as fast as possible.
Stand to full lockout with control against the increasing band tension, reset your breath and brace, and repeat each rep with maximum bar speed.

name: Speed Squats
instructions: Set up inside a squat rack with the bar at roughly upper-chest height and load it to a moderate weight (typically 50 to 70 percent of your max) that lets you move fast.
Step under the bar and rest it across your upper traps and rear delts, slightly below the base of your neck.
Grip the bar with both hands just outside shoulder width, pull your shoulder blades together, and unrack it by extending your legs and straightening your torso.
Step back and set your feet in a shoulder-width stance with toes turned slightly out, chest up, head facing forward, and back straight. This is your starting position.
Take a breath, brace your core hard, and begin lowering by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your torso upright and knees tracking over your toes.
Descend under control until your thighs reach just below parallel, with the angle behind your knees slightly under 90 degrees, inhaling on the way down.
Reverse direction and drive up as fast as possible, pushing through your heels and midfoot to extend your knees and hips, exhaling as you accelerate.
Move the weight explosively without using any bounce or momentum, never sacrificing form for speed, and reset your brace before each rep. Re-rack carefully when finished.

name: Spell Caster
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated (palms-down) grip, arms hanging in front of your thighs.
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width, hips and knees extended, core braced, and your chest up. This is your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight and the dumbbells side by side and parallel to the floor, pull both dumbbells toward one hip while rotating your torso to that side.
Lead the movement with your core rotation rather than your arms, letting your torso turn while your hips stay relatively stable.
From that side, rotate your torso powerfully in the opposite direction, swinging the dumbbells across your body to the other hip at the same height.
Keep the dumbbells level and parallel to the ground throughout the arc, and avoid letting them drop low or swing wildly.
Continue alternating side to side under control, exhaling on each rotation, until you complete the prescribed reps.

name: Spider Crawl
instructions: Begin in a prone position with your weight supported on your hands and toes, feet together and body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to roughly 90 degrees so your chest hovers a few inches off the floor, keeping your core tight and hips level with your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Brace your abs and raise one foot slightly off the ground, externally rotating that leg so the knee opens out to the side.
Drive that knee forward toward the same-side elbow, bringing it as far up alongside your torso as your mobility allows.
Keep your hips low and your back flat throughout; do not let your hips pike up or sag toward the floor.
Return the leg under control to the starting position without letting your body rise out of the low push-up hold.
Repeat on the opposite side, alternating legs in a controlled crawling rhythm for the prescribed reps or distance.

name: Spider Curl
instructions: Place the loaded E-Z curl bar on the flat seat side of a preacher bench, aligning it so it is balanced and will not roll off.
Move to the front (angled) side of the preacher bench and lean your torso and stomach against the steep front of the pad so your body is at roughly a 45-degree incline.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor, weight on your toes for balance, and drape your upper arms over the top edge of the pad so they hang straight down.
Reach down and grasp the E-Z bar with a supinated (palms-up) grip on the angled inner grooves, hands about shoulder width or slightly closer.
Let your arms hang fully extended with a slight bend to keep tension on the biceps. This is your starting position.
Exhale and curl the bar upward by flexing only at the elbows, keeping your upper arms pressed against the pad and stationary.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top and hold the contracted position for a one-count, avoiding any swinging or shoulder involvement.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly and under control back to full extension, resisting the weight the entire way down, and repeat for the prescribed reps.

name: Spiderman Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width, fingers forward, arms straight, and your body in a rigid line from head to heels.
Brace your core and glutes, set your shoulder blades, and keep your neck neutral. This is your starting position.
Inhale and begin lowering your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
As you descend, lift one foot and draw that knee out to the side and forward toward the same-side elbow, keeping your hips level.
Lower until your chest is just above the floor with your knee tucked alongside your elbow, maintaining a tight, flat body line.
Exhale and press explosively back up while simultaneously returning your foot to the starting position.
Alternate the knee-drive side on each successive rep, keeping your hips from rotating or sagging, and continue for the prescribed reps.

name: Spinal Stretch
instructions: Sit upright in a sturdy chair with your back straight, feet planted flat on the floor about hip-width apart.
Interlace your fingers behind your head, draw your elbows out wide, and tuck your chin gently toward your chest.
Brace gently and rotate your upper body to one side, twisting a little further with two or three small, gentle pulses to deepen the rotation comfortably.
From that rotated position, lean your torso forward and down, guiding your elbow toward the floor on the inside of the opposite knee until you feel a stretch through your mid and upper back.
Hold the stretch for several seconds, breathing slowly and avoiding any forcing or bouncing.
Return smoothly to the upright seated position, then repeat the twist, lean, and reach to the other side for an equal hold.

name: Split Clean
instructions: Load a barbell on the floor and stand with your feet directly under your hips, roughly hip-width apart, toes pointed slightly out, with the bar over the middle of your feet and nearly touching your shins.
Squat down and take an overhand (pronated) hook grip just outside your legs, hands about shoulder-width apart, arms long and relaxed.

Set your starting position: drop your hips so your weight is on your heels, lift your chest, brace your core, flatten your lower back into a tight arch, look forward, and position your shoulders slightly in front of and over the bar with shins lightly touching it.

Begin the first pull by driving through your heels and extending the knees to lift the bar off the floor; keep your back angle constant, arms straight, and the bar tracking close to your shins until it passes the knees.

Initiate the second pull as the bar reaches mid-thigh: explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in a jumping motion, brushing the bar against your thighs and accelerating it straight up while keeping the arms straight and the bar close.
At full extension, with your body tall and leaning slightly back, shrug the traps aggressively and pull yourself under the bar by whipping the elbows up, out, and then fast around the bar.

Receive the bar in a split stance: drive one foot forward and the other back as you rack the bar on the front of your shoulders, elbows high so the bar rests on the protracted shoulders and lightly touches the throat, hands relaxed.
Sink into the catch with the front knee tracking over the foot, the rear knee bent, torso upright, and elbows high to secure the rack position.
Recover by driving through your heels, keeping the torso vertical and elbows up; step the front foot back partway, then bring the rear foot up to finish standing tall with feet together.

Breathe in and brace before each rep; exhale at the top of the recovery. Keep the bar close to your body throughout and never let the elbows drop, which causes the bar to roll forward off the shoulders.

name: Split Jerk
instructions: Begin with the barbell racked across the front of your shoulders in the front-rack position, elbows lifted, hands just outside shoulder-width with a loose grip so the bar sits on the shoulders, not the hands.
Stand tall with feet directly under your hips, hip-width apart, weight balanced over your whole foot, core braced, and torso vertical.

Begin the dip: bend only at the knees, keeping the torso perfectly upright and the hips directly under you, dropping straight down a short distance (about a quarter squat) without shifting the hips back.
Reverse the dip explosively by driving straight up through your heels, transferring the leg power into the bar so it leaves the shoulders fast and travels straight up.
As the bar leaves your shoulders, snap your head and chin slightly back out of the bar's path so it can travel in a straight vertical line.
The instant your feet leave the floor, split them aggressively: drive one foot forward and the other backward into a split stance, both knees partially bent, to drop your body under the bar.
Punch your arms to full lockout overhead as you split, receiving the bar with elbows straight, the bar directly over the back of your head, and your weight balanced between the front and rear legs.
Stabilize the catch with a vertical torso, front shin near vertical, rear knee soft, and the bar stacked over your midfoot and shoulders.
Recover by stepping the front foot back a half step, then bringing the rear foot forward to finish standing with feet together and the bar still locked overhead.
Inhale and brace before the dip; keep the bar overhead and arms locked until you have fully recovered. Avoid pressing the bar out with the arms before the legs have driven it up.

name: Split Jump
instructions: Stand tall, then step one foot forward and the other back into a lunge stance, feet about hip-width laterally so you are balanced and not on a tightrope.
Lower into the lunge until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and your rear knee is nearly touching the ground.
Check your position: the front knee should track over the midline of the front foot, torso upright, chest up, and core braced.
Load both legs and swing your arms back behind you to prepare to drive upward.
Explode straight up by extending both legs powerfully through the hips, knees, and ankles, swinging your arms forward and up to gain maximum lift.
While airborne, briefly bring your feet roughly together, then reset them back to the same split position before landing.
Land softly on the balls of the feet first, then absorb the impact by sinking back down into the bottom lunge position with control.
Keep the front knee tracking over the foot on landing and avoid letting it cave inward; reset and repeat for reps, then switch which leg is forward.
Exhale on the jump and inhale as you reset. Stay tall and avoid letting your torso pitch forward over the front knee.

name: Split Snatch
instructions: Load a barbell on the floor with the bar close to or touching your shins, and stand with feet directly below your hips, toes turned out as needed.
Squat down and take a wide (snatch-width) overhand hook grip so that with the bar at your hip crease your arms would be straight and the bar high on the thigh.
Set the start position: drop the hips, lift the chest, brace your core, arch the lower back tightly, look forward, and place your shoulders just in front of and over the bar with arms long.
Begin the first pull by driving through the front of your heels to lift the bar smoothly off the floor, keeping the back angle constant and the bar close until it passes the knees.
Transition into the second pull: explosively extend the hips, knees, and ankles, sweeping the bar in close to the body and accelerating it straight up as fast as possible.
At peak extension, shrug the shoulders hard and allow the elbows to bend high and to the sides to keep pulling the bar upward and yourself down.
Split your feet forcefully into a lunge stance, one foot forward and one back, as you pull yourself under and punch the bar to full lockout overhead.
Receive the bar overhead with arms fully extended and locked, body as low as possible in the split, the bar stacked over the back of the head and your base.

Stand up out of the split by stepping the front foot back, then bringing the rear foot forward to finish with feet together, the bar still locked overhead and over the front of your heels, head and chest up.
Lower the bar under control and carefully return it to the floor. Breathe in and brace before the pull; keep the bar close throughout and never let it swing out in front of you.

name: Split Squat with Dumbbells
instructions: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and let them hang at your sides with a neutral grip, arms straight, shoulders pulled back and down.
Step into a staggered stance: place one foot forward and rest the top of the rear foot on a bench, box, or step behind you so the rear foot is elevated.
Position the front foot far enough forward that when you descend, the front shin stays close to vertical and the front knee can track over the foot rather than jamming far past the toes.
Set your posture: stand tall with chest up, core braced, and a slight forward lean from the hips; this is your starting position.
Descend by bending the front knee and hip, lowering straight down with control until the front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and the rear knee drops toward the ground.
Keep the front knee tracking in line with the front foot and your weight loaded through the front heel and midfoot, not the toes.
Drive up through the front heel, extending the knee and hip to return to the starting position, keeping the torso stable and the dumbbells hanging quietly.
Inhale on the way down and exhale as you drive up. Complete all reps on one leg, then switch the front foot and repeat. Avoid pushing off the rear foot to do the work.

name: Split Squats
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, chest up, and core braced; this is a jumping split-squat (split jump) drill performed for reps.
Jump up and split your legs in the air, landing softly with one leg forward and one leg back in a lunge stance, knees bent and hips lowered slightly on contact.
Land on the ball of the front foot and absorb the impact by flexing both knees, front thigh moving toward parallel and the rear knee dropping toward the floor.
Keep the torso upright and the front knee tracking over the front foot, avoiding any inward collapse of the knee.
Immediately reverse direction, exploding straight up and switching the position of your legs in mid-air so the opposite foot lands forward.
Cushion each landing softly and stay light on your feet, keeping a steady rhythm.
Exhale on each jump and stay braced throughout. Repeat for 5-10 reps per leg, keeping the chest tall and avoiding a forward torso pitch over the front knee.

name: Squat Jerk
instructions: Begin with the barbell racked across the front of your shoulders in the front-rack position, elbows high, hands just outside shoulder-width, the bar resting on the shoulders with a loose grip.
Stand with feet directly under your hips, hip-width apart, torso vertical, weight balanced over the whole foot, and core braced.
Dip by bending only at the knees, keeping the hips directly underneath and the torso perfectly upright, dropping straight down a short distance without letting the hips shift back.
Reverse the dip explosively, driving straight up through your heels to send the bar off the shoulders as fast and powerfully as possible.
As the bar leaves your shoulders, snap your head slightly back out of the bar's path so it can rise in a straight vertical line.
The instant your feet leave the floor, drive them out to just outside your hips, toes turned out as needed, and pull yourself straight down under the bar.
Receive the bar in a full overhead squat: arms fully extended and locked overhead, body sinking into a deep squat, the bar stacked directly over the back of your head and midfoot.
Stabilize the bottom with chest up, elbows locked, and the bar balanced over the front of your heels.
Stand up out of the squat by driving through your heels, keeping the head and chest up and the arms locked overhead, until you are fully erect.

Lower the bar under control and return it carefully to the floor. Inhale and brace before the dip; keep the bar locked overhead until you have fully stood up. This is a technically demanding lift requiring excellent overhead mobility.

name: Squat with Bands
instructions: Set up resistance bands by looping them over the bar sleeves and securing the bottoms to band pegs, the rack base, or heavy dumbbells so there is tension at the top and increasing tension as you stand.
Step under the bar inside the rack and place it across the back of your shoulders on the upper traps (high bar) or across the rear delts (low bar), centering it evenly.

Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and rotate your elbows forward as if trying to bend the bar across your back to lock in a tight upper-back shelf.

Take a big breath into your belly, create a tight arch in your lower back, un-rack the bar by standing up, and step back into position with feet set wide, toes pointed slightly out, head facing forward.
Brace your core hard and begin the descent by pushing your knees out and sitting your hips back, keeping your shins as vertical as possible and the bar tracking over your midfoot.
Continue lowering under control, leaning the torso forward only as much as the bar position requires to keep the bar over your heels, until you break parallel (hip crease below the top of the knee).
Drive up by pushing through your heels and spreading the knees and feet out, leading with your head and chest while accelerating against the increasing band tension.
Continue upward, staying tight from head to toe, until you lock out fully at the top in the starting position.

Exhale forcefully near the top of the rep and re-brace before each descent. Do not let the knees cave inward or the bar drift forward off the heels; the bands accelerate at the top, so keep driving hard until full lockout.

name: Squat with Chains
instructions: Set up the chains by looping a lighter leader chain over each bar sleeve, then attaching the heavy chain to the leader with a snap hook; adjust the leader length so a few links of the heavy chain stay on the floor at the top of the rep.
Step under the bar inside the rack and place it across the back of your shoulders on the upper traps (high bar) or rear delts (low bar), centered evenly.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, squeeze the shoulder blades together, and rotate the elbows forward as if bending the bar across your back to build a tight upper-back shelf.
Take a deep breath into your belly, set a tight arch in the lower back, un-rack the bar, and step back into a wide stance with toes pointed slightly out and head facing forward.
Brace hard and begin the descent by pushing the knees out and sitting the hips back, keeping the shins as vertical as possible and the bar over your midfoot.

Lower under control, leaning the torso forward only as much as the bar position requires to keep the bar over the heels, until you break parallel (hip crease below the top of the knee); the chains deload onto the floor at the bottom, lightening the bar.
Drive up by pushing through your heels and spreading the knees and feet out, leading with the head and chest as the chains progressively lift off the floor and add weight.
Continue upward, staying tight head to toe, until you reach full lockout at the top.
Exhale near the top and re-brace before each rep. Keep the knees tracking out and the bar over the heels; expect the load to feel heaviest at lockout as the chains hang fully off the floor.

name: Squat with Plate Movers
instructions: Set the bar in a rack just below shoulder height and place a sturdy weight plate flat on the floor a couple of feet behind the rack as your moving platform.
Step under the loaded bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders on the upper traps, gripping it with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and elbows pulled forward.
Un-rack the bar by driving up with your legs while straightening your torso, then step back away from the rack.
Adopt a wide stance with toes pointed slightly out and place one foot on the weight plate, the other flat on the floor; keep your head up and chest tall. This is your starting position.
Brace your core and slowly lower into the squat by bending the knees and hips, sitting back, until the angle between your upper leg and calf is slightly less than 90 degrees.
Drive back up as you exhale by pushing through the heels and extending the hips and knees to return to standing.
At the top, side-step toward the foot that is off the plate, bringing your feet together on the opposite side of the plate.
Use your inside foot to push the weight plate, sliding it across the floor to the spot where you were just standing.

Place your inside foot back onto the plate and re-establish the wide stance, then perform the next repetition. Keep the knees tracking over the toes and the torso braced throughout; move the plate in a controlled manner without rushing.

name: Squats - With Bands
instructions: Take a resistance band and stand on the middle of it with both feet about shoulder-width apart so the band is split evenly between your left and right sides.
Grab a handle or end of the band in each hand and bring them up so each rests next to the corresponding side of your face, using a pronated grip with palms facing forward.
Confirm the band tension is even on both sides and equal in height; stand tall with chest up, core braced, and head facing forward. This is your starting position.
Begin the descent by pushing your hips back and bending the knees, sitting down under control until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor while you exhale.
Keep the knees tracking out over the toes, the torso upright, and your weight on the heels and midfoot throughout the descent.
Drive back up to standing by pushing through your heels and extending the hips and knees, keeping the hands fixed beside your face against the increasing band tension.
Exhale on the way up and inhale on the way down; keep the band stable and avoid letting the knees collapse inward. Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Stairmaster
instructions: Step onto the StairMaster and stand upright on the moving steps, holding the side or front handrails lightly for balance and safety.
Use the console to select your workout: choose a manual setting or a preset program, and enter your age and weight if prompted so it can estimate calories burned.
Start at a low level to warm up, then increase the speed or resistance to your target intensity, finding a steady, sustainable climbing rhythm.
Drive the pedals down with your legs in a controlled cadence, stepping fully but not letting the step bottom out on the floor.
Keep your torso tall and upright, shoulders back, core engaged, and avoid hunching over or leaning your full weight onto the handrails, which reduces the workout and strains the wrists.
Step through the whole foot, pushing through the heel and midfoot rather than only the toes, to keep the work in the glutes, quads, and calves.
Use the heart-rate sensors in the handles periodically to monitor your intensity and stay in your target zone.

Maintain a smooth breathing pattern and keep your steps even between legs; finish with a few minutes at a lower level to cool down. Expect this to be more demanding than walking, with a 150 lb person burning over 300 calories in roughly 30 minutes.

name: Standing Alternating Dumbbell Press
instructions: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, knees slightly soft, and core braced to keep the torso stable.
Curl or raise both dumbbells up to shoulder height, palms facing forward and elbows pointing out and down so the dumbbells sit just outside your shoulders. This is your starting position.
Keeping your core tight and torso upright, press one dumbbell straight up overhead until the arm is fully extended, while holding the opposite dumbbell still at your shoulder.
Drive the dumbbell in a straight vertical path and avoid leaning to the side, arching your lower back, or using your legs to jerk the weight up.
Pause briefly with the arm locked out overhead, keeping the wrist stacked over the elbow.
Lower that dumbbell back to the shoulder under control to the starting position.
Press the opposite arm overhead in the same manner, continuing to alternate sides for the prescribed reps.
Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower. Keep the non-working dumbbell stationary at the shoulder and the glutes and core tight to prevent the torso from swaying.

name: Standing Barbell Calf Raise
instructions: Set a barbell in a squat rack at about upper-chest height for safe pickup, and load it with your working weight.
Step under the bar and position it across the back of your shoulders on the upper traps, slightly below the neck, gripping it with both hands at each side.
Un-rack the bar by driving up with your legs and straightening your torso, then step back clear of the rack.

Set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes pointed slightly out, keep your head up and back straight, and maintain a very slight bend in the knees that you will hold throughout (never lock or bend them during the rep). This is your starting position. For greater range of motion you can place the balls of your feet on a sturdy block, though this requires more balance.
Raise your heels as high as possible by extending the ankles and squeezing the calves, exhaling as you rise, while keeping the knees fixed and the body upright.
Hold the fully contracted top position for a one-count to maximize calf tension.
Lower your heels slowly under control as you inhale, bending only at the ankles until you feel a full stretch in the calves at the bottom.
Keep the movement strictly at the ankles with no knee bend or bouncing, and avoid leaning forward or back. Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Standing Barbell Press Behind Neck
instructions: Set a barbell in a squat rack at about upper-chest height for an easy pickup, and load it with your working weight.
Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, slightly below the neck on the upper traps, gripping it with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Un-rack the bar by driving up with your legs and straightening your torso, then step back clear of the rack.
Set your feet about shoulder-width apart with toes pointed slightly out, keep your back straight and chest up, and brace your core. This is your starting position.
Press the bar straight up overhead behind your head by fully extending your arms while breathing out, keeping the bar path vertical and the torso upright.
Lock out with the arms fully extended and the bar stacked directly over the back of the head and shoulders, and hold the contraction for a second.
Lower the bar slowly and under control back down behind the neck to the starting position as you inhale, stopping at about ear or upper-neck height.

Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows and avoid bouncing the bar off the shoulders or pressing with poor shoulder mobility, as this places the shoulders in a vulnerable externally rotated position. Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Standing Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip, palm facing your torso, and stand with feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the waist, keeping your back flat and straight until your torso is almost parallel to the floor, and keep your head up.

Raise the working upper arm so it is tucked close to your torso and parallel to the floor, with the forearm hanging straight down so there is a 90-degree bend at the elbow. This is your starting position; you may brace your free hand on your thigh or a bench for stability.

Keeping the upper arm completely stationary and pinned to your side, extend the elbow to lift the dumbbell back and up until the forearm is parallel to the floor and the whole arm is straight, exhaling as you do so.
Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension and hold the contracted position for a one-count.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the 90-degree starting position under control as you inhale, moving only at the elbow.
Keep only the forearm moving throughout; do not let the upper arm drop or swing, and avoid using momentum from the torso. Complete the prescribed reps, then switch arms and repeat.

name: Standing Bent-Over Two-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Select a light pair of dumbbells and stand with your feet roughly hip to shoulder width apart, knees softly bent to take pressure off your lower back.
Hold one dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and let your arms hang.

Hinge forward at the hips, pushing your hips back and keeping your spine flat and neutral, until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Keep your head in line with your spine, gaze a few feet ahead of you on the floor.

Brace your core and pull your shoulder blades slightly back. Raise your upper arms until they are pinned tight against your sides and parallel to the floor; let the forearms hang straight down so there is roughly a 90-degree angle at the elbow. This is your starting position.

Keeping your upper arms completely locked in place against your torso, exhale and extend your elbows, driving the dumbbells back and up until your arms are fully straight and the weights are behind your hips.
Squeeze your triceps hard at full extension and hold for one second; the only joint moving should be the elbow.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the 90-degree starting position under control, resisting the weight the whole way.
Do not swing the dumbbells or let your upper arms drop, and avoid rounding your back or raising your torso to cheat the weight up. Keep the movement slow and strict.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: Standing Biceps Cable Curl
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ curl bar to the low pulley of a cable station and select a moderate weight.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder width apart, about one to two feet back from the pulley so the cable stays under tension at the bottom.
Grip the bar with an underhand (supinated) grip at roughly shoulder width, palms facing up.
Stand tall with your chest up, shoulders back, core braced, and a slight bend in your knees. Pin your elbows close against your sides; this is your starting position with arms nearly fully extended.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and your elbows locked to your torso, exhale and curl the bar up by contracting your biceps until the bar reaches shoulder level.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top and hold the contracted position for one second.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position under full control, fully straightening the arms without letting the weight stack slam down.
Do not swing your torso, lean back, or let your elbows drift forward to generate momentum; only the forearms should move.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Standing Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart, chest lifted and core gently engaged.
Reach both arms behind your back and clasp your hands together with your palms pressed together.
Straighten your arms fully, then rotate your hands so that your palms face downward toward the floor.
Keeping your arms straight and your torso upright, slowly raise your clasped hands up and away from your body until you feel a stretch across the front of your upper arms, chest, and shoulders.
Avoid hunching your shoulders up toward your ears or rounding your upper back; keep your chest open and stand tall.
Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and relaxing deeper into it, then release.

name: Standing Bradford Press
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at about shoulder height and load it with a light to moderate weight; this is a higher-rep, controlled movement.
Step under the bar and grip it with a pronated (overhand) grip just outside shoulder width, then unrack it so it rests across the front of your shoulders at collarbone height.
Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, knees slightly bent, core braced tight, and glutes squeezed to keep your torso stable and upright.
From the front-rack position, exhale and press the bar upward, but only until it clears the top of your head; do not lock out the elbows.
Lower the bar in a controlled arc down behind your head until your elbows reach roughly a 90-degree angle, keeping the bar path close to your skull.
Press the bar back up over the top of your head, again stopping just short of lockout.
Lower the bar back down to the front starting position at your collarbones to complete one full repetition.
Keep the bar moving smoothly just over the crown of your head throughout; avoid leaning back, flaring the lower ribs, or jerking with the legs.
Maintain continuous tension and never lock the elbows out, which keeps the load on the shoulders.
Alternate front-to-back in this manner for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Standing Cable Chest Press
instructions: Set both pulleys of a dual cable station to roughly chest height and attach a single handle to each, selecting a moderate weight.
Grab one handle in each hand, then step forward to face away from the machine so the cables run behind you and stay under tension.
Position your feet in a staggered stance, one foot ahead of the other, for stability, and brace your core.
Bring your hands up so your upper arms are roughly at a 90-degree angle out to your sides, elbows bent, with your shoulder blades pulled together and chest up. This is your starting position.
Keeping your torso upright and the rest of your body still, exhale and press the handles forward and slightly inward, extending through the elbows until your hands nearly meet in front of your chest.
Squeeze your chest at the end of the press and pause for a moment.
Inhale and return the handles to the starting position under control, letting your elbows travel back and your chest stretch without letting the shoulder blades collapse forward.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears or arching your lower back excessively.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.

name: Standing Cable Lift
instructions: Attach a single standard handle to a cable tower and set the pulley to the lowest position; select a light to moderate weight.
Stand with one side facing the machine and grab the handle with your near (lower) hand, then step away until you are about arm's length from the pulley with tension on the cable.
Set your feet shoulder width apart with your outstretched arm aligned with the angle of the cable.
Squat down slightly and bring your other hand onto the handle so both hands grip it down by your hip on the side nearest the machine; keep your arms extended. This is your starting position.
Brace your core hard and keep your back straight throughout the movement.

In one controlled motion, pull the handle up and diagonally across your body, rotating your torso, pivoting your back foot, and straightening your legs until your arms finish fully extended above the opposite shoulder.
Drive the movement with your hips and core rotation rather than just your arms, keeping your arms relatively straight.
Reverse the motion slowly and under control, lowering back down and rotating your torso to return to the squatted starting position.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then switch your stance so the other side faces the machine and perform the same number of reps on that side.

name: Standing Cable Wood Chop
instructions: Attach a single standard handle to a cable tower and set the pulley to the highest position; select a light to moderate weight.
Stand with one side facing the machine and grab the handle with your near (upper) hand, then step away until you are about arm's length from the pulley with the cable under tension.
Set your feet shoulder width apart with your outstretched arm aligned with the angle of the cable up and away from you.
Reach up with your other hand and grip the handle with both hands overhead on the side nearest the machine, arms extended. This is your starting position.
Brace your core tight and keep your back and arms straight throughout.
In one controlled motion, pull the handle down and diagonally across your body toward your opposite knee, rotating your torso, pivoting your back foot, and bending your knees as you chop downward.
Drive the rotation from your core and hips rather than yanking with the arms, keeping your arms long.
Slowly and under control, reverse the path back up and across to the overhead starting position, letting your torso un-rotate.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, then reposition so the opposite side faces the machine and perform the same number on that side.

name: Standing Calf Raises
instructions: Adjust the shoulder pads of the standing calf raise machine so that when you stand on the platform with knees nearly straight, the pads sit snugly on your shoulders.
Step onto the foot platform and place the balls of both feet on the edge of the block with your heels hanging off the back.
Duck under the pads and settle them across your shoulders, then grip the handles and stand tall to take the weight off the support.

Set your toes pointing straight ahead (or slightly out to bias the inner calf, or slightly in to bias the outer calf). Extend your hips and knees so your torso is upright, keeping a very slight bend in the knees that never locks out. This is your starting position.
